# Herdr: add/remove/edit inline notes on any markdown document

## Problem statement

Herdr's generic markdown viewer renders `.podcast.md` scripts and any `.md` Key File in a **read-only** preview: inline `[NOTE <id>: ...]` markers (PRD §7.1) render as clickable `<id>↗` links, but a human reviewer cannot **add, edit, or delete** a note on a paragraph while reviewing the document. This feature adds an interactive note-edit mode to the markdown viewer so any markdown document can be annotated in place with `[NOTE <id>: ...]` markers — not just podcast scripts.

## Users

- **Podcast producer** — reviewing a `.podcast.md` script; wants to move the cursor onto a paragraph and press a key to add/edit an inline `[NOTE ...]` marker with editorial feedback, without leaving Herdr.
- **General reviewer** — annotating any markdown file (wiki pages, docs, other `.md` Key Files) with the same mechanism.

### User stories

- As a podcast producer, I want to review a `.podcast.md` script, move the cursor onto a paragraph, and press a key to add or edit an inline `[NOTE ...]` marker on that paragraph, so I can give editorial feedback without leaving Herdr.
- As a reviewer, I want to press another key to delete an existing note from a paragraph, so I can withdraw or clear feedback.
- As a user, I want this to work on any markdown file (not just podcast scripts), so I can annotate docs, wiki pages, and other `.md` content with the same mechanism.

## Expected behaviour

1. In the markdown viewer, the cursor can select any paragraph/block of the document (paragraph-by-paragraph or line-based selection within a paragraph).
2. An add/edit key chord on the selected paragraph opens an input form: pre-filled with the existing note text if the paragraph already carries a `[NOTE <id>: ...]` marker (edit mode), otherwise empty (add mode).
3. Saving writes the marker inline in the paragraph at a stable position, following the PRD §7.1 convention `[NOTE <id>: ...]` — `<id>` is a Worklog note-child id when the document is linked to an episode work item; a local placeholder scheme otherwise.
4. A delete key chord removes the existing note marker from the selected paragraph.
5. The edited markdown is written back to the file (surgical edit — all other content preserved), and the viewer reflects the change.
6. Non-podcast markdown documents behave identically.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Cursor navigation in the markdown viewer can select any paragraph/block of a `.md` document.
- [ ] Add/edit on a selected paragraph with no existing note creates an inline `[NOTE <id>: ...]` marker with the entered text.
- [ ] Add/edit on a paragraph that already has a note opens the form pre-filled with the current note text; saving updates the marker in place.
- [ ] Delete on a paragraph with a note removes the marker from the file.
- [ ] The edited document is persisted to disk and the viewer reflects the change; all other file content is preserved byte-for-byte.
- [ ] Behaviour works identically for any markdown file, not only podcast scripts.
- [ ] Existing inline-note link rendering (`<id>↗`) still works after edits.
- [ ] When editing a podcast script with a known episode id, note-child work items are created/resolved per PRD §7.3 (`wl create --parent <episode>` on add; `DONE` marker + resolution comment on delete/resolve).
- [ ] Automated tests cover add, edit, delete, and persistence for both podcast and generic markdown documents.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (README "Generic md viewer" / "Inline note links" sections, code comments).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Reuse the existing generic markdown viewer (`packages/herdr/src/md-viewer.ts`), chord/shortcut machinery (`shortcuts.json`, `src/shortcut-config.ts`), and modal form-dialog machinery (`src/form-dialog.ts`).
- Marker format must follow PRD §7.1 exactly: `[NOTE <id>: ...]` inline in the paragraph; resolved notes use `[NOTE <id>: DONE ...]` (§7.3). Note text may span multiple lines and runs to the first `]` (`NOTE_MARKER_RE` in `md-viewer.ts`).
- Note-child sync applies only when the document is a podcast script with a resolvable episode work item id; for generic markdown use a local placeholder id scheme and skip `wl` child creation (never silently skip when an episode *is* resolvable — mirror the podcast-script skill's warning behaviour).
- File path resolution for both read and write-back must follow the existing `resolveKeyFilePath` convention (WL-0MSGEA9AY0080V4Q): resolve against the worklog root, not the plugin process CWD.
- Writer must be side-effect-free/testable like the rest of `md-viewer.ts` (pure functions with dependency-injected file reader/writer where practical).

## Existing state

- `md-viewer.ts` renders read-only: `renderNoteLinks()` rewrites `[NOTE <id>: ...]` markers to `<id>↗` links; `renderMarkdown()` / `renderMarkdownViewer()` produce ANSI viewer lines (frontmatter skipped for file bodies).
- The detail view embeds the viewer via `renderFileViewer()` in `src/worklist.ts`; navigation is currently scroll-based (`[↑↓/j:k] scroll`, `[g/G] top/bot`, `[esc] back`, `[q] quit`) with a focus model (`detailToCFocus`) distinguishing ToC from document scroll region.
- Chord commands already drive modal full-pane form input for unknown `<identifier>` placeholders (`form-dialog.ts`); `<id>` is an auto-resolved known identifier.

## Desired change

Interactive note editing on top of the existing viewer: add a cursor/selection model over markdown blocks, wire add/edit/delete chords through the existing shortcut registry, reuse the form dialog for note text entry (pre-filled in edit mode), persist edits back to the file, and (for podcast scripts with a known episode id) drive the PRD §7.3 note-child lifecycle through the `wl` CLI.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/md-viewer.ts` — NOTE-marker detection/extraction helpers; possible insert/update/remove helpers for markers within a paragraph (or a new sibling module, e.g. `md-note-edit.ts`).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — viewer pane integration: paragraph cursor/selection, chord handling, write-back, episode-id resolution and note-child sync.
- `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts` — reuse/extend modal form for note text entry (pre-filled in edit mode).
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` / `src/shortcut-config.ts` — new chords for add/edit note and delete note.
- `packages/herdr/src/md-viewer.test.ts` (and/or a new test module) — add/edit/delete/persistence tests for podcast and generic markdown.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document the new interactive note-edit mode in the "Generic md viewer" / "Inline note links" sections.

## Related work

- WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29 — Related Docs row + open in viewer (completed) — introduced the md viewer entry points.
- WL-0MSGEA9AY0080V4Q — md viewer path resolution against worklog root (completed) — `resolveKeyFilePath` convention to reuse for write-back.
- WL-0MSKFFJWD002BQJ5 — proper markdown renderer (completed) — the GFM rendering stack being extended.
- WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I — detail view ToC (completed) — focus/scroll model precedent (`detailToCFocus`, ToC vs document region).
- WL-0MSHWHP0S0036DDU — tests: Related Docs row, detail ToC, open-in-viewer (completed) — existing test patterns for the viewer.
- WL-0MSNSZ4R6009AU0N — herdr plugin `npm run build` fails (TS6059 rootDir violations from test files) (open) — **blocker**: build currently fails, so the "full test suite passes" criterion cannot be verified until fixed.
- `.pi/skills/wiki-podcast-script/SKILL.md` (open_source_llm) — `[NOTE <id>: ...]` marker convention (PRD §7.1) and note-child lifecycle (PRD §7.3); reference only, unchanged by this feature.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Keybinding conflict** — the description's suggested `n` chord likely collides with the existing `/intake` chord in the worklist view (`shortcuts.json`). Assumption: implementer verifies the chord registry and picks non-conflicting chords (possibly view-scoped). Flag for decision at implementation, not a blocking question.
- **Local placeholder id scheme** — unspecified for generic markdown; assumption: implementer defines a documented, stable scheme (e.g. `LOCAL-<seq>`), kept idempotent across re-opens where practical.
- **File-write safety** — write-back must be a surgical paragraph-level edit preserving all other file content; recommend a test asserting byte-level preservation of untouched sections.
- **Marker-parsing edge cases** — `NOTE_MARKER_RE` is non-greedy to the first `]`, so note text containing `]` (or `[NOTE`) would parse incorrectly; implementer should document this limitation and, where practical, prevent/escape such content in the editor.
- **Scope-creep risk** — keep note-child sync limited to podcast scripts with a resolvable episode id; generic markdown stays local-only. Extra opportunities (note list panel, cross-file annotation, undo history) should be filed as separate work items, not folded into this one.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Any interview questions? — Answer (intake, `Map`): **No interview required.** The existing work-item description (created 2026-08-08, updated 2026-08-13) already contains a summary, three user stories, expected behaviour, a suggested implementation approach, nine acceptance criteria, and references — sufficient seed context to draft the brief directly. Source: WL-0MSKV6SKK008MMXR description.
- Assumption: keybinding choice and local placeholder id scheme left as implementer decisions (see Risks & assumptions) — flagged, not blocking.
- Blocked-by: WL-0MSNSZ4R6009AU0N (herdr build failure) recorded as a blocking relationship on the work item; verified locally that `npm run build` in `packages/herdr` currently fails with TS6059.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSKFFJWD002BQJ5** – Use a proper markdown renderer for detail view description and md viewer (completed)
- **WL-0MSHUMX5C004NC4O** – Extensible shortcuts.json: bundled defaults + project-local overrides (open)
- **WL-0MNX8MASB007TADZ** – Add tests for dialog focus cycling and multiline update comment (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: acceptance, add, adds, already, another (+156 more)

## Summary

`wl sync`'s merge logic can enter a self-sustaining conflict loop that silently corrupts item state. Observed in the field (LP-0MSDRRPV0001TCLX in /home/rgardler/projects/llm): a completed, audit-approved item's local `updatedAt` advanced at every sync (21:36:19Z → 21:53:40Z → 21:57:35Z) and the final sync chose a local `deleted` state (empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason`) over the remote `open` state — soft-deleting the item while the remote `worklog/data` ref still had it `open`/`plan_complete`. No agent ran `wl delete`; the state arose purely from merge behavior. The item had to be manually restored via `StatusLifecycle`.

## Root-cause hypothesis (verified against src/sync.ts)

1. **Same-timestamp merge bumps `updatedAt` unconditionally.** `mergeSameTimestampItems` (src/sync.ts ~L423) sets `merged.updatedAt = new Date().toISOString()` whenever local and remote have the same `updatedAt` but different content (e.g. a `sortIndex` conflict from concurrent `wl re-sort`, or any divergent field). This bump makes the item *newer* than the remote on the next sync, so the local value keeps winning and the timestamp keeps advancing on every sync — a conflict loop with no real user edit behind it. Under auto-sync / multi-pane / multi-agent use this can repeat indefinitely.

2. **Unattributed soft-delete wins over a live remote item.** `deleteSingle` (node_modules/@worklog/shared/src/database.ts) sets `status: 'deleted'` but leaves `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` empty. In `mergeDifferentTimestampItems`, `status` is resolved by plain timestamp recency: `status='deleted'` is a non-default value, so if the local copy is (artifactually) newer, `status` flips to `deleted` even though `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` are empty — silently soft-deleting an item the remote still considers open. There is no delete-side equivalent of the close-preservation logic that protects `status='completed'`/`stage='done'`.

## Expected behaviour

- Repeated syncs of the same divergent state must converge: once both sides hold the merged item, `updatedAt` must stop advancing and the item must not flip-flop.
- An unattributed delete marker (status='deleted' with empty deletedBy/deleteReason) must never override a remote item that is open/in-progress/completed. Deletes should only propagate when they are real, attributed deletes (non-empty deletedBy or deleteReason), mirroring the close-preservation model.

## Suggested approach

- In `mergeSameTimestampItems`, only bump `updatedAt` when the merge actually changed a user-visible field (or converge without bumping when the merged result equals one side). Consider whether `sortIndex` conflicts alone should bump at all.
- Add delete-side protection in `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` (and same-timestamp path): treat `status='deleted'` like `status='completed'` — require the delete to be the newer change AND attributed (deletedBy/deleteReason non-empty) before propagating it; otherwise keep the remote live status.
- Add regression tests in tests/sync.test.ts reproducing both failure modes.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Regression test: two divergent copies with the same `updatedAt` (differing only in `sortIndex` or one metadata field) synced repeatedly converge — `updatedAt` stops advancing after the merged state is present on both sides (no unbounded bumping).
- AC2: Regression test: local `status='deleted'` with empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` vs remote `status='open'` — merge keeps the remote `open` state (or at minimum never produces a soft-deleted item with no attribution).
- AC3: Regression test: an *attributed* delete (non-empty `deletedBy`) that is newer than the remote still propagates (delete remains possible when intentional).
- AC4: Full existing test suite (npm test) passes with no regressions.

## Key Files

- `src/sync.ts` — Contains `mergeSameTimestampItems` and `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` functions that need modification
- `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` — Merge utility functions (`isDefaultValue`, `stableValueKey`, etc.)
- `tests/sync.test.ts` — Existing sync tests; new regression tests should be added here
- `node_modules/@worklog/shared/src/database.ts` — `deleteSingle` function that creates unattributed deletes

## Related Work

- **WL-0MSOYWZTH003JFVD**: Sync: regression guard — refuse import of default-value regressions from newer remote state
- **WL-0MT2KZH0I005XUWE**: Deletion propagation in delta exports
data.title: Fix sync-conflict loop: same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt indefinitely and unattributed soft-delete wins over remote open item

## Summary

**Re-scoped** follow-up to the completed twin **WL-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO** (shipped in
v1.0.13, commit `9e8ca646`, epic WL-0MTFNII4X00632CG), which already delivered this
item's original AC1–AC3 (the unbounded same-timestamp conflict loop and the
unattributed-soft-delete override). Those are now shipped; this item is narrowed to the
**residual** that the earlier fix left in place.

**Residual defect:** `mergeSameTimestampItems` still writes a **fresh wall-clock
`updatedAt`** whenever a non-`sortIndex` field is reconciled and the merged result
differs from local (`src/sync.ts` ~L833):

```ts
if (nonSortIndexMerged && !mergedEqualsLocal) {
  merged.updatedAt = new Date().toISOString();   // <-- wall-clock stamp on a merge
}
```

A merge is not a user edit. Stamping "now" silently re-timestamps audit-fresh items and
marks valid audits stale, and it feeds further timestamp churn on subsequent syncs.

## Problem

Observed on 2026-09-21: a single sync (`18:35:58 → 18:36:17`) logged **244 conflicts**
and re-timestamped **95 items** to `2026-09-21T18:36:06` (48 of them `completed`).
**14 `completed`/`in_review` items lost audit freshness purely from merge churn** — e.g.
*Sync: regression guard…* (`WL-0MSOYWZTH003JFVD`) was audited 2026-08-31, had no activity
since, yet became "stale" because the merge moved `updatedAt`.

Because `updatedAt` underpins `isAuditFresh` (until the content-fingerprint gate lands,
P1), merge churn drives false staleness → redundant downtime re-audits → more writes →
more churn.

## Expected behaviour

- A merge must **never** introduce a wall-clock `updatedAt`. A same-timestamp merge
  inherits an existing timestamp (the two sides are equal by definition), so repeated
  syncs of the same divergence are **quiescent**.
- Merged content still converges on both sides.
- Audit freshness is unaffected by a merge that did not change user-authored content.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: `mergeSameTimestampItems` no longer calls `new Date().toISOString()` for
  `updatedAt`; the merged item inherits the (equal) existing timestamp.
- AC2: Regression test: two divergent copies with the same `updatedAt` (differing in one
  non-`sortIndex` field) merged repeatedly are quiescent — `updatedAt` never advances and
  content converges.
- AC3: Regression test: a same-timestamp conflict resolved to remote content leaves
  `updatedAt` unchanged and `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` true for a prior valid
  audit.
- AC4: `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` continues to inherit the winning side's timestamp
  (no wall-clock); an explicit assertion is added.
- AC5: Full existing test suite passes, including the sync convergence + delete-protection
  tests shipped under WL-0MTFNII4X00632CG.

## Notes / open questions

- The original bump existed so the merged side would be unambiguously "newer" on the next
  sync. With both sides writing the merged result, convergence should hold without it;
  confirm via the AC2 quiescence test.
- A same-timestamp `sortIndex`-only conflict already never bumps (unchanged).

## References

- discovered-from: WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE
- shipped predecessor (do not re-implement): WL-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO (completed/done,
  v1.0.13, `9e8ca646`), WL-0MTFNII4X00632CG, WL-0MT2KZH0I005XUWE
- related-to: WL-0MUBVH5S0008NQ9K (P1 — content-fingerprint freshness gate)
- evidence: `.worklog/logs/sync.log` (2026-09-21T18:35:58 → 18:36:17)
data.title: Sync merges must not re-timestamp audit-fresh items (remove wall-clock updatedAt bump)

# Intake Draft — Herdr selection list: collapsible group headings with item counts

**Work item:** WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94

## Problem statement

The Herdr work-item selection list renders group separators (`── Group 1 ──`, `── Idea ──`, `── In Review ──`) between items, but these heading rows are pure chrome: they carry no item count, they cannot be collapsed to hide a group's items, and up/down navigation skips over them entirely (the cursor can never land on a heading). With several groups on screen this wastes vertical space and gives the user no way to focus on one group.

## Users

- **Herdr plugin users** (operators running the work-item selection list pane).

User stories:
- "As a producer reviewing the worklist, I want each group heading to show how many items it contains, so I can see at a glance where the bulk of the work is."
- "As a producer, I want to collapse a group by pressing Tab while its heading is selected, so I can hide items I'm not interested in and focus on the rest."
- "As a producer, I want up/down navigation to land on heading rows, so I can reach them to collapse/expand them."

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Each group heading row displays the label plus the number of items in that group (e.g. `── Group 1 (4) ──`). The count reflects the top-level items assigned to the group in the current view (post stage-filter), regardless of collapse state.
- AC2: Up/down navigation (j/k and arrow keys) moves the selection onto heading rows as well as items; headings are no longer skipped. Page up/down, first/last, and wrap-around behave consistently with the heading rows included.
- AC3: Pressing Tab while a heading row is selected toggles that group's collapse state: collapsed hides the group's items from both the render and navigation; expanded shows them. Tab on an item row keeps its existing expand/collapse-children behaviour unchanged.
- AC4: Collapsed-group state lives in memory for the session (like `expandedItems`), survives list refreshes, and does not persist across pane restarts.
- AC5: When a heading is selected, the metadata panel shows the group info (label + count) rather than stale item metadata; Enter on a heading is a no-op (only Tab toggles).
- AC6: The `rows - 1` line-count invariant, code-freeze banner, metadata-panel sizing, and stage-filter views keep working; full Herdr test suite (vitest for packages/herdr) passes.
- AC7: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and any relevant docs site entries.

## Constraints

- The change is confined to the Herdr plugin (`packages/herdr`) — the Pi TUI Worklog extension has its own browse implementation and is out of scope.
- `packages/herdr` has zero npm dependencies; the implementation must stay self-contained (the existing duplicated `grouping.ts` pattern).
- Tab already toggles hierarchy expand/collapse for items with children — that behaviour must not regress.
- The renderer must never exceed `rows - 1` lines (pane line-count invariant, WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO).

## Existing state

- Group separators are rendered by `createListRenderer` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` when the `group` field changes between items in the flattened list; they are derived at render time and are NOT rows in any navigation model.
- Navigation (`WorkItemListState.moveUp/moveDown/pageUp/pageDown`, `_clampSelection`, `_adjustScroll`, `flatCount`) indexes into the flattened items list, so headings are never selected.
- Tab maps to the `'toggle-expand'` action (`keyToAction`), which expands/collapses top-level items with children; the main TUI loop fetches children on demand for that action.
- Group assignments come from `regroupWorkItems` (packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts), which stamps every selected item with a numeric `group` and a `groupLabel` (`Critical Group N`, `Group N`, `Idea`, `Other`, `In Review`).

## Desired change

Introduce a first-class **display-rows model** in `WorkItemListState` that interleaves heading rows with item rows:

- New heading entry type (e.g. `{ kind: 'heading', group, groupLabel, count, collapsed }`) produced by a `getDisplayRows()`-style method over the flattened items (children of expanded parents included; items of collapsed groups excluded).
- Navigation, clamping, and scrolling operate over display rows so the cursor lands on headings; `getSelectedItem()` returns `null` for a heading selection (metadata panel then renders group info).
- New collapsed-groups state (`Set<number>` in memory) with toggle on Tab when a heading row is selected; refresh carries the set over (by group number, mirroring `expandedItems` handling).
- `createListRenderer` renders heading rows directly from the display model (label + `(count)` + collapse arrow) and stops deriving separators from group transitions; the visible-window budget logic (`countSeparators`) is reworked for heading rows.
- Tab routing: heading row → toggle group; item row → existing expand/collapse-children path (including the on-demand children fetch in the TUI loop).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — display-rows model, heading type, collapse state, navigation over rows, Tab routing, renderer heading rows + counts.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — heading rendering (counts, collapse arrow), navigation onto/over headings, Tab toggle, metadata panel on heading selection.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-expand-refresh.test.ts` — collapsed groups survive refresh; Tab-on-item children fetch unaffected.

## Assumptions

- "Headings" = the group separator rows (`── <Group Label> ──`) produced by `regroupWorkItems` group assignments. No other heading type exists in the list.
- Count = top-level items in the group in the current view; children of expanded parents do not add to the count (they never carry group metadata).
- Count is shown whether the group is collapsed or expanded.
- Enter on a heading is a no-op; Tab is the only toggle key (per request).
- Collapsed state is in-memory only, consistent with `expandedItems` (no settings persistence).
- Collapse keyed by group number; if a refresh regroups and renumbers groups, the collapsed set may apply to a shifted group — acceptable in-session, same class of behaviour as `expandedItems`.
- **Scope-creep risk:** extending this to the Pi TUI Worklog extension or persisting collapse state to settings would expand scope — record such follow-ups as separate work items rather than folding them in.
- **Regression risk:** reworking the navigation model from `flatCount` (items only) to display rows touches clamping, scroll adjustment, wrap-around, refresh selection-restore, and the renderer's line budget — the existing expand/refresh and line-count tests must stay green.

## Related work

- WL-0MSAK8YLB0025EGW — Herdr plugin: fix work item list grouping (duplicate In Review sections, wrong group order): introduced the render-time group separators this feature builds on.
- WL-0MSAKPVR9005B6XJ — Rewrite assignItemGroups + next.ts ordering: canonical group ordering/labelling used by the headings.
- WL-0MS8XOOMN0022LLH — Pi TUI browse flow: re-fetch + heading count: heading counts exist in the Pi TUI browse widget; Herdr parity for counts.
- WL-0MS4L81QF0013081 — Tab key to expand/collapse children in selection browser: established the Tab expand/collapse pattern this feature extends.
- WL-0MSBVBNGH002RDP5 — Herdr worklist: expanded items momentarily collapse on list refresh (flicker): refresh/children handling this feature must preserve.
- WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO — pane line-count invariant (renderer budget) this feature's heading-row accounting must preserve.
- WL-0MS39YPR5005MJ81 — Feature gap analysis: Pi TUI Worklog extension vs Herdr plugin: prior comparison of the two selection lists (find_related automated match).

Automated find_related report: full (untruncated) version persisted at `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should up/down navigation land on heading rows? — Answer (operator): the request notes "moving up and down does not select the heading lines" as the current gap; selectable headings are required for Tab-on-heading to work, so the feature includes heading selection. Source: interactive request.
- Q: What does the count show? — Answer (assumption documented, no question asked): top-level items in the group, current view, both collapsed and expanded. Source: reasonable default consistent with the data model.
- Q: Should collapsed state persist across restarts? — Answer (assumption documented, no question asked): no — in-memory like `expandedItems`. Source: consistent with existing hierarchy expand state.

# Feature Request: --fields field-selection for wl list / wl search

## Problem statement

wl list and wl search return full work-item records (or compact snippets for search), with no way to request only the fields a caller needs. Full-record dumps are the root cause of token waste documented in SA-0MSLVQMKF000ESPZ (SorraAgents): bare wl list --json = 5.3 MB / 1,861 records; wl list --status completed = 4.9 MB; scripts (ship gates, triage, code-review) download tens-to-hundreds of KB of fields they never read (e.g. full descriptions) when they only need id, title, status, stage, priority.

## User stories

- As a release-gate script, I want wl list --stage in_review --fields id,title,status,stage,needsProducerReview --json so I stop downloading 4.9 MB of descriptions I discard.
- As an agent running /skill:audit, I want a compact project-status query (fields id,title,status,stage,priority) so the worklog overview stays in the low-KB range.
- As a triage helper, I want wl list --priority critical --tags test-failure --fields id,title,description --json so my match heuristics get exactly the fields they need.

## Expected behaviour

- New option on wl list and wl search: --fields comma-separated (e.g. id,title,status,stage,priority).
- Output objects contain ONLY the requested fields (plus id always, for usability); unknown field names are rejected with a clear error listing valid fields.
- wl list and wl search share the same field vocabulary: id, title, description, status, stage, priority, issueType, assignee, tags, createdAt, updatedAt, parentId, needsProducerReview, sortIndex.
- --json output shape unchanged (same keys; omitted fields absent). Human output uses the same projection for concise display.
- -f as shorthand is acceptable; must not clash with existing flags (-F/--format already taken).

## Acceptance criteria

1. wl list --fields id,title --json returns objects with only id/title; verified for filters and bare queries.
2. wl search term --fields id,title,status --json returns compact objects with only those fields.
3. Invalid field names produce a non-zero exit and a clear error listing valid fields.
4. Output size reduction verified: wl list --stage in_review --fields id,title --json is smaller than the full-record equivalent (target: >=90% reduction for the completed-status case cited above).
5. Existing output without --fields is unchanged (backward compatible); full test suite passes.

## Plan

### Child Work Items (dependency-ordered)

1. **WL-0MT5L3BGA001MKOP** - Create pickFields() projection helper module
2. **WL-0MT5L4MGL000Z43Y** - Write unit tests for pickFields projection helper (depends on 1)
3. **WL-0MT5L55AQ002WTGQ** - Add --fields option to wl list (depends on 1, 2)
4. **WL-0MT5L6G88006N4WD** - Add --fields option to wl search (depends on 1, 2)
5. **WL-0MT5L6TLQ004NDLK** - Integration test: end-to-end --fields flag verification (depends on 3, 4)

### Implementation Approach

1. Create packages/shared/src/fields.ts with pickFields(item, fields?) helper
2. Add fields?: string to ListOptions and SearchOptions in cli-types.ts
3. Apply pickFields projection in list.ts before JSON output
4. Apply pickFields projection in search.ts before JSON output
5. Write unit tests and integration tests

### Review Stages Summary

1. Requirements & AC alignment: All 5 ACs map to user stories and expected behaviour. No gaps or contradictions.
2. Completeness: Description has all required sections. Key files are valid.
3. Sequencing & dependencies: Test items before implementation items. Dependencies properly set.
4. Scope sizing: Small effort, Low risk - appropriate for scope.
5. Acceptance & testability: All ACs are testable with clear pass/fail criteria.
6. Polish & handoff: Plan is copy-pasteable and actionable.

## Plan Changelog

- 2026-08-23T09:09Z - Plan created with 5 child work items. Pre-check: Small effort, Low risk. All review stages passed.

## Appendix

- Q: Should --fields support nested field access (e.g. auditResult.readyToClose)? Answer (plan agent): No. The work item scope is flat field selection only. Nested access can be added later if needed. Final: not in scope.
- Q: Should -f shorthand be supported? Answer (plan agent): Yes, but -f is not taken in either list or search. Final: -f can be added as shorthand.

# Feature Request / Bug: FTS index freshness + silent query-error swallowing

## Problem statement

`wl search` help advertises "Full-text search over work items (title, description, comments, tags)" — and comment indexing is implemented and *works after a manual rebuild* (verified: column-scoped `comments:"Closed with reason"` MATCH returns rows; 1,567/2,462 indexed rows contain comment text; `wl search '"v0.1.11"'` returns comment matches). Two defects make comment search unreliable in practice:

1. **The FTS index is never updated incrementally.** `upsertFtsEntry(item)` (dist/persistent-store.js:963) is defined but has **zero call sites** — it is dead code. `saveWorkItem` / `saveComment` do not touch `worklog_fts`. The index only refreshes via the manual `wl search --rebuild-index` command. Any work item or comment created/edited since the last rebuild is invisible to search — silently stale results (recent items/comments missing, duplicates not detected by triage heuristics).

2. **Malformed FTS5 queries fail silently.** An unquoted punctuated query such as `wl search v0.1.11` produces an FTS5 syntax error (`fts5: syntax error near "."`) that the catch block (persistent-store.js ~1157) swallows, returning `[]` with no warning. Users cannot distinguish "no matches" from "invalid query". Version strings, file paths, and ids (all common search targets in this tool) are exactly the strings that trip this.

## User stories

- As an agent deduplicating test-failure work items, I want recently added comments and items to appear in `wl search` without requiring a manual `--rebuild-index`, so I don't create duplicates.
- As a user searching for `v0.1.11` or a file path, I want either correct matches or an explicit "invalid query" error, not a silent empty result.

## Expected behaviour

- Creating/updating a work item or adding/deleting a comment keeps the FTS index current (call `upsertFtsEntry` from the save paths; call `deleteFtsEntry` from item/comment delete paths).
- FTS5 query syntax errors are surfaced to the user (non-zero exit + clear message), not swallowed; only genuinely zero-match queries return empty results.
- Consider quoting/escaping hygiene: document (and optionally auto-quote) punctuated terms; an option like `--rebuild-index` remains as the backstop for bulk migrations.
- Optional: automatic index rebuild (or per-item reindex) when the index is detected empty/stale (e.g. hash-based staleness already used for embeddings).

## Suggested implementation approach

1. Wire `upsertFtsEntry` into `saveWorkItem` (dist/persistent-store.js:299) and into `saveComment`/comment-delete paths (comments currently don't trigger any FTS update at all).
2. Change `searchFts`'s catch block to rethrow/flag syntax errors (or validate the query with a dry MATCH first) so the command layer can report `error: invalid query syntax` with the offending term.
3. Add unit tests: new item searchable immediately after save; new comment searchable immediately after add; punctuated query error surfaces; delete removes from index.

## Acceptance criteria

1. After `wl create` + `wl comment add`, both the title and the comment text are found by `wl search` WITHOUT running `--rebuild-index`.
2. `wl search v0.1.11` (unquoted punctuated term) exits non-zero with a clear "invalid query — quote phrases" message instead of silently returning 0.
3. Deleting an item/comment removes it from subsequent search results.
4. `wl search --rebuild-index` still works as the manual backstop; full test suite passes.

## Related work

- related-to: SA-0MSLVQMKF000ESPZ (SorraAgents) — its analysis assumed comments were not searchable; this request resolves that gap and would enable comment-based remediation queries (e.g. `shipped in v1.0.0` close-reason sweep).
- related-to: WL-0MSLW8GHQ0092PJK — `--fields` projection for list/search; both improve wl CLI efficiency.
data.title: FTS search: keep index fresh (wire upsertFtsEntry into save paths) and surface query syntax errors

# Downtime audit-tier wl failure silently collapses to null

**discovered-from:** WL-0MSKUG2WW0058A7W (audit gap AC3, follow-up 1 of 3)

## Problem

The downtime worker's audit tier swallows wl failures as if the tier were empty. `getNextAuditCandidate` (packages/herdr/src/index.ts:389-391) returns `null` in its catch block for ANY wl CLI error or unparseable output — identical to a genuinely empty audit tier (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts:374`). The caller `dispatchDowntimeWork` (packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:523) cannot distinguish the two, so:

- An audit-tier wl failure counts as NO strike (the three-strike rule never fires for it — only plan/intake-tier failures do).
- No log entry is written — the failure is invisible.
- The worker falls through to the plan tier and appears healthy even when the audit query is persistently broken (e.g. a wl failure specific to `wl list --status completed --stage in_review`), silently disabling the audit dispatch tier forever.

Contrast: the plan/intake tiers use `DowntimeNextResult` with an `ok:false` channel that the worker counts as a CLI-error strike (downtime-worker.ts:555-566). The audit tier has no error channel.

## User story

"As an operator, when the downtime audit tier's wl lookup fails, I want that failure to be observable (a strike or a log entry) rather than silently treated as 'no audit candidates', so a persistently broken audit tier cannot silently stop producing audits."

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `getNextAuditCandidate` distinguishes a wl/parse failure from a genuinely empty tier (returns an error outcome, not `null`).
- [ ] An audit-tier failure counts toward the three-strike rule (or otherwise leaves a durable trace via recordError) instead of silently falling through.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: failure → strike/log; empty → no-candidate behavior unchanged; success path unchanged.
- [ ] packages/herdr/README.md failure-path logging section updated to reflect the fixed behavior.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/index.ts:356-391 (getNextAuditCandidate)
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:523, 555-566 (dispatch + strike handling)
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts (tests)

# Intake Brief: Downtime claim failure discarded — dispatch proceeds and is recorded as success

## Problem statement

A bug was discovered during audit gap AC3 (WL-0MSKUG2WW0058A7W) where the downtime worker's pre-dispatch claim failure was silently discarded — the claim dep returned `{success, error}` but the result was ignored, so the dispatch proceeded and was recorded as SUCCESS even when the claim failed. This could allow duplicate sessions (two panes dispatching the same item) and false success audit records.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Claim failure leaves a durable trace (log entry, error record, or outcome reason)
2. Dispatch outcome reflects claim failure (design: fail-closed vs proceed-but-mark)
3. Unit tests cover claim failure → observable outcome; claim success → unchanged
4. packages/herdr/README.md failure-path logging section updated

## Current state (absorbed)

This bug was **already fixed** by commit `76ac767e` (WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN: "Downtime dispatcher CAS claim + plan/intake marker exclusion"), which explicitly states it "absorbs WL-0MSLWJ310000ND0X and WL-0MSLWJ3I70031Z8U". The fix was implemented as part of the RCA fix design (WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT).

# Downtime pane spawn failure invisible — dispatch still logged as success

**Headline:** A spawn-to-pi.sh failure in `spawnDowntimePane` is invisible to the downtime worker, and the dispatch is incorrectly recorded as a success.

## Problem statement

`spawnDowntimePane` (packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:662-671) spawns detached with `stdio: 'ignore'` and `unref()`s the child — there is no `error` listener and no `exit` handler. A spawn-level failure (ENOENT/EACCES on send-to-pi.sh) can crash the plugin process, and a script-level failure (non-zero exit) is invisible. `recordDispatchAudit` always writes SUCCESS, conflating "dispatch attempted" with "agent pane actually opened".

## Users

- **As an operator**, when the downtime worker cannot open the agent pane, I want that failure to be observable (handled error, exit-status trace, or a non-success outcome) so the dispatch log does not claim success for a pane that never appeared.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A spawn `error` event is handled (no unhandled-exception crash of the plugin process).
2. A spawn failure or non-zero script exit is observable: an error/exit trace is recorded and the dispatch outcome reflects the actual state (design: attach exit/error handlers and distinguish "attempted" from "opened" in `recordDispatchAudit`).
3. Unit tests cover: spawn error → handled + observable; non-zero exit → observable; success path unchanged.
4. `packages/herdr/README.md` failure-path logging section updated.
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Fire-and-forget semantics:** The spawn is currently fire-and-forget; handlers must not block or change the detachment behavior (child must remain detached and unref'd).
- **Backward compatibility:** The success path (pane opened successfully) must continue to record dispatch as SUCCESS with no behavioral change.
- **Audit log integrity:** The dispatch log format must accommodate a new outcome state (e.g., "failed" or "attempted") without breaking downstream consumers.

## Existing state

- `spawnDowntimePane` uses `child_process.spawn` with `stdio: 'ignore'`, `detached: true`, and `child.unref()` (downtime-worker.ts:662-671).
- `recordDispatchAudit` always writes a SUCCESS entry (downtime-worker.ts:582-600).
- Call sites in `dispatchDowntimeWork` await `spawnAgentPane` (returns immediately) then call `recordDispatchAudit`.
- No error or exit handlers exist on the spawned child process.

## Desired change

1. Add `error` and `exit` event handlers to the spawned child process that capture failure states.
2. Modify `recordDispatchAudit` (or the call chain) to accept an outcome parameter and distinguish "attempted" from "opened" — record error/exit details when applicable.
3. Add unit tests for all three paths: spawn error, non-zero exit, success.
4. Update documentation in `packages/herdr/README.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:656-671` — `defaultDowntimeSpawn` + `spawnDowntimePane` (needs error/exit handlers)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:582-600` — `recordDispatchAudit` (needs outcome parameter)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:525-527, 537-539, 551-553` — spawn → record call sites
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — needs new tests for failure paths
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — failure-path logging section

## Related work

- **WL-0MSKUG2WW0058A7W** (Evaluate downtime-worker config and silent-failure paths) — Parent item; this is follow-up #3 of the audit gap AC3 findings.
- **WL-0MSLWJ310000ND0X** (Downtime claim failure discarded) — Related failure-path issue in the same subsystem.
- **WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT** (RCA: Downtime dispatcher re-dispatches same item) — Related dispatch reliability issue.
- **WL-0MSK9TUCA00206M7** (RCA: no downtime dispatch overnight) — Related idle-window polling issue.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope risk:** Changes to `recordDispatchAudit` may affect other dispatch callers. **Mitigation:** Review all call sites (downtime-worker.ts:525-553) and update consistently.
- **Audit log format change:** Adding a new outcome state may affect consumers of the dispatch log. **Mitigation:** Use a backward-compatible approach (e.g., add `outcome` field, keep `success: true/false`).
- **Assumption:** The spawn error handler and exit handler can be added without changing the fire-and-forget semantics of the detached child process.
- **Assumption:** Unit tests can be written to mock `child_process.spawn` and verify error/exit handling paths.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Additional failure-path improvements (e.g., retry logic, alerting) are out of scope and should be captured as separate work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1:** "What should the dispatch outcome be when spawn fails or the script exits non-zero?" — Answer (inferred from description): The dispatch should NOT be recorded as `success`. Design: record the outcome as `attempted` or `failed` with error/exit details in the audit log. Source: work item description states "dispatch outcome is not success".
- **Q2:** "Should the spawn remain fire-and-forget?" — Answer (inferred): Yes, the child process should remain detached and unref'd; handlers only capture state for audit logging, they do not block or wait on the child. Source: the spawn is fire-and-forget and this behavior should not change.
- **Q3:** "Should `recordDispatchAudit` be modified or should a wrapper function be created?" — Answer (agent recommendation): Modify `recordDispatchAudit` to accept an optional `outcome` parameter with a default of `success` for backward compatibility. Source: minimal change principle — one function update rather than introducing a new function.

## Problem

# Dispatch low-risk work items from plan_complete stage

## Problem statement

The herdr downtime worker (`dispatchDowntimeWork` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`) dispatches work during local-LLM idle time, but only `/skill:audit` (completed/in_review), `/skill:plan` (intake_complete) and `/skill:intake` (idea). Items that have completed planning (`plan_complete`) are never implemented during downtime, so the backlog's highest-value next step — actually implementing ready items — requires manual invocation. Items ready for implementation that are low-risk and small-effort are ideal autonomous candidates: cheap, safe, and they advance the backlog toward review.

## Users

- **Worklog operators / producers** — anyone who wants ready-to-implement items progressed automatically during local-LLM downtime.
  - *User story:* "When my local LLM is idle, I want herdr to run `/skill:implement` on the next open `plan_complete` item that is Low-risk and Small-effort, so the backlog advances without my involvement."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the downtime worker is idle (per existing idle-detection), the first dispatch attempt after the audit tier targets an **open `plan_complete` item** with **risk `Low` (or lower)** and **effort `Small` (or lower)** → `/skill:implement <id>`. Dispatch priority: **audit → implement → plan → intake** (audit stays first as the release gate).
2. "Low (or lower)" = risk exactly `Low` (canonical scale: Low < Medium < High < Critical — nothing below Low). "Small (or lower)" = effort `Small` or `Extra Small` (canonical scale: Extra Small < Small < Medium < Large < Extra Large). Items with **unset/empty** risk or effort are **never** eligible (fail-closed — an absent estimate is not "≤ Low/Small").
3. Candidate selection is **priority-aware and dependency-blocked-aware**: the implement tier selects via `wl next --stage plan_complete --risk low --effort small -n N --json` (new `wl next` risk/effort filters from WL-0MSMAIP5F003WAGG, which excludes dependency-blocked items by default), plus the client-side **status=open** check (`wl next --stage plan_complete` keeps completed items by design) and the **dispatched-marker exclusion** (kind `implement`, `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`, WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY pattern) so an item whose dispatched run reverted to plan_complete is never immediately re-dispatched.
4. The dispatched pane runs `/skill:implement <id>` (visible pane, `--no-focus`, named e.g. `Downtime implement`), following the existing `buildDowntimePaneArgs`/`spawnDowntimePane` pattern; the implement lifecycle (worktree, status, stage) is managed by the implement skill itself — no dispatch-side status changes beyond the existing pre-dispatch claim pattern (`claimItem`, which is idempotent with `implement.py start`'s own claim).
5. When no implement candidate exists, the worker falls back to the existing plan (`intake_complete`) then intake (`idea`) tiers, unchanged.
6. Dispatch audit trail: successful implement dispatches are recorded like other downtime dispatches (item comment + rolling `.worklog` downtime log) with kind `implement`.
7. Selection is deterministic and single-flight: at most one dispatch per idle period (existing tracker/`dispatchInFlight` behaviour); a `wl next` CLI error at the implement tier does NOT short-circuit the plan/intake fallback (mirrors the existing tier-2-error handling).
8. Tests cover: risk/effort threshold boundaries (Low only; Small and Extra Small; unset excluded), status=open filter, dispatched-marker exclusion, and dispatch audit logging (kind `implement`) in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`; blocked-item exclusion via the end-to-end fixture (`packages/herdr/src/implement-tier-blocked-exclusion.test.ts`, real dep-edge through the exact implement-tier invocation), the wiring assertion that the invocation never passes `--include-blocked` (`packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts`), the CLI-level fixture (`tests/cli/next-risk-effort-cli.test.ts`), and the DB-filter exclusion (`tests/next-risk-effort-filter.test.ts`); implement-tier priority (audit → implement → plan → intake), fallback order, and no-candidate handling in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`.
9. ## Constraints

- Selection uses `wl next` (priority-focused, blocked-excluded by default) — NOT `wl list` (which includes blocked items and has no risk/effort filters). The `--risk`/`--effort` filter flags on `wl next` are delivered by the blocking child **WL-0MSMAIP5F003WAGG** (add risk/effort filters to wl next and convert herdr downtime dispatch selection to wl next).
- The dispatched-marker exclusion stays client-side in herdr (dispatcher-local state, not a wl concern), mirroring the audit tier (WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY).
- Do NOT change the implement skill itself (worktree lifecycle, claim, stage transitions) as part of this work — the dispatcher only opens a pane running `/skill:implement <id>`.
- The pre-dispatch claim (`claimItem`) is retained for cross-pane serialization; it is idempotent with `implement.py start`'s own claim (`StatusLifecycle.update_status(id, "in_progress")`).

Add an **implement tier** to the herdr downtime worker, after the audit tier and before the plan tier:

4. Wire into `createDowntimeWorker` tick flow (same idle → dispatch path; no-candidate/cooldown semantics unchanged — implement tier's empty result falls through to plan/intake).

- **Prerequisite dependency:** the implement tier consumes `wl next --risk/--effort` from blocking child WL-0MSMAIP5F003WAGG. Fallback if the child lands late: `wl next --stage plan_complete -n N --json` + client-side risk/effort/status filtering (still priority-ordered and blocked-excluded via `wl next`) — record which path was taken.
- **Re-selection loop:** a dispatched `/skill:implement` run that aborts (implement.py resets the item to open/plan_complete) must not be immediately re-dispatched — the kind `implement` dispatched-marker exclusion (WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY pattern) closes this loop, same as the audit tier.
- **Claim-before-dispatch:** the pre-dispatch claim (status → in_progress) is retained for cross-pane serialization and is idempotent with `implement.py start`'s own claim. If the pane fails to spawn after the claim, the item stays in_progress until the implement skill's abort resets it — consistent with the existing tiers (known silent-path WL-0MSLWJ310000ND0X); no new handling here.
- **Long-running panes:** implement runs are longer than plan/intake and consume the local slot for the duration — this is the intended use of idle capacity; existing single-flight and fresh-idle-period rules apply unchanged.
- **No issue-type restriction (assumption):** an epic at plan_complete with Low/Small estimates would be dispatched; the risk/effort gate makes this unlikely and the implement skill operates on whatever item it is given.
- **Scope-creep guard:** out of scope — modifying the implement skill, adding risk/effort filters to `wl list`, changing the audit tier's selection, or changing `wl next` semantics. Any follow-ups get their own work items.

Answer (user@ContextHub): "a" — approved audit → implement → plan → intake. Source: interactive reply.

# Show complete, right-aligned model name on footer Line 3 (remove 30-col truncation)

## Problem statement

The Worklog extension's custom TUI footer Line 3 (session-health) displays the session's model identifier (e.g. `code → openai/gpt-4`) on the right side of the line, but the identifier is capped at 30 visible columns and truncated with an ellipsis (`code → openai/gpt-4-abcdefghij…`), and it is not flush-right — it sits directly after the `│` separator that follows the command preview. The operator wants the full model name visible (never truncated) and right-aligned to the terminal edge.

## Users

End users of the Pi TUI with the Worklog extension enabled, including herdr-spawned pi panes. The footer Line 3 is the at-a-glance readout of which model is serving the session. A truncated model name is hard to read/verify; right-alignment gives the readout a stable, scannable position at the terminal edge.

User story: "As a pi user, I want to see the full resolved model name (e.g. `openai/gpt-4-abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz`) without truncation, flush right on the footer line, so I can always verify exactly which model is serving my session."

## Acceptance Criteria

- The model identifier (selected alias → resolved provider/model, `(resolving)`, resolved-only, or `—`) is always rendered in full on footer Line 3 — the 30-column `modelPartMaxWidth` cap (and its ellipsis truncation) is removed.
- The model identifier is right-aligned: its right edge is flush with the terminal's right edge (line width). When an initial prompt preview exists, it stays left-aligned with padding between the preview and the model; when no prompt exists, the model alone is padded to the right edge.
- The command/prompt preview yields space to the model: the preview is truncated (with `...`) as needed so the full model name fits; the model name is never truncated by the budget logic.
- Safety clamp at ultra-narrow widths: if the full model name plus separator cannot fit alongside the prompt, the prompt (and then the separator) is dropped before any part of the model; only when the model name alone exceeds the terminal width is the final `truncateToTerminalWidth(…, width)` clamp allowed to clip it (physically unavoidable).
- Footer Lines 1–2 (extension statuses, session health) and the no-model `—` fallback are unchanged.
- Unit tests in `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.test.ts` ("model line in footer") are updated: assert full (untruncated) model rendering, right-edge alignment (model's visible right edge at `width`), prompt truncation/yield behavior, and the narrow-width safety clamp; the full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Change only footer Line 3 rendering in `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.ts` (the `render()` function inside `setFooter`); do not alter Lines 1–2, the herdr pane, or `model-display.ts`.
- Preserve the grey/dim styling, the `│` separator, the `truncateWorkItemId` compaction of the prompt preview, and terminal-width-aware measuring (`visibleWidth` / `truncateToTerminalWidth`).
- Keep the change surgical: no refactoring of unrelated code.

## Existing state

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.ts` — custom footer via `ctx.ui.setFooter()`. Line 3 currently: builds `modelPart` (`alias → provider/model`, `(resolving)`, `—` fallbacks), caps it with `const modelPartMaxWidth = 30; cappedModelPart = truncateToTerminalWidth(modelPart, 30)`, then composes `${promptPart}${separator}${cappedModelPart}` and pushes `truncateToTerminalWidth(theme.fg('dim', label), width)`. The prompt budget is `width − modelWidth − separatorWidth`, so the model cap of 30 guarantees the prompt gets most of the line.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.test.ts` — "model line in footer" describe block asserts: exact string `'Fix the bug by adding validation  │  code → openai/gpt-4'`; commandPart > modelPart measurement; the 30-col cap case (asserts NOT containing `qrstuvwxyz`); narrow-width no-overflow; prompt truncation with `...  │  code →`; model-only cases.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/terminal-utils.ts` — provides `visibleWidth()` and `truncateToTerminalWidth()` (already imported).

## Desired change

In `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.ts` (footer `render()`), Line 3 composition:

1. Build `modelPart` exactly as today (alias → resolved model, `(resolving)`, `—` fallbacks); drop `modelPartMaxWidth`/`cappedModelPart` and use `modelPart` untruncated.
2. Compute `modelWidth = visibleWidth(modelPart)` and `separatorWidth = visibleWidth(separator)`.
3. Prompt budget = `max(0, width − modelWidth − separatorWidth)`; truncate the compacted prompt preview to that budget with `...` as today.
4. Compose `label = promptPart ? `${promptPart}${separator}${modelPart}` : modelPart`.
5. Right-align: insert padding between the prompt and the separator (or leading padding when there is no prompt) so the model's visible right edge equals `width` — pad = `width − visibleWidth(promptPart) − separatorWidth − modelWidth` (or `width − modelWidth` for the no-prompt case); drop the prompt/separator first if there is no room, then apply the final `truncateToTerminalWidth(…, width)` safety clamp.

## Key Files

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.ts` — Line-3 label composition, right-alignment padding, and budget logic (primary change).
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.test.ts` — update "model line in footer" tests for full model rendering + right alignment; add right-edge assertion and prompt-yield cases.

## Related work

- WL-0MSHENVKR002HZT5 — "Swap model identifier and command positions on herd status line" (completed): introduced the current Line-3 layout (command left, model right) and the 30-column model cap this item removes.
- WL-0MRF6JXMD003KHLQ — "Show initial prompt preview in footer info line" (completed): introduced the prompt preview on Line 3.
- WL-0MRF19R71004YJND — "Add model/provider line to TUI status bar footer" (completed): introduced the model footer line.
- WL-0MRDRZ32L00404D0 — "Session Health Extension for Pi Footer" (completed): the custom footer this change lives in.

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: "thrdr plugin" = the Worklog extension's session-health footer Line 3 (the only surface that displays the model name; it renders in pi panes spawned by herdr). Recorded in the Appendix; if the operator meant a different surface, revisit.
- Assumption: "right aligned" = model's right edge flush with the terminal's right edge (width), with the prompt preview left-aligned and padding between. Recorded in the Appendix.
- Edge case: a model name longer than the entire terminal width cannot be fully displayed; the final clamp clips it (documented in AC4 as physically unavoidable). All other cases show the model complete.
- Scope-creep risk: no adjacent polish (e.g. separator style, prompt truncation style) — out of scope unless it blocks right-alignment.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which surface is 'thrdr plugin'?" — Answer (repo inspection, no interactive reply needed): the Worklog Pi extension's custom footer Line 3 (`session-health.ts`), the only place a model name is displayed; it renders in herdr-spawned pi panes. Source: grep of `packages/herdr/src/` (no model display) and `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.ts` (Line 3 model display). Prior item WL-0MSHENVKR002HZT5 resolved the same ambiguity ("herd status line" = pi TUI footer model line).
- Q: "What does 'right aligned' mean given the model is already on the right side?" — Answer (interpretation, recorded as assumption): the model should be flush with the right edge of the terminal, with the prompt preview left-aligned and flexible padding between them. Today the model sits directly after the separator at a variable position. No user clarification requested — the pairing with "complete (not truncated)" makes the intent clear; flagged as assumption in Risks & assumptions.
- Q: "When the full model name competes with the prompt preview for width, which wins?" — Answer (interpretation): the model name wins; the prompt preview (already a truncated preview) yields space first. Recorded as AC2/AC4. The request's emphasis on "complete (not truncated)" model name supports this; flagged as assumption.
## Related work (automated report)

# Auto-continue after mid-session compaction (session_compact event handling)

## Problem statement

When Pi completes a **mid-session compaction** (as opposed to an end-of-session compaction), the agent is left stopped and the user must manually type "continue" to resume work. The Worklog extension's recovery module handles `agent_end` errors (CONTEXT_LENGTH → invisible continue) but does not listen to Pi's `session_compact` / `compaction_end` events at all, so nothing resumes the agent automatically after a compaction completes mid-session.

## Users

- **Long-session Pi users** — Anyone running long agent sessions where context grows and Pi auto-compacts while the agent is still working. They lose momentum and must manually prompt "continue" after every mid-session compaction.

Example user stories:

- "As a long-session user, when Pi auto-compacts mid-session because context crossed the threshold while my agent was still working, I want the agent to automatically continue instead of stopping and waiting for me to type 'continue'."
- "As a user running `/compact` while wrapping up a session, I do NOT want an unexpected auto-continue — end-of-session compaction should leave the agent stopped."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The extension registers a handler for Pi's `session_compact` (and/or `compaction_end`) event in `register-recovery.ts`.
2. When Pi completes a **mid-session** compaction (agent was actively working — e.g., a turn was in progress or interrupted — or `ctx.hasPendingMessages()` is true), the extension automatically triggers the existing invisible-continue machinery (`agent.prompt([])` via the `triggerInvisibleContinue`-style loop) so the agent resumes without user input. Default detection: `hasPendingMessages() || lastAssistant.stopReason ∈ {length, error} || agent was running when compaction started`.
3. **Overflow** compaction (`willRetry: true`) does **not** trigger a second continuation — Pi already retries the aborted turn natively; the handler must skip `willRetry: true` to avoid a double-continue.
4. **End-of-session** compaction (agent settled/idle, no pending work — e.g., user manually runs `/compact` after the turn completed) does **not** auto-continue.
5. The auto-continue respects existing safety guards: user abort (ESC), session switches (`/new`, `/resume`), and the retry mutex (`_continueInProgress`) — no continuation starts when the user has aborted or the session changed.
6. Unit tests cover: mid-session threshold compaction → auto-continue fires; overflow (`willRetry: true`) → no continuation; end-of-session/manual compaction with settled agent → no continuation; abort/session-switch guards respected.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and any relevant README/docs entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline. CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope.

## Constraints

- Pi natively auto-continues **only** overflow recovery (`willRetry: true`); threshold compaction is explicitly designed to *not* auto-retry ("user continues manually" — Pi source comment, and Pi change #6074 made pre-prompt compaction stop rather than continue). The extension must add this behavior without racing or conflicting with Pi's own flows.
- The extension context exposes `ctx.isIdle()`, `ctx.hasPendingMessages()`, `ctx.compact({ onComplete })`; the extension already captures the live `Agent` instance (via monkey-patched `subscribe`) for `agent.prompt([])`.
- The recovery module currently registers only `agent_end`, `turn_end`, `session_start` handlers; `session_compact` is a valid extension event (`pi.on("session_compact", handler)` with `SessionCompactEvent` carrying `reason` and `willRetry`).
- The 10-second-ish behavior of existing `triggerInvisibleContinue` (wait-for-idle → remove error → backoff → `prompt([])`) should be reused rather than reimplemented; compaction continuation is the same "prompt the agent to resume" primitive.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Double-continue risk:** if the `session_compact` handler fires for overflow (`willRetry: true`) while Pi is already retrying, two continuations could race. Mitigation: skip `willRetry: true` and reuse the `_continueInProgress` mutex.
- **Infinite-loop risk:** an over-aggressive mid-session definition could keep re-prompting the agent after every compaction (e.g., if `hasPendingMessages()` stays true). Mitigation: continuation count tracking via existing `ContinuationState`, and end-of-session detection that excludes settled/idle agents.
- **Overlap with CONTEXT_LENGTH path:** the existing `agent_end` CONTEXT_LENGTH branch already calls `triggerInvisibleContinue()`; the new `session_compact` path must not double-trigger for the same incident (mutex + state checks).
- **Assumption (OPEN):** the precise mid-session definition and whether manual `/compact` mid-session is in scope were not explicitly confirmed with the operator; the defaults above are documented and should be validated during implementation.

## Existing state

- `register-recovery.ts` wires `agent_end` → `classifyError()` → dispatch. CONTEXT_LENGTH triggers `triggerInvisibleContinue()` which removes the error message from agent state and calls `agent.prompt([])` in a loop. It is not compaction-specific and does not listen to `session_compact`.
- Pi's `_runAutoCompaction(reason, willRetry)` emits `compaction_start` → (extension `session_before_compact` optional hook) → `session_compact` → `compaction_end`. Only overflow (`willRetry: true`) causes Pi to continue the aborted turn itself.
- Threshold auto-compaction fires after `agent_end` when context tokens exceed the threshold (`_checkCompaction` Case 2) and on pre-prompt submission; it returns `agent.hasQueuedMessages()` so queued messages are delivered once, but otherwise the agent stops.
- Manual `/compact` aborts the current agent operation first (`abort()`), compacts, and does not continue.

## Desired change

1. **`register-recovery.ts`** — add a `pi.on("session_compact", ...)` handler (alongside existing handlers) that:
   - Skips when `event.willRetry === true` (Pi's native overflow continuation handles it).
   - Determines "mid-session" vs "end of session": mid-session when the agent has pending work — e.g., `ctx.hasPendingMessages()`, or the agent was interrupted mid-turn (an `agent_start` occurred without a completing `agent_end` / the last assistant message stopReason is `length`/`error`), or the session is not settled; end-of-session when the agent is idle/settled with no pending messages (e.g., manual `/compact` after a completed turn).
   - When mid-session, reuses the invisible-continue loop (`agent.prompt([])`) guarded by the existing mutex, user-abort flag, and session-generation checks.
2. **`register-recovery.ts` / shared state** — expose a small helper (e.g., `triggerCompactionContinue()`) or reuse `triggerInvisibleContinue()` with a compaction-specific entry point, keeping the CONTEXT_LENGTH path intact.
3. **Tests** — extend `compact-continue.test.ts` (or add a new test file) covering the three classification cases and guard behavior.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts` — add `session_compact` handler; mid-session/end-of-session detection; wire to invisible-continue.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/recovery.ts` — shared state (if the mutex/abort flags need compaction-specific handling).
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/compact-continue.test.ts` (or a new test file) — unit tests for classification and guards.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/index.ts` — only if registration entry needs updating (likely not; `registerRecoveryModule(pi)` is already called).

## Related work

- WL-0MR5QR1790034LXA — *Fix: Auto-continue after compaction for max output tokens (CONTEXT_LENGTH)* — predecessor: added `triggerInvisibleContinue()` call in the CONTEXT_LENGTH branch. Completed.
- WL-0MR269PDV00970YP — *Impl: Compact-and-Continue Handler* — built the compact-and-continue machinery. Completed.
- WL-0MR2661WZ0044A3Y — *Test: Compact-and-Continue Handler* — test coverage for the handler. Completed.

# Herdr plugin: activity-gated proxy mode switching (cheap on operator idle, fast on operator command)

## Problem statement

The llama-proxy runs in two operating modes — **fast** (cloud-backed, 3-slot pool) and **cheap** (2-slot local-first pool). Today mode is switched manually (admin API/UI) or on a fixed time schedule; there is no link between *operator presence* and mode. When an operator is actively working through the herdr plugin, every Pi command should be served by **fast** mode; when the operator leaves (no agent-route Pi commands through the plugin for a configurable window), the proxy should drop to **cheap** mode so the downtime worker's autonomous dispatches consume only the cheap local pool.

## Users

- **Operator running the herdr worklog plugin + llama-proxy** — wants fast responses while actively working and zero-cost cheap mode when away, without touching the mode API by hand.

Example user stories:

- *"As an operator, when I issue an agent command (/skill:*, /intake, /plan, /prompt:) through the herdr plugin, I want the proxy switched to fast mode immediately so my session is served by the cloud-backed pool."*
- *"As an operator, when I have issued no agent-route Pi commands through the plugin for 15 minutes, I want the proxy switched to cheap mode (only when it is idle) so the downtime dispatcher's work runs on the cheap local pool."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Operator-activity tracking:** the plugin records a timestamp on every **agent-route** command (`/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`, `/prompt:` — the routes that spawn a pi agent pane); shell shortcuts (`!!`/`!`) and plain commands do NOT count as operator activity.
- [ ] **Cheap switch on idle:** when no operator agent-route command has been routed for ≥ `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs` (default `900000` = 15 min, configurable) **AND** the proxy reports idle (reusing the existing `/llama/local/status` idle evaluation: llama-server running, no active local query, no model switch, no local lease, all required slots free), the worker POSTs `/admin/set-mode {"mode":"cheap"}`. A busy proxy (active local query) **delays** the switch (never kills in-flight work).
- [ ] **Fast switch on command:** when a new operator agent-route command is routed through the plugin, it immediately POSTs `/admin/set-mode {"mode":"fast"}` (fire-and-forget; a failed switch never blocks or delays the command dispatch — the pane opens regardless, fail-open).
- [ ] **No redundant switching / no hammering:** the worker skips a switch when the persisted mode already matches the target (track last-known mode; refresh via `GET /admin/mode` on poll). At most one switch per state change; a `409` (mode-switch restart in progress) is treated as a no-op and retried on a later tick.
- [ ] **Fail-closed everywhere:** endpoint failures, timeouts, network errors, and ambiguous responses yield no switch and never crash or block the plugin. On plugin restart the idle clock resets to "active now" (fail-safe: the proxy stays fast until a fresh full idle window passes).
- [ ] **Configurable via plugin settings** (`~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json`): enabled toggle, idle threshold ms, poll interval ms; settings re-read every tick so changes apply without a plugin restart. The proxy URL is shared with the downtime worker (`downtimeProxyUrl`).
- [ ] **Coexistence with the proxy's built-in schedule:** the plugin's switches are manual overrides (the API's native semantics, LP-0MSMF25V9002AY1J); the proxy's time-based schedule (cheap 01:00–10:00, fast 10:00–01:00) reclaims control at its next boundary. Documented behavior, not a conflict.
- [ ] **Testing & validation:** unit tests cover idle-window evaluation, last-command tracking, cheap/fast switch triggers, restart reset, fail-closed paths, and settings clamps. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, the herdr README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Only **agent-route** commands count as operator activity (operator decision Q1).
- The cheap switch is gated on proxy idle — it must never kill in-flight work (operator decision Q4b).
- Mode switches never block the TUI or command dispatch: all HTTP calls are fire-and-forget (fast switch) or scheduled task work (cheap switch).
- Fail-closed at every boundary: no crash, no hammering, no repeated identical POSTs.
- The seed mentions "the `/admin/mode` API": `GET /admin/mode` only *reads* the mode; the switch endpoint is `POST /admin/set-mode`. The brief targets `/admin/set-mode`.

## Existing state

- Mode API + UI exist on the proxy: `GET /admin/mode`, `POST /admin/set-mode` (LP-0MSLMYEEU002IBH6); mode persisted in `proxy/.mode`, defaults to `fast`.
- Time-based automatic mode switching exists on the proxy (cheap 01:00–10:00, fast 10:00–01:00, LP-0MSM5K4TX004MICX) with manual-override persistence until the next scheduled change (LP-0MSMF25V9002AY1J). A mode switch restarts the proxy (terminates in-flight requests; clients retry — documented accepted behavior).
- The herdr plugin already has: settings system (`~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json`, re-read per tick), a consolidated scheduler (worklist.ts), and a downtime worker that polls `/llama/local/status` with fail-closed idle evaluation (WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K + children). The mode-switch worker reuses this infrastructure.

## Desired change

Add a mode-switch worker to the herdr plugin:

1. `index.ts` `onCommand` (agent route) records `lastOperatorCommandAt = Date.now()` and fires the fast switch (`POST /admin/set-mode {"mode":"fast"}`, fire-and-forget, fail-open).
2. A new scheduler task (pattern-matched on the existing `downtime` task) ticks on `modeSwitchPollIntervalMs`: if `lastOperatorCommandAt` is null/older than the threshold AND the proxy is idle (reuse the local-status poller/idle evaluation), POST `/admin/set-mode {"mode":"cheap"}` — skipping when the persisted mode already is cheap.
3. New settings: `modeSwitchEnabled`, `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs`, `modeSwitchPollIntervalMs` (reusing `downtimeProxyUrl`); re-read each tick.
4. Restart behavior: worker construction sets `lastOperatorCommandAt = Date.now()` (reset to active).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts` — new worker: idle-window evaluation, mode-state tracking, `/admin/set-mode` HTTP client (POST) + `GET /admin/mode` read, fail-closed
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.test.ts` — unit tests (test-first)
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — new settings keys + clamps + defaults
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — scheduler task wiring + TUI options plumbing
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — agent-route hook: record last-command timestamp + fire fast switch
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — settings and behavior documentation

## Related work

- **WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K** — "Herdr to consume local LLM in downtime" (parent of the downtime worker; the poller/settings/scheduler infrastructure this feature reuses)
- **LP-0MSLMYEEU002IBH6** (llm-manager) — Web API/UI to toggle fast/cheap modes (the `/admin/mode` + `/admin/set-mode` endpoints)
- **LP-0MSM5K4TX004MICX** (llm-manager) — Time-based automatic mode switching (built-in schedule)
- **LP-0MSMF25V9002AY1J** (llm-manager) — API mode override persists until the next scheduled change
- **WL-0MSMIPPJI007GU9N / LP-0MSMZOAJW002UR2A** (llm-manager) — cheap-mode profile definition (2-slot pool)
- find-related automated report: WL-0MRCTZZ82000X7TM, WL-0MP15AMKV002F3U4, WL-0MS6AAW3M004JK9U (weak keyword matches; not design-relevant)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Mode switch restarts the proxy** (kills in-flight requests). Mitigated for the cheap direction by the idle gate (Q4b); the fast direction can still kill a cheap-mode downtime request when the operator returns — accepted (documented proxy behavior; the downtime dispatch's work retries on the next idle period).
- **Multiple plugin panes** could each run a mode-switch worker → duplicate POSTs. Same-mode POSTs are API noops and the worker skips already-matching modes, so the system converges; per-process single-flight is applied.
- **Schedule reassertion at boundaries** may flip the mode shortly after a plugin switch near a boundary — accepted; every new operator command re-switches to fast immediately (design intent).
- **`GET /admin/mode`/`POST /admin/set-mode` may not be reachable** from the plugin host — fail-closed (no switch), never crash; the plugin logs a warning.
- **Scope-creep risk:** related but out-of-scope opportunities (e.g., reflecting the active mode in the herdr UI, per-slot idle gating for the cheap switch, or activity-based mode tracking for non-plugin pi panes) are recorded as linked work items, not scope.
- **Assumption:** "operator-issued Pi command" ≡ agent-route commands routed through the herdr plugin (Q1). Commands issued directly in a pi pane (not via the plugin) are out of scope.
- **Assumption:** the existing idle evaluation (`evaluateIdle` with `requiredFreeSlots = 0`, all slots free) is the busy/idle gate for the cheap switch; if per-slot data later arrives (WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG), the gate follows the same semantics.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should only the agent-route commands (/skill:*, /intake, /plan, /prompt: → new pi pane) count as 'operator Pi commands' for the idle timer, or any command routed through the plugin?" — Answer (operator): "only agent-route". Source: interactive reply. Research: `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` `routeCommand`/`isAgentCommand` distinguishes agent vs pane vs stdout routes.
- Q2: "Should the herdr plugin's activity-based switching (a) coexist as manual overrides — the schedule eventually reclaims control — or (b) fully own the mode while enabled?" — Answer (operator): clarified intent: "if the operator issues an agent-command it is *always* processed as 'fast', but if the operator leaves and the downtime dispatcher starts sending commands they are 'cheap'." Interpretation recorded: plugin switches are immediate manual overrides (fast on command, cheap on idle); the proxy's time schedule remains as a background fallback (coexistence, option a). Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "After a plugin restart, should the idle clock (a) reset to 'active now' — stay fast until a fresh full idle window — or (b) treat restart as idle and switch to cheap immediately?" — Answer (operator): "a". Source: interactive reply.
- Q4: "Cheap-switch gating vs proxy busy state: (a) switch at the threshold unconditionally (can kill in-flight downtime dispatch), or (b) switch only when the proxy also reports idle?" — Answer (operator): "b". Source: interactive reply. Research: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `evaluateIdle`/`isIdleStatus`; `llm-manager/proxy/proxy/handlers.py` `/admin/set-mode` restart semantics.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MRCTZZ82000X7TM** – RCA: wl sync pre-push hook destroyed Tableau-Card-Engine repository (completed)
- **WL-0MP15AMKV002F3U4** – Event emitter and UI hook API (completed)
- **WL-0MS6AAW3M004JK9U** – Reselect item after list reorder from status change (completed)

- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MSI4TAT70058921-rename-podcast-editing-tab-to-worklog/packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: api, auto, command, commands, configurable, fast, herdr, immediately, last, minutes, mode, new, operator, passed, plugin, proxy, sent, switch, using
