# Herdr selection list: let list take as much space as it needs; metadata fills the rest and scrolls (WL-0MSQ44MDX008U69J)

## Headline

Flip the space priority in the Herdr worklist pane: the selection list may use up to the full available pane height (including its header lines), and the metadata section fills whatever space remains — expanding when the list is short, sitting below the fold (revealed by scrolling down) when the list is long — scrolling internally when its content overflows.

## Problem statement

The metadata section below the selection list currently reserves a fixed 20–40% of the pane height (`computeMetadataPanelHeight`), squeezing the list. When the list needs more vertical space than it is allotted, it scrolls and the header/top lines scroll off the top of the pane, even though the metadata section below is eating rows the list could use. The metadata section should no longer force the list to scroll off the top.

## Users

- **Herdr users (human and AI agent)** browsing the work item list in a pane, who want the selection list — including its header line — to use as much vertical space as it needs, up to the maximum available, so items don't scroll off the top prematurely.

### User stories

- As a Herdr user, when the list is long, I want the list (header + items) to take up to the full pane height so I can see as many items as possible without the top scrolling off.
- As a Herdr user, when the list is short, I want the metadata section to expand into the leftover space so the pane still shows the selected item's metadata.
- As a Herdr user, when the list fills the full pane, I want to scroll the pane down to expose the rest of the list and then the metadata section, with the initial view starting at the top of the selection list.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **List takes as much space as it needs, up to the max available**: The selection list (header line + items + group separators + footer) can use up to the maximum number of vertical lines available in the pane (pane rows minus the reserved notification row). The metadata section no longer reserves a fixed 20–40% share that forces the list to scroll.
2. **Initial view at top**: When the list fills the full vertical space, the view starts at the top of the selection list (header + first items visible). Scrolling the pane down exposes the rest of the list and, at the end, the metadata section.
3. **Metadata fills the rest**: When the list content is shorter than the available height, the metadata section expands to fill the leftover space below the list.
4. **Metadata scrolls if necessary**: When the metadata content overflows the space allotted to it, it scrolls independently using the existing `m`/`M` keys and `metaScrollOffset` (with the existing `[m/M scroll NN%]` indicator), and the selection-driven reset behaviour is preserved.
5. **No regression**: Keyboard navigation (arrows/j/k, PgUp/PgDn, g/G, wrap), stage filtering, group separators, auto-refresh, code-freeze banner, and the reserved notification row continue to work; rendered output never exceeds the pane's `rows` budget.
6. **Testing**: Unit tests cover (a) list height = min(content need, max available), (b) metadata expansion when the list is short, (c) reveal-by-scroll when the list fills the pane and initial view at top, (d) metadata scroll clamping under the new layout, and (e) the output line-count invariant (≤ `rows`).
7. **Docs**: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** — managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Plugin-local change in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; no `wl` CLI or backend schema changes.
- The rendered output must never exceed the pane's `rows` budget (last row reserved for the notification line; group-separator accounting must not overflow) — the invariant from WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO must hold.
- Preserve existing keyboard bindings: `m`/`M` for metadata scrolling, and all list-navigation keys unchanged.
- Must compose with the description preview feature (WL-0MSFZKQL700381P3, in progress) which adds up to 3 preview lines to the metadata panel content.
- The metadata panel keeps a small minimum height (~3 rows) whenever it is rendered (short list or scrolled into view) so it remains usable, even if that means its content scrolls internally.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — document-flow layout**: the user's answers describe the list and metadata section as stacked content within one scrollable viewport (view starts at top; scrolling down reveals the rest of the list, then the metadata). An alternative pinned-footer layout (metadata always visible at the pane bottom) does not match the answers and is out of scope.
- **Assumption — header behavior**: "start the view at the top of the selection list" is interpreted as the initial render showing header + first items; the exact pin-vs-scroll behaviour of the header line during scroll is an implementation detail, but the header must be visible initially (matching the WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO invariant that the header is never cut off).
- **Risk — line-count regression**: changing the list/metadata space split could reintroduce output overflowing the pane (the WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO bug). Mitigation: keep the ≤ `rows` invariant as an explicit test.
- **Risk — metadata scroll clamping**: if the panel's allotted height changes dynamically, `metaScrollDown`'s clamp against content height must still hold; keep the existing clamp tests and update them for the new sizing.
- **Risk — scope creep**: "below the fold" indicators (WL-0MSG8YXYJ008PWJJ), mouse/touch scrolling (WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ), and metadata panel content changes (WL-0MSHIJR7T007Q9R7) are related but separate items — do not implement them here.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`:
  - `computeMetadataPanelHeight(rows)` (lines ~85–119) — reserves a 20–40% share of pane rows for the metadata panel (min 3 rows), from WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X.
  - `WorkItemListState._listHeight()` (line ~681) — `max(3, rows - 4 - panelHeight)`; used by `_adjustScroll` and `getVisibleItems`.
  - `createListRenderer()` (line ~1830) — computes `panelHeight = computeMetadataPanelHeight(rows)`, `listArea = rows - 1 - panelHeight`, `listHeight = rows - 4 - panelHeight`; renders header + items + separators + fill + footer + metadata panel lines, clamped to `rows - 1`.
  - `formatMetadataPanel()` (line ~982) — renders exactly `panelRows` lines with independent scroll offset and `[m/M scroll NN%]` indicator; `metaScrollDown` clamps against content height.
  - `metaScrollOffset` reset on selection change (`_resetMetaScroll`).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — `computeMetadataPanelHeight` responsive-ramp tests (lines ~1448), metadata scroll clamp tests (line ~1663), renderer line-count invariant tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — entry point wiring (render callback passes `metaScrollOffset`/`metaLastCommand`).

## Desired change

- In `createListRenderer()`: compute the list's space need from its content (header + banner + items + separators + footer), capped at the maximum available rows (`rows - 1` minus the notification budget). The metadata section is allotted the remainder: it expands to fill leftover space when the list is short, and when the list fills the pane it is positioned below the list content so scrolling down reveals the rest of the list and then the metadata section.
- Initial view starts at the top of the selection list (scroll offset 0 / header visible) even when the list is long.
- Keep `computeMetadataPanelHeight` (or replace its call sites) such that the fixed 20–40% reservation no longer forces the list to scroll; the metadata panel keeps a small minimum height (~3 rows) and scrolls internally via `metaScrollOffset`/`m`/`M` when its content overflows.
- Keep `formatMetadataPanel`'s independent-scroll contract (exactly `panelRows` lines) and the `[m/M scroll NN%]` indicator.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — list/metadata space split, initial view-at-top, metadata scroll clamping; primary change location.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — update responsive-ramp tests; add list-height/content-need, metadata-expansion, reveal-by-scroll, and line-count invariant tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — render callback wiring (`metaScrollOffset`, `metaLastCommand`), only if the space split needs state/context passed through.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X** (completed) — introduced the metadata panel and the fixed 20–40% reservation this item reverses; its AC1 said the list "always keeps the majority of the space (≥60%)" — this item changes that priority.
- **WL-0MSFZKQL700381P3** (in progress) — adds a description preview to the metadata panel (up to 3 lines), which makes the metadata content taller; this item must compose with it.
- **WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO** (completed) — the output line-count invariant (`≤ rows`) this item must preserve.
- **WL-0MSG8YXYJ008PWJJ** (open) — "no indication of items below the fold" — related scrolling UX; not required by this item but related.
- **WL-0MSHIJR7T007Q9R7** (open) — drops the duplicate ID row from the metadata panel; touches the same `formatMetadataPanel` output.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "When the list is long and fills the pane, should the metadata panel keep a small guaranteed minimum (e.g., ~3 rows, as today) so it stays visible and scrolls within that, or may it shrink all the way to zero (hidden)?" — Answer (user): "If the selection list takes up the full vertical space scrolling the pane down should expose the rest of the list and the meta-data section. However we should start the view at the top of the selection list." Source: interactive reply. Interpretation: when the list fills the pane, the metadata section sits below the list content and is revealed by scrolling the pane down; the initial view starts at the top of the selection list (header visible). Research: inspected `computeMetadataPanelHeight` (20–40% fixed reservation) and the renderer's `listArea`/`listHeight` budget in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.
- Q2: "When the list has only a few items, should the list take only the rows it needs (header + items + separators + footer) and let the metadata panel expand to fill the leftover space, or should the list always occupy the full available height and the metadata panel stay at a fixed small size?" — Answer (user): "meta-data can expand to fill space." Source: interactive reply. Interpretation: the list takes only what it needs when short; the metadata section expands into the leftover space.
- Q3: "Should the existing m/M metadata scrolling behavior stay as-is, just operating in the new (possibly smaller) panel space?" — Answer (user): "yes". Source: interactive reply. Research: `metaScrollOffset`, `_resetMetaScroll` on selection change, `metaScrollUp/Down` clamping and the `[m/M scroll NN%]` indicator already exist in `worklist.ts`.
data.title: Herdr selection list: let list take as much space as it needs; metadata fills the rest and scrolls

# RCA: Downtime dispatcher re-dispatches same item (audit + plan)

**Headline:** The herdr downtime worker still dispatches the same work item more than once. Two distinct root causes are proven from dispatch-log evidence: (1) a same-instant cross-pane race (audit tier — item dispatched twice 14 ms apart) that the dispatched-marker exclusion cannot prevent because selection happens before claim/marker write; and (2) the plan tier has **no** dispatched-marker exclusion, so any item whose stage does not durably leave `intake_complete` (plan session abort/error resets status to `open` while leaving stage at `intake_complete`) is re-dispatched on the next idle window. Deliverable: this RCA + a fix design; implementation is a follow-up work item.

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher (`dispatchDowntimeWork`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`) dispatched the same work item more than once, for `/skill:audit` and for `/skill:plan`. The previous fix for audit re-dispatch (WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY, durable dispatched-marker exclusion, landed 2026-08-09) closed the *re-selection loop* (an item reverting to `completed`/`in_review` after a dispatched audit) but not the *same-instant race* (two panes selecting the same candidate before either writes a marker), and the plan/intake tiers were explicitly left unguarded on an assumption ("stage transitions self-guard") that does not hold in production.

## Users

- **Operators running multi-pane herdr setups with the downtime worker enabled** — duplicate dispatches waste local-LLM idle time, spawn confusing repeated agent panes for the same item, and (for plan) can loop unboundedly (observed: one item plan-dispatched 7× in ~7 h).
- **User story:** "As an operator, when the downtime worker dispatches `/skill:audit` or `/skill:plan` on an item, I want at most one pane per item until the item's state actually changes, so my idle time is never spent on duplicate sessions."

## RCA findings (evidence)

### RC-1 — Same-instant cross-pane race (audit tier; affects all tiers)

- **Evidence:** `SA-0MSN4AXIQ007IZG2` (SorraAgents root) — `kind=audit` dispatched at `2026-08-10T21:20:53.909Z` **and** `21:20:53.923Z` — two log entries **14 ms apart**, same item, same root, both recorded as success. This is post-fix (marker exclusion landed 2026-08-09).
- **Mechanism (code-traced):** every herdr pane runs its own `dispatchDowntimeWork` (`dispatchInFlight` is per-process only; cross-pane serialization is explicitly delegated to the pre-dispatch claim, per the code comment). Selection happens **before** claim: `getNextAuditCandidate` reads the dispatch log (no marker yet) → selects the item → `claimItem` → `spawnAgentPane` → `recordDispatch` (marker written **after** spawn). Two panes in the same idle window both pass selection before either claims. `claimWorkItem` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`) runs `wl update <id> --status in_progress`, which is idempotent — a re-claim on an already-`in_progress` item also "succeeds", so both panes proceed. Claim failures are discarded by `claimItem` (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts:456-462`; pre-existing open item WL-0MSLWJ310000ND0X). Result: two identical audit panes for one item.
- **Why the existing marker cannot prevent it:** the dispatched-marker exclusion is read-then-write (TOCTOU) on `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`; both panes read the log before either appends the marker. The log is written after spawn, so even a correct read could not block the second pane in time.

### RC-2 — Plan tier has no dispatched-marker exclusion; "stage self-guard" fails

- **Evidence (post-fix, plan tier):**
  - `SA-0MSN04X2S006ONH0` — `kind=plan` ×2: `2026-08-12T11:05:30Z` and `2026-08-13T05:19:08Z` — no implement/audit between the two, i.e. the first plan run left the item selectable again.
  - `SA-0MSMAZP6T007NM0O` — `kind=plan` ×2: `2026-08-12T06:59:43Z` and `2026-08-13T04:50:06Z` — second plan dispatch occurred even though the item had completed a full plan → implement → audit cycle.
  - `SA-0MSJI53RX006E2PS` — `kind=plan` ×7 in ~7 h (`2026-08-09T00:46Z`–`07:31Z`) — pre-fix, but demonstrates the unbounded loop severity of the same tier.
- **Mechanism (code-traced):** the plan tier (`getNextItem('intake_complete')` → `wl next --stage intake_complete --json`) has no dispatched-marker exclusion, unlike the audit/implement tiers. The plan skill's error/abort path is `StatusLifecycle.update_status(<id>, "open")` — **status only; stage is left at `intake_complete`** (`skill/plan/SKILL.md` "On error/abort"). A plan pane that aborts (model error, infra failure, killed session) therefore resets the item to `open`/`intake_complete`, and the dispatcher re-selects it on the next idle window. The audit runner has a similar restore-to-captured-state path (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` finally block) that can likewise leave an item selectable.
- **Amplifier:** `wl next`'s stage filter does **not** remove completed items (`filterCandidates` step 3 in `packages/shared/src/database.ts`: completed items removed only when no stage filter is active), and the plan tier has no client-side `status === 'open'` guard (the implement tier has one; the plan/intake tiers do not). So even a `completed`/`in_review` item whose stage equals `intake_complete` is selectable for `/skill:plan`.

### RC-3 (contributing, audit tier) — marker fragility

- The audit-tier marker exclusion works for the re-selection loop (no post-fix audit re-dispatch beyond RC-1), but it is per-worklog-root (`.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` at `<cwd>`), bounded at `DOWNTIME_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES = 100`, and written **after** spawn — so a pane that dies before `recordDispatch` leaves no marker. These are noted residual risks, not the observed failure.

## Desired change — fix design (for follow-up implementation)

1. **Verified conditional claim (compare-and-swap) before spawn — closes RC-1.** Make the pre-dispatch claim atomic at the DB layer: transition to `in_progress` only if the item is still in the selectable state the tier chose it in (e.g. `wl update <id> --status in_progress --if-status <open|completed> [--if-stage <stage>]`, or an equivalent guarded DB update). Exactly one concurrent pane wins; a loser (0 rows changed, or claim failure) **aborts the dispatch** — no pane, no marker, no success log. This also absorbs WL-0MSLWJ310000ND0X (claim failures must not be silently discarded when they mean "another pane won").
2. **Marker write before spawn + fail-closed — hardens RC-1 at the log layer.** Move `recordDispatch` (log append) ahead of `spawnAgentPane`; if the marker cannot be written, abort the dispatch (fail-closed) rather than dispatching an unmarked item.
3. **Extend the dispatched-marker exclusion to the plan and intake tiers — closes RC-2.** Add kind-scoped marker sets (`plan` / `intake` entries) with a change-guard: exclude while the item is still at the stage it had at dispatch (`intake_complete` for plan, `idea` for intake); a stage advancement or an explicit human/state change releases the item for a legitimate retry.
4. **Client-side open-status guard on plan/intake tiers — closes the amplifier.** Filter to `status === 'open'` in the plan/intake parse/select paths (mirroring the implement tier's guard) so a `completed` item whose stage matches the filter is never dispatched for `/skill:plan`/`/skill:intake`.
5. **Dependencies/follow-ups to record:** WL-0MSLWJ3I70031Z8U (spawn failure still logged as success — with marker-before-spawn this becomes an abort path), and documenting the 100-entry log-roll limit (or extending it) as a residual risk.

## Acceptance Criteria (this item: RCA + fix design)

- [ ] **RCA documented with evidence:** both root causes (same-instant race; plan-tier marker gap), affected tiers, evidence log entries with timestamps/roots, and the mechanism traced through code (dispatch tier order, claim path, `filterCandidates` stage-filter semantics, plan-skill error path). Verified by reproducing the duplicate scan across all 5 `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` roots.
- [ ] **Fix design covers all four mechanisms** (conditional claim/CAS, marker-before-spawn fail-closed, plan/intake marker extension with change-guard, open-status guard) with file-level pointers and explicit option choices (e.g. `wl update --if-status` vs DB-level guarded update).
- [ ] **Scope guard:** implementation is explicitly deferred to a follow-up work item; this item's deliverable is the RCA + design (and any validation script used).
- [ ] **Traceability:** prior work (WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY scoping decision and where its "self-guard" assumption failed), open dependencies (WL-0MSLWJ310000ND0X, WL-0MSLWJ3I70031Z8U), and regression tests (WL-0MSLUANM5004NNPU) correctly referenced.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the findings (herdr README downtime section, this wiki, and the work-item description).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Fail-closed dispatch philosophy** (existing module contract): never dispatch on ambiguous signals; never crash. The claim-CAS and marker-write failure modes must abort dispatch without crashing the worker or wedging the poll loop.
- **No scope creep:** this item is RCA + design only; the five design points are candidates for the follow-up implementation item, not work to be performed here (unless the operator redirects).
- **Backwards compatibility:** the marker log format (`itemId`/`kind`/`dispatchedAt`/`cwd`/`title`) is unchanged; new kinds (`plan`/`intake`) extend it, and existing entries remain valid.

## Existing state

- `dispatchDowntimeWork` tier order: audit (marker-excluded) → implement (marker-excluded) → plan (`wl next --stage intake_complete`, no marker) → intake (`wl next --stage idea`, no marker). Code-freeze gate skips audit/implement during freezes.
- Pre-dispatch claim (`claimItem` → `claimWorkItem`) sets `status=in_progress` best-effort; failures discarded; no conditional/atomic semantics.
- Dispatch log: `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`, bounded at 100 entries, per worklog root; written after spawn; doubles as the marker source for audit/implement tiers.
- `wl next --stage X` keeps completed items under a stage filter (`filterCandidates` step 3) — plan/intake tiers lack the implement tier's client-side `status === 'open'` guard.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchDowntimeWork` tier order; `selectAuditCandidate`/`selectImplementCandidate`; where `getNextItem` for plan/intake is called without markers.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `getNextAuditCandidate` (lines ~378-410), `getNextImplementCandidate` (~413-455), `getNextItem` (~351-383), `claimItem` (~456-462, discarded claim result), `recordDispatch` (~465-490).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `claimWorkItem` (~623, `wl update --status in_progress`, never throws, 3 s timeout).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — `readDowntimeLogEntries`/`auditDispatchedItemIds`/`implementDispatchedItemIds`/`appendDowntimeLogEntry` (the marker source; extend with `plan`/`intake` kinds).
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `filterCandidates` (stage filter keeps completed items) — the amplifier for plan/intake selection.
- `src/commands/update.ts` + `packages/shared/src/database.ts` `update()` — where a conditional claim (`--if-status`/`--if-stage`) would be added.
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — error/abort path resets status only, leaving stage `intake_complete` (the RC-2 mechanism).
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — finally-block status/stage restore path.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY` "Downtime dispatcher triggers multiple identical sessions" (completed) — prior fix; audit-tier-only marker exclusion; the "self-guard" assumption this RCA refutes. Commit `228019bd`.
- `WL-0MSLUASNF001LLAT` "Dispatched-marker exclusion in audit-tier selection" (completed) — the exclusion implementation.
- `WL-0MSLUANM5004NNPU` "Regression tests for audit-tier re-dispatch exclusion" (completed) — test suite to extend for plan/intake.
- `WL-0MSLWJ310000ND0X` "Downtime claim failure discarded — dispatch proceeds and is recorded as success" (open, high) — directly implicated in RC-1; absorbed by design point 1.
- `WL-0MSLWJ3I70031Z8U` "Downtime pane spawn failure invisible — dispatch still logged as success" (open, high) — implicated in RC-2 (plan run never happens but dispatch logged); absorbed by design point 2.
- `WL-0MSMAYPQP001FLR6` "Implement tier end-to-end" (completed) — implement-tier marker pattern to extend.
- `WL-0MSI7DQL10016QYX` "worklog-root routing" (completed) — shared per-root log across panes.
- Wiki: `concepts/downtime-dispatch`, `concepts/audit-reject-workflow`, observations `obs-2026-08-08-rca-premise-wrong-*` (multi-pane polling counts).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — same-host multi-pane is the observed scope.** The RC-1 evidence is same-host (SorraAgents root, one host). Cross-host duplicates (two hosts sharing a worklog root) remain out of scope; the per-item worklog comment remains the durable cross-machine trail.
- **Risk — conditional claim semantics change claim behavior for all dispatches** (implement tier uses `claimItem` too): the CAS must not break legitimate claims (e.g. `--if-status` must accept every status the tier's query can return: `open` for plan/intake/implement, `completed` for audit).
- **Risk — plan retry starvation:** design point 3 must release the marker when the item legitimately advances (stage change) so a genuinely replanned item is not permanently blocked; the change-guard must be defined precisely and tested.
- **Risk — log roll:** the 100-entry bound can silently drop markers for long-unaudited items; documented residual risk (design point 5) unless trivially extended.
- **Scope-creep guard:** absorbing the two open silent-failure items (claim discard, spawn failure) is proposed; if the operator prefers separate items, they remain dependencies rather than in-scope work.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Deliverable of this item: is it the RCA + fix design only, with implementation as a follow-up?" — Answer (operator seed): the request was "Conduct an RCA and design a fix" — yes, RCA + fix design is the deliverable; implementation deferred (recorded as a follow-up item). Source: interactive request (2026-08-13).
- Q: "For the same-instant race, do you prefer the DB-level conditional claim (recommended) or a log-level lock?" — Answer: pending — draft proposes the conditional claim (`--if-status`/`--if-stage` guarded update) as primary with marker-before-spawn as hardening; operator may redirect during review. Source: draft feedback round.
- Q: "Should the plan/intake marker exclusion permanently exclude a dispatched item, or release it when its stage changes?" — Answer: proposed change-guard (release on stage advancement/human change) — retry semantics preserved; operator may redirect. Source: draft feedback round.

---

## Implementation notes (RCA delivered, 2026-08-13)

- **RCA + fix design committed:** `packages/herdr/docs/downtime-redispatch-rca-2026-08-13.md` (evidence scan, mechanism trace, design points, option choices, risks).
- **Evidence reproduced:** `packages/herdr/scripts/scan_duplicate_dispatches.py` (+ tests) — 17 duplicate (kind, itemId) pairs across all 5 roots; post-fix pairs: audit 14 ms race (SA-0MSN4AXIQ007IZG2, RC-1), plan pairs (SA-0MSMAZP6T007NM0O, SA-0MSN04X2S006ONH0, RC-2); plan ×7 severity demo pre-fix (SA-0MSJI53RX006E2PS).
- **Follow-up implementation item:** WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN (feature, high, blocked-by this item).

Design doc: `packages/herdr/docs/downtime-redispatch-rca-2026-08-13.md`. Evidence scan tool: `packages/herdr/scripts/scan_duplicate_dispatches.py`.

## Design points (from the RCA)

1. **Verified conditional claim (compare-and-swap) before spawn** — `wl update <id> --status in_progress --if-status <open|completed> [--if-stage <stage>]` (or DB-level guarded update) in `src/commands/update.ts` + `packages/shared/src/database.ts update()`; wire into `claimWorkItem` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`) so a losing pane (0 rows changed / claim failure) **aborts the dispatch** — no pane, no marker, no success log. Absorbs WL-0MSLWJ310000ND0X.
2. **Marker write before spawn + fail-closed** — move the `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` append ahead of `spawnAgentPane` in all four tiers (`dispatchDowntimeWork`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`); abort dispatch if the marker cannot be written. Absorbs WL-0MSLWJ3I70031Z8U (spawn failure becomes an abort path).
3. **Plan/intake dispatched-marker exclusion with change-guard** — kind-scoped `plan`/`intake` marker sets in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` + selection wiring in `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` `getNextItem`; exclude while the item is still at its dispatched-at stage; release on stage advancement/human change.
4. **Client-side `status === 'open'` guard on plan/intake tiers** — mirror the implement tier's guard in the plan/intake parse/select paths (`DowntimeCandidate` gains `status`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two concurrent panes selecting the same candidate: exactly one dispatches; the loser aborts with no pane, no log entry, no success record (unit tests simulating the race).
- [ ] Plan/intake dispatched items are excluded while their stage is unchanged; a stage advancement releases them (unit tests).
- [ ] A `completed`/`in_review` item whose stage matches the plan/intake filter is never dispatched (client-side open-status guard).
- [ ] Marker write failure aborts the dispatch (fail-closed) rather than dispatching an unmarked item.
- [ ] Claim failure is never silently discarded (recorded per WL-0MSLWJ310000ND0X).
- [ ] `packages/herdr/scripts/scan_duplicate_dispatches.py --since <deploy-ts>` shows no audit duplicates beyond a same-instant race and no plan/intake duplicates while items stay at their dispatched stage.
- [ ] Extend regression tests WL-0MSLUANM5004NNPU for plan/intake; full project test suite passes.

## Dependencies

- Prior: WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY, WL-0MSLUASNF001LLAT, WL-0MSLUANM5004NNPU (regression tests to extend).
- Absorbs: WL-0MSLWJ310000ND0X, WL-0MSLWJ3I70031Z8U (open silent-failure items).

## Problem

`npm run build` runs `scripts/install-herdr.sh` via the root postbuild hook. The script links the `worklog-selection-list` plugin with `herdr plugin link ${REPO_ROOT}/packages/herdr/herdr-plugin.toml`. When the build runs inside a git worktree (as happens during /skill:implement), `REPO_ROOT` resolves to the worktree path.

When `implement.py finish` later deletes the worktree, the herdr plugin registry (~/.config/herdr/plugins.json) points at a nonexistent manifest. Herdr then silently skips loading the plugin (warning: 'manifest unavailable: No such file or directory'), so the `prefix+l` keybinding invokes a non-existent action and nothing happens.

## Evidence (2026-08-13)

- plugins.json pointed at /home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT-.../packages/herdr/ (deleted)
- `herdr plugin list` showed: warning: manifest unavailable: No such file or directory (os error 2)
- `herdr plugin action invoke worklog-selection-list.open-podcast-editor-tab` did nothing
- Fix applied manually: re-linked from main checkout + `herdr server reload-config`; prefix+l works again

## Fix direction (options)

1. install-herdr.sh: resolve REPO_ROOT against the main checkout even when run inside a worktree (e.g. git worktree list / main worktree detection), OR
2. Skip the postbuild plugin-link step when inside a worktree (only the main checkout should register the global herdr plugin), OR
3. Make the link resilient: verify the manifest exists after linking and warn/self-heal.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Running `npm run build` inside a worktree never leaves a dangling herdr plugin link after that worktree is cleaned up
- [ ] `herdr plugin list` shows no warnings for worklog-selection-list
- [ ] `prefix+l` continues to work after a worktree-based build + cleanup cycle
- [ ] Unit test or script-level test covering the worktree scenario

## Problem

`prefix+l` in herdr (→ `worklog-selection-list.open-podcast-editor-tab`) crashed immediately: the spawned worklist pane exited with code 1 within ~0.3s.

## Root cause

The pane runs `npx tsx src/index.ts`; the plugin crashed on startup with:

```
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'marked' imported from .../packages/herdr/src/md-viewer.ts
```

`marked` (and the `@worklog/shared` file dependency) are declared in `packages/herdr/package.json` but were not installed. The root `npm run build` postbuild hook (`scripts/install-herdr.sh`) links the plugin and registers the prefix+l keybinding but never runs `npm install`, so a fresh clone (or a node_modules cleanup) leaves the plugin broken with a confusing 'crash on prefix+l' symptom.

## Fix

Ensure dependencies are installed as part of the plugin build. Options:
- Run `npm ci` (or `npm install`) in `packages/herdr` inside the `[[build]]` step or the root postbuild hook
- Verify the installed herdr plugin starts (`npx tsx src/index.ts`) after build

## Problem

`wl doctor prune --days N` hard-deletes items locally, but the next `wl sync` re-adds them all from the remote ref, because `mergeWorkItems` (src/sync.ts) re-imports every remote item missing locally (`if (!localItem) { mergedMap.set(remoteItem.id, remoteItem); }`). There is no `--no-pull` and prune has no push/rewrite path.

## Observed (2026-08-13)

- Ran `wl doctor prune --days 0` → 1,034 items hard-deleted locally (2941 → 1907 items)
- Ran `wl sync` → 'Work items added: 1034' — all resurrected from `refs/worklog/data` (back to 2941)
- Net result: prune is a no-op in a synced setup; items remain soft-deleted forever (the 'deleted but not pruned' backlog)

## Proposed fix

Add `--push` (or auto-push) to `wl doctor prune` that, after hard-deleting locally, rewrites the remote worklog ref with the pruned local state — mirroring `doctor foreign-items --apply --push` which already uses `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` (src/sync.ts:1130).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl doctor prune --days N --push` leaves the remote ref without the pruned items
- [ ] A subsequent `wl sync` does NOT resurrect the pruned items
- [ ] `--dry-run` unchanged; default remains no-push (safe)
- [ ] Unit/integration test covers prune+push against a temp git repo
data.title: wl doctor prune cannot persist: sync re-adds pruned items from remote ref

# Herdr downtime dispatcher: scheduled prompts (best-effort frequency)

## Problem statement

The Herdr downtime dispatcher only ever dispatches worklog-derived work (audit → implement → plan → intake tiers). There is no mechanism for periodic, project-scoped prompts (e.g. `/skill:refactor`) to run during downtime on a best-effort cadence, so recurring maintenance must be triggered manually.

## Users

- Operators running the Herdr downtime worker who want recurring maintenance prompts executed automatically during local-LLM idle time.

### User stories

- As an operator, I want `/skill:refactor` to run automatically at least every three days during downtime so the codebase stays clean without manual intervention.
- As an operator, I want scheduled prompts stored in a config file carrying each prompt's desired frequency and last-triggered datetime so I can add, remove, or adjust entries without code changes.
- As an operator, I want a scheduled prompt to dispatch only when the downtime dispatcher actually has a free LLM slot, so maintenance never interrupts active work.
- As an operator, I want scheduled prompts held during a code freeze so no new code changes land mid-release.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl init` provisions a project-local config file `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` containing the base set of scheduled commands — starting with a single `/skill:refactor` entry (`intervalDays: 3`, `lastTriggeredAt: null`) — via a default config template (e.g. `templates/scheduled-prompts.json`). Provisioning is create-if-absent: re-running `wl init` never clobbers an existing file (user edits and `lastTriggeredAt` state are preserved).
2. The config file holds a list of scheduled prompts; each entry has a stable id, the prompt text (any text the pi agent pane can run, e.g. `/skill:refactor`), a best-effort frequency in days (`intervalDays`), and `lastTriggeredAt` (ISO-8601 UTC datetime; `null` = never run). When the file is absent (e.g. a worklog root created before this feature) the worker treats the set as empty: no scheduled dispatch, a logged notice, and existing tiers unaffected (fail-closed; `wl init` is the provisioning path). Malformed files also fail closed: no scheduled dispatch, error logged, existing tiers unaffected.
3. The downtime dispatch pipeline checks scheduled prompts FIRST (before the audit/implement/plan/intake tiers): when an LLM slot is idle and the threshold is met, an entry is due iff `lastTriggeredAt` is null or `now - lastTriggeredAt >= intervalDays` (best effort — a delayed dispatch never fires more often than the frequency). A due entry dispatches a pi agent pane through the existing spawn path (`send-to-pi.sh`, `--pane-name Downtime <id>`, `--no-focus`, `--cwd <wlRoot>`, `--model <downtimeModel>`) running the prompt text.
4. On successful spawn of a scheduled prompt: `lastTriggeredAt` is updated to `now` and persisted to the config file (atomic tmp+rename write), and the dispatch is recorded in `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` with kind `scheduled` (no work-item comment/claim — there is no item). Fail-closed: if the config update or the log-marker write fails, the spawn ABORTS (an unrecorded dispatch never runs) and the entry remains due for the next idle slot.
5. Code-freeze gate applies to scheduled prompts exactly as to the audit/implement tiers: while the marker is frozen or ambiguous (fail-closed), scheduled prompts are skipped and dispatch falls through to the plan/intake tiers (unchanged existing behaviour).
6. When no scheduled prompt is due, the existing tier pipeline runs unchanged (audit → implement → plan → intake). A due scheduled prompt dispatches instead of reaching the backlog tiers, so it never triggers the no-candidate cooldown; when no prompt is due and the backlog is genuinely empty, the existing no-candidate cooldown applies unchanged.
7. Config entries with invalid `intervalDays` (missing, non-finite, or ≤ 0) or missing/empty prompt text are skipped with a logged warning (fail-closed, never a crash); entries missing `lastTriggeredAt` are treated as due. When multiple entries are due, they dispatch one per idle slot in config order.
8. Unit/integration tests cover: `wl init` provisioning (file created with the base set on first init; untouched on re-init), due-check arithmetic (null lastTriggeredAt, boundary, not-yet-due), config parse/defaults/atomic-write, absent/malformed-config fail-closed, freeze gating, cooldown interaction, spawn args, and the `scheduled` log-marker record.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (e.g. `packages/herdr/README.md`, `PLUGIN_GUIDE.md`, `CONFIG.md` downtime sections).
10. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Follow the worker's existing fail-closed philosophy at every boundary: never dispatch, never throw.
- Scheduled check is the first tier of `dispatchDowntimeWork`, gated by the same fresh-read code-freeze marker as audit/implement.
- Per-process single-flight guard (`dispatchInFlight`) applies to scheduled dispatch too — one dispatch per idle slot.
- Reuse the existing scheduler-loop wiring (`createDowntimeWorker.tick`); no new timer infrastructure.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchDowntimeWork` tier pipeline (freeze gate → audit → implement → plan → intake), `buildDowntimePrompt`/`buildDowntimePaneArgs`, `DowntimeWorkerDeps` injectable boundary, no-candidate cooldown + three-strike rule in `createDowntimeWorker.tick`, settings clamps.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — wires deps (`getNextItem`, `getNextAuditCandidate`, `getNextImplementCandidate`, `readCodeFreezeStatus`, `claimItem`, `spawnAgentPane`, `recordDispatch`, `recordError`).
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — JSON-file settings store pattern (`~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json`), defaults-merge + clamp pattern to mirror.
- `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` — rolling dispatch markers (kind `plan|intake|audit|implement`).
- Code-freeze marker: `.worklog/code-freeze.json` (WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY).

## Desired change

Add a scheduled-prompts tier as the first dispatch stage, provisioned by `wl init`. CLI side: `src/commands/init.ts` copies a default config template (new `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` with the `/skill:refactor` base set) into `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` when absent (create-if-absent, never clobber). Plugin side: new module `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` (config load/save/due-check, mirroring `settings.ts` patterns); extend `DowntimeWorkerDeps` with `getDueScheduledPrompt(cwd)` (or equivalent) and reuse `recordDispatch` with kind `scheduled` + a `ScheduledPrompt` event shape; add `dispatchScheduledPrompt` beside `dispatchClaimedTier` (update+persist lastTriggeredAt → log-marker → spawn, abort before spawn on failure); insert the tier in `dispatchDowntimeWork` under the freeze gate. Wire the fs-backed deps in `index.ts`.

## Key Files

- `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` (new) — default config template: base set with the `/skill:refactor` entry (`intervalDays: 3`, `lastTriggeredAt: null`).
- `src/commands/init.ts` — provision `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` from the template, create-if-absent (never clobber); `src/commands/init.test.ts` (or existing init tests) for provisioning + no-clobber.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` (new) — config schema, load (absent ⇒ empty set, fail-closed), atomic save, due-check (`isDueScheduledPrompt` / `getDueScheduledPrompt`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `ScheduledPrompt` types, `DowntimeDispatchEvent`/`DowntimeDispatchOutcome` kind `scheduled`, `dispatchScheduledPrompt`, tier insertion in `dispatchDowntimeWork`, deps additions.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — wire fs-backed scheduled-prompt deps (read config, persist lastTriggeredAt, rolling-log record).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` (+ new `scheduled-prompts.test.ts`) — due-check, config, freeze, cooldown, spawn-arg, log-marker tests.
- `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` — runtime per-worklog-root config (created by `wl init`, then updated in place by the worker; not committed).
- Docs: `packages/herdr/README.md`, `PLUGIN_GUIDE.md`, `CONFIG.md` — document the config file, `wl init` provisioning, frequency semantics, and freeze behaviour.

## Related work

- WL-0MRHYQU1S009DJ9B — *Add periodic request scheduling to pi worklog plugin* (completed): cron-based scheduling in the pi extension (`ctx.isIdle()` + `pi.sendUserMessage()`); related pattern, different plugin — reuse the "any prompt text" lesson, not the cron model.
- WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K — *Herdr to consume local LLM in downtime*: parent of the downtime worker.
- WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY — code-freeze gate (freeze semantics reused here).
- WL-0MSI7DQL10016QYX — no-candidate cooldown (interaction confirmed in AC5).
- WL-0MSMAYPQP001FLR6 — implement tier (tier ordering).
- WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8 — dispatch logging (rolling `.worklog` log + item comments; `scheduled` entries are log-only).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the provisioning path for the config file is `wl init` (the standard worklog-root setup command); the plugin treats an absent file as an empty set (fail-closed, logged) rather than synthesizing defaults.
- **Assumption:** frequency granularity is whole days (`intervalDays`); "every three days" = 72 h. Best-effort means a dispatch may be delayed (no idle slot, cooldown, freeze) but never happens more often than the frequency.
- **Assumption:** multiple due entries dispatch one per idle slot in config order; the single-flight guard prevents overlap.
- **Risk:** concurrent user edit vs worker write of the config file (last-writer-wins) — mitigated by atomic tmp+rename writes and re-reading before each persist.
- **Risk:** clock skew/stale `lastTriggeredAt` makes an entry appear immediately due — acceptable (best-effort), documented.
- **Risk:** `/skill:refactor` runs while the operator is actively working — mitigated: dispatch only happens when an LLM slot is actually idle for the full threshold, unchanged from existing behaviour.
- **Scope creep:** cron-style schedules, per-prompt model overrides, TUI editing of prompts, per-project prompt defaults beyond refactor — record as separate linked work items, not this scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Where should the scheduled-prompts config file live?" — Answer (user/rgardler): "as recommended" — project-local `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, scoping prompts per worklog root (the dispatcher's `cwd`). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "During a code freeze (ship-it marker), should due scheduled prompts still dispatch?" — Answer (user/rgardler): "not during a code-freeze" — scheduled prompts are held by the same freeze gate as the audit/implement tiers (frozen OR ambiguous ⇒ skip; plan/intake still run). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Should a due scheduled prompt bypass the empty-backlog no-candidate cooldown?" — Answer (user/rgardler): "confirmed" — the scheduled check is the first dispatch tier, so a due prompt dispatches instead of reaching the backlog tiers and never triggers the cooldown; when none are due, existing backlog + cooldown behaviour is unchanged. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Requirement (user/rgardler, mid-draft directive): "Add a requirement that wl init will add a base set of scheduled commands, starting with just /skill:refactor (provide a default config file for this purpose)" — Answer: accepted verbatim; `wl init` provisions `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` from a `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` default (base set = `/skill:refactor`, `intervalDays: 3`, `lastTriggeredAt: null`), create-if-absent, never clobbering user edits or `lastTriggeredAt` state. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

# Implement: paragraph cursor + note chords in md viewer

## Summary
Interactive note editing in the detail-view md viewer: block-level cursor/selection over markdown paragraphs, add/edit/delete chords wired through the shortcut registry (view-scoped to `detail`, verified non-conflicting), FormState reuse for note text entry (pre-filled in edit mode), surgical write-back via `resolveKeyFilePath`, and viewer refresh — for any `.md` Key File, podcast or generic.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The cursor can select any paragraph/block of the rendered md document (extending the existing `detailToCFocus` focus model; ToC focus behaviour unchanged).
- [ ] Add/edit chord opens the FormState dialog — empty in add mode, pre-filled with the existing note text in edit mode.
- [ ] Saving inserts/updates the `[NOTE <id>: ...]` marker in the source file via surgical write-back (all other file content preserved byte-for-byte) and the viewer reflects the change.
- [ ] Delete chord removes the marker from the file; the viewer updates.
- [ ] Existing inline-note link rendering (`<id>↗`) still works after edits; behaviour is identical for generic markdown files (not only podcast scripts).
- [ ] New chords are registered in `shortcuts.json` with view `detail` (e.g. `e`/`d` or `n,e`/`n,d` — avoiding the single-key `n` collision with `/intake <id>`) and appear in the chord hints.

## Minimal Implementation
- Cursor/selection state and rendering in the `worklist.ts` viewer pane: map rendered lines back to source paragraphs via the markdown token walker.
- New chord entries in `src/shortcuts.json` (view `detail`); handle add/edit/delete in `handleKeypress`/chord dispatch using the `md-note-edit.ts` helpers.
- Write-back: `resolveKeyFilePath` + dependency-injected writer (side-effect-free/testable); re-render from the updated content.
- Reuse `FormState` for note text entry (pre-fill via the field default mechanism).

## Dependencies
- Prereq: #2 (marker edit helpers) and the #1 tests item.
- Path resolution per WL-0MSGEA9AY0080V4Q (`resolveKeyFilePath` against the worklog root).

## Deliverables
- Working add/edit/delete note editing on any md Key File; viewer integration tests green.

## Key Files:

# Intake Draft: Downtime dispatcher — priority-first selection with round-robin tie-break across tied items + jittered probes

## Problem statement

When multiple instances of the herdr plugin are active on the same machine, the same instance often wins the race to dispatch in downtime — with a deterministic ascending-sortIndex tie-break, the same lowest-sortIndex item is always picked first by whichever instance is fastest, so one instance monopolises dispatch and tied-priority items are never rotated. Probes also fire in lockstep (all instances at the same fixed poll interval), which amplifies the same-winner effect and gives other machines no chance to get into the loop.

## Users

- **Operator with several herdr panes/instances on one machine** — wants the downtime work spread fairly: highest-priority items first, tied-priority items rotated round-robin, and no single instance hogs all dispatches.
- **Operator with multiple machines sharing the llama proxy** — wants probes desynchronised so each machine gets a fair chance to dispatch first.

### User stories

- As an operator running N herdr instances on one machine, when multiple candidates tie on priority, I want them dispatched in round-robin rotation (shared across instances) so no single item/instance dominates.
- As an operator with several machines on the proxy, I want each downtime probe delayed by a random amount (within ±50% of the poll interval) so instances do not probe in lockstep and other machines can win the dispatch race.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Priority-first selection is preserved: a higher-priority candidate is always selected before any lower-priority candidate, regardless of round-robin state (all tiers: audit, implement, plan/intake).
- [ ] Round-robin tie-break: among candidates sharing the same priority level, selection rotates through them using a shared, durable cursor persisted under `<cwd>/.worklog/` (e.g. `downtime-round-robin.json`), so repeated dispatches of a tied group do not always pick the same item; two instances selecting from the same group pick different items when the cursor has advanced. Unit tests cover rotation across repeated selections and across the three tier selectors.
- [ ] Shared state is fail-open and never blocks dispatch: a missing, unreadable, or corrupt round-robin file degrades to default (no rotation) behaviour; the cursor write failure is tolerated (marker/log write ordering unchanged — the dispatched-marker remains the authoritative guard against re-dispatch).
- [ ] Probe jitter: the downtime task's effective poll interval is jittered ±50% of the configured `downtimePollIntervalMs` per tick (random, injectable RNG for deterministic tests); two workers with identical configuration do not probe in lockstep. Jitter range is verified by unit tests (min/max bounds).
- [ ] Absorbs WL-0MSMHX6IR007F3H6 (Stagger herdr plugin downtime checks) — the jitter subsumes the stagger intent; that item is marked absorbed/blocked-by this item.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Round-robin grouping key is the **priority level** (critical/high/medium/low), not sortIndex (operator answer).
- Coordination state lives in the existing shared `.worklog/` files — no new daemons, no DB schema change.
- Jitter range is exactly ±50% of the configured poll interval (operator answer).
- Fail-closed / fail-open conventions preserved at every boundary (existing design doctrine); round-robin must never weaken the existing dispatched-marker exclusion or the CAS claim.
- No scope creep: no changes to `wl` CLI selection order (`src/commands`), the Pi TUI mirror, or the grouping/fetcher list ordering.

## Existing state

- `dispatchDowntimeWork` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`) runs tiers in order: audit → implement → plan (`intake_complete`) → intake (`idea`).
- Selection (`selectNextCandidate` / `selectAuditCandidate` / `selectImplementCandidate`) sorts candidates ascending by `sortIndex` and picks the first — deterministic, so a tied group always resolves to the same item; the fastest instance wins the CAS claim every time.
- Scheduler (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`) registers a fixed-interval `downtime` task (`intervalMs = downtimePollIntervalMs`, default 30s); all instances poll in lockstep.
- Dispatch markers (`downtime-dispatches.log`) + CAS claim (WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN) prevent double-dispatch of the same item but do not address "same instance always wins" or tied-item rotation.

## Desired change

1. **Shared round-robin registry** (`<cwd>/.worklog/downtime-round-robin.json`): map priority level → last-dispatched item id (or rotation cursor). New read/write helpers alongside `downtime-log.ts` (same fail-open discipline). Selection consults the registry: among same-priority candidates, pick the item after the cursor; record the pick before dispatch (write-then-spawn ordering, mirroring the dispatched-marker discipline).
2. **Jittered probes**: the downtime scheduler task's effective interval = `downtimePollIntervalMs + uniform(-50%..+50%)` per tick (injectable RNG; deterministic tests). This absorbs the stagger intent of WL-0MSMHX6IR007F3H6.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — round-robin selection logic (`selectNextCandidate`, `selectAuditCandidate`, `selectImplementCandidate` gain a rotation-aware variant or shared helper); jitter helper.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — new `downtime-round-robin.json` read/write helpers (mirror existing dispatch-log helpers).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — downtime scheduler task uses jittered interval per tick.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — wire rotation registry path into `createDowntimeDeps`/`createDowntimeWorker` (cwd-scoped).
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts` — only if the interval-mutation approach needs a small hook (prefer mutating the task's `intervalMs` inside its run, which the scheduler already re-reads at reschedule time).
- Tests: `downtime-worker.test.ts`, `downtime-log.test.ts`, `worklist.test.ts` / `scheduler.test.ts`.

## Related work

- WL-0MSMHX6IR007F3H6 — Stagger herdr plugin downtime checks (open, medium): **absorbed by this item** (probe jitter supersedes).
- WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN — Downtime dispatcher: conditional claim + marker exclusion (completed): the CAS/claim infra this builds on; round-robin must compose with it.
- WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT — RCA: Downtime dispatcher re-dispatches same item (completed): context for the marker/CAS design points.
- WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8 — Log herdr downtime dispatches (completed): the `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` pattern reused for the round-robin file.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** round-robin rotates *items within a priority level* and is shared across instances on one machine via the local `.worklog/` file; cross-machine fairness relies on jitter + the existing CAS claim (no cross-machine shared state) — consistent with operator answers.
- **Risk:** cursor-write races between instances on the same file. Mitigation: reuse the existing flock/atomic-rename pattern used by the dispatch log; a lost update degrades to a repeated pick, never a wrong-priority pick.
- **Risk:** jitter delays dispatch by up to +50% of the poll interval when a machine would otherwise be first. Accepted per operator instruction (fairness over latency).
- **Risk (scope creep):** do not extend round-robin into `wl` CLI ordering or list rendering; tie-break is a herdr-client concern. Extra opportunities (e.g. cross-machine leases) are recorded as linked work items, not scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Round-robin scope — across instances (competing herdr instances take turns) or across items (tied-priority items dispatched in rotation)?" — Answer (user): "(b) across items — when several items tie on priority, they get dispatched in rotation." Source: interactive reply, 2026-08-14.
- Q2: "Coordination mechanism — shared state in `.worklog/` or purely instance-local probabilistic?" — Answer (user): "existing is fine" (shared `.worklog/` files acceptable). Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Random delay bounds — range and placement (between probes only, or also pre-dispatch backoff)?" — Answer (user): "±50% of the poll interval" (between probes). Source: interactive reply.
- Q4: "Tie definition — same priority level regardless of sortIndex, or identical sortIndex?" — Answer (user): "(a) same priority level (critical/high/medium/low)". Source: interactive reply.
- Q5: "Rotation state scope — shared (one rotation per priority group in `.worklog/`) or per-instance?" — Answer (user): "(a) shared — all instances on the machine rotate together". Source: interactive reply.
- Q6: "Relationship to existing stagger item WL-0MSMHX6IR007F3H6?" — Answer (user): "absorb". Source: interactive reply.

# Intake Brief: Set up memory pressure monitoring and alerting

**Work Item:** WL-0MT1KJNGA006EEHU  
**Type:** task  
**Priority:** high  
**Derived from:** RCA of system hang 2026-08-20

---

## Problem statement

During the 2026-08-20 system hang, "Under memory pressure, flushing caches" appeared 10+ times in the journal between 13:27 and 13:40 with no alert and no early warning. The system ran for 21 days with accumulating memory pressure and no monitoring to catch it before it became unresponsive.

## Users and user stories

- **System operator / SRE:** "As a system operator, I want to be alerted when memory pressure is high so I can intervene before the system becomes unresponsive."
- **Incident responders:** "As an incident responder, I want historical memory trend data so I can diagnose memory exhaustion after the fact."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A cron-based monitoring script is installed (`/etc/cron.d/memwatch`) that checks `/proc/meminfo MemAvailable` every minute, with two configurable thresholds: warning at ~4 GB (17% of RAM) and critical at ~2 GB (8% of RAM).
2. Alerts are written to journald with a `MEMWATCH:` prefix and `user.warning` severity, with one log line per interval containing timestamp, available memory value, and threshold status.
3. sysstat's memory data collection is verified (10-minute interval, 7-day retention) and documented with an example query (`sar -r`) for historical trend analysis.
4. The alert mechanism is tested end-to-end once (verified alert emission in journald).
5. Setup, thresholds, and usage are documented in the script file comments and referenced from this work item.

## Constraints

- Must be lightweight — no new daemons or dependencies (cron + shell only).
- Must not generate excessive log noise (deduplicate repeated alerts; one log line per minute regardless of severity).
- Must run as root (requires reading /proc/meminfo and writing to journald with proper severity).
- Thresholds should be configurable via file-level variables at the top of the script.

## Existing state

- **sysstat** is installed and actively collecting memory data every 10 minutes via cron (`sa1`), with 7-day raw data retention and 10-day compressed retention.
- `sar -r` can query historical memory data from `/var/log/sysstat/`.
- No existing memory monitoring or alerting: no `earlyoom`, no custom cron jobs, no PSI monitoring.
- **PSI** (`/proc/pressure/memory`) is available on this kernel (7.0.0-31-generic) but not monitored.
- System has ~24 GB total RAM.

## Proposed change

Install `/etc/cron.d/memwatch` containing a shell script that:

1. Reads `MemAvailable` from `/proc/meminfo` every minute.
2. Compares against two thresholds (warning: ~4 GB, critical: ~2 GB).
3. Writes a structured log line to journald via `logger -p user.warning "MEMWATCH: ..."` with timestamp, available memory, and threshold breached.
4. De-duplicates repeated alerts for the same condition (e.g., one line per interval, not per-check).
5. Includes configurable thresholds and documentation in comments.

## Risks and assumptions

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|
| Script runs as root — security exposure if script is modified by non-root | Script owned by root:root with 0644 permissions; only root can write to /etc/cron.d |
| Log flooding if memory pressure is sustained | One log line per interval (cron minute), no retries or repeated logging |
| Threshold too aggressive causing alert fatigue | Two-tier approach with higher warning threshold; operator can tune |
| sysstat data retention (7 days) may not be sufficient for long-term trend analysis | Documented in brief; could be extended later via `/etc/default/sysstat` HISTORY variable |
| MemAvailable does not account for swap — system could be under pressure with large swap usage | Future enhancement: add swap usage monitoring as a follow-up task |

## Scope boundary

- This task covers MemAvailable-based monitoring only.
- PSI monitoring (`/proc/pressure/memory`), swap monitoring, and external alert channels (email, Slack, PagerDuty) are explicitly out of scope — they may be tracked as follow-up work items.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `/etc/cron.d/memwatch` — New cron job file with monitoring script
- `/proc/meminfo` — Source metric for MemAvailable
- `/var/log/sysstat/` — Existing historical memory data (read-only for this task)
- `journald/syslog` — Alert delivery target

## Related work

- Discovered from: RCA of system hang 2026-08-20 (session analysis)
- sysstat is already active (`/var/log/sysstat/`, 7-day retention)
- No directly related work items found in worklog

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Alert delivery mechanism?** — Answer (intake): journald + syslog via `logger -p user.warning` — lightweight, no external dependencies, visible in `journalctl -p warning`. Source: agent recommendation for headless server.
- **Q: Threshold strategy?** — Answer (intake): Two-tier — warning at ~4 GB (17%), critical at ~2 GB (8%). Source: agent recommendation based on ~24 GB total RAM and original incident severity.
- **Q: PSI monitoring?** — Answer (intake): Out of scope for this task — MemAvailable-only. Source: agent recommendation for simplicity; PSI can be a follow-up.
- **Q: sysstat memory data collection status?** — Answer: Active. `sar -r` returns memory data. Data every 10 minutes. 7-day raw retention. Source: system inspection.
data.title: Set up memory pressure monitoring and alerting

# Implement auto-downgrade of critical priority on terminal transitions

## Goal
When a work item with `priority=critical` transitions to a terminal state (status=completed or stage=in_review), automatically downgrade its priority to `high`.

## Implementation Details

### 1. Downgrade Logic

Add a helper function to detect and perform the auto-downgrade:
- Location: `packages/shared/src/database.ts` alongside the existing `cascadePriorityDowngrade`
- Function: `downgradeIfTerminal(item)` or inline check
- Logic: if item's new state has `status=completed` or `stage=in_review` AND `priority=critical`, set `priority=high`

### 2. Call Sites

Invoke from terminal-transition paths:
- `src/commands/update.ts` — after status/stage update, before response
- `src/commands/close.ts` — after close logic, before response

Prefer explicit call sites to avoid interfering with internal DB `update()` cascade calls.

### 3. Reporting

Report the downgrade in both output formats, mirroring the existing `downgradedChildren` pattern:
- JSON output: add `downgradedItem` field (or similar) with `{id, priority}` 
- Human-readable: add a summary line like `Downgraded priority from critical to high`

### 4. Constraints

- Only affect `critical` → `high` downgrade
- No change to other priorities (high/medium/low remain untouched)
- Only trigger on terminal transitions: `--status completed`, `--stage in_review`, or `wl close`

# Intake Draft — Double-click heading to expand/collapse

**Work item:** WL-0MT2S3LMW0016DN3

## Problem statement

The Herdr selection list supports Tab-to-toggle group collapse on heading rows (WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94 T3), but there is no mouse shortcut for this operation — a double-click on a heading row currently does nothing useful (it falls through to `open-detail` which is a no-op for headings since `getSelectedItem()` returns null). Power users who navigate with the mouse would benefit from a double-click-to-collapse pattern that mirrors the keyboard Tab behaviour.

## Users

- **Herdr plugin users** (operators running the work-item selection list pane) who use mouse interaction (click, double-click, wheel) alongside keyboard navigation.

User stories:
- "As a producer reviewing the worklist with a mouse, I want to double-click a group heading to collapse/expand it, so I can quickly hide groups I'm not interested in."
- "As a producer, I want double-clicking a heading to work the same way as pressing Tab on a heading, so my muscle memory carries across keyboard and mouse."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** Double-clicking a group heading row (two left presses on the same row within `DOUBLE_CLICK_WINDOW_MS`) toggles that group's collapse state — collapsed hides the group's items from render and navigation; expanded shows them.
- **AC2:** Double-clicking a work item row continues to open the detail view (existing behaviour unchanged).
- **AC3:** Single-clicking a heading row selects it (existing behaviour unchanged).
- **AC4:** The group collapse toggle on double-click preserves the existing in-memory state model (`collapsedGroups` Set, survives refresh, no persistence across restarts).
- **AC5:** When a heading is collapsed via double-click, the selection clamps to a visible item (the heading stays visible, but the collapsed items disappear).
- **AC6:** Full herdr test suite passes with the new changes.
- **AC7:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments.

## Constraints

- The change is confined to the Herdr plugin (`packages/herdr`) — specifically `worklist.ts` and its test files.
- Must be consistent with the existing mouse interaction model (double-click window, click tracking, drag-vs-click isolation).
- The Tab-key toggle for headings (WL-0MT1JGTJR002RTCB) must not regress.
- The renderer must never exceed `rows - 1` lines.

## Existing state

- Display-rows model (`WorkItemListState.getDisplayRows()`) interleaves `DisplayHeadingRow` objects with `WorkItem` objects.
- `isHeadingRow(row)` type guard identifies heading rows.
- `WorkItemListState.toggleGroupCollapse(group)` toggles a group's entry in the `collapsedGroups` Set.
- `handleKeypress` with `toggle-expand` on a heading row calls `toggleGroupCollapse` + `clampSelection` (lines ~3404–3414).
- `mapMouseToAction` double-click handling in list mode maps to `open-detail` for any non-null row index (line ~3738).
- `handleMouseInput` dispatches `open-detail` which calls `getSelectedItem()` — returns `null` for headings, so no-op (line ~3971).
- `DOUBLE_CLICK_WINDOW_MS = 400` (line 3453).
- `MouseClickState` tracks `lastClick { x, y, at }` for double-click detection.

## Desired change

1. **Add `toggle-group-collapse` action** to the `MouseAction` union type in `worklist.ts`.
2. **In `mapMouseToAction`** — when a double-click is detected in list mode, resolve the display row at the clicked index. If it is a heading row (`isHeadingRow`), return `{ type: 'toggle-group-collapse' }` instead of `{ type: 'open-detail' }`.
3. **In `handleMouseInput` dispatch** — add a case for `toggle-group-collapse` that calls `state.toggleGroupCollapse(row.group)` and `state.clampSelection()`, mirroring the keyboard `toggle-expand` heading path.
4. **Tests** — update `worklist-mouse.test.ts` to cover double-click on heading rows toggling collapse, and verify single-click, double-click on items, and double-click on different rows still work correctly.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `MouseAction` type, `mapMouseToAction` double-click logic, `handleMouseInput` dispatch case
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-mouse.test.ts` — test coverage for heading double-click toggle

## Assumptions

- Double-click on heading = toggle group collapse (same as Tab on heading). This is the natural mapping and matches user expectations from other list-based UIs (file explorers, etc.).
- The heading row stays visible after collapse (items disappear, heading remains as the group label) — consistent with existing Tab-toggle behaviour.
- No visual feedback beyond the existing collapse indicator (arrow) changing — no additional animation or flash required.
- The `DOUBLE_CLICK_WINDOW_MS` constant (400 ms) is reused — no new timing threshold needed.

## Risks & Mitigations

- **Risk:** Double-click on heading could conflict with drag-to-scroll if a user accidentally double-presses. Mitigation: the double-click detection is strict (same coordinates, within window) — a drag that crosses the threshold restores the pre-press selection (AC3 of drag isolation). A genuine double-press (no motion past threshold) is a valid toggle.
- **Risk:** The `mapMouseToAction` change must correctly identify heading rows from a screen-row coordinate. Mitigation: use the existing `mapListRowToIndex` + `getDisplayRows()[index]` + `isHeadingRow` — this is the same pattern the keyboard path uses to distinguish heading from item selection.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Adding click-to-toggle (single click) would change the interaction model and could interfere with selection — this is out of scope. Only double-click is requested.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94** — Herdr selection list: collapsible group headings with item counts (parent feature — display-rows model, heading selection, Tab toggle).
- **WL-0MT1JGTJR002RTCB** — T3: Tab toggle for group collapse (keyboard toggle path for heading rows).
- **WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ** — Herdr selection list: mouse and touch support (mouse interaction model, double-click for detail view, drag-to-scroll).
- **WL-0MSI72S0Y0060BRK** — Drag-to-scroll implementation (drag-vs-click isolation).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should double-click on a heading toggle collapse (like Tab) or open something? — Answer (assumption, consistent with keyboard): toggle group collapse, same as Tab on heading. Source: the request says "double clicking a heading should expand/collapse it."
- Q: Should single-click on a heading toggle? — Answer (assumption, no): single-click selects the heading (existing behaviour); only double-click toggles. Single-click toggle would conflict with the selection model. Source: operator did not request single-click toggle; keyboard path uses Enter as no-op, Tab as toggle.
- Q: Does the heading stay visible when collapsed? — Answer (assumption, yes): heading stays visible as a group label; only the items in that group are hidden. Source: consistent with existing Tab-toggle behaviour (WL-0MT1JGTJR002RTCB).

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, when the local LLM is idle, I want the herdr downtime
worker to avoid starting **non-critical** implementations while the
completed/in_review review queue is already deep enough to fill the
selection list, so the producer-review bottleneck is not overloaded.
Auditing, intake, and planning can still be dispatched — only the
implement tier is gated.

## Background

- Dispatch tier order (dispatchDowntimeWork): scheduled prompts → audit →
  implement → plan → intake. The code-freeze gate (WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY)
  already skips audit+implement during a release; this is a second,
  orthogonal implement-tier-only throttle on the producer-review queue.
- The herdr selection list displays up to `browseItemCount` items
  (default 20, clamp 1–50, packages/herdr/src/settings.ts).
- Review-queue count = completed/in_review **root** items
  (`wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only --json`) —
  same query family as the audit tier (WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG) and the
  selection list's mandatory review subset (WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B).
  Operator decision (2026-08): count is ROOT-ONLY, not all items.
- Implement candidates carry `priority` (critical/high/medium/low) via
  parseImplementCandidatesOutput.

## Design notes

- Gate: when `reviewQueueCount >= browseItemCount`, the implement tier
  selects only candidates with `priority === 'critical'`; non-critical
  candidates are excluded and dispatch falls through to plan/intake.
- Critical priority BYPASSES the gate — a critical implement always stays
  eligible regardless of queue depth.
- Fail-closed: a wl error counting the review queue → gate active (only
  critical implements), consistent with the code-freeze "ambiguous ⇒
  frozen" convention.
- `browseItemCount` is re-read live from settings on each dispatch (no
  plugin restart needed), matching the existing config() re-read pattern.
- The gate skip must NOT look like an empty backlog: when implement
  candidates exist but are gated AND plan/intake are empty, the outcome
  must be a neutral reason (never 'no-candidate'), so the worker's
  no-candidate cooldown is not triggered — polling continues and a
  critical implement / new plan / intake item dispatches immediately
  (mirrors the code-freeze 'code-freeze' reason convention).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A critical-priority implement candidate is always eligible regardless
   of review-queue depth (critical bypasses the gate).
2. When reviewQueueCount < browseItemCount, implement-tier selection is
   UNCHANGED: all priorities eligible; risk/effort/dispatched-marker
   filters unchanged.
3. When reviewQueueCount >= browseItemCount, non-critical implement
   candidates are excluded; if only non-critical candidates remain,
   getNextImplementCandidate resolves null and dispatch falls through to
   plan/intake (no-candidate only when plan AND intake are genuinely
   empty; a gate skip with an empty plan/intake backlog is a neutral
   reason, never 'no-candidate').
4. The gate applies ONLY to the implement tier — audit, plan, intake,
   and scheduled-prompt dispatch are unaffected.
5. The review-queue count query is bounded by DOWNTIME_WL_TIMEOUT_MS and
   fail-closed (error ⇒ gate active).
6. Tests cover: gate boundary (count == listSize − 1 vs count == listSize),
   critical bypass, root-only counting, fall-through outcome, and the
   neutral (no-cooldown) reason on a gate skip with empty plan/intake.

## Related work

- WL-0MSMAYPQP001FLR6 — Implement tier end-to-end in herdr downtime worker
- WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG — Audit tier (completed/in_review without valid audit)
- WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY — Code-freeze gate
- WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B — Selection list must always show all
  completed/in_review and critical items
