# Recovery: classify the proxy "All providers unavailable … time window" 503 as SERVER_ERROR

## Problem statement

When every llama-proxy provider is outside its scheduled `available_times`
window the proxy returns a 503 whose body reads
`All providers unavailable: no provider is available during the current scheduled time window`.
The Worklog recovery classifier does not match that wording, so `classifyError()`
returns `ErrorCategory.UNKNOWN` → `register-recovery.ts` displays
`Unrecognized error: …` and performs **no** retry, silently stalling a long-running agent turn.

## Users

- **Primary: the autonomous agent session (e.g. herdr downtime worker)** running a long task
  through the local llama-proxy — a provider quiet-hours window should trigger a retry, not a stall.
  - *As an unattended agent, when the proxy reports no provider is currently scheduled, I want the
    recovery loop to retry with backoff so my task resumes automatically once a provider becomes available.*
- **Secondary: the operator monitoring sessions** — should see a retryable server-error notice rather
  than an "Unrecognized error" terminal message they must intervene on.
  - *As an operator, I want transient proxy scheduling windows to self-heal so I am not paged for a
    recoverable condition.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The exact proxy string
  `All providers unavailable: no provider is available during the current scheduled time window`
  is classified by `classifyError()` as `ErrorCategory.SERVER_ERROR` (not `UNKNOWN`).
- [ ] `DEFAULT_SERVER_ERROR_PATTERNS` matches the new wordings case-insensitively —
  `all providers unavailable`, `no provider is available`, `scheduled time window`, and
  (recommended, low-risk) `outside its available_times` — and matching does not alter any other
  category (each new pattern must not match the timeout/context-length/compaction-gate patterns).
- [ ] A test in `error-classification.test.ts` asserts (a) the full proxy string classifies as
  `SERVER_ERROR`, (b) each new pattern variant matches, and (c) the existing
  `all providers exhausted` / `no provider available` cases remain unaffected.
- [ ] No regression: all existing error-classification and recovery-module tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] Recursively resolving a SERVER_ERROR classification reaches the retryable
  `serverError` path (`triggerInvisibleContinue`/retry loop) rather than the `UNKNOWN`
  no-retry branch — verified by an existing or new assertion.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README,
  and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Scope boundary (deferred):** the original "prefer a stable machine-readable `code`/`type` field
  over prose" AC is **out of scope here** — it depends on the proxy exposing such a field
  (tracked proxy-side as `LP-0MU56ZM0K005F69G`). Recorded as a follow-up, not implemented in this item.
- **Classifier ordering:** `classifyError()` checks `TIMEOUT` before `SERVER_ERROR`. New patterns
  must not be subsumed by an earlier, broader category (e.g. avoid a bare `time` token that could
  interact with `/timeout/i`).
- **Regex-only change:** no new dependencies, no changes to the category set or retry mechanics.
- **Idempotent additions:** reuse/overlap with existing patterns (`no provider available`) is
  acceptable but must not create duplicate or unreachable patterns.
- Keep the change minimal and surgical — pattern list plus tests (and a short comment).

## Existing state

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-patterns.ts` — `DEFAULT_SERVER_ERROR_PATTERNS`
  already contains `/all providers exhausted/i` and `/no provider available/i` (added by the
  predecessor `WL-0MT656GDS0052FTK`), but **not** the "unavailable"/"is available" wordings.
- `classifyError()` order: `COMPACTION_GATE` → `CONTEXT_LENGTH` → `RATE_LIMIT` → `AUTH_ERROR` →
  `QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` → `TIMEOUT` → `SERVER_ERROR` → `TERMINATED` → `PARSE_ERROR` → `UNKNOWN`.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts` (`UNKNOWN` default branch,
  ~line 184) emits `Unrecognized error: …` and does not retry.
- `error-classification.test.ts` has `isServerError` cases for "all providers exhausted" and
  "no provider available", and a `classifyError` case asserting SERVER_ERROR for those strings —
  but no coverage of the scheduled-window wording.

## Desired change

1. Add to `DEFAULT_SERVER_ERROR_PATTERNS` (with a brief comment citing this item + predecessor):
   - `/all providers unavailable/i`
   - `/no provider\s+(is\s+)?available/i`
   - `/scheduled time window/i`
   - `/outside its available_times/i` (recommended)
2. Extend `error-classification.test.ts`:
   - `isServerError` cases for each new wording (mixed case).
   - A `classifyError` case asserting the exact full proxy message → `ErrorCategory.SERVER_ERROR`.
3. Confirm the `UNKNOWN` no-retry branch is not reached for this message; if practical, assert the
   retryable path is selected.
4. Add/refresh the code comment noting the longer-term preference for a machine-readable
   `code`/`type` field (follow-up `LP-0MU56ZM0K005F69G`).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-patterns.ts` — add the new
  `DEFAULT_SERVER_ERROR_PATTERNS` entries + comment (primary change).
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-classification.test.ts` — new
  `isServerError`/`classifyError` assertions for the scheduled-window wording.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts` — no change expected;
  verify the SERVER_ERROR branch is reached (read-only).
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/recovery.ts` / `retry-logic.ts` — likely read-only;
  only touch if a retry-path assertion is required.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — exact wording.** The proxy body is exactly
  `All providers unavailable: no provider is available during the current scheduled time window`
  (confirmed in the proxy repo by the investigation comment `WL-C0MU570W3B000H4FI`).
- **Risk — recurrence.** This is the *second* prose-wording fix of the same class (after
  `WL-0MT656GDS0052FTK`); the proxy can rephrase again. Mitigation: cover several variants now and
  pursue the structured `code` field (`LP-0MU56ZM0K005F69G`) rather than relying on prose alone.
- **Risk — over-broad patterns.** A too-generic pattern could reclassify unrelated errors.
  Mitigation: use anchored/qualified phrases and add regression assertions for the other categories.
- **Risk — retry budget vs window length.** SERVER_ERROR backoff is 2s→60s; a provider quiet-hours
  window may outlast the retry budget, in which case the task still fails (now retried rather than
  instantly dropped). Related: `WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM` (honour long Retry-After hints).
- **Scope-creep risk.** Ideas beyond the pattern/test change (e.g. structured-code handling) are
  recorded as linked work items rather than pulled into this item.

## Related work

- **`WL-0MT656GDS0052FTK` — Classify 'All providers exhausted' for automatic retry (completed, high):**
  direct predecessor; added `/all providers exhausted/i` and `/no provider available/i`. This item is
  the same class of fix for the scheduled-window wording.
- **`WL-0MUVXR39A0081774` / `WL-0MUVYA3VW008CH6I` (children of `WL-0MUQO8AEE003G1Z2`)** — analogous
  pattern-plus-test work for the "Provider finish_reason: error" string; a useful template for the
  implement/test split.
- **`WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM` — Honour long server Retry-After hints (do not clamp to 60s)** — adjacent
  retry-quality work; not a dependency.
- **`LP-0MU56ZM0K005F69G` (proxy side)** — stable machine-readable error `code`; the deferred
  follow-up that would let classification key off a structured field instead of prose.
- **`LP-0MU56Z3XY001I0NO` (proxy epic)** — time-window exhaustion response wording.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview round was required: the seed context (description + investigation comment
`WL-C0MU570W3B000H4FI`, plus predecessor `WL-0MT656GDS0052FTK`) already specified the problem,
the exact change, and the target category. Decisions taken by the agent and recorded here:

- Q: Is the machine-readable `code` preference (original AC4) in scope? — Answer (agent, from seed):
  No; it is explicitly marked "(follow-up)" and depends on proxy work `LP-0MU56ZM0K005F69G`
  (proxy epic `LP-0MU56Z3XY001I0NO`). Recorded as deferred, not implemented here. Source: seed description.
- Q: Should the optional `/outside its available_times/i` pattern be included? — Answer (agent):
  Yes (recommended, low risk) — it captures the same failure class if the proxy rephrases the body.
  Source: seed description ("optionally").
- Q: Is a dedicated docs update needed? — Answer (agent): No user-facing recovery doc exists for
  pattern lists; documentation obligations are satisfied by the code comment plus the standing docs AC.
  Source: repo search (`grep` over `*.md` found only `docs/design/compaction-gate.md`).
- OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking): priority remains `medium` (as created). This is an "important bug"
  that silently drops long work and its predecessor was `high`; the operator may wish to raise it.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQN2RPP9006XZQC** – wl tui: catch uninitialized worklog error and show friendly message to run wl init first (completed)
- **WL-0MTBOXEGR009KDP6** – Client-side compaction response to llm-proxy compaction gate (cheap hard-cap 4xx) (completed)
- **WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM** – Honour long server Retry-After hints (do not clamp to 60s) so the client waits until models return (open)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: acceptance, add, added, adds, available (+68 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: add, adds, asserts, available, change (+64 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: add, added, adds, available, change (+58 more)

# Intake Brief — Herdr stage vocabulary out of sync with wl CLI (WL-0MU624MF7004WYMI)

## Problem Statement

The Herdr plugin still enumerates two stage values that the `wl` CLI no longer
accepts (`in_progress`, `completed`) and omits nothing for `done` any more, but
its display and filter paths were only partially brought in line. The result
is a stage filter that can select stages with no (`in_progress`/`completed`)
backing data and shows misleading empty worklists, and code paths that key off
`stage === 'in_progress'` semantics that no longer exist in the CLI vocabulary.

## Users

- **Herdr plugin users (developers / agents)** browsing with the `f i/f n/f p/f r`
  stage-filter chords or `/wl <stage>`, who currently hit dead filter states.
- **Producers / reviewers** relying on the Herdr list to reflect the same
  pipeline stages as `wl` and the Pi TUI, so an item's stage means the same
  thing everywhere.
- **Maintainers** of the shared icon/colour maps, who need the stage vocabulary
  to be a single source of truth.

### Example User Stories

- As a **Herdr user**, I want the stage filter to cycle only through stages the
  CLI actually recognises (`idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`,
  `in_review`, `done`), so I never land on a filter that can only ever be empty.
- As a **Herdr user**, I want legacy items carrying `stage=done` (2,355 in the
  current DB) to render the completed-style checkmark rather than a fallback
  question mark.
- As a **Herdr user**, I want an item being actively worked (its `status` is
  `in-progress`) to keep the metadata Last-command panel even though its
  `stage` is `plan_complete`/`intake_complete`.
- As a **maintainer**, I want the Herdr stage vocabulary to be derived from (or
  asserted equal to) the shared `wl` stage rules, so it cannot drift again.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` `STAGES` equals exactly the CLI vocabulary `['idea','intake_complete','plan_complete','in_review','done']` (`in_progress` and `completed` removed); `Stage` (and any derived types) continue to typecheck, and no Herdr code hard-codes the removed values as valid stages.
- [ ] `STAGE_MAP` accepts only the CLI-valid canonical names and supported shorthand aliases; the `progress → in_progress` alias is removed, while `intake`/`plan`/`review`/`done` aliases still resolve. `/wl progress` and `/wl completed` fail soft (no crash, no invalid filter applied) consistent with the existing `/wl <bogus>` behaviour.
- [ ] `StageFilter` cycles only the five valid stages (then clears to `null`); `fetchItemsByStage` guards unknown/invalid stages fail-soft so it never issues `wl list --stage <invalid>` and never throws (returns an empty or fallback list). A regression test proves `in_progress`/`completed`/ `bogus` cannot produce a CLI invocation and do not throw.
- [ ] Herdr behaviour that previously keyed off `stage === 'in_progress'` (the list-row stage tag suppression, the metadata-panel Last-command reservation and lookup) is re-based on `status === 'in-progress'`, so actively-worked items keep the same UI behaviour under the current status-only claim model.
- [ ] The shared icon/colour maps (`packages/shared/src/icons.ts` `STAGE_ICONS`/`STAGE_FALLBACK`/`stageColor`) include `done` mapped to the completed-style checkmark/colour, and every valid stage plus an unknown stage render deterministically (unknown falls back to the question-mark icon without throwing). New/updated tests cover `done` and an unknown stage.
- [ ] Tests are added/updated for: the exact `STAGES` list, `StageFilter` cycling/wrapping, `STAGE_MAP` alias resolution and invalid-alias fail-soft, `fetchItemsByStage` invalid-stage guarding, and status-based in-progress UI behaviour; all existing tests continue to pass.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md`, and any relevant `CLI.md` / docs entries describing the Herdr stage vocabulary and filter chords. (CHANGELOG.md is excluded — managed by the ship release pipeline.)
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Align to the CLI, do not change it.** The `wl` stage vocabulary is
  `idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`, `in_review`, `done`
  (`.worklog/config.defaults.yaml:21-31`). Do not add stages to `wl` config as
  part of this work item.
- **Preserve legacy rendering.** 2,355 persisted items carry `stage=done`; the
  plugin must keep rendering them correctly. `done` must remain a displayable
  stage even though it is the post-release terminal stage.
- **Support legacy `stage=in_progress` rows fail-soft.** The current DB has one
  `stage=in_progress` item; removing the value from `STAGES` must not crash any
  code path that renders it.
- **Status semantics unchanged.** `status=in-progress` remains the "actively
  worked" signal (SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9); do not reintroduce a stage for it.
- **No scope creep into `wl` core** (config/validation/doctor) — those were
  handled by WL-0MTOHS5B4001Y9FX; this item is the Herdr/shared-display
  follow-up only.
- Respect `.gitignore` / agent-framework ignore rules in searches.

## Existing State

- **CLI valid stages** (`npx tsx`/config inspection of
  `.worklog/config.defaults.yaml:21-31`):
  `idea, intake_complete, plan_complete, in_review, done`. `in_progress` and
  `completed` are not accepted by `wl update`/`wl next` validation
  (`src/commands/status-stage-validation.ts:76`).
- **Herdr `STAGES`** (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts:166-174`):
  `idea, intake_complete, plan_complete, in_progress, in_review, completed,
  done` — two invalid values present (added as legacy alias handling in
  WL-0MU3U1AMP0044WUX).
- **Herdr `STAGE_MAP`** (`worklist.ts:180-194`) includes `progress →
  in_progress` and self-mappings for `in_progress`/`done`.
- **`STAGE_STATUS`** (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:632-636`) only special-cases
  `in_review`, `plan_complete`, `intake_complete`; anything else defaults to
  `--status open`, so `fetchItemsByStage('in_progress'|'completed')` issues
  `wl list --status open --stage in_progress|completed --root-only` and returns
  an empty, misleading list.
- **`stage === 'in_progress'` keyed behaviour** remains in
  `worklist.ts:1355` (row stage-tag suppression), `worklist.ts:2020-2026`
  (metadata Last-command reservation), and `worklist.ts:6252` (last-command
  lookup). These predate the stage removal and now never fire for
  status-only claims.
- **Shared icons** (`packages/shared/src/icons.ts:51-68, 608-617`) already
  include `done` keys (added by WL-0MU3U1AMP0044WUX) but still carry
  `in_progress`/`completed` stage entries.
- **DB stage distribution** (measured `wl list --json`): `done` 2,355,
  `in_review` 6, `intake_complete` 14, `idea` 45, `plan_complete` 2,
  `in_progress` 1 (status `blocked`), `completed` 0.
- **Research note:** the seed's claim that `wl list --stage <invalid>` raises a
  CLI error was **not reproducible** in the current build — `wl list --stage
  bogus`/`--stage completed` return `success:true, count:0`. The defect is
  therefore a misleading empty filter plus a missing fail-soft guard, not a
  hard CLI error. (The validation error is real for `wl update`.)

## Desired Change

- Replace Herdr's `STAGES` with the exact CLI vocabulary
  `['idea','intake_complete','plan_complete','in_review','done']` and update
  the `Stage` type/consumers accordingly.
- Trim `STAGE_MAP` to CLI-valid names plus shorthand aliases; drop the
  `progress`/`in_progress` alias (and any `completed` mapping).
- Make `fetchItemsByStage` fail-soft for unknown/invalid stages: do not invoke
  `wl` with an invalid `--stage`, return an empty (or sensible fallback) list,
  and never throw.
- Re-base `stage === 'in_progress'` UI behaviour on `status === 'in-progress'`.
- Confirm/retain `done` in `STAGE_ICONS`/`STAGE_FALLBACK`/`stageColor` and add
  regression coverage for `done` and unknown stages.
- Prefer deriving `STAGES` from the shared status-stage rules (or assert
  equality against them in a test) so future drift is caught.
- Update `tests/herdr/worklist.test.ts`, `tests/herdr/fetcher.test.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/stage-status.test.ts`, `tests/herdr/icons.test.ts`, and
  any other test asserting the old seven-stage list.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `STAGES` (line ~166) and `STAGE_MAP`
  (line ~180) trimmed to the CLI vocabulary; `StageFilter`; `stage ===

# Intake Brief: Fix mode-switch flip-flop — leader election for proxy mode changes

## Problem statement

When multiple herdr panes are open, each creates an independent `ModeSwitchWorker` with its own idle clock. Active and idle panes fight over the same proxy — the active pane's fast flips are immediately undone by idle panes' cheap flips, causing a rapid flip-flop pattern (13–20 second cycles) in logs.

## Users

- **Primary:** Operator using herdr with multiple panes — experiences unreliable proxy mode switching due to flip-flopping.
- **Secondary:** herdr developers debugging proxy mode behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Leader-only mode switching:** Only the downtime leader performs mode switches (cheap POST). Non-leader instances skip `tick()` cheap-switch logic entirely.
2. **Shared activity broadcast:** All instances read/write a shared `mode-activity.json` file in the coordination directory. Any instance receiving a command broadcasts; all instances use the shared timestamp. Proxy stays fast while *any* pane has recent activity.
3. **60-minute idle threshold:** `DEFAULT_MODE_SWITCH_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS` changed from 900,000 ms (15 min) to 3,600,000 ms (60 min). A clamped-settings test verifies the new default.
4. **No flip-flopping:** With two panes open (one active, one idle), the proxy remains in fast mode while the active pane receives commands, regardless of the idle pane's local clock.
5. **Graceful leader transitions:** On leadership change, the new leader reads the shared activity file and continues from correct state — no spurious mode changes during election.
6. **Fail-closed on broadcast failure:** If shared activity state cannot be read/written, the instance falls back to its local clock (safe: stays fast longer rather than risking premature cheap switch).
7. **Full test suite passes.**

## Constraints

- Must reuse the existing downtime leader (`DowntimeWorker.isLeader`), not create a separate leader election.
- Shared activity file lives in the coordination directory (`~/.herdr/downtime/` or `HERDR_COORDINATION_DIR` override).
- Fail-closed: if coordination fails, the instance must not prematurely switch to cheap mode.
- All related work (leader election, downtime dispatcher, mode-switch idle trigger) is already completed.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts:319` — `lastOperatorCommandAt` tracked per-instance, no inter-instance coordination.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts:1401` — `createModeSwitchWorker()` called once per pane, before `createDowntimeWorker()`.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts:125` — `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs: 900_000` (15 min).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:3951` — `DowntimeWorker.isLeader` exists as a readonly boolean.

## Desired change

1. Wire `downtimeWorker.isLeader` into `ModeSwitchWorker` via `createModeSwitchWorker()` constructor options.
2. Add shared activity file read/write in the coordination directory (`mode-activity.json`).
3. `tick()`: non-leaders return immediately; leaders evaluate and fire cheap POST.
4. `onOperatorCommand()`: all instances update shared activity; only leader fires fast POST.
5. On `tick()`, both leaders and non-leaders read shared activity file for unified idle evaluation.
6. Change default idle threshold from 15 min to 60 min.
7. Add comprehensive tests.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts` — leader-gated `tick()` and `onOperatorCommand()`; shared activity broadcast/read
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — change `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs` default from 900_000 to 3_600_000
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — pass `downtimeWorker.isLeader` and `coordinationDir` into the mode-switch worker (may need to reorder creation to happen after `createDowntimeWorker()`)
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.test.ts` — new tests for leader-gating, shared activity broadcast, no flip-flop, graceful leader transitions
- README — document the 60-minute default, leader-gating, and shared activity broadcast

## Risks & Assumptions

1. **Leader election overlap during transitions:** Brief dual-leadership during lease handoff could cause double mode switches. Mitigation: `tick()` is already single-flighted (`switchInFlight` guard); a double switch would resolve to the correct state on the next poll.
2. **Coordination directory existence:** The shared activity file requires the coordination directory to exist. Assumption: `createDowntimeWorker` already ensures directory creation (confirmed via existing `getMachineCoordinationDir()` usage).
3. **Concurrent file writes:** Multiple instances writing `mode-activity.json` simultaneously. Mitigation: use atomic writes (write to temp file, then rename) or rely on small synchronous writes that are atomic at the OS level for small JSON objects.
4. **Reordering `createModeSwitchWorker`:** In `index.ts`, the mode-switch worker is currently created *before* the downtime worker so it can accept the `onProxyIdle` callback. Passing `isLeader` requires creating the downtime worker first. Mitigation: the callback can be wired after both workers exist — no ordering change needed for the callback itself.
5. **Scope creep:** This fix is scoped to leader-gating and shared activity. Do not add new coordination protocols, gossip, or network-based mechanisms.

## Related work

- **WL-0MTF0KLO10043YAN** — Single machine-wide downtime leader across all worklogs (completed, done)
- **WL-0MSXH3UF5000HJUS** — Implement leader election module with 5-minute lease management (completed, done)
- **WL-0MU4MKVR4005WPBJ** — Herdr mode-switch worker: modeSwitchEnabled defaults to false (completed, in_review)
- **WL-0MSN3FWV5008KQE9** — Herdr plugin: activity-gated proxy mode switching (completed, done)

- Q: None — the work item was sufficiently defined to proceed without clarification.

# [downtime] Release stale dispatch success-markers when the item has not advanced

Discovered-from: WL-0MT32F908002YFFA (release stranded items) — that fix covered only `marker-write-failed` and `spawn-failed`. This item covers the remaining, more common failure mode: a **successful** pane spawn whose agent never advances the item.

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatch pipeline writes a durable *dispatched marker* to `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` **before** spawning the agent pane, to prevent duplicate dispatch. Marker readers (`dispatchedItemStages`, `dispatchedItemIds`, `recentDispatchedItemIds` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`) then exclude that item from re-dispatch **while it remains at its dispatched-at stage**.

If the pane spawns successfully but the agent never advances the item — crash, manual close, silent failure, or an agent that exits without progressing — the success marker remains **forever**. The item is permanently invisible to the tier that would retry it, and can only leave that stage by completing the very step that will never be scheduled. This is a deadlock.

WL-0MT32F908002YFFA made only `outcome: 'spawn-failed'` entries non-excluding. A successful spawn with no progress is not covered, and there is **no TTL and no stage-change guard** on success markers.

## Users

- **Producer / operator** — unattended work must recover from a dead pane without manual intervention; today it silently strands and the whole dispatch queue starves.
- **Dispatch agent** — must not deadlock the pipeline when a peer pane fails to progress.

## Live evidence (2026-09-18)

Three open **critical** items are stranded this way, all with success markers at stages they never left:

| Item | Project | Stranded marker(s) |
|---|---|---|
| `CG-0MU4U38HU000AXU2` | Tableau-Card-Engine | `plan` @ `intake_complete` |
| `WL-0MU55UDBJ008DJ67` | ContextHub | `plan` @ `intake_complete`, `implement` @ `plan_complete` |
| `SA-0MSYPAV1R000SMHK` | SorraAgents | `intake`, `plan`, `implement` |

In Tableau-Card-Engine alone the same mechanism strands 6 `implement` and 3 `intake` markers, exhausting the entire dispatch window (see the sibling item on window starvation).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A success marker whose item is **still at the marker's stage** and whose age exceeds a configurable staleness window (default 24 h) no longer excludes the item — it becomes re-selectable.
2. A marker whose item has **advanced** past the stage stays non-excluding, exactly as today (no behaviour change for healthy flow).
3. The staleness window is configurable and clamped to a sane range; the default and clamp are documented.
4. The three live stranded critical items above are re-dispatched within one idle cycle after the fix, with **no manual intervention**.
5. Unit tests cover: fresh marker still excludes; stale marker at unchanged stage does not exclude; stage-advanced marker does not exclude; unparseable/missing `dispatchedAt` fails closed (keeps excluding).
6. `npm run build` and the existing suites pass.

## Key files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — marker readers (`dispatchedItemStages` / `dispatchedItemIds` / `recentDispatchedItemIds`)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — marker-exclusion filters on the Herdr head
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — settings wiring / clamp
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — marker-lifetime contract

## Constraints

- Must not weaken duplicate-dispatch protection for genuinely in-flight work (a marker for a pane that is still running must keep excluding).
- No second ranking: this changes marker *lifetime*, not candidate ordering.

# [downtime] Dispatch window can starve: the Herdr head cap can exclude the only dispatchable item

Parent: WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2

## Problem statement

`getHerdrListHead` calls `fetchNextItems(30)` → `selectWorkItems(merged, 30)` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts`). Mandatory items (all `priority=critical` + all `completed`/`in_review`) are always included, and the remaining slots are filled from "other" items in Herdr order:

```
othersLimit = max(0, 30 − (criticals + reviews))
```

When the mandatory set is large, the window holds very few "other" items — and the first genuinely dispatchable candidate can fall outside it. The dispatcher iterates **only** the returned head, so such an item is invisible and no offer is produced.

The windowing is mandated by parent AC3 ("`browseItemCount` windowing of 'other' items"), so this fix must preserve the single-ranking contract ("dispatcher == Herdr list head; gates are filters, not ranking") while guaranteeing the dispatch path can always reach a dispatchable candidate.

## Live evidence (2026-09-18, Tableau-Card-Engine)

- Mandatory set = 1 critical + 8 `in_review` = 9 → `othersLimit = 21` → head = 30 items.
- All 30 were blocked: 8 freshly audited, 11 `needsProducerReview`, 6 `implement`-marker, 3 `intake`-marker, 1 `plan`-marker, 1 risk-too-high.
- The **only** genuinely dispatchable item, `CG-0MTZO0YIM000VAIQ` (high, `idea`, no markers, not producer-review), was the **22nd** "other" — cut off by the 21-slot cap.
- Result: `computeMostImportantItem` → `noCandidate`, the machine coordination file stayed `{"entries":[]}`, and **zero dispatches occurred for 31 h** despite a healthy leader.

## Acceptance criteria

1. When the Herdr head contains no dispatchable candidate but the broader backlog does, the dispatcher considers additional candidates beyond the `browseItemCount` window **in the same Herdr priority order** (extended window — never a second ranking).
2. The extension is bounded by a documented maximum, and does not regress worklist rendering (which keeps `browseItemCount`).
3. A regression test reproduces the starvation scenario (mandatory items fill the window; the first dispatchable item lies beyond the cap) and asserts a candidate is found.
4. `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` states that the dispatch window extends at least to the first dispatchable candidate, up to the documented maximum; the "no candidate" contract applies only to a genuinely empty dispatchable backlog.
5. `npm run build` and the existing suites pass.

## Key files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `fetchNextItems` / window sizing
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — `selectWorkItems`
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `getHerdrListHead`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — offer/dispatch iteration
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — contract

## Constraints

- No second ranking. Ordering must remain `fetchNextItems` / `selectWorkItems` order.
- `browseItemCount` clamping (1–50), root-only and `done`-exclusion rules respected.
- The TUI worklist must keep showing exactly `browseItemCount`-bounded output.

# [downtime] Critical items blocked by a filter are never escalated (critical override is dead code)

Parent: WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2

## Problem statement

The dispatcher once had a *critical-first* tier: `getNextCriticalCandidate()` enumerated open critical items across **all** stages and dispatched the highest-priority one with its stage-appropriate skill (implemented by WL-0MTJDZY5E003D6CO, marked completed).

That tier now lives **only** in the legacy tier chain, which runs **only when the Herdr head is empty**. The current source says so explicitly (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` ~line 1700): the tier is *"dead whenever the Herdr head is non-empty"*. Because mandatory critical/`in_review` items always populate the head, the override **never fires**. This is a silent regression introduced by the Herdr-head migration (WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2).

Consequence: a critical item blocked by **any** filter — stale success marker, producer-review flag, audit-freshness, risk/effort — is treated exactly like an ordinary item and is never escalated. It can sit indefinitely while lower-priority work consumes the window.

## Live evidence (2026-09-18)

All three open critical items across the workspace went undispatched for 30+ hours while the dispatcher reported `noCandidate`:

- `CG-0MU4U38HU000AXU2` — Tableau-Card-Engine (`intake_complete`, blocked by stale `plan` marker)
- `WL-0MU55UDBJ008DJ67` — ContextHub (`plan_complete`, blocked by stale `implement` marker)
- `SA-0MSYPAV1R000SMHK` — SorraAgents (`plan_complete`, blocked by stale `implement` marker)

The stale-marker cause is the sibling item. This item addresses the missing **escalation guarantee** for critical work regardless of cause.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The highest-priority open critical item is escalated/re-dispatched within one idle cycle even when a **non-safety** filter (e.g. stale marker) currently excludes it.
2. Genuine **safety** gates still block escalation: `needsProducerReview === true`, code-freeze/ambiguous, active-audit single-flight, per-process single-flight, and the pre-dispatch CAS claim.
3. No second ranking is introduced: critical items are already mandatory-always in the Herdr head; the fix only guarantees a blocked critical item is not starved by non-critical items occupying the window.
4. Regression tests: (a) a critical item blocked by one non-safety filter is dispatched ahead of lower-priority dispatchable items; (b) a critical item blocked by a safety gate is **not** dispatched.
5. Contract documented in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (what "critical-first" now means under the Herdr-head contract).
6. `npm run build` and the existing suites pass.

## Key files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchDowntimeWork` / offer computation (re-introduce a live critical pass on the Herdr-head path)
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `getNextCriticalCandidate` wiring
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — contract
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — regression tests

## Constraints

- Must not resurrect the retired tier ordering as a *ranking*; keep "gates are filters on the Herdr sequence".
- Preserve the three-strike / cooldown and single-flight semantics.

# Herdr dispatcher ignores `needsProducerReview` on the live dispatch path

<<discovered-from>>:WL-0MU6UL3GQ0015AA5

## Problem

`dispatchFromHerdrList` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`) builds the
`DowntimeItemInfo` passed to `classifyItemForDispatch` from the Herdr head item
but OMITS `needsProducerReview`. `classifyItemForDispatch` blocks an item when
`info.needsProducerReview === true`, so on the live Herdr-head dispatch path the
flag is silently ignored and a `needsProducerReview: true` item dispatches anyway.

Reproduced while implementing WL-0MU6UL3GQ0015AA5: `dispatchDowntimeWork` with a
Herdr head item `{ status:'open', stage:'plan_complete', priority:'critical',
risk:'Low', effort:'S', needsProducerReview:true }` dispatches it as
`/skill:implement` — the flag never reaches `classifyItemForDispatch`.

The offer path (`computeMostImportantItem`) passes the item object DIRECTLY to
`classifyItemForDispatch`, so the flag IS honoured there. The two paths disagree,
so the live dispatch path can auto-dispatch items the producer has explicitly
flagged for review.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `dispatchFromHerdrList` threads `needsProducerReview` into the
   `classifyItemForDispatch` input, so `needsProducerReview === true` items are
   never dispatched on the live Herdr-head path.
2. A regression test proves the flag blocks a `plan_complete`/idea/intake
   candidate on `dispatchDowntimeWork` (currently it does not).
3. The direct and offer paths agree on the producer-review gate.
4. `npm run build` and the suites pass.

## Constraints

- No second ranking: the fix is a field-threading correction on the existing
  sequential filter, not a new ordering.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: N/A — auto-plan (effort/risk below threshold, no decomposition needed).
  The item is a focused bug fix with clear ACs. Code fix was already applied in
  commit 022f1b24 (WL-0MU6UL3XY001M3VT). Remaining gap: AC2 regression test
  for non-critical items on the normal dispatch path.

# Intake Brief — Dispatched panes should go under the project workspace (WL-0MU7JZE04008VKP0)

**Headline**: Automated downtime dispatch panes currently land in a machine-wide `Dispatcher` workspace grouped into per-prefix tabs; change this so each pane is spawned in the same tab as that project's herdr (Worklog) plugin pane, inside the project's own herdr workspace. **Blocked on duplicate reconciliation with `WL-0MU321YK70035AYT` — see the Appendix (OPEN QUESTION Q1).**

## Problem statement

Automated downtime dispatches spawn into a dedicated machine-wide `Dispatcher` workspace (`downtime-dispatch-anchor.json`) and, after C1, route by work-item prefix into per-prefix tabs inside that workspace (`downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json`). The producer has rejected the per-project-tab approach and wants automated panes to land **inside the project's own herdr workspace**, in the **same tab as that project's herdr plugin (Worklog) pane**, so automated work is co-located with the project it belongs to.

## Users

- **Herdr operator running 2+ project workspaces** (ContextHub `WL`, Tableau Card Engine `CG/TCE`, AI Hell `AH`, SorraAgents `SA`):
  > "As an operator, I want automated downtime panes for project `X` to appear next to that project's Worklog pane in project `X`'s workspace, so I see a project's automated activity in context instead of in a separate neutral workspace."
- **Overnight / on-call dispatch reviewer**:
  > "As an on-call engineer, I want each project's automated panes to sit in that project's workspace tab, so projects never intermix and I do not have to hunt through a Dispatcher workspace."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Project-workspace placement** — for an automated dispatch of work item `<PREFIX>-<hash>` whose worklog root is `R`, the spawned `Downtime triggered …` pane's `workspace_id` and `tab_id` equal those of the herdr plugin pane (`label == "Work Items"`) whose logical project root is `R`; verified with `herdr pane list` / `herdr tab list`. No pane for root `R` lands in the `Dispatcher` workspace or in another project's workspace.
2. **Deterministic project→workspace resolution** — resolution matches the candidate's worklog root `R` against the plugin pane's logical project root (`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`, read via `herdr pane process-info --pane <id>` + `/proc/<shell_pid>/environ`), **not** against pane `cwd` (plugin panes report the plugin directory) and **not** against the workspace label. Ambiguous or failed resolution is fail-closed.
3. **Placement within the project workspace** — the anchor used to split is the project's plugin/worklist pane, so the new pane opens in the same tab as the Worklog pane (per the duplicate item's wording "same tab as the herdr extension"). `send-to-pi.sh --anchor <paneId>` + `grid.py` are reused; no new pane-creation mechanism.
4. **Per-prefix `Dispatcher` routing retired from the worklog dispatch path** — `getDispatcherTabAnchor` / `downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json` are no longer used for worklog-item dispatch (fate of the `Dispatcher` workspace/anchor file is OPEN QUESTION Q2).
5. **No regression** — selection/ranking, coordination/leader election, round-robin, CAS claim (`--if-status/--if-stage`), staged-marker exclusion, `code-freeze` and `needsProducerReview` gates, per-item `cwd` forwarding, pane naming, and the dispatch audit log kinds are unchanged.
6. **Applied to every automated spawn** — worklog tiers and scheduled prompts (which carry a worklog root `cwd`) use the same resolver; manual `open-worklist` / `open-pi-agent` flows are unchanged.
7. **Tests** — unit/integration coverage for: resolution success, no-plugin-pane handling, multiple-plugin-pane handling, malformed `pane list` / `process-info` output (fail-closed), anchor forwarding to `send-to-pi.sh --anchor`, and removal of per-prefix routing from the worklog path; existing `packages/herdr` tests adjusted and green.
8. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Automated downtime dispatch only (`dispatchClaimedTier` / `dispatchFromCoordination` / `dispatchScheduledPrompt`); manual flows keep current behaviour.
- Reuse the existing spawn surface: `send-to-pi.sh --anchor <paneId>` and `grid.py`.
- Reuse existing fail-closed conventions (no pane / no marker on an unresolvable target) and the existing machine coordination dir + `tryAcquireCoordLock`; no new lock mechanism.
- herdr CLI output shape varies (`pane_id`/`paneId`, nested `result`) — parsers tolerate variants and log raw output on parse failure (existing convention).

## Existing state

- **C0 (`WL-0MTR01EU7005SYZG`, completed)** — `dispatcher-anchor.ts` provisions one `Dispatcher` workspace + anchor pane (`downtime-dispatch-anchor.json`); `dispatchClaimedTier` forwards its pane id as `anchorId`.
- **C1 (`WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC`, open, `plan_complete`; audit rejected: "We are not getting per project tabs")** — `getDispatcherTabAnchor()` routes `<PREFIX>` to a tab inside the `Dispatcher` workspace (`downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json`).
- **Live state (this host):** `Dispatcher` workspace `w34` holds prefix tabs `WL`, `AH`, `SA`, `CG`, `OSL`; each project's workspace hosts a plugin pane labelled `Work Items` (e.g. `w2V:pB` → `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD=/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`, `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID=w2V`, `HERDR_TAB_ID=w2V:t4`; `w2Y:pW` → `.../Tableau-Card-Engine`, `w2Y`). The plugin pane's reported `cwd` is the plugin directory, so resolution must use `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`.
- **Duplicate/related item:** `WL-0MU321YK70035AYT` "Downtime dispatcher should dispatch into project workspace" (open, `idea`, `needsProducerReview=true`) states the same intent and already has a full brief with the same OPEN QUESTIONS. See Appendix Q1.
- **Prior art:** `packages/herdr/scripts/open.sh` / `open-podcast-editor-tab.sh` already read `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` from a plugin pane's shell process.

## Desired change

1. Add a project-workspace resolver (in `dispatcher-anchor.ts` or a sibling module) that, given worklog root `R`, returns the plugin pane's anchor `{ paneId, workspaceId, tabId } | null` by enumerating `herdr pane list`, filtering plugin panes (`label == "Work Items"`), reading each pane's `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` via `process-info` + `/proc/<shell_pid>/environ`, and matching `R`.
2. Wire it into `dispatchClaimedTier` (replacing `getDispatcherTabAnchor` / `getDispatcherAnchor` on the worklog path) and `dispatchScheduledPrompt`; forward the pane id as `anchorId`.
3. Retire per-prefix tab routing from the worklog dispatch path (stop reading/writing `downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json`; fate of the `Dispatcher` anchor per Q2).
4. Add tests and update `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts` — new project-workspace/plugin-pane resolver; retire per-prefix tab provisioning/persistence.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchClaimedTier` / `dispatchScheduledPrompt` anchor resolution; dep type changes.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `createDowntimeDeps` / resolver wiring.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` — resolution + integration tests; remove/adjust per-prefix tests.
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh`, `packages/herdr/shared/grid.py` — no behavioural change expected (verify).
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` — replace C0/C1 placement sections.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: no plugin pane open for a project** → dispatcher cannot resolve a target. Assumption (recommended): fail-closed (no dispatch this cycle), never a wrong-project fallback; fallback policy is OPEN QUESTION Q2.
- **Risk: multiple plugin panes for one root** → ambiguous. Assumption: choose deterministically (first matching pane id) and fail-closed on ambiguity; confirm during implementation.
- **Risk: `/proc` env read is Linux-specific** — same mechanism already used by `open.sh`; non-Linux → fail-closed.
- **Risk: splitting the plugin pane shrinks the worklist / disturbs layout** — `grid.py` rebalance mitigates; alternative placements are OPEN QUESTION Q3.
- **Risk: scope creep** — `WL-0MU2EOHK900425VU` (Dispatcher workspace useless pane) and leftover `Dispatcher` workspaces are adjacent cleanup; out of scope unless Q2 chooses removal.
- **Assumption:** plugin panes are identifiable by `label == "Work Items"` and carry `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` / `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` in the shell process environment (verified live).
- **Assumption:** scheduled prompts use the same resolver (their `cwd` is the project worklog root).
- **Scope-creep guard:** out of scope — changing selection/ranking, the audit freshness gate, or the coordination/leader model.

## Related work

- **WL-0MU321YK70035AYT — "Downtime dispatcher should dispatch into project workspace"** (open, `idea`, high, `needsProducerReview`) — **duplicate of this item**; same intent, same target design, existing brief + open questions. Reconciliation is Appendix Q1.
- **WL-0MTR01EU7005SYZG — C0 anchor-by-ID into dedicated Dispatcher workspace** (completed) — the design this item reverses.
- **WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC — per-project tabs in Dispatcher workspace** (open, `plan_complete`; audit rejected) — the C1 work this item retires.
- **WL-0MTRBOU0Y002M2CX — "Downtime dispatches land in Podcast workspace instead of Dispatcher workspace"** (completed) — incident that motivated the Dispatcher anchor; context for moving placement back deliberately.
- **WL-0MU2EOHK900425VU — "dispatcher workspace has useless pane"** (open, `intake_complete`) — adjacent cleanup; likely moot if the Dispatcher workspace is retired.
- **WL-0MU2LF6SZ000JQYI / WL-0MU2LFHBH004VF48** (completed) — C1 per-prefix provisioning and integration tests to be retired.
- **`packages/herdr/scripts/open.sh`** — prior art for reading `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` from a plugin pane's shell process.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MLSHA2FE0T8RR8X** – Implement multi-directory plugin discovery with precedence (completed)
- **WL-0MP15J7DR000KDDG** – TUI: Docs & developer guide (completed)
- **WL-0MLC7I1V31X2NCIV** – Enable workflow_dispatch for CI (completed)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### OPEN QUESTION Q1 — duplicate item reconciliation (BLOCKING)

- Q: "`WL-0MU321YK70035AYT` ("Downtime dispatcher should dispatch into project workspace", open/`idea`/high, `needsProducerReview`) describes the same change and already carries a full intake brief with these same open questions. Both items cannot be implemented independently. How should we reconcile them? Options: (a) keep `WL-0MU321YK70035AYT` canonical and close `WL-0MU7JZE04008VKP0` as a duplicate; (b) keep `WL-0MU7JZE04008VKP0` canonical and close the other; (c) make one a child of the other; (d) implement both separately." — **Status: OPEN QUESTION** (awaiting producer). Party asked: producer/operator. Evidence: identical intent; `WL-0MU321YK70035AYT` comment 2026-09-27T21:47:32Z already asked this exact question.
  **Recommended:** (a) keep `WL-0MU321YK70035AYT` canonical and close `WL-0MU7JZE04008VKP0` as a duplicate — the sister brief is more complete and is already flagged for review.

### OPEN QUESTION Q2 — fallback when no plugin pane exists for the item's project

- Q: "When a candidate's worklog root `R` has no live herdr plugin pane, what should the dispatcher do? Options: (a) fail-closed — no dispatch this cycle; (b) fall back to the existing `Dispatcher` workspace anchor; (c) fall back to the leader's current pane; (d) skip this candidate and continue." — **Status: OPEN QUESTION** (awaiting producer; already asked on `WL-0MU321YK70035AYT`). Evidence: current code fails closed on `anchor-unavailable`; the 2026-09 31 h zero-dispatch incident shows fail-closed can starve work.

Options: (a) split the project's plugin/worklist pane — same tab as the Worklog pane; (b) open a new tab in the project workspace; (c) split the project's terminal pane; (d) provision a dedicated anchor pane per project workspace." — **Status: OPEN QUESTION** (awaiting producer; already asked on `WL-0MU321YK70035AYT`). # Problem statement

The `a-r` (audit reject) chord in herdr fails with `bash: -c: unexpected EOF while looking for matching '`'` when the user-entered rejection reason contains an apostrophe. The `substituteIdentifiers` function in `form-dialog.ts` performs raw string replacement, inserting user text into a shell command template where the placeholder sits inside single quotes — an unescaped apostrophe terminates the quote early.

## Headline

Fix `a-r` audit reject shortcut to properly shell-escape user-entered reason text, preventing bash parsing errors when the reason contains apostrophes or other shell metacharacters.

## Users

- **Primary**: Operators who reject audited work items via `a-r` and need to explain why.
- **Secondary**: Any user running chord commands with user-provided text.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `a-r` shortcut handles reason text containing apostrophes, double quotes, dollar signs, backticks, and other shell metacharacters without breaking.
2. The audit-set summary is correctly persisted with the full reason text, verbatim.
3. All other chord commands (a-y approve, producer review, update, search, note-edit, prompt) continue to handle valid input unchanged.
4. Regression tests verify shell metacharacter safety for user-provided shortcut values.
5. All existing herdr tests pass.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts` — `substituteIdentifiers` does raw replacement; needs shell-escaping
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — `a-r` command template embeds `<reason>` in single quotes
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — form dialog dispatches the substituted command
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `buildRunInPaneArgs` / `run-in-pane.sh` execution path

## Constraints

- Fix must not change the `a-r` chord key binding or its visible behaviour (form dialog, pane, confirmation).
- The fix should be scoped to `substituteIdentifiers` in `form-dialog.ts`; avoid changes to `wl` CLI unless necessary.
- Must work cross-platform (Linux, macOS, Windows).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk**: Escaping strategy must cover all shell metacharacters (quotes, backticks, `$()`, `|`, `&`, `;`, `\`, newlines). **Mitigation**: use `printf '%q'` or equivalent well-tested escaping; test with comprehensive metacharacter set.
- **Risk**: Other shortcuts with user-provided identifiers (`<producer_comment>`, `<search_term>`, `<status>`, `<stage>`, `<title>`, `<description>`, `<prompt>`, `<note_text>`) likely share the same vulnerability. **Mitigation**: document as a follow-up; scope this item to `a-r` only.
- **Risk**: Changing the escaping strategy may require updating all shortcut templates to remove pre-existing quotes. **Mitigation**: if template changes are needed, apply consistently across all shortcuts in this item.
- **Risk**: Choosing a file-based approach (`--summary-file`) for `wl audit-set` adds complexity. **Mitigation**: prefer shell-escaping of the substituted value as the minimal fix; defer file-based approach to follow-up.
- **Risk**: `printf '%q'` output may differ between bash and zsh. **Mitigation**: test on the two most common shells; use `printf '%q'` which is POSIX-compatible in practice.
- **Assumption**: The `a-r` chord is the only shortcut currently reported as broken by metacharacters in user input.
- **Assumption**: `wl audit-set --summary` correctly accepts arbitrary text when properly quoted by the shell.
- **Scope-creep risk**: Fixing all shortcuts at once would be a larger feature. Record as a linked discovery item rather than expanding scope.

## Related work

- WL-0MP082Y1Q003GCUM — Audit internal shell command construction for proper escaping of user text (Worklog src/ only, not herdr)
- WL-0MOZUVGL6008QV45 — Prevent shell command substitution in wl audit text updates (added --audit-file, but herdr shortcut path still uses --summary in shell)
- WL-0MRSGMTYU009OZCF — Add --audit-file to wl audit-set (completed, but --summary-file not added)

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQOIBTHR002VMEK** – Add Guardrails to Protect Worklog Data Integrity (completed)
- **WL-0MQDUOK9K002QHJU** – Stage-based shortcut condition filters (completed)
- **WL-0MQDR5JBV0054CBY** – End-to-end test for detail view shortcut result handling (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — relevant to shell command execution and pane handling
- `CLI.md` — documents shortcut chords and `a-r` command
- `CHANGELOG.md` — tracks shortcut chord history

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What error occurs when reason text contains an apostrophe?" — Answer (user): `bash: -c: line 1: unexpected EOF while looking for matching '`'`. The shell command fails to parse because the apostrophe in the reason text terminates the single-quoted string early. Source: user report. Final: confirmed.
- Q: "Is this the only shortcut affected by this class of bug?" — Answer: Not known yet; other shortcuts with user-provided identifiers (`<producer_comment>`, `<search_term>`, `<title>`, etc.) may have the same vulnerability but have not been reported. Source: code review. Final: likely, but scope this item to `a-r` only.
- Q: "Should we add a --summary-file to wl audit-set instead of shell-escaping?" — Answer: Shell-escaping is the minimal fix; file-based handoff adds complexity and is deferred to follow-up. Source: prior work WL-0MOZUVGL6008QV45 established file-based handoff as the preferred long-term pattern; this item is scoped to the quickest path to fixing the reported bug. Final: shell-escaping for this item.

# RCA: downtime dispatcher sends nothing in cheap mode despite 2–3 idle slots

## Symptom

In cheap mode the local llama-proxy reports 3 slots with 2–3 idle for extended periods, yet the
herdr downtime dispatcher produces no dispatches. Observed in the window immediately before the
proxy was switched to fast mode (2026-09-19 ~00:13Z).

## Evidence (llama-proxy status log, proxy clock = UTC+1)

Source: `GET http://192.168.0.199:8000/logs/tail?source=proxy&lines=100000` (log file starts at
proxy 00:00 = UTC 23:00 on 2026-09-18).

- Window proxy 01:01–01:12 = **UTC 00:01–00:12**: `mode=cheap`, `total_slots=3`,
  `available_slots=2` (constant — 2 slots idle), and **zero** dispatches in
  `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`.
- `local_owner_session_id = ["http://localhost:8080","herdr-1789775322-722064-10708"]` — the owner
  is a **dispatched downtime pane** (`Downtime triggered implement … CG-0MTIOLY2A0092OT1`), whose
  local dispatch lease ran 836s → 0 across the window (`local_active_query=true` throughout).
- Across the whole UTC 23:00–04:11 log: **56%** of status samples had ≥2 idle slots **and** an
  active lease; **10%** had all slots idle **and** an active lease.

## Root cause

`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `tick()`:

```ts
const ownerLeaseHeld = /* local_owner_session_id string OR local_owner_lease_remaining_seconds > 0 */;
const slotOwned = ownerLeaseHeld && (runningPanes ?? 0) > 0;
const contentionQueueDepth = ...;
if (slotOwned) return { polled: true, dispatched: false, idle: true };
if (contentionQueueDepth > 0) return { polled: true, dispatched: false, idle: true };
```

This gate runs **before** the coordination file is read, is **machine-wide**, and has **no per-slot
branch** — it fires even in per-slot mode (`requiredFreeSlots=1 < total=3`). While any dispatched
agent is alive and holds the shared local-dispatch lease, the dispatcher refuses to dispatch at
all, leaving the remaining unowned free slots unused. In cheap mode a single long-running agent
therefore monopolises the dispatcher's permission for the whole generation (adaptive lease up to
`local_dispatch_lease_max_seconds`, default 1500s; observed 840s).

The code comment claims the gate is only a single-slot (count-based) fallback superseded by per-slot
identity, and that leases expire in ~180s. Both assumptions are false for this deployment.

## Contributing causes

1. **Owner-signal schema drift** — the proxy serves `local_owner_session_id` as a JSON **array**;
   `parseLlamaStatus` expects a **string** and silently drops it, so the worker cannot identify the
   owning slot/session and falls back to `lease_remaining > 0`.
2. **No queue-depth signal** — `contention_queue_depth` is not served in this configuration.
3. **Header vs proxy UI disagree** — the herdr header only shows idle when *all* slots are idle,
   while the proxy UI shows `available_slots`; "idle slots but no dispatches" is invisible in herdr.
4. **Scheduler targets the affected window** — the mode scheduler is `[('01:00','cheap'),('10:00','fast')]`,
   so the overnight window is precisely the one this gate wastes.

## Goal

Restore cheap-mode overnight throughput by removing the machine-wide dispatch block, aligning the
owner-lease contract, and making the gate decision observable.

## Acceptance criteria

1. In cheap mode with ≥1 unowned free slot, a dispatched agent holding a lease no longer prevents
   dispatch (measured: dispatches resume during agent runs).
2. The proxy owner-lease payload is parsed without silent data loss and covered by a contract test.
3. The dispatcher records *why* it did not dispatch (`slotOwned` / `contention` / `no-candidate` /
   `review-queue-hold` / `code-freeze`) to `downtime-coordination.log` and the header.
4. The lease-TTL assumption in `downtime-worker.ts` matches the proxy's adaptive-lease behaviour.

## Related work items

Children cover each fix; see the child items of this RCA.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MTF4A4V90055K7P** – Zombie dual-instance regression test (integration) (completed)
- **WL-0MTBOXEGR009KDP6** – Client-side compaction response to llm-proxy compaction gate (cheap hard-cap 4xx) (completed)
- **WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K** – Herdr to consume local LLM in downtime (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `package/packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: acceptance, active, affected, agent, alive (+160 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: acceptance, active, affected, agent, alive (+160 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: active, agent, alive, available, back (+135 more)
## Plan: changelog

# Make the downtime owner-lease gate per-slot

Parent RCA: WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28.

## Goal

In cheap mode (3 slots) the downtime dispatcher must keep dispatching into **unowned free slots**
even while another dispatched agent holds the shared local-dispatch lease. Today it dispatches
nothing for the whole duration of any agent run, wasting 2–3 slots.

## Problem

`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `tick()` applies a **machine-wide** gate before reading the
coordination file:

```ts
const ownerLeaseHeld = /* local_owner_session_id string OR local_owner_lease_remaining_seconds > 0 */;
const slotOwned = ownerLeaseHeld && (runningPanes ?? 0) > 0;
if (slotOwned) return { polled: true, dispatched: false, idle: true };
```

There is no per-slot branch — it fires even when `requiredFreeSlots < total_slots` (per-slot mode).
So a single working agent that holds a lease blocks all dispatch, despite `countFreeUnownedSlots`
reporting free slots. Evidence: proxy UTC 00:01–00:12, cheap mode, `total_slots=3`,
`available_slots=2`, lease held by a dispatched pane, **zero dispatches**.

The gate's comment claims it is only the count-based (single-slot) fallback and is superseded by
per-slot identity. That is not what the code does.

## Required behaviour

- Detect per-slot mode from the status (`Array.isArray(status.slots)` and a usable slot array).
- In per-slot mode, allow dispatch while `countFreeUnownedSlots(status.slots) >= <tier minimum>`;
  the global owner lease must not block dispatch into free unowned slots.
- Keep the conservative gate only for the count-based (single-slot / no per-slot data) path, so a
  truly owned sole slot is still protected.
- Never dispatch into a slot whose per-slot `owner_session_id` is set.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Unit test: per-slot status with 3 slots, 1 owned/busy and 2 free unowned, a held global lease,
   and `runningPanes > 0` → dispatch **proceeds** (regression test for this RCA).
2. Unit test: count-based status (no `slots`), `local_lease_active`/owner held, `runningPanes > 0`
   → dispatch is **refused** (single-slot protection preserved).
3. Unit test: per-slot status where every slot is owned → dispatch refused.
4. Audit-tier minimum (`DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2`) is evaluated against the per-slot
   unowned-free count.
5. Integration/manual evidence: in cheap mode, dispatches are observed in `downtime-dispatches.log`
   while a previously dispatched agent is still `working`.

## Notes

- `countFreeUnownedSlots` and `isSlotOwned` already exist and exclude owned slots.
- Do not weaken the single-slot path: an owned sole slot must still block.
data.title: Downtime dispatcher: owner-lease gate must be per-slot (slotOwned blocks dispatch despite free slots)

# parseLlamaStatus: accept the proxy's array local_owner_session_id (+ per-slot owner contract test)

Parent RCA: WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28.

## Goal

Stop silently dropping the proxy's local-owner signal so the dispatcher can reason about ownership
per slot instead of falling back to `lease_remaining > 0`.

## Problem

The llama-proxy now serves `local_owner_session_id` as a JSON **array**, e.g.:

```json
"local_owner_session_id": ["http://localhost:8080", "herdr-1789775322-722064-10708"],
"local_owner_lease_remaining_seconds": 29.99
```

`parseLlamaStatus` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:838`) accepts only a **string**:

```ts
local_owner_session_id: typeof o.local_owner_session_id === 'string' ? o.local_owner_session_id : undefined,
```

The array is dropped → `ownerLeaseHeld`'s string clause is dead code, and the worker cannot tell
which session (or slot) holds the lease. This blocks the per-slot fix (WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28 child).

## Required behaviour

- Parse both shapes: legacy string and the current array. Normalise to a stable internal form
  (e.g. `local_owner_session_ids: string[]`) while keeping the legacy `string` field for
  compatibility with existing call sites.
- Fail-closed on an unparseable owner value (treat as ambiguous → busy), consistent with the rest
  of the parser.
- Keep per-slot `owner_session_id` parsing as-is (already string|null).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Unit test: legacy payload (`local_owner_session_id` string) parses and preserves the owner.
2. Unit test: current payload (2-element array) parses; the owner session is recovered (not
   `undefined`) and the URL element is ignored/handled deterministically.
3. Unit test: malformed owner (number/object/empty array) → fail-closed (busy / undefined), no throw.
4. A contract test pins the exact array shape observed from the live proxy
   (`["http://localhost:8080", "<session-id>"]`).
5. `fetchLocalStatus` never throws on either shape (poller result is a valid `LlamaStatus` or null).

## Notes

- Capture the fixture from `GET /llama/local/status`; the array shape was observed on
  2026-09-19 with proxy mode `cheap`, `total_slots=3`.
data.title: Herdr parseLlamaStatus: accept array local_owner_session_id from llama-proxy (+ per-slot owner contract test)

# Log the dispatcher's actual no-dispatch reason (make gate decisions observable)

Parent RCA: WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28.

## Goal

Make it possible to diagnose "idle slots but no dispatches" from the logs alone. This RCA took hours
because the gate decision was invisible: the only persisted outcomes are successful dispatches and
3-strike errors.

## Problem

`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `tick()` returns neutral outcomes for several blockers
without recording *why*:

- `slotOwned` → `{ polled: true, dispatched: false, idle: true }` (no log)
- `contentionQueueDepth > 0` → same (no log)
- `no-candidate` / `review-queue-hold` / `code-freeze` / `fresh-audit-skip` / `audit-in-flight`
- the idle-duration gate not yet met (`polled: true, idle: true`)

The herdr header only distinguishes dispatching / off / paused / idle / busy, and idle only shows
when *all* slots are idle (per-slot tracker). There is no record of `slotOwned` blocking dispatch,
so the proxy UI shows idle slots while the dispatcher is refusing.

## Required behaviour

- On each tick that polls and does not dispatch, append a structured entry to
  `.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` (or a dedicated decision log) with: outcome reason, free
  slot count / total slots, owner present, `runningPanes`, contention depth, and tick timestamp.
- Rate-limit / de-duplicate so a healthy idle loop does not flood the log (e.g. log on reason
  change or at most once per N minutes per instance).
- Surface the current blocking reason in the worklist header (extend `renderDowntimeStatus`, e.g.
  `[downtime held: slot-owner]`) without changing the existing state labels.
- Do not log on every 10s tick while genuinely idle-and-eligible (no candidate vs gate-blocked are
  distinct): only record actionable refusals.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A tick refused by `slotOwned` writes one decision log line containing the reason and the
   observed slot/owner fields.
2. A tick refused by `contentionQueueDepth > 0` writes the reason and depth.
3. Repeated identical refusals are rate-limited (bounded lines per hour) — asserted by test.
4. The header shows the active blocking reason distinct from plain `idle`/`busy`.
5. Existing dispatch/error log schemas are unchanged (additive only); all consumers/tests updated.
data.title: Downtime dispatcher: log the actual no-dispatch reason (slotOwned/contention/no-candidate) + header

# Re-verify the local dispatch-lease TTL assumption; exclude leases held by our own panes

Parent RCA: WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28.

## Goal

Align the dispatcher's owner-lease model with what the proxy actually does, so the gate is neither
over- nor under-conservative.

## Problem

`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` documents and relies on the assumption that local proxy
leases "expire ~180 s after activity stops". Observation from the live proxy contradicts this:
during UTC 00:01–00:12 a dispatched pane's lease was `local_owner_lease_remaining_seconds`
**836 → 0** (≈840 s), i.e. an order of magnitude longer than the code assumes. The proxy
(`llm-manager` `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`) computes an **adaptive** lease with
`local_dispatch_lease_max_seconds` defaulting to 1500 s, plus chunk/prefill refresh buffers. So a
long agent generation holds the lease for its whole run.

Consequence: any gate keyed on "lease held" blocks for the entire generation, not ~3 minutes.
This amplifies the `slotOwned` defect (the per-slot fix is the primary remedy; this item removes the
stale assumption and the self-blocking case).

## Required behaviour

- Re-read the proxy lease semantics (static + adaptive + refresh buffers) and document the real
  bounds in `downtime-worker.ts`, replacing the "~180 s" claim.
- If the dispatcher spawns a pane, it knows that pane's session id; a lease held by one of the
  dispatcher's own live panes must not be treated as "someone else owns the target slot"
  (it already owns its slot, not the free ones).
- Keep fail-closed behaviour when the proxy serves no lease information.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The lease-TTL comment/constant in `downtime-worker.ts` reflects the proxy's actual maximum
   (adaptive lease max), with a unit test bounding the waited-out/refusal behaviour.
2. A lease attributable to a dispatcher-spawned pane does not block dispatch into other unowned
   free slots (test).
3. No regression: a lease held by an unknown/operator session on a count-based single-slot setup
   still blocks dispatch.
4. `docs/` (or the module header) records the proxy lease contract and the cross-repo dependency
   (`llm-manager`), so the assumption does not silently drift again.

## Notes

- Cross-repo: the lease implementation lives in `llm-manager` (`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`).
  If that repo changes the defaults, this item's constant must be revisited.
data.title: Downtime dispatcher: correct local dispatch-lease TTL assumption; do not block on leases held by own panes

# Wire `wl interview` into the `r-i` shortcut chord

## Problem statement

The `r-i` chord is documented as "walk through outstanding interview questions on the selected work item", and `shortcuts.json` already maps it to `!!wl interview <id>`. However, the command family is **not recognised by the worklist dispatcher** (`dispatchChordCommand`): it falls through to the generic callback rather than the explicit `!!wl` routes used by `reviewed`/`close`/`delete`/`update`/`search`, it is not treated as a data-modifying command (so the list does not refresh after answers are recorded), and no dispatch-path test covers it. This item is also largely superseded by the completed **WL-0MU95SGEB006HQAM**, which added the `r-i` entry.

## Users

- **Map** (agent operator): wants to press `r i` on an item that needs producer review and answer the outstanding clarifying questions in an interactive pane, without leaving the worklist.
  - User story: *As an agent operator, I press `r i` on an item in `in_review` so that `wl interview <id>` opens and I can answer the outstanding questions; when I finish, the list reflects that the item no longer needs producer review.*

## Acceptance Criteria (recommended scope — pending producer confirmation, see Open Questions)

1. The `r-i` chord resolves to `!!wl interview <id>` and the dispatcher recognises the `!!wl interview` family explicitly (it no longer relies solely on the generic fallback); pressing `r i` on a selected item routes `wl interview <id>` into a visible pane.
2. The interview command is treated as a data-modifying command for list-refresh purposes (alongside `close`/`delete`/`update`/`reviewed`/`search`) so the selection list reflects recorded answers / a cleared `needsProducerReview` flag after it completes.
3. At least one automated test asserts the dispatch path: the `r-i` entry resolves to the expected command **and** `dispatchChordCommand` recognises/routes `!!wl interview <id>` (including the resolved id), with `isWlModifyingCommand` covering `interview`. *(testing/validation criterion)*
4. The end-to-end behaviour inside a herdr pane is verified (interview prompts accept input) **or** the non-TTY limitation is explicitly documented if the pane cannot supply interactive stdin. *(validation criterion)*
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The canonical CLI form is `wl interview <id>` (see `CLI.md` §`interview`); `wl <id> interview` is **not** valid CLI syntax. The item title's ordering should be read as referring to the same command.
- The `r` key is already a prefix key (`r-p` Producer Review, `r-i` interview); do not reintroduce a single-key `r` binding.
- If the outcome is "duplicate", the correct action is to close WL-0MU90US3L002HEHF as superseded by WL-0MU95SGEB006HQAM — **no code change**.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — `r-i` entry present: `"command": "!!wl interview <id>"`, `"label": "interview"` (added by WL-0MU95SGEB006HQAM, commit `652ec575`).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `dispatchChordCommand` recognises `!!wl reviewed`, `!!wl (close|delete|update|search)`, and compound `&& wl audit-set`; `!!wl interview` is **not** matched. Probe result at intake time: `dispatchChordCommand('!!wl interview <id>')` → `false`; `executeResolvedCommand('!!wl interview <id>')` → `'callback'` with `onCommand('!!wl interview TEST-123', …)` (so it currently still opens a pane via the generic fallback).
- `isWlModifyingCommand` (`worklist.ts`) lists `close|delete|update|reviewed|search` only.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts` — asserts the `r-i` entry exists and resolves to `!!wl interview <id>`; no dispatch-path test.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — documents `r`, `i` → "Walk through outstanding interview questions … (`wl interview`)".
- `src/commands/interview.ts` — `wl interview <id>` walks the clarifying-questions appendix, persists answers per prompt, and clears `needsProducerReview` when all are answered. Requires interactive stdin.

## Desired change

*(Recommended, pending confirmation)*
- Add `!!wl interview` to the recognised `!!wl` family in `dispatchChordCommand` and to `isWlModifyingCommand` so the chord dispatches through the explicit route and the list refreshes after the interview.
- Add a dispatch-path test covering `r-i` → `!!wl interview <id>`.
- Document any pane/TTY limitation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — add `interview` to the recognised `!!wl` family (`dispatchChordCommand`) and to `isWlModifyingCommand`.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — dispatch-path test for `!!wl interview <id>`.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts` — existing `r-i` entry assertion (already present; extend if needed).
- `packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh` — only if pane TTY behaviour needs investigation/documented.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — shortcut documentation.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Duplicate risk (primary)**: WL-0MU95SGEB006HQAM already added the `r-i` entry, so this item may be fully superseded. Confirmation required before implementing.
- **Scope-creep risk**: Improving the interview command itself (question extraction, output formatting) is out of scope and is tracked separately (WL-0MUKCGV3X0030W6K, WL-0MUH765F1003FKRK, WL-0MUH7ACKJ0024VGF, WL-0MU64XHIZ004LFM1).
- **Assumption**: the generic fallback currently dispatches `!!wl interview` (verified at intake time), so the user-visible symptom is a missed immediate refresh rather than a dead chord — the exact remaining defect needs producer confirmation.
- **TTY risk**: `wl interview` requires interactive stdin; whether a herdr command-output pane supplies a TTY is unverified.

## Related work

- **WL-0MU95SGEB006HQAM** — Wire up interview command to shortcut chord (completed; added the `r-i` entry and shortcut-config tests). Likely the implementing item for this request.
- **WL-0MU55UDBJ008DJ67** — Interview replay feature (completed; added the `wl interview` command).

1. **OPEN QUESTION** — Q: This request appears already satisfied by the completed WL-0MU95SGEB006HQAM (which added `r-i` → `!!wl interview <id>`). Should this item be (a) closed as a duplicate/superseded, or (b) kept to harden the wiring (explicit `dispatchChordCommand` recognition + modifying-command refresh + dispatch test)? — Answer: *(awaiting producer)*. **Recommended:** (b) keep only if the missed-refresh/dispatch-recognition gap matters; otherwise (a) close as duplicate — the chord already exists and dispatches via the generic fallback.

# Wire up interview command to shortcut chord

## Problem statement

Herdr's `r` key is currently a single-key Producer Review shortcut. Convert it to a prefix key, adding `r-p` (Producer Review) and `r-i` (`wl interview`) as two-key chords — enabling a consistent `r`-prefix axis for work-item review workflows.

## Users

- **Map** (agent operator): Wants faster access to interview mode for work items with outstanding producer review questions, via a consistent `r` prefix axis alongside other work-item management chords (e.g. `a` for audit, `u` for update, `x` for close).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The `r` key is converted from a single-key shortcut to a prefix key with two children:
   - `r-p`: Runs Producer Review (the existing single-key command moved to chord)
   - `r-i`: Runs `wl interview <id>` to walk through outstanding interview questions on the selected work item
2. No existing shortcut functionality is lost — Producer Review still works via `r-p`.
3. The shortcut hints in the help line correctly display `r-p: Producer Review` and `r-i: interview` when `r` is pressed as a prefix.
4. All existing shortcut chords (audit `a-*`, update `u-*`, filter `f-*`, etc.) remain unaffected.

5. At least one automated test validates the new `r-p` and `r-i` chords (e.g. a `shortcut-config` unit test asserting both chords resolve to the expected commands).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- This is a configuration-only change in `shortcuts.json`; no code changes needed.
- The chord system already supports multi-key chords (e.g. `a,a`, `u,p,l`), so no changes to `shortcut-config.ts` are required.

## Existing state

- `shortcuts.json` entry for `r`: single-key chord running `!!wl reviewed <id> && wl comment add <id> --body '<producer_comment>' --author <author>` (Producer Review).
- The chord system in `shortcut-config.ts` already supports arbitrary-length chords and leader-key prefix lookups via `getChordByLeader()`.

## Desired change

- Replace the single-key `r` entry with two two-key entries:
  - `r-p`: `!!wl reviewed <id> && wl comment add <id> --body '<producer_comment>' --author <author>`
  - `r-i`: `!!wl interview <id>`
- Remove `r` as a single-key shortcut.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — chord registry; edit to replace `r` entry with `r-p` and `r-i` entries

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep risk**: This is narrowly scoped to shortcuts.json. Adding more `r`-prefix chords (e.g. `r-n` for intake, `r-s` for ship) are out of scope but could be follow-up work items.
- **Breaking change**: The `r` single-key shortcut is removed; users who relied on `r` for quick Producer Review must use `r-p` instead.
- **Assumption**: The chord system's prefix handling in `shortcut-config.ts` already works correctly when a single-key entry is replaced by two-key entries starting with the same key — no code changes needed.

## Related work

- WL-0MSHUMX5C004NC4O — Extensible shortcuts.json: bundled defaults + project-local overrides
- WL-0MSKV6SKK008MMXR — Herdr: add/remove/edit inline notes on any markdown document (adds `n-e` and `n-d` chords)

## Clarifying questions and answers

1. Q: Should `r` become a prefix only (removing single-key Producer Review), or use a different prefix key? — A: `r` becomes prefix only (option a). The work item description explicitly states "Make r a prefix key" and "r-p: Move the existing Producer Review command to r chord". Source: work item description + code inspection.
2. Q: Should the interview command be `!!wl interview <id>` (shell) or `/herdr:interview <id>` (agent command)? — A: `!!wl interview <id>`. The interview command is a `wl` subcommand, not a `/herdr:` agent command, so it must be a shell command. Source: `wl --help` inspection.
