# Pi processes should start in a work item tab (WL-0MUKZGEQ2007FECS)

**Headline**: Route every pane spawned by a worklist dispatch that carries a work-item ID — interactive pi agent panes (`send-to-pi.sh`) and shell/command-output panes (`run-in-pane.sh`) — into a tab labelled with the exact work-item ID in the invoking pane's **current workspace**, creating the tab on first use and reusing it thereafter (the new pane splits the item tab's root pane). Panes with no work-item association keep today's behaviour: split the current pane in the current tab.

## Problem statement

Interactive dispatches from the worklist selection list currently split the invoking pane, so the panes for one work item are scattered across whatever tab the user was in. The automated downtime dispatcher already co-locates its panes in a per-work-item-ID tab (WL-0MU321YK70035AYT / WL-0MUR5FUWD00024XN), but that item explicitly scoped out the manual/interactive flows. This item applies the same co-location to interactive dispatches so all work for a work item is grouped in one reusable tab.

## Users

- **Herdr operator dispatching work from the worklist**:
  > "As an operator, when I run `/skill:implement WL-…` (or any ID-carrying shortcut) from the worklist, I want the new pane to open in a tab named after that work item, so all my panes for that item are grouped together and easy to find."
- **Operator juggling several work items**:
  > "As an operator working several items, I want each item's panes in their own tab — created on first dispatch, reused afterwards — so I never have to hunt through mixed panes."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Item-ID tab for ID-carrying interactive agent dispatches** — when a worklist agent dispatch (`/skill:* <id>`, `/intake <id>`, `/plan <id>`, ID-carrying `/prompt:`) carries a work-item ID, the spawned pi pane's tab is labelled exactly `<itemId>` in the invoking pane's current workspace. Verified via `herdr tab list --workspace <ws>` (`label == <itemId>`) and `herdr pane list` (new pane's `tab_id` equals that tab's `tab_id`).
2. **Item-ID tab for ID-carrying shell/command-output panes** — the same placement applies to `run-in-pane.sh` panes for `!!`/`!` shortcuts and plain commands that carry a work-item ID.
3. **Reuse, never duplicate** — a second dispatch for the same item adds a pane to the existing item-ID tab; no duplicate tab is created for the same workspace + item ID. (Tab label is the key, discovered via `herdr tab list`.)
4. **No-ID panes unchanged** — panes with no work-item association (the unbound **Open Pi Agent** action, the `P n` blank-prompt session, generic/no-ID commands) still split the current pane in the current tab.
5. **Fail-open provisioning** — if the item-ID tab cannot be resolved or created, the dispatch falls back to the current-pane split (the user's dispatch is never blocked, and never lands in a wrong-project tab).
6. **Reuse existing machinery** — reuse `getItemTabAnchor` / `createDispatcherAnchorDeps` from `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts` (create-or-reuse under the coordination lock, CLI-shape tolerance, fail-closed parsing); `run-in-pane.sh` gains `--anchor <paneId>` support mirroring `send-to-pi.sh`; no new pane/tab mechanism is invented.
7. **Root-pane cleanup** — after the first pane spawns into a freshly created item tab, the tab's placeholder root pane is closed (fail-safe: only when liveness positively confirms it is not a live tracked pi/shell pane); a later dispatch reuses the surviving pane as the split anchor.
8. **Tests** — automated coverage (unit and/or integration) for: item-tab resolution on both channels, create-or-reuse (first creates, second reuses), no-ID fallback to the current pane, fail-open when tab provisioning fails, `--anchor` forwarding in `run-in-pane.sh`, and root-pane cleanup. Existing herdr tests remain green.
9. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
10. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Interactive path only.** The automated downtime path is already implemented (WL-0MU321YK70035AYT) and is unchanged.
- **Current workspace, not project-resolved workspace** (Q2): the item tab lives in the workspace of the invoking pane. The plugin process reads `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` from its environment (present in the plugin pane env); a fallback may resolve the invoking pane's workspace via the herdr CLI.
- **No focus stealing.** Item tabs are created with `--no-focus` and existing `--no-focus` dispatch defaults are preserved; the item tab must not grab focus.
- **Reuse, don't duplicate, the anchor machinery.** `getItemTabAnchor` already keys tabs by exact label and fails closed on unparseable CLI output; extend/reuse it rather than adding a second mechanism.
- **Fail-open for interactive, fail-closed within provisioning.** Tab provisioning itself stays fail-closed (no wrong-tab placement), but an interactive dispatch must degrade to the current-tab split rather than be dropped.
- **CLI shape tolerance.** Any new parsing (e.g. `run-in-pane.sh --anchor` split output) tolerates the existing `pane_id`/`paneId`/`id` variants and nested `result` envelopes, logging raw output on parse failure.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` `onCommand`:
  - Agent route: `buildSendToPiArgs(command, targetCwd, model, paneIdFile, paneName, focus)` — passes `--cwd`, `--pane-name`, `--model`, `--pane-id-file`, focus flag, **no `--anchor`**.
  - Shell/plain routes: `buildRunInPaneArgs(clean, targetCwd, shellPaneName, focus)` — passes `--cwd`, `--pane-name`, focus flag, **no `--anchor`**.
  - `extractWorkItemId(command)` already derives the work-item ID for both routes.
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` **already supports `--anchor <paneId>`** (resize mode grows the grid around the anchor; no-resize splits `--pane <id>`).
- `packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh` **has no `--anchor`**: it always `herdr pane split --current`.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts` already provides `getItemTabAnchor(cwd, deps, workspaceId, itemId)` (label = key, coordination lock, double-check, fail-closed) and `createDispatcherAnchorDeps(cwd, herdrBin)`.
- `index.ts` already has `defaultItemTabAnchorResolver(cwd, workspaceId, itemId)` (module-private) used by the downtime deps.
- `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` is present in the plugin pane environment (verified: current session env carries `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID=w45`).
- Downtime placement (`downtime-worker.ts` `dispatchClaimedTier`) resolves the *project* workspace via `resolveProjectWorkspace` then uses `getItemTabAnchor`; the interactive path per Q2 uses the **current** workspace instead.

## Desired change

1. In `onCommand`, when `extractWorkItemId` returns an ID and a pane will be opened, resolve the item tab anchor once: `workspaceId = process.env.HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` (fallback: resolve from the invoking pane), then `getItemTabAnchor(targetCwd, deps, workspaceId, itemId)`.
2. Forward that anchor to both channels: `buildSendToPiArgs(..., anchor)` → `send-to-pi.sh --anchor <paneId>` (already supported), and `buildRunInPaneArgs(..., anchor)` → a new `run-in-pane.sh --anchor <paneId>` (split that pane instead of `--current`).
3. When resolution fails or no ID is present, omit `--anchor` (current-pane behaviour) — fail-open.
4. Add `--anchor` support to `run-in-pane.sh`, mirroring `send-to-pi.sh`'s semantics (resize and no-resize modes), with the existing CLI-shape tolerance.
5. After a pane spawns into a freshly created item tab, close the placeholder root pane using a fail-safe liveness check (only close when the anchor is confirmed not to be a live tracked pi/shell pane); reuse the same convention as the downtime root-pane cleanup (WL-0MU2EOHK900425VU).
6. Add tests and update `packages/herdr/README.md` (+ the relevant docs section) to describe the interactive item-ID-tab placement and its fallbacks.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `onCommand` item-tab resolution for agent and shell routes; `buildSendToPiArgs` / `buildRunInPaneArgs` gain an optional anchor parameter; current-workspace resolution (`HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`); fail-open fallback; post-spawn root-pane cleanup.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh` — add `--anchor <paneId>` (split that pane instead of `--current`), mirroring `send-to-pi.sh`, with tolerant `pane_id` parsing.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/send-to-pi.sh` — no behavioural change expected; verify `--anchor` forwarding (already present).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts` — reuse `getItemTabAnchor` / `createDispatcherAnchorDeps`; possibly expose a "created" signal or a shared root-pane cleanup helper for the interactive path.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` — item-tab resolution and `--anchor` forwarding tests for both channels; no-ID fallback; fail-open.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/tests/test_run_in_pane.sh` — `--anchor` argument/behaviour tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts` / a new integration test — create-or-reuse for the interactive flow.
- `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (or a sibling doc) — document interactive item-ID-tab placement, current-workspace choice, fail-open fallback, and root-pane cleanup.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (Q2a): the item tab lives in the invoking pane's current workspace.** Interactive dispatch originates in the worklist pane (already in the project workspace), so no `/proc`-based project resolution is needed; this keeps the interactive path cheap and predictable. (Contrasts with the downtime path, which may run from a different workspace/root.)
- **Assumption (fail-open):** if the item tab cannot be provisioned, the interactive dispatch falls back to the current-pane split rather than being dropped — a bad UX would be worse than the status quo. The downtime path remains fail-closed for its automated dispatch.
- **Risk: root-pane cleanup closing a live pane.** The anchor may be a reused live pi pane (existing item tab) rather than a fresh placeholder. Cleanup must close the anchor only when liveness positively confirms it is not a live tracked pane (same fail-safe convention as WL-0MU2EOHK900425VU); when liveness is unknown, leave it open.
- **Risk: tab-label collision with an operator-created tab.** An operator tab already named exactly `<itemId>` in the workspace is reused (intended), meaning the dispatcher may add a pane to an operator's tab; `--no-focus` prevents focus stealing.
- **Risk: concurrent dispatches for the same new item** may both try to create the tab. `getItemTabAnchor` already uses the coordination lock with a double-check; no new lock mechanism.
- **Risk: workspace-id drift.** If `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` is absent in some launch contexts, resolution must fall back to reading the invoking pane's workspace, else fail-open to the current pane.
- **Scope-creep guard:** out of scope — changing the downtime placement path, shell-pane behaviour that carries no ID, pane-title/agent-tracker changes, and selection/ranking. Extra opportunities discovered during implementation are recorded as linked work items, not absorbed here.

## Related work

- **WL-0MU321YK70035AYT — "Downtime dispatcher should dispatch into project workspace"** (completed, shipped v1.0.18) — built `resolveProjectWorkspace` + `getItemTabAnchor` (create-or-reuse item-ID tabs, coordination lock, fail-closed parsing) for **automated** downtime dispatch and explicitly scoped out manual flows. This item is the manual/interactive counterpart.
- **WL-0MUR5FUWD00024XN — "Downtime dispatcher → project workspace: root-pane cleanup"** (completed) — the fail-safe placeholder root-pane cleanup this item mirrors for interactive tabs.
- **WL-0MU7JZE04008VKP0 — "Dispatched panes should go under the project workspace"** (closed as duplicate of WL-0MU321YK70035AYT).
- **WL-0MU2EOHK900425VU — "dispatcher workspace has useless pane"** (completed) — root-pane cleanup precedent.
- **WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC — "Downtime dispatcher: per-project tabs in Dispatcher workspace"** (completed) — earlier per-prefix tab routing, superseded.
- **WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y — pane-title builders** (`pane-title.ts`) — pane naming convention shared by manual and downtime spawn paths; unchanged, but adjacent.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts`, `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh`, `packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh`, `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Q1 — scope of "new pi process" launch paths (RESOLVED)

- Q: "Which 'new pi process' launch paths should place the pane in a work-item-ID tab? Options: (a) interactive worklist agent dispatch only (`send-to-pi.sh` from the selection list `onCommand` for ID-carrying commands); (b) also apply to shell/command-output panes (`run-in-pane.sh`) carrying an item ID; (c) re-scope — the downtime path already covers it; reassess/close this item." — **Answer (producer): (b) — also apply to shell/command-output panes (`run-in-pane.sh`) carrying an item ID.** Source: interactive reply. Implication: scope = interactive pi agent panes **and** shell/command-output panes whenever a work-item ID is present; non-ID panes unchanged.

### Q2 — workspace that hosts the item tab (RESOLVED)

- Q: "Which workspace hosts the item tab? Options: (a) the invoking pane's current workspace (where the shortcut was pressed); (b) the resolved project workspace for the item's worklog root (`resolveProjectWorkspace`, as the downtime path does)." — **Answer (producer): (a) the invoking pane's current workspace.** Source: interactive reply. Implication: use `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` (with an invoking-pane fallback); no `/proc`-based project resolution on the interactive path.

### Q3 — item-tab contents / placeholder root pane (RESOLVED)

- Q: "When creating a new item tab, herdr provisions a placeholder root pane used as the split anchor. After the pane spawns, should the placeholder be closed? Options: (a) close the placeholder root pane (same fail-safe cleanup as the downtime path); (b) leave the placeholder in place." — **Answer (producer): (a) close the placeholder root pane.** Source: interactive reply. Implication: mirror the downtime root-pane cleanup, fail-safe (only close when the anchor is confirmed not to be a live tracked pane).

### Resolved by research (not producer questions)

- Q: "Does the interactive path already create item-ID tabs?" — Answer (research): no. `onCommand` builds `buildSendToPiArgs`/`buildRunInPaneArgs` with `--cwd`/`--pane-name`/focus flags but no `--anchor`, so panes split the current pane. Evidence: `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` (`onCommand`, lines ~2056–2130).
- Q: "Is the item-ID-tab machinery available to reuse?" — Answer (research): yes — `getItemTabAnchor(cwd, deps, workspaceId, itemId)` and `createDispatcherAnchorDeps(cwd, herdrBin)` in `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts`, plus a module-private `defaultItemTabAnchorResolver(cwd, workspaceId, itemId)` in `index.ts`. Evidence: source inspection.
- Q: "Does `run-in-pane.sh` support an anchor?" — Answer (research): no — it always runs `herdr pane split --current`; `send-to-pi.sh` already supports `--anchor <paneId>`. Evidence: `packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh`, `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh`.
- Q: "Is the current workspace id available to the plugin process?" — Answer (research): yes — the plugin pane environment carries `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` (verified live in this session: `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID=w45`, `HERDR_PANE_ID=w45:p13`).

# Herdr: Drain sessions before switching to cheap mode

> When the herdr extension chooses to switch the proxy to cheap mode due to
> inactivity, it first waits until the active session count falls to the number
> of slots available in cheap mode. No new work items are dispatched until this
> requirement is met and the proxy has been switched to cheap. If an interactive
> command is given while draining, the switch is cancelled and the time is reset.
> The inactive time is set to 15 minutes.

## Problem statement

When the herdr mode-switch worker detects operator inactivity, it switches the
llama-proxy from fast (3-slot cloud-backed pool) to cheap (2-slot local-first
pool) mode. Currently this switch happens immediately once the idle threshold
is met and the proxy reports idle. This can interrupt in-flight operator work
that happens to be using a slot at the moment of the switch, and it can allow
more active sessions than the cheap pool can sustain (up to 3 in fast mode,
only 2 in cheap).

## Users

- **Operator running the herdr worklog plugin + llama-proxy** -- wants the proxy
  to drop to cheap mode based on their absence, but only after active work has
  naturally subsided to fit within the cheap pool.

User story:

- *As an operator, when I stop issuing agent-route commands through the herdr
  plugin for the idle window, I want the proxy to drain active sessions down to
  the cheap pool size before switching -- so I do not lose in-flight work and
  the cheap pool has capacity. If I return (issue a command), I want the process
  to cancel and reset.*

## Original acceptance criteria (drain plan — withdrawn)

- [ ] **Drain state:** when the idle threshold is met and the proxy reports
  idle, the mode-switch worker enters a **draining** state instead of switching
  immediately. It periodically checks whether the active session count (busy
  slots) has fallen to <= the cheap mode slot budget (2, i.e.
  `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS` free slots).
- [ ] **Dispatch pause during drain:** while in the draining state, the downtime
  dispatcher does **not** dispatch new work items. Existing in-flight work
  continues; the idle gate prevents new panes from spawning.
- [ ] **Drain completion:** once the proxy reports sufficient free slots (>= 2
  free), the drain ends and the proxy switches to cheap mode immediately.
- [ ] **Drain cancellation:** if an operator issues an agent-route command while
  draining, the drain is cancelled, the switch-to-cheap is abandoned, and the
  idle timer resets to "active now" (the proxy stays fast).
- [ ] **No redundant switching / no hammering:** skip when the persisted mode
  already matches the target; 409 treated as no-op; single-flight; at most one
  switch per state change.
- [ ] **Fail-closed everywhere:** endpoint failures, timeouts, and ambiguous
  payloads yield no switch; the worker stays in its current mode.
- [ ] **Idle threshold changed:** the default `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs` is
  changed from 60 minutes to 15 minutes.
- [ ] **Tests:** unit tests cover -- drain state entry/exit, dispatch pause,
  operator-command cancellation, threshold change, all existing fail-closed
  paths unchanged. Full project suite green.

## Constraints

- The cheap mode slot budget is 2 slots (`DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS`). The
  drain condition is `freeSlots >= 2`.
- Draining must not kill in-flight work -- it only prevents *new* dispatches.
- The fast direction (operator command --> mode=fast) is unaffected; only the
  cheap idle switch path changes.
- The existing idle-clock reset mechanism (`lastOperatorCommandAt`) is reused
  for drain cancellation.
- Fail-closed remains the safe default at every boundary.

## Existing state

- The mode-switch worker (`mode-switch-worker.ts`) already tracks operator
  activity, polls `/llama/local/status` for idle evaluation, and switches to
  cheap on idle.
- The downtime worker (`downtime-worker.ts`) already controls dispatch based on
  the idle gate (`evaluateIdle`).
- The cheap mode slot budget is `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2` (parent
  WL-0MT9F67Y3008S0PR).
- The default idle threshold is `DEFAULT_MODE_SWITCH_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS = 3_600_000`
  (60 minutes).

## Desired change

Add a **draining** sub-state to the mode-switch worker's idle-to-cheap path:

1. **Entry:** After the idle threshold is met and the proxy reports idle, enter
   the drain state instead of switching.
2. **Polling during drain:** Each tick, check whether `freeSlots >= 2`. If so,
   switch to cheap and exit drain. If not, continue draining.
3. **Dispatch signal:** While in drain state, signal to the downtime worker to
   pause new dispatches.
4. **Cancellation:** If `onOperatorCommand()` fires during drain, exit drain
   immediately, reset the idle clock, and keep the proxy in fast mode.
5. **Default threshold:** Change `DEFAULT_MODE_SWITCH_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS` from
   3,600,000ms (60 min) to 900,000ms (15 min).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts` -- Add draining state, drain logic,
  cancel on operator command, threshold constant change
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.test.ts` -- Drain state tests, cancel
  tests, dispatch-signal tests
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` -- Respect drain signal from mode-switch
  worker to pause dispatch
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` -- No change (threshold constant lives in
  mode-switch-worker, settings re-reads it per tick)

## Related work

- **WL-0MT9F67Y3008S0PR** -- Per-slot operator gate for cheap switch (completed)
- **WL-0MSN3FWV5008KQE9** -- Activity-gated proxy mode switching (completed)
- **WL-0MU6MXCZZ007ZXT9** -- Leader-only cheap switching (completed)
- **WL-0MU4MKVR4005WPBJ** -- Idle-trigger sources (completed)
- **WL-0MT1EE3S7005DJ1F** -- Tests: mode-switch worker core (completed)
- **WL-0MT1EEHQI002MOVT** -- Implement: mode-switch worker core (completed)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** Adding a drain state introduces a new state machine transition path.
  **Mitigation:** Keep the drain logic simple -- poll free-slots each tick,
  cancel on command. Reuse existing single-flight and fail-closed mechanisms.
- **Risk:** Race between operator command and slot freeing during drain. If both
  happen simultaneously, the operator command path takes priority -- the drain
  cancels and the idle clock resets, so the proxy stays fast. This is the
  correct user-facing behaviour.
- **Assumption:** The downtime worker can receive a signal from the mode-switch
  worker about the drain state. This is implemented via a callback on the
  mode-switch worker or a shared holder method (index.ts already uses the
  `modeSwitchHolder` pattern for the worker reference).
- **Assumption:** The "number of slots available in cheap mode" is the constant
  `DOWTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2`.
- **Assumption:** Process restart during drain is safe -- the idle clock already
  resets to "active now" on construction (fail-safe: proxy stays fast until a
  fresh full idle window passes).
- **Scope control:** Making the drain threshold configurable is a follow-up
  opportunity, not in scope for this work item.
- **Scope control:** No change to the fast-switch path (operator command -->
  mode=fast); only the cheap idle-switch path gains drain semantics.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

This intake was completed without additional questions -- the work item
description provided sufficient detail to draft a clear brief.

## Revision (2026-10-06): verification, intent, and decision

### Verification outcome

All five children reached a terminal stage and their commits are on `dev`
(`956237e6`, `2c3db331`, `386733c1`, `a22442d0`, `d9ea2100`); unit tests
(66 in `mode-switch-worker.test.ts`) and the drain-dispatch integration tests
(3) are green. The feature is nevertheless **broken in production and has
never once completed a drain**.

### Root causes (why it can never work as written)

1. **Slot model inverted.** The brief assumed fast = 3 slots and cheap = 2.
   The live proxy config is the reverse: fast = 1 slot (`config.yaml`,
   `session_slot_pool_size: 1`), cheap = 3 slots (`config-cheap.yaml`,
   `session_slot_pool_size: 3`; raised 2 -> 3 after this brief was written).
   So cheap has *more* capacity than fast, and there is nothing to shed.
2. **Budget borrowed from the wrong constant.** Drain completion requires
   `freeSlots >= MODE_SWITCH_DRAIN_FREE_SLOTS`, which was set to
   `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2`. That constant is the minimum free
   slots an *audit dispatch* needs (parent + Phase 2 child) -- not the cheap
   pool size. In a 1-slot fast pool `freeSlots` can never reach 2, and
   `isIdleStatus` returns false whenever `required > total_slots`, so
   `evaluateIdle(status, 2)` is permanently false.
   (`mode-switch-worker.ts:116,619`; `downtime-worker.ts:817-828`.)
3. **The drain is unbounded.** Unlike the server-side drain (capped at
   `MODE_SWITCH_DRAIN_MAX_SECONDS`), the client drain has no timeout -- only
   operator-command cancellation. Once entered it therefore latches:
   `getIsDraining()` stays true and the downtime dispatcher stops issuing new
   panes until an operator command arrives.

### Intent reconstruction -- the client drain is a *sibling* of the server-side drain

The proxy already carries a **bounded mode-switch drain**
(`LP-0MT631JKW008WAKE` / `LP-0MT60S55M000TK1H`). Both mechanisms have the same
shape: defer a mode transition, stop admitting **new** work during the
deferral, and let **in-flight** work finish without killing it.

| | Server-side (proxy) | Client-side (herdr plugin) |
|---|---|---|
| Armed by | `set_mode` (switch already requested) | idle window met + proxy idle |
| Defers | the proxy restart | the `POST /admin/set-mode cheap` |
| New work | chat requests get 503 + Retry-After | downtime dispatches paused (`drainPaused`) |
| Waits for | in-flight local streams | `freeSlots >= budget` |
| In-flight work | never killed | never killed |
| Bound | **bounded** (`MODE_SWITCH_DRAIN_MAX_SECONDS`, 90s) | **unbounded** -- operator command only |

The dispatch pause is load-bearing specifically *because* the switch was made
**deferred** rather than immediate: the downtime dispatcher's job is to fill
idle proxy capacity with backlog work, so left alone it keeps re-occupying the
slots the mode-switch worker is trying to accumulate, starving the completion
condition. Pausing new dispatches is what lets the pool quiesce and the switch
proceed. (This starvation role is *not* stated in the original brief, which
framed the drain around in-flight protection and capacity fit; it is a
reconstruction consistent with the code and with the dispatch-pause comment in
`downtime-worker.ts`.)

The **starvation rationale remains conceptually valid**; the **capacity-fit
rationale is inverted** by the current config. The sibling relationship is
structural, but the client drain did not copy the server drain's most important
property: the time bound that stops a stream of new work from postponing the
transition forever.

### Evidence

- No `draining` decision entry exists in any retained
  `.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` (all 100 entries are `checkin`).
- Proxy log (2026-10-06, retained window 07:55-09:26): the only fast->cheap
  switch (09:19:13) was not reachable via the drain path -- the shared idle
  clock was last set at 09:06:41 (12.5 min < 15 min) and the completion gate is
  unsatisfiable anyway. Startup lines confirm `mode=cheap ... slots=3` and
  `mode=fast ... slots=1`.
- Live proxy at verification time: `GET /admin/mode` -> `fast`;
  `GET /llama/local/status` -> `total_slots=1`.

### Decision

**This feature is no longer needed and is withdrawn.** It is superseded by the
proxy's own schedule (`mode_schedule.yaml`: cheap 01:00-10:00, fast 10:00-01:00)
and the server-side bounded drain, both of which own transition mechanics
correctly. The blocking defect filed during verification is
**WL-0MUWF763Q003MGUM** (superseded once the revert lands).

### Recommended remediation

See the `## Recommendation` section below.

## Recommendation

### Recommended end state

Reclaim a single coherent mode-transition story: **the proxy owns all
transition mechanics; the herdr plugin is a thin policy layer that only chooses
the target mode.** Concretely:

- Keep the plugin's two signals -- **fast on operator command**
  (`onOperatorCommand`) and **cheap on operator idleness** -- plus the existing
  safeguards (leader-only cheap switching, shared cross-pane activity, the
  server-side fast->cheap cooldown).
- Put **no** slot-budget or dispatch-pause logic in the plugin. Any need to
  quiesce before a restart is already met by the proxy's bounded server-side
  drain.
- Never hardcode pool sizes in the plugin: derive from the live proxy status or
  don't reference them at all. (The cheap pool silently changed 2 -> 3 after
  this brief; that drift is what made the hardcoded `2` unreachable.)

### Work to be done (recommended order)

1. **Revert the drain mechanism** (F1/F2/F4/F5 equivalents). Reuse this parent
   as the revert work item, or create a child:
   - `mode-switch-worker.ts`: remove `draining`, `getIsDraining()`,
     `MODE_SWITCH_DRAIN_FREE_SLOTS`, the `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS` import,
     and the drain-clearing branches; restore the direct
     `await fireSwitch(opts.proxyUrl, 'cheap')`.
   - `index.ts`: remove the single `drainPaused:` line.
   - `downtime-worker.ts`: remove `drainPaused?: boolean` from the config type
     and the `if (cfg.drainPaused === true)` gate.
   - Tests/docs: delete `drain-dispatch-integration.test.ts`; remove the
     drain-specific cases from `mode-switch-worker.test.ts` /
     `downtime-worker.test.ts`; drop the drain paragraphs from
     `docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md`.
   - Prefer a targeted manual revert over `git revert` of the five SHAs:
     unrelated commits landed between them in the same files, so raw reverts
     will conflict, while every drain line is still cleanly attributable to the
     feature commits.
2. **Decide the idle threshold (F3/AC7).** The 15-minute default is separable
   from the drain. Recommended: **keep 15 minutes** (responsive cheap-on-idle)
   unless the observed mode-churn argues for the original 60; record the choice.
3. **Add a regression guard.** A test pinning that the mode-switch worker does
   **not** gate the cheap switch on a slot count (and does not import audit slot
   budgets), so the inverted-budget bug cannot silently return.
4. **Close the lifecycle loop.** Mark `WL-0MUWF763Q003MGUM` superseded/won't-fix
   once the revert merges; re-run `/skill:test` and `/skill:audit` on this
   parent; advance to release only after the revert is green.
5. **Only if starvation is later observed**: add a **bounded** dispatch pause
   modelled on the server-side drain (`max_seconds`, direction-aware), not a
   free-slot gate. Do not reintroduce an unbounded client drain.

### Non-goals / cautions

- Do **not** duplicate the server-side restart drain on the client. The proxy
  already defers new chat requests and waits (bounded) for in-flight streams.
- Do **not** remove the fast-on-command switch: the proxy schedule alone would
  leave the operator in cheap during 01:00-10:00 while actively working.
- Keep the drain and mode-switch concerns separate from dispatch scheduling;
  coupling them (as this feature did) lets a bad mode-switch condition stall
  work dispatch for the whole machine.

### Open decisions for the operator

1. Idle threshold after revert: **15 min (recommended)** or 60 min.
2. Idle cheap switch: **keep** (recommended) or delegate entirely to
   `mode_schedule.yaml`.
3. Whether to file a small, separate `docs`/`chore` item recording the
   fast/cheap slot-count contract so future client logic cannot assume a pool
   shape.

## Decisions (2026-10-06)

Operator confirmed:

1. **Idle threshold after revert:** keep **15 min** (`900_000` ms).
2. **Idle cheap switch:** **keep** -- the plugin retains the cheap-on-idle signal.
3. **Revert scope confirmed:** revert F1/F2/F4/F5 (drain state, dispatch-pause
   wiring, drain tests, drain docs); keep fast-on-command; leave the proxy's
   server-side bounded drain untouched; the client drain is removed entirely.
4. **Slot-count contract:** chore filed -- **WL-0MUWH45RF004URWP**.
5. **Stale `lastKnownMode` gap in the fast path:** **fix now**, in scope.
6. **Implementation item:** reuse this item as the epic -- the revert is a child, **WL-0MUWIHUL2000JEFR** (`Implement` cannot target an all-terminal parent directly: `phase_parent` advances it instead of working it).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The client drain mechanism is removed from `mode-switch-worker.ts`
      (`draining`, `getIsDraining()`, `MODE_SWITCH_DRAIN_FREE_SLOTS`, the
      `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS` import, drain-clearing branches), and the
      cheap path calls `fireSwitch('cheap')` directly.
- [ ] `drainPaused` is removed from `index.ts` and `downtime-worker.ts`.
- [ ] Drain tests and `drain-dispatch-integration.test.ts` are removed; docs
      are trimmed.
- [ ] `DEFAULT_MODE_SWITCH_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS` remains `900_000` (15 min).
- [ ] Cheap-on-idle and fast-on-command are both retained, with the existing
      leader-only / shared-activity safeguards.
- [ ] The command-path fast switch is robust to a stale cached mode: an agent
      command issued while the proxy is actually cheap always results in a fast
      switch (no reliance on a possibly-stale `lastKnownMode`).
- [ ] Regression test: the mode-switch worker does not gate the cheap switch on
      a slot count and does not import audit slot budgets.

# Audit Worklog recovery module for other retained stale ExtensionContext async paths

## Headline

The recovery-extension crash fixed for `_notifyFn` (WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B) may be
one of several retained-`ctx` async paths. Audit the recovery module (and
adjacent Worklog extension code) for other captured/stored `ExtensionContext`
references that are invoked asynchronously after a session replacement/reload,
and harden them with the same defensively-guarded pattern.

## Context / Discovered from

- **Discovered from:** WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B (stale-ctx `_notifyFn` crash). The
  parent deliberately scoped only the `_notifyFn` notify path and recorded
  broader stale-ctx hardening as separate work (see the parent's
  "Risks & Assumptions" section: "record broader stale-ctx hardening as
  separate work").

## Goal (user story)

**As a pi extension maintainer**, I want every asynchronous path in the Worklog
recovery extension that can outlive its original `ExtensionContext` to degrade
gracefully (skip the operation) rather than throw an uncaught exception, so
that a session replacement/reload cannot crash a headless pi run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written audit enumerates every module-level or long-lived reference to a
  handler `ctx` (or a closure capturing it) in
  `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/` and classifies each as either **safe**
  (ctx used only synchronously within the handler) or **at risk** (invoked
  from a timer/async callback after the handler returns).
- Each at-risk path is either hardened with the guarded pattern established by
  WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B or recorded as a new blocking work item with rationale.
- Regression coverage is added for each hardened path (no throw with a
  stale/invalidated ctx, operation skipped).
- No change to retry semantics, backoff, attempt counts, or
  abort/session-generation guards.
- The Worklog extension test suite passes and the full project test suite
  passes with the changes.

## Out of scope

- Changes to retry/backoff semantics or the `_notifyFn` notify path itself
  (fixed under WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B).
- Third-party/consumer extensions (e.g. SorraAgents' `pi-client`) — tracked
  separately by that project.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts`
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/*.test.ts`
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/` (other modules retaining `ctx`)
- `packages/tui/extensions/README.md`

discovered-from:SA-0MUA8BSAG000YZA2 (SorraAgents worklog)

## Goal

The producer (SorraAgents work item SA-0MUA8BSAG000YZA2, epic SA-0MUJL211C008GHMZ)
asked for a ContextHub work item that investigates **why** a raised host-wide
test-concurrency cap (`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY`) was believed present in the
downtime/herdr harness, and that agrees an alternative approach with the agent;
the offending override is then to be removed.

## Producer decision (2026-09-28)

1. Raise a work item here to investigate why the override is present and agree an
   alternative with the agent.
2. Remove it.

## Investigation result (evidence)

**No `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` override exists in the ContextHub/herdr harness.**

- `git log --all -S "TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY"` in ContextHub returns **no commits** —
  the string has never existed on any branch (source, `dist`, or config).
- No occurrence in `packages/herdr` source or `packages/herdr/dist`, the shipped
  `herdr` binary (`grep -a`), `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`,
  `~/.config/herdr/plugins*`, `~/.herdr/downtime/*`, or any shell dotfile.
- No occurrence in the environments of the herdr server, the `run-pi-agent.sh`
  wrappers, or the dispatched pi agents (checked `/proc/<pid>/environ`).
- The audit debug log from the incident
  (`~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/green_suite_SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX_20260927T111823.log`)
  records the actual value at the time:
  `test concurrency slot busy: no free slot within 600s (TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2)`
  — the default, **not** a raised cap.
- `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` (separate `"audit"` namespace, default 1) does appear in
  ContextHub history, but it is unrelated to the `"test"` namespace.

## Actual cause of the observed oversubscription

The apparent "~8 concurrent suites" was **not** a harness env override. It was:

1. **Unpaced call paths** that call `run_cached()` directly instead of the test
   skill's semaphore-guarded `run_tests.py`: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
   (route fixed by SA-0MUKHCO02009EQFG) and the audit F3 auto-execution path
   (SA-0MUJK94QN0015925). Those executions bypass the host-wide `"test"` semaphore.
2. **Stale semaphore slot files** `/run/user/1000/pi-semaphores/test/2..9`.
   `Semaphore._ensure_slots` only ever *adds* slots (up to `max_workers`) and never
   prunes extras. The extras are inert for a process with `max_workers=2` (its
   `_try_acquire_slot` iterates `range(max_workers)`), but they misled diagnosis and
   were cited as evidence of an 8-slot ceiling.

## Proposed alternatives (to agree with the agent)

1. **No harness-level `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` override** — none exists today; keep the
   test skill's env-var + default-2 as the single source of truth.
2. **Prune stale slots in `Semaphore._ensure_slots`** (SorraAgents
   `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py`) so the on-disk slot count converges to
   `max_workers`, removing the misleading residue.
3. **Close the unpaced call paths** (owned by the SorraAgents children named above)
   so every real suite execution acquires the host-wide `"test"` semaphore.
4. **Optional dispatcher deferral** — treat host-wide test saturation as a reason to
   defer test/implement dispatch, analogous to the existing audit-slot dispatch gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Recorded, with evidence, whether any harness/herd code sets `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY`;
      if none, close the item with that finding and no harness code change.
- [ ] An agreed alternative documented (env-only, prune stale slots, close unpaced paths,
      optional dispatcher deferral).
- [ ] If pruning/coordination is agreed, a test proves the on-disk slot count converges
      to `max_workers` after a higher-`max_workers` run.
- [ ] Cross-references SA-0MUJL211C008GHMZ and SA-0MUA8BSAG000YZA2 (SorraAgents).

## Interim action taken

The stale test-namespace slot files `2..9` (unused by any `max_workers=2` process;
slots `0..1` were held by live suites) were removed on 2026-09-28 as the concrete
raised-capacity artefact. This is a one-off cleanup; the durable fix is AC2 (pruning).

## Related

- SA-0MUJL211C008GHMZ — Implement test job pacing to prevent resource oversubscription (epic)
- SA-0MUA8BSAG000YZA2 — Browser suite contention: TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2 starvation
- SA-0MUKHCO02009EQFG — Route implement.py test execution through the test skill pacer
- SA-0MUJK94QN0015925 — audit F3 auto-execution bypasses the test concurrency semaphore

# Log projection helper: recentDispatchedItems

**Parent:** WL-0MUGLL9SS002E1D2 (Recent dispatches summary)

## Goal

Add a projection function to `downtime-log.ts` that reads the rolling dispatch log via the existing fail-safe reader and returns the up-to-20 most recent dispatched work items, deduplicated by id and ordered newest-first.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New exported function `recentDispatchedItems(cwd, limit?)` reads via the existing fail-safe `readDowntimeLogEntries(cwd)`; a missing/unreadable/empty/malformed log yields `[]` with no throw.
- Non-dispatch-marker entries (pane-close/lifecycle entries with `entryType: 'pane-close'`) are ignored by the projection.
- Rows are deduplicated by work item id — one row per id — using that item's most recent log entry for ordering and metadata.
- Rows are ordered by their most recent log-entry timestamp, newest first.
- The result is capped at 20 rows (configurable via `limit`, default 20).
- Each row is a `RecentDispatchRow` carrying at least: `itemId`, `title`, `kind`, `latestOutcome` (when a pane-close entry exists), and `latestTimestamp`.
- A missing/empty title falls back to a placeholder (e.g. `[unknown]`) rather than a blank row; malformed JSONL lines are skipped without throwing.
- Unit tests cover: dedup by id, newest-first ordering, 20-row cap, kind/outcome mapping, missing title, malformed lines, and the empty/missing-log fail-safe path.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Define exported interface `RecentDispatchRow` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`.
2. Implement `recentDispatchedItems(cwd, limit = 20)` reading entries and reducing into a `Map<itemId, RecentDispatchRow>` keyed by id (last-write-wins on the newest entry).
3. Sort by latest timestamp descending, slice to `limit`.
4. Add unit tests to `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.test.ts` (test-first: write the projection tests before the helper body).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- None.

# Problem Statement

`implement.py finish` runs only the pytest test suite because `_detect_test_tooling()` prefers pytest whenever the repo contains pytest-style test files. This silently ignores the canonical full suite declared in `.pi/test-config.json` `suiteCommands`, which for ContextHub is `npm --silent test -- tests/cli` and `npm --silent test -- tests/unit`. As a result, the finish gate never runs the vitest suite, creating a false sense of test coverage.

# Users

- **AI agents** running `/skill:implement` — the finish step's test gate must exercise the project's real full suite so that a push to dev is properly validated.
- **The herdr downtime worker** — auto-dispatches implement sessions; relies on finish's test gate being accurate.

# Acceptance Criteria

1. **`implement.py finish` honours `.pi/test-config.json` `suiteCommands` when present.** The test step uses the declared command list as the primary source and does not fall back to convention detection (pytest/npm/node) when `suiteCommands` is set.
2. **`run_tests()` in `implement.py` delegates to `full_suite_commands()` from the test skill.** The function resolves suite commands in the same order as `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`: extension file first, then convention detection.
3. **Changed-file scope (`scope="changed"`) is preserved.** When the test skill's changed-file selector is available and applicable, `implement.py` uses it; when unavailable (e.g. custom `suiteCommands` not introspectable), it falls back to the full suite with a logged warning.
4. **The fix is backward-compatible for repos without `suiteCommands`.** Repos that rely on convention detection (pytest-only, npm-only, node-only) continue to work as before, with the test skill's own convention detection replacing `implement.py`'s duplicate logic.
5. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** All existing tests in both `implement.py` and the test skill must pass after the refactor.

# Constraints

- The change must not break repos that already have `suiteCommands` but use a different tooling mix (e.g. pytest + npm).
- No new external dependencies — reuse the existing import of `full_suite_commands` from the test skill.
- The `IMPLEMENT_TEST_COMMAND` env-var override retains highest precedence (unchanged).

# Existing State

- `_detect_test_tooling()` in `implement.py` checks: pytest → npm → repo-script → unity.
- `run_tests()` in `implement.py` branches on the detected tooling and runs only that suite.
- `full_suite_commands()` in `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` checks `suiteCommands` first, then conventions.
- The test skill's `changed_scope_commands()` is already imported (as `_changed_scope_commands`) but only used for pytest-specific subset selection.
- ContextHub's `.pi/test-config.json` declares: `["npm --silent test -- tests/cli", "npm --silent test -- tests/unit"]` — both are npm/vitest commands.

# Desired Change

Make `implement.py`'s `run_tests()` delegate to `full_suite_commands()` for the full suite, and to `changed_scope_commands()` (when available) for changed-file scope, matching the test skill's resolution order exactly.

# Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `run_tests()`, `_detect_test_tooling()`, `_has_pytest_suite()`, `_has_test_script()`
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `full_suite_commands()`, `changed_scope_commands()` (reference only)

# Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep risk:** This fix only addresses `implement.py`'s `run_tests()` function. Other consumers of `_detect_test_tooling()` (if any outside the test step) should be audited, but scope is limited to the finish test gate.
- **Assumption:** `_detect_test_tooling()` is only called from `run_tests()` and has no other callers in the implement skill. If it does, those callers need separate review.
- **Risk:** Changing the detection order may alter which repo-scope commands are selected in `changed_scope` mode for repos with `suiteCommands` + pytest. However, `changed_scope_commands()` in the test skill already returns `None` when `suiteCommands` is present (since it's not introspectable), so the fallback is always the full suite — the same behaviour as before (just now logged explicitly rather than silently).
- **Risk:** The test skill's `full_suite_commands()` is imported conditionally (in the try/except block). The fix must preserve the existing graceful degradation: when the test skill is partially installed, the full suite still falls back to convention detection.

# Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

No clarifying questions needed — the bug is self-evident from the code and the `.pi/test-config.json` declaration.

# Related Work

- WL-0MU1EWMHN000YUCG (Invalidating an audit) — the item from which this bug was discovered.
- SA-0MSTMYE79006NA61 — Feature 2: test skill honours `suiteCommands`.
- F2 AC4 — `full_suite_commands()` is the single source of truth for suite-command resolution.
- WL-0MSGQ64N2006TQB2 (implement.py worktrees lack node_modules) — related implement/test integration issue.
data.title: implement.py finish runs pytest instead of the declared canonical suite

# ChatClient: OpenAI-compatible chat completions

## Goal

Add a reusable `ChatClient` class that makes `POST /v1/chat/completions` calls — the sibling of `OpenAIEmbedder` but for text generation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. New file `src/lib/llm.ts` containing `ChatClient` interface and `OpenAIChatClient` implementation.
2. Interface: `ChatClient { readonly available: boolean; complete(prompt: string, options?: { maxTokens?: number; timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<string> }`.
3. `OpenAIChatClient` posts to `${baseUrl}/chat/completions` with message array \[{ role: 'user', content: prompt }], model from config (default: `compact`).
4. Config resolution: constructor accepts optional config, falls back to env vars then defaults (mirroring `OpenAIEmbedder` pattern).
5. Bounded call: 15-second timeout default, configurable via options/config.
6. Graceful degradation: `available = false` when unconfigured; `complete()` throws descriptive error when not available.
7. No new runtime dependencies — uses `fetch` (Node 18+ native).

## Goal

Create a pure filter function that checks whether a non-terminal cooldown
applies to an item+kind pair, based on the rolling pane-close log.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Function `isNonTerminalCooldownActive` in `downtime-log.ts`:
   - Reads `entryType: "pane-close"` entries from the passed entries array
   - Non-terminal reason codes: anything except `"none"` (e.g. `agent-ended-no-terminal`, `audit-ended-no-result`, `producer-review`, `risk-effort-incomplete`, `reached-in-review`)
   - Terminal outcomes have `reasonCode: "none"` - they do NOT trigger cooldown
   - Returns true when: a non-terminal close for the same itemId+kind exists AND cooldownMs has NOT elapsed since the close timestamp
   - Returns false when: no close record, or the close is older than cooldownMs, or the close was terminal
   - Fail-closed: missing/unparseable timestamp returns true (skip dispatch)

2. Stage advancement releases (AC4 of parent):
   - The function receives itemStage (current worklog stage of the item)
   - If the current stage rank is HIGHER than the dispatched-at stage rank, return false (released)
   - Stage rank ordering: idea=0, intake_complete=1, plan_complete=2, in_review=3

3. Tests: Unit tests covering:
   - (a) non-terminal close then immediate idle returns true (skip)
   - (b) close older than cooldownMs returns false (eligible)
   - (c) stage advancement mid-cooldown returns false (eligible)
   - (d) terminal success reasonCode equals none returns false (eligible)
   - (e) missing/unparseable close timestamp returns true (fail-closed skip)
data.title: Create non-terminal cooldown filter function

## Goal

Wire the non-terminal cooldown filter into both the Herdr-list-head path
(dispatchFromHerdrList) and the coordination offer path (computeMostImportantItem
+ dispatchFromCoordination).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. dispatchFromHerdrList integration:
   - Read pane-close entries once per dispatch cycle (same as dispatched markers)
   - Apply cooldown filter AFTER dispatched-marker exclusion, BEFORE code-freeze
   - Pass the current item stage and dispatched-at stage to the filter
   - Cooldown skip is a plain `continue` (neutral, like code-freeze)

2. computeMostImportantItem integration:
   - Same placement: after dispatched-marker exclusion, before code-freeze
   - Uses the same filter with the same semantics
   - Cooldown skip is a plain `continue` (neutral, like code-freeze)

3. dispatchFromCoordination integration:
   - Same filter applied in the offer filter sequence
   - Placed after classifyItemForDispatch, before free-slot minimums
   - Cooldown skip is a `continue` (entry kept, skipped this cycle)

4. Module header documentation:
   - Update the downtime-worker.ts module JSDoc header to mention the new
     non-terminal cooldown filter as a sequential gate

5. No-candidate and three-strike semantics preserved:
   - Cooldown skip does NOT count toward three-strike rule
   - Cooldown skip does NOT trigger the no-candidate cooldown
   - The dispatch outcome reason remains distinguishable
data.title: Integrate cooldown filter into both dispatch paths

## Feature 3: Implement core pane-triage logic (enumerate, classify, report)

### Summary
Implement the core Python module: workspace resolution, pane enumeration via shelling out to the reaper CLI `--json` mode, report rendering (Idle/Active tables, log tails, recommendation rules), and the approval-gated close flow.

### Acceptance Criteria
1. `resolve_workspace()` returns the workspace from `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` or falls back to `herdr pane current`; reports only that workspace.
2. `enumerate_and_classify()` shells out to the reaper CLI (`--json`), parses the JSON output, and enriches each pane with work-item context. The item id is derived from the shared `paneItemIdFromLabel` (exposed in the reaper JSON), not re-parsed in Python. The `needsProducerReview` value is obtained via `wl show <id> --json` for the parsed item id.
3. `build_report()` renders Idle and Active tables (tab, title, pane id) and, for idle items, the work item id and `needsProducerReview` value. **Idle** specifically means the shared classifier's reasonCode is `'marker'` (the `</end_session>` marker is present at the end of the final assistant message), per parent AC2.
4. Each idle item's last 20 log lines are printed under the heading `<pane title> Needs Review <true|false>`.
5. Recommendation rules: the "Recommended to close" table excludes the invoking pane (`HERDR_PANE_ID`) and panes with `needsProducerReview=true`. Additionally, panes with reasonCode `implement` or `live-children` (inherited from the shared classifier's never-close guards) are also excluded.
6. Re-verify-before-close: re-reads `herdr pane list` immediately before each close; any pane that became active is skipped with a reason in the Closed ledger.

### Constraints
- Shared classifier is mandatory: consume idle classification from the ContextHub reaper CLI (`--json`), never re-implement the `</end_session>` check.
- Never-close guards are universal (per producer Q-OPEN-2): `needsProducerReview=true` panes are never closed, by manual skill or automatic reaper. `implement` panes and panes with live child processes are also excluded (inherited from the shared classifier).
- Workspace-scoped only — no cross-workspace roll-up.
- Fail-closed on herdr CLI errors: clear message, no partial mutation.

### Deliverables
- `SorraAgents/skill/pane-triage/scripts/pane_triage.py` (full implementation)
- Updated `SKILL.md` documenting report shape and rules

### Key Files
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/pane-triage/scripts/pane_triage.py`
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/pane-triage/SKILL.md`

# Intake Brief — When dispatching a new workload, first scan all workspaces and panes for stalled work (WL-0MUMA5OMH0024PN1)

## Problem statement

When the Herdr downtime dispatcher finds idle local-LLM capacity it always picks
the next item from the Herdr-list head and spawns a **new** pane, even when an
existing pane already holds work for a non-terminal item whose agent is no longer
working (its pi agent is `idle`, or has exited as `done`, without the item reaching
a terminal stage). Those items silently occupy a workspace and a session but never
finish "unattended", and fresh capacity is spent on new work instead of completing
the stalled work.

## Users

- **Operator / producer** running the machine-wide downtime dispatcher who wants
  more panes to complete their work unattended, without manually noticing and
  poking stalled panes.
  - *As an operator, when capacity is free I want the dispatcher to notice a pane
    whose agent stopped working on an unfinished item and resume that work, so I
    stop accumulating half-finished work.*
  - *As an operator, I do not want the dispatcher to keep opening new panes for
    new work while older dispensed work sits stalled.*
- **Dispatcher maintainers** who need the new behaviour to compose with the
  existing safety guards (in-flight guard, CAS claim, dispatch markers,
  non-terminal cooldown, attempt cap, review-queue gate, code freeze).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Stall detection (pre-dispatch).** On an idle dispatch cycle, and **before** selecting a new work item, the dispatcher scans the machine-wide `herdr pane list` and identifies *stalled* panes. A pane is stalled when **all** hold: it hosts a live `pi` agent (an `agent` value is present); its label suffix parses to a work-item id whose item is non-terminal (status not `completed`/`deleted`, stage not `in_review`/`done`); its `agent_status` is not `blocked`; and its not-`working` state has persisted at least the configured stall threshold (default 5 min).
- **Resume in place.** Each stalled candidate is resumed **in place**, reusing its session — no new pane is spawned for that item: a live agent receives `herdr agent prompt <paneId> continue`; a pane whose agent has exited (`agent_status: done`) has pi relaunched in the same pane continuing the session (via `herdr agent start` / `pi --continue` / `--session <path>`), after which the literal `continue` prompt is submitted.
- **Preference ordering.** When at least one stalled candidate is resumed successfully, the dispatcher does **not** dispatch a new work item in that cycle. When no stalled candidate is resumable, the existing dispatch path proceeds unchanged.
- **Safety and no-progress exclusions.** The scan skips items with `needsProducerReview === true`, items held by the non-terminal pane-close cooldown, items at/over the per-item/per-kind attempt cap, panes whose agent is `blocked`, and panes whose item has already advanced past the pane's dispatched kind (e.g. label `implement` but the item is now `completed`/`in_review`). A skip is **neutral** — not a CLI-error strike and not a `no-candidate` cooldown.
- **Bounded, idempotent, cross-root.** A resume reuses the existing claim/attempt bookkeeping (records a dispatch attempt for `(item, kind)`, honours the attempt cap and escalates via `needsProducerReview` when exhausted); concurrent resumes of the same pane/item are prevented; and a stalled pane for an item in another worklog root is resumed against **that** root (resolved from the pane's `cwd` / `agent_session`), not the leader's root.
- **Fail-safe and configurable.** An unreadable/unparseable `herdr pane list`, a resume failure, or unwired deps degrade to "no stalled resume" and normal dispatch (never a crash, never a duplicate); the scan-enable flag and stall threshold are plugin settings, read live per tick and clamped to a sane range. 
## Constraints

- **Capacity unchanged.** The stall scan runs only when the dispatcher is already
  idle-gated and would otherwise dispatch; the LLM idle / free-slot check remains
  the sole concurrency limiter (no re-introduction of a running-pane cap,
  WL-0MU2EP6JL006A1U3).
- **Reuse existing guards.** The resume path must compose with — never bypass —
  the CAS claim, dispatched-marker change-guard, non-terminal cooldown,
  per-item/per-kind attempt cap, producer-review gate, review-queue depth gate,
  code-freeze split-by-skill, and host-wide audit single-flight.
- **`herdr agent prompt` semantics.** The CLI rejects a submission when the agent
  is already `blocked`, and returns `agent_prompt_stalled` when an accepted
  submission does not reach `working`/`blocked` within 5 s. Both outcomes are
  treated as "not resumed this cycle" (neutral), not as a strike.
- **Do not disturb the operator.** Prefer not to hijack a pane the operator is
  actively using; this is bounded by the `blocked` exclusion and the stall
  threshold (residual risk accepted, see Risks).
- **Single machine, v1.** Matches the existing machine-coordination contract
  (`machine-coordination.ts`); multi-machine is out of scope.
- **Repository boundaries.** No edits to `.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/`, or other
  agent-infrastructure directories.

## Existing state

- `dispatchDowntimeWork` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`) elects/uses a
  machine-wide leader, waits for the LLM idle gate, then dispatches from the
  Herdr-list head through sequential safety filters (CAS claim → marker → spawn).
- The item-scoped in-flight signal already exists:
  `runningDowntimePaneItemIds` / `resolveInFlightPanes` return the set of items
  with a **`working`** downtime pane; today it is consulted only by the
  critical-first guard. Its complement (a pane for a non-terminal item that is
  **not** `working`) is exactly the "stalled" signal this item needs.
- Panes are discoverable machine-wide from `herdr pane list`, which carries
  `label` (suffix ` - <ITEM-ID>`), `agent`, `agent_status`, `cwd`, and
  `agent_session` (the pi session log path). Both `Downtime triggered …` and
  `Manually triggered …` labels carry the item id and kind.
- Herdr primitives available: `herdr agent prompt <pane> <text>` (submits to a
  live agent, rejects `blocked`), `herdr agent start pi --kind pi --pane <id>`
  (relaunch an agent in a pane at a shell prompt), and `pi --continue` /
  `pi --session <path>`.
- `.worklog/agent-panes.json` (per root) already maps work-item → pane for
  worklist-spawned panes, with the original command; `agent-tracker.ts`
  normalises raw status to `idle | working | blocked | done | unknown`.
- A scheduled pane-closure reaper (WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS) closes panes whose agent
  emitted `</end_session>` (or, if enabled, idle beyond a threshold); the
  dispatch monitor (`pane-lifecycle.ts`) is disabled.

## Desired change

Add a **stalled-work scan-and-resume step** ahead of new-item dispatch on every
idle dispatch cycle:

1. A pure classifier (new module, e.g. `stalled-work.ts`) maps a `herdr pane list`
   record + item info + guard inputs to `{ stalled: true, kind }` or
   `{ stalled: false, reason }`, applying AC1/AC4 and deriving the pane's
   dispatched kind from its label.
2. An orchestrator attempts the in-place resume (AC2) against the item's own root,
   records the attempt (AC5), and reports a neutral outcome for skips/failures.
3. `dispatchDowntimeWork` (and the coordination offer/leader paths) consult the
   scan first; a successful resume short-circuits new-item dispatch for the cycle
   (AC3); any failure falls through to the unchanged normal path (AC6).
4. Settings gains `downtimeStallScanEnabled` (default on) and
   `downtimeStallThresholdMs` (default 5 min, clamped), re-read per tick.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/stalled-work.ts` — **new**: pure stall classifier + resume
  orchestrator (`classifyStalledPane`, `resumeStalledPane`).
- `packages/herdr/src/stalled-work.test.ts` — **new**: unit tests for detection,
  exclusions, no-progress guard, resume dispatch, fail-safe.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — insert the scan before new-item
  dispatch; extend `DowntimeWorkerDeps` with `scanStalledPanes` /
  `resumeStalledPane`; thread through `dispatchDowntimeWork`,
  `dispatchFromHerdrList`, `computeMostImportantItem`, `dispatchFromCoordination`.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — wire production deps in `createDowntimeDeps`
  (reuse the existing `herdr pane list` read/parse), plus the `herdr agent prompt`
  / `herdr agent start` seams.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-herdr.ts` — reuse/refactor the `herdr pane list`
  parser and agent-status probe for the stall scan.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — reuse the non-terminal cooldown and
  attempt-cap predicates and record the resume attempt.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — add `downtimeStallScanEnabled` /
  `downtimeStallThresholdMs` plus clamp helpers.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts`
  — integration coverage (scan-before-dispatch, ordering, cross-root, fail-safe).
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — document the stalled-work scan-and-resume
  behaviour, settings and timing defaults.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — package-level mention of the new behaviour.

## Related work

- **Herdr downtime dispatcher: remove the client-side running-pane cap so the LLM
  idle/free-slot check is the concurrency limiter (WL-0MU2EP6JL006A1U3)** — the
  capacity model the scan must not change.
- **RCA: Downtime dispatcher re-dispatches CRITICAL implement items (duplicate
  panes on one work item) (WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4)** — the `working`-pane in-flight
  signal (`runningDowntimePaneItemIds`) reused (inverted) here.
- **[downtime] Release stale dispatch success-markers when the item has not
  advanced (WL-0MU6UL0RJ008IHGT)** — related "stranded item" recovery.
- **[downtime] Add minimum cooldown before re-dispatching after a non-terminal
  pane close (WL-0MUKYERLZ006ELL5)** — cooldown the scan must honour.
- **[downtime] Enforce a per-item dispatch-attempt cap and flag items that exhaust
  it (WL-0MUKYEXMK0033MFK)** — attempt bookkeeping the resume reuses.
- **Herdr worklist: track agents spawned per work item and show their status icon
  (WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9)** — pane↔item tracking and status normalisation.
- **Investigate why completed plan/intake sessions are not closed on completion
  — the pane-closure reaper (WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS)** — concurrent closer; the
  resume must be race-safe against it.
- **Dispatcher only dispatches work from current sprint — the sprint-view-only
  dispatch window (WL-0MUNS8X97007C9H9)** and **Downtime dispatch: gate
  non-critical implement tier on review-queue depth (WL-0MT2UQWOR007CYY9)** —
  filters the normal path keeps.
- **Herdr downtime dispatcher: allow blocked-status dispatch (WL-0MUBUA9C8009N0K5)**
  — item `blocked` status is dispatchable (distinct from the `blocked` agent
  status excluded here).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Operator-pane hijack (medium).** Resuming an `idle` pane the operator is
  reading/typing in could be disruptive. Mitigation: exclude `blocked` agent panes
  and require a stall threshold; residual risk accepted by the operator.
- **Resume race with the reaper (medium).** The reaper may close a `done` pane
  while the scan tries to relaunch it; the resume must be idempotent and treat a
  vanished pane as a neutral skip.
- **Duplicate work (medium).** Stage-propagation lag could make an already-advanced
  item look stalled; mitigated by the no-progress guard plus the attempt cap.
- **Resume-failure noise (low).** `agent_prompt_stalled` / `agent_blocked` / CLI
  errors must be neutral outcomes and fall through to normal dispatch (never a
  strike, never a crash, never a duplicate).
- **Wrong-root resume (low).** Resolve the root from the pane's `cwd` /
  `agent_session`; fail closed (skip) when the root cannot be resolved
  unambiguously.
- **Assumption:** `agent_status` is one of `idle | working | blocked | done |
  unknown`; the active set is `work/working/busy/running` (matches
  `pane-close.ts`).
- **Assumption:** the default stall threshold is 5 min (aligned with the reaper's
  5-min grace period) and a successful resume records a dispatch attempt so the
  existing attempt cap applies.
- **Assumption:** the literal resume prompt text is `continue`.
- **Assumption:** the dispatched kind is derived from the pane label
  (`Downtime triggered <kind> …` / `Manually triggered <kind> …`).
- **Scope-creep risk (low).** Extending the scan to non-`pi` agents, to closing
  stale panes, or to multi-machine coordination is out of scope — record any such
  opportunity as a separate linked work item rather than widening this one.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

Interview round 1 (session `herdr-1791407063-235270-15430`, 2026-10-07):

- Q1: "What does 'restart the work' mean — re-dispatch through the existing
  pipeline, resume the existing pane in place, or release only?" — **Answer
  (operator): B — Resume the existing pane in place, reusing its agent session.**
  Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Scope of the scan — all downtime panes machine-wide, own root only, or all
  agent panes including manually opened ones?" — **Answer (operator): C — All
  agent panes, including manually opened ones.** Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "What counts as stalled — not-working + no-progress + grace, include
  `blocked`, or any non-working immediately?" — **Answer (operator): A —
  Not-working + no-progress + grace; excludes `blocked` agent status,
  `needsProducerReview`, cooldown and attempt-cap-held items.** Source:
  interactive reply.

Interview round 2 (same session):

- Q4: "Which states do we resume, and how — resume both `idle` and exited `done`
  in place, only `idle` in place with `done` fallback, or only `idle`?" —
  **Answer (operator): A — Resume in place for both `idle` and exited `done`
  agents.** Source: interactive reply.
- Q5: "What text do we send on resume — the stage-appropriate skill command, a
  fixed neutral nudge, or a configurable template?" — **Answer (operator):
  `continue`** (fixed literal continuation prompt). Source: interactive reply.
- Q6: "Candidate discovery source — one machine-wide `herdr pane list` scan,
  per-root `.worklog/agent-panes.json`, or both?" — **Answer (operator): A — One
  machine-wide `herdr pane list` scan** (item id parsed from the label suffix;
  root resolved from the pane's `cwd` / `agent_session`). Source: interactive
  reply.

## Research notes

- Inspected `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (ranking contract, in-flight guard,
  success-marker lifetime, non-terminal cooldown, attempt cap, pane-closure
  reaper), `packages/herdr/shared/herdr-agent-state-protocol.md` (agent states),
  `packages/herdr/src/pane-close.ts`, `agent-tracker.ts`, `pane-close-herdr.ts`,
  and `downtime-worker.ts` (`runningDowntimePaneItemIds`, `resolveInFlightPanes`,
  `evaluateCriticalFirstGuard`).
- Verified live CLI surface: `herdr pane list` (fields incl. `label`, `agent`,
  `agent_status`, `cwd`, `agent_session`), `herdr agent prompt` (rejects
  `blocked`; `agent_prompt_stalled` semantics), `herdr agent start`, and
  `pi --continue` / `--session`.

- **WL-0MSIXMKOX0052514** – Align wl init with SorraAgents install: delegate agent-guidance/workflow setup instead of duplicating (completed)
- **WL-0MSB3NYMW008APQC** – Tests: pane visibility detection module (visibility.test.ts) (completed)

# Improve pane auto-close logic (WL-0MUMCZAC40058HCC)

## Problem statement

The current pane auto-close logic (controlled by `paneCloseEnabled`) is closing panes that should remain open. Since the default has been changed to `false`, the feature is currently inert — but when enabled, the classification logic needs improvement to avoid false-positive closes.

## Background

- **WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS** — "Investigate why completed plan/intake sessions are not closed on completion" — established the pane-close scheduler and reaper infrastructure.
- **WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN** — "Log all dispatches and auto close all completed dispatch panes, except implement" — created the pane-lifecycle classifier.
- The auto-close feature is now **disabled by default** (`paneCloseEnabled: false`) until the classification logic is improved.

## Current issues

The classification logic in `pane-lifecycle.ts` and `pane-close-reaper.ts` has been observed to close panes prematurely in certain scenarios:

1. **Intake panes** — May close before the operator has a chance to answer questions (when `needsProducerReview` is true but the state hasn't propagated).
2. **Plan panes** — May close before the producer has reviewed the output.
3. **Agent panes with long-running operations** — May be classified as idle when they are actually working but temporarily silent.
4. **Race conditions** — The pane-lifecycle monitor and the reaper may both attempt to close the same pane.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — No false-positive closes.** Pane auto-close must never close a pane where the operator might still need to interact (e.g. awaiting producer review, actively working, or has live child processes).
- **AC2 — Producer-review guard is robust.** A pane with `needsProducerReview=true` on its item must never be auto-closed, regardless of idle time or agent state.
- **AC3 — Active-agent detection is improved.** Pane-lifecycle classification must use additional signals beyond simple idle timeouts — e.g. recent file modifications, active network connections, or live child processes.
- **AC4 — Idempotent closes.** The reaper and the lifecycle monitor must not race; a pane can be closed at most once, with the outcome logged idempotently.
- **AC5 — Configurable grace period.** Add a `paneCloseGracePeriodMinutes` setting (default 5 minutes) — no pane is eligible for close within N minutes of its first dispatch, giving the agent time to start working.
- **AC6 — Better logging.** Every close decision includes a detailed reason with the full state snapshot (agent state, idle duration, item stage, needsProducerReview flag, child processes).
- **AC7 — Tests.** Table-driven tests for every classification path, including negative tests for the scenarios that previously caused false-positive closes.

## Key files

- `packages/herdr/src/pane-lifecycle.ts` — Classification logic
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-reaper.ts` — Reaper orchestration
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-scheduler.ts` — Scheduling and defaults
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — Logging schema
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — Configuration options

# Improve Mechanism A idle timeout algorithm and re-enable auto-close

## Problem statement

Mechanism A (the scheduled reaper, `pane-close.ts::classifySession`) has two
classification bugs and should be re-enabled once they are fixed:

1. `!agentProcessAlive` (step 6) currently closes the pane (`dead-agent`).
   A dead agent does not mean the pane is safe to close — the operator may
   still need to read the final output. This should be **no close**.
2. The idle timeout (step 7) only supports a positive threshold. It should
   accept `<= 0` meaning **never close on idle**, with a **default of `0`**
   (idle-based closing disabled by default).

With the idle default at `0`, the auto-close feature can be safely re-enabled
via `paneCloseEnabled` (currently `false`).

## Background

- **WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN** — created the pane-lifecycle classifier.
- **WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS** — established the pane-close scheduler and reaper.
- **WL-0MUMCZAC40058HCC** — parent improvement item for pane auto-close.
- Mechanism A was disabled by default (`paneCloseEnabled: false`) pending
  classification fixes; this item covers the fixes needed to re-enable it.

## Current behaviour

- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close.ts::classifySession` — step 6 returns
  `{ close: true, reasonCode: 'dead-agent' }` when `!agentProcessAlive`.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close.ts` — `DEFAULT_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000`
  (30 minutes); no `<= 0` handling.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-scheduler.ts` — `DEFAULT_PANE_CLOSE_ENABLED = false`,
  `DEFAULT_PANE_CLOSE_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MINUTES = 30`.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — `paneCloseEnabled`, `paneCloseIdleThresholdMinutes`.

## Desired change

- Dead-agent path returns `{ close: false, reasonCode: 'dead-agent' }`.
- Idle threshold `<= 0` returns `{ close: false }` (never close on idle),
  with `DEFAULT_PANE_CLOSE_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MINUTES = 0`.
- `clampPaneCloseIdleThresholdMinutes` must permit `0` (so the minimum range
  becomes `0..1440`, and the scheduler must not coerce `0` back to a positive
  default).
- `DEFAULT_PANE_CLOSE_ENABLED = true` to re-enable Mechanism A auto-close.
- Update the classifier doc comment to reflect the new outcome ordering.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 — Dead agent does not close.** `classifySession` returns
   `{ close: false, reasonCode: 'dead-agent' }` when `agentProcessAlive` is
   `false` (and no higher-precedence guard/close applies).
2. **AC2 — Idle `<= 0` never closes.** With `idleThresholdMs <= 0`,
   `classifySession` never returns a close decision via the `idle-threshold`
   path, regardless of `idleMs`.
3. **AC3 — Default idle threshold is 0.** `DEFAULT_PANE_CLOSE_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MINUTES`
   is `0` and `clampPaneCloseIdleThresholdMinutes` accepts `0`.
4. **AC4 — Auto-close re-enabled.** `DEFAULT_PANE_CLOSE_ENABLED` is `true`,
   so the scheduled reaper runs by default.
5. **AC5 — Tests.** Table-driven tests cover the dead-agent no-close path and
   the `<= 0` idle-threshold no-close path (including negative tests proving
   the previous false-positive closes no longer occur).
6. **AC6 — Docs.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
   site entries.
7. **AC7 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new
   changes.

## Key files

- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close.ts` — Classification logic and default threshold
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-scheduler.ts` — Defaults and clamping
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — Configuration options
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close.test.ts` — Classifier tests
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-scheduler.test.ts` — Scheduler tests

## Related work

- WL-0MUMCZAC40058HCC — Improve pane auto-close logic (parent)
- WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN — pane-lifecycle classifier origin
- WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS — pane-close scheduler/reaper origin

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What should the dead-agent path do?" — Answer (operator):
  "should be no close". Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "What should the idle timeout default and `<= 0` semantics be?" —
  Answer (operator): "should allow a value of <=0 which means never close on
  idle. This should be set to a default of 0." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Should auto-close be re-enabled?" — Answer (operator): "Then re-enable
  autoclose via mechanism A". Source: interactive reply.
data.title: Improve Mechanism A idle timeout algorithm and re-enable auto-close
