# Intake Brief — Make Herdr UI refresh snappy after agent work-item updates (WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN)

## Problem statement

After an agent writes to a work item (e.g. `wl update`, `wl close`, `wl claim`), the Herdr Work Items pane can take up to 30 s to reflect the change — and when the refresh does run, the read cache has just been invalidated by the write, so the pane spawns ~4–5 cold `wl` processes (cold `wl next` measured at ~1.5 s; each warm spawn ~0.4–0.65 s) for a multi-second update. The list therefore lags behind agent activity and feels unresponsive precisely when the operator is watching an agent work.

## Users

- **Agent operators running the Herdr Work Items pane** — the primary user; they watch the list while an agent claims, updates, and closes items, and expect it to track the agent within a second or two.
  - *As an operator watching an agent work, when the agent updates or closes a work item, I want the Work Items list to reflect the change within ~2 s without me pressing `r`, so I can trust the list is current.*
  - *As an operator, when a burst of agent writes lands (claim + update + comment), I want the list to settle on the final state promptly without a refresh storm, so the pane does not thrash.*
- **Multi-pane / multi-agent setups** — several Herdr panes share one `.worklog`; each must react to writes without multiplying spawn churn or lock contention.
- **Herdr plugin and `wl` CLI maintainers** — need a detection path that is robust (fallback to polling), cheap when idle, and does not regress the existing zero-spawn-when-idle guarantee.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Event-driven detection ≤ 2 s:** After an agent completes a work-item write against the shared `.worklog`, the Herdr Work Items pane triggers a refresh within **2 s** (wall-clock, p95 over a representative run) via an event-driven watch on the cross-process DB-change signal (state counter and/or SQLite `worklog.db`/`-wal`), without waiting for the 30 s auto-refresh tick. Verified by an automated integration test that emulates a write and asserts a refresh is triggered within the bound, plus a manual note on a real agent write.
- **Idle no-op and fallback preserved:** When nothing has changed, the pane still spawns **zero** `wl` processes per tick and the 30 s auto-refresh tick remains the fallback (no stale-forever when the watch is unavailable). Watch events are debounced/coalesced so a burst of writes causes **at most one trailing refresh** (no refresh storm). Covered by automated tests (extending the WL-0MSJ1OLTL009N4IQ and WL-0MTIB7JAN004MQ8N guarantees).
- **End-to-end refresh ≤ 2 s:** Once triggered, a refresh of the default view attaches fresh data and renders within **2 s** wall-clock end-to-end on a representative dataset (≥ 1000 work items, ≥ 20 expanded children), measured by a repeatable benchmark and recorded in a manual verification note.
- **Input responsiveness non-regression:** Pane keyboard input stays responsive during and after the refresh (≤ 100 ms p95 input lag, consistent with WL-0MUY0RDBQ001H74P); the watch/refresh path must not block the TUI event loop. Covered by an automated responsiveness regression test that fails if the fix regresses.
- **Validation/testing criterion:** Automated unit + integration tests cover (a) the watch trigger and its debounce/coalescing, (b) the fallback to the 30 s tick when the watch is unavailable/fails open, and (c) the cold-refresh spawn-count reduction; a runnable performance benchmark is added to guard against regression.
- **Documentation criterion:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **Full suite criterion:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Do not regress the zero-spawn-when-idle guarantee** (WL-0MSJ1OLTL009N4IQ): with no DB change and a fresh sync heartbeat, a tick must still spawn nothing.
- **Preserve `doRefresh` single-flight + trailing-coalescing semantics** (WL-0MSBVYBMD004007C, WL-0MTIB7JAN004MQ8N); the watch must feed the existing gate, not bypass it.
- **Preserve visibility and typing gates:** hidden panes and open text-input overlays must still skip refresh work.
- **Fail open, never stale-forever:** any watch read error or `fs.watch` failure must fall back to the existing polling tick.
- **No new runtime dependencies** unless explicitly justified; prefer Node built-ins (`node:fs` watch).
- **No work-item data-semantics changes** and no change to `wl` write-path correctness (writes must never be served from, or leave behind, stale cache).
- **No regression for other `wl` read consumers** (Pi TUI, CLI scripts) when `wl` core is touched.
- **Cross-platform:** `fs.watch` behaviour differs by platform (Linux inotify, macOS FSEvents, Windows); the design must degrade gracefully where watching is unreliable.
- **Input responsiveness is currently acceptable** — the fix must not make the pane input-laggy.

## Existing state

- **`packages/herdr/src/db-change.ts`** — `DbChangeTracker` reads the cross-process monotonic state counter (`~/.cache/wl/state/<hash>.json`) to decide whether the DB changed since the last tick; the refresh/sync scheduler gates on it. Reads only — no watch today.
- **`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`** — `doRefresh` (~L5227) with single-flight + trailing coalescing; the scheduler `refresh` task (~L6444) gated by `isDbUnchanged` + visibility + typing; the `sync` task; the resume-poll; the event subscriber (only `pane_focused` today, no work-item-update event).
- **`packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts`** — consolidated tick loop (1 s base tick) dispatching due, non-in-flight, gate-approved tasks.
- **`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`** — `runWl` spawn path (binary `wl`/`worklog`), `DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS`, in-process in-flight memo (WL-0MSGAEPOJ002824S), `fetchNextItems` + `fetchMandatorySubsets` (2 extra `wl list`), `fetchActionableCount`, `fetchReviewQueueState`, `fetchChildrenForItem`.
- **`packages/herdr/src/index.ts`** — constructs the default `fetcher` (~L2258) and resolves the worklog dir handed to `fetcher.setWorklogDir`.
- **`src/read-cache.ts` / `src/read-cache-cli.ts`** — on-disk read cache keyed by (worklog-dir, argv, version) with WAL-aware fingerprint + state counter (`bumpStateCounter` on every write; `invalidateOnWrite`); TTL default 30 s. This is why an agent write invalidates the cache and makes the next refresh cold.
- **`src/persistent-store.ts` / `src/database.ts`** — the `wl next` / `wl list` compute path (N+1 fixes landed under WL-0MQFRY8TM006DIJ6).
- **Measurements (this machine):** `wl list` warm ≈ 0.45–0.65 s, `wl next -n 30 --include-in-progress` warm ≈ 0.4 s but cold ≈ 1.5 s; node startup ≈ 0.15 s. Default view spawns ~5 `wl` processes per refresh (next + 2 mandatory subsets + actionable count + review queue) plus one child fetch per expanded parent plus `herdr` CLI calls for agent icons. State cache dir currently holds ~175 k counter files; DB ≈ 97 MB.

## Desired change

1. **Event-driven detection.** Add a watch in the Herdr plugin on the cross-process change signal (the state-counter file and/or `worklog.db` + `-wal`) that wakes the existing scheduler/`doRefresh` path promptly (debounced) on an agent write, with the 30 s tick retained as fallback and the idle no-op preserved.
2. **Faster application.** Cut the end-to-end refresh cost on the cold path — reduce the number of `wl` spawns per refresh (e.g. consolidate the mandatory-subset/actionable-count/review-queue queries, or read the SQLite DB in-process for the pane), and/or speed up the cold `wl next`/`list` path in `wl` core (in scope). Ensure caches are warm or bypassed without a spawn storm.
3. **Wire-through.** Feed the watch into the existing gated, single-flight, coalesced `doRefresh`; keep visibility/typing gates and fail-open fallback.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/db-change.ts` — Add a watch API (e.g. `watchDbChanges`) alongside `DbChangeTracker`: watch the state-counter file (and/or `worklog.db`/`-wal`), debounce, emit a change callback; fail-open.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Wire the watch to the gated `doRefresh`; ensure debounce + single-flight/coalescing + visibility/typing gates; reduce spawn count in the refresh path.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts` — Register/integrate the watch trigger (or expose an immediate-run hook) without disturbing the tick model.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — Reduce/parallelise `wl` spawns for the default view; extend the in-flight memo; possibly add a low-latency read path.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — Construct/pass the watcher and worklog dir; teardown on pane exit.
- `src/read-cache.ts` / `src/read-cache-cli.ts` — Cache-hit/cold-path improvements (e.g. proactive warming or narrower invalidation) if needed to hit the target.
- `src/persistent-store.ts` / `src/database.ts` — Cold `wl next`/`list` performance (only if needed; keep data semantics unchanged).
- `packages/herdr/src/db-change.test.ts` (new/reused), `packages/herdr/src/worklist-inflight.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/hydrator-responsiveness.test.ts` (precedent) — tests.
- `bench/` (e.g. `bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts`) — repeatable refresh benchmark.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSJ1OLTL009N4IQ** — Herdr selection list: gate background/foreground sync on DB-update check before spawning wl commands. Introduced the `DbChangeTracker` + idle no-op we must preserve and build the watch on.
- **WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3** — Central cache for wl read results to cut Herdr refresh spawn churn. The on-disk read cache whose invalidation makes post-write refreshes cold.
- **WL-0MSGAEPOJ002824S** — In-process fetch memoization (F4 of the read-cache epic).
- **WL-0MSBVYBMD004007C** — Herdr worklist: in-flight guard to prevent overlapping refresh cycles.
- **WL-0MTIB7JAN004MQ8N** — Refresh trailing/coalescing to avoid refresh storms.
- **WL-0MUY0RDBQ001H74P** — Hydrate task timeouts cause HERDR UI to become unresponsive to commands. Precedent: bounded timeouts, stdio isolation, p95 input-lag < 100 ms; this item's responsiveness constraint mirrors it.
- **WL-0MUY1CZES0099A04** — Herdr: UI responsiveness regression test (child of the above).
- **WL-0MQFRY8TM006DIJ6** — Investigate and fix wl next performance bottlenecks. Prior work on the cold `wl next` path.
- **WL-0MSG8EG7P002MX2I** — Investigate WAL growth/checkpointing under concurrent writers. Relevant to watching `-wal` and to cold-read cost.
- **Pi-TUI precedents:** WL-0MKXN75CZ0QNBUJJ (*Auto-refresh TUI on DB write*), WL-0MQ3LYSPS006V60H (*TUI does not auto-refresh after CLI audit update*) — prior DB-write-triggered refresh in the sibling UI.
- **Automated find-related report** (find-related skill, keyword-based; embedded here so it survives description updates):

  **Related work items**
  - **WL-0MQOIBTHR002VMEK** – Add Guardrails to Protect Worklog Data Integrity (completed)
  - **WL-0MV16PXJ6003FEYT** – Rewrite README opening to lead with Herdr agent-orchestration role, then Worklog (completed)
  - **WL-0MLYEW3VB1GX4M8O** – Add closed count to GithubSyncResult and sync output (completed)

  **Repository file matches**
  - `standups/2026_10_10.md` — seed line for this work item
  - `packages/herdr/README.md` — Herdr plugin documentation
  - `CHANGELOG.md` — excluded from doc updates (managed by the release pipeline)

## Risks & assumptions

- **`fs.watch` reliability** — events can be dropped/coalesced and differ by platform/filesystem (NFS, containers). **Mitigation:** debounce, keep the 30 s tick as fallback, fail open, and test the fallback path explicitly.
- **Performance target is environment-dependent** — ≤ 2 s may be unachievable on a fully loaded host. **Mitigation:** pair the absolute target with a repeatable benchmark and a relative-improvement assertion so regression is caught regardless of host load; record a manual verification note.
- **Scope creep into `wl` core** — breadth is plugin + `wl` core, which can balloon. **Mitigation:** land the plugin-side win first; if `wl`-core work grows, split it into a child work item rather than expanding scope.
- **Watch overhead across many panes** — N watchers on one DB. **Assumption:** watching is cheap (one watcher per pane, debounced); if it proves costly, a shared watcher or heartbeat-based single-watcher can follow.
- **Correctness after write** — a watch must never serve stale data or race the write. **Mitigation:** reuse the existing state-counter/WAL fingerprint semantics; never bypass the DB-change check.
- **Assumption:** the cross-process state counter and SQLite `worklog.db`/`-wal` are the right watch targets; confirmed by reading `src/read-cache.ts`/`read-cache-cli.ts` and `packages/herdr/src/db-change.ts`.
- **Scope-creep risk (explicit):** any further opportunities discovered (e.g. reducing state-counter file count, WAL checkpointing) are recorded as linked work items, not absorbed here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: Which UI surface is in scope?** — Answer (user@rgardler, interactive): **A — Herdr plugin worklist pane only (`packages/herdr`)**. Source: interactive reply. Implication: the Pi TUI Worklog extension is out of scope; sibling TUI items are referenced as precedents only.
- **Q2: What is the primary symptom to fix?** — Answer (user@rgardler, interactive): **A — latency: the list takes too long to reflect an agent's change; pane input is currently responsive and must not regress**. Source: interactive reply. Implication: ACs target end-to-end latency; a responsiveness non-regression guard is included.
- **Q3: How far may the fix reach?** — Answer (user@rgardler, interactive): **B — Herdr plugin and the `wl` CLI/core**. Source: interactive reply. Implication: both the detection path (plugin) and the cold read path (`wl` core) may be changed; constraints protect other consumers.
- **Q4: What end-to-end target defines "snappy"?** — Answer (user@rgardler, interactive): **B — ≤ 2 s from agent write to list reflecting it**. Source: interactive reply. Implication: AC1/AC3 use 2 s as the measurable bound, paired with a benchmark and manual note because absolute timings are host-dependent.
- **Q5: How should the pane detect an agent's write?** — Answer (user@rgardler, interactive): **A — event-driven `fs.watch` on the cross-process state counter / SQLite WAL, keeping the 30 s tick as fallback**. Source: interactive reply. Implication: no `wl` write-path contract change is required; the existing `DbChangeTracker`/state-counter signal is reused as the watch target, with fail-open fallback.


## Plan: changelog

The r i (producer interview) fix added tab focus to run-in-pane.sh: a focused pane anchored to a work-item-ID tab now runs herdr tab focus before the pane zoom, because pane zoom alone cannot switch tabs.

shared/send-to-pi.sh has the same latent gap: its --focus path only runs pane zoom. Apply the same best-effort tab-focus (herdr pane get <pane> -> herdr tab focus) to send-to-pi.sh, mirroring run-in-pane.sh, with bash tests in packages/herdr/shared/tests/.

## Summary

Cross-repo fix for the 2026-09-26 leaked-`GIT_DIR` incident (SorraAgents
investigation SA-0MUIZSXEY008NGR8, evidence child SA-0MV0G9BF7008S01K).

Evidence: `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` in
`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` builds child environments with
`{ ...process.env, HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD, AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM }`. Any
repository-override git variable already present in the herdr process
(`GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_CONFIG*`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`,
`GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES`) is forwarded to every spawned pane
(`send-to-pi.sh` -> `run-pi-agent.sh` -> `pi` -> test subprocesses). Git
honours `GIT_DIR` over `cwd`, so a leaked value can redirect a `git` command
into the live checkout.

The SorraAgents side already scrubs these vars at every in-repo execution path
(SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX); this item removes the export at the launcher source, so
the in-repo scrub is not the only line of defence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` filters all repository-override variables from the forwarded environment (`GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_CONFIG`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`, `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM`, `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES`).
- [ ] `send-to-pi.sh` and/or `run-pi-agent.sh` unset the same variables as a shell-side defence layer.
- [ ] A ContextHub regression test asserts the spawn path's env contains no repository-override variables even when the parent process carries a poisoned `GIT_DIR`.
- [ ] Agent/test sessions spawned via herdr panes inherit no repository-override git variables.

## Evidence references

- SorraAgents parent: SA-0MUIZSXEY008NGR8.
- Reproducible tracer: `docs/dev/trace_git_env_propagation.py` (SorraAgents) — `spawn_forwards_overrides: true`, `hook_git_env: {GIT_EXEC_PATH, GIT_PREFIX}`.
- SorraAgents in-repo regression coverage (already green): `tests/test_repository_override_isolation.py`, `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py`.

## Key files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions`.
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh`, `packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`.

# Intake Brief — Rewrite README opening to lead with Herdr agent-orchestration role, then Worklog (WL-0MV16PXJ6003FEYT)

**Headline**: The README opens by calling the project "a lightweight, Git-friendly issue tracker", which mis-frames it. Rewrite the opening so it first presents the project as an extension for Herdr that manages and orchestrates teams of AI agents, then introduces Worklog as the issue tracker that doubles as project history/memory — giving each agent the context it needs for the job it is given.

## Problem statement

The project's README (`README.md`) currently leads with the issue-tracker framing: the H1 is `# Worklog` and the first sentence is "A lightweight, Git-friendly issue tracker designed for AI agents and development teams." This describes only the Worklog data layer and hides the project's primary value — it is a Herdr extension that manages and orchestrates teams of agents. A reader (or an agent onboarding from the README) is left thinking this is "just another issue tracker" and misses that the Worklog is the shared project memory which ensures agents receive the relevant context for the work they are dispatched.

## Users

- **Agent operators / team leads** running teams of agents who are deciding whether to adopt the project.
  - *As an agent operator, I want the README to tell me up-front that this is a Herdr extension for managing and orchestrating teams of agents, so I understand what problem it solves before I read about its data layer.*
- **New developers and agents onboarding to the project** who read the README as the entry point.
  - *As a new contributor/agent, I want the README to explain that Worklog is both an issue tracker and the project history, so I understand where agent context comes from.*
- **Existing users** who want a one-glance correct description when sharing/quoting the project.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The README opening (title area plus the descriptive paragraph(s) immediately preceding `## Features`) presents the project first as an **extension for Herdr** that assists with the **management and orchestration of teams of agents**; the description no longer *opens* with the issue-tracker framing.
2. Immediately afterwards, the README describes **Worklog** as (a) the issue tracker and (b) a **project history / context source** that ensures agents get the relevant context for the job they are given — explicitly linking the tracker to agent context rather than listing it as a standalone tool.
3. The existing README structure and content below the opening (Features, Installation, Quick Start, documentation index, Tutorials, Shell Completion, Development, License) remain intact; no existing documentation links are broken.
4. Capability claims in the new lede are accurate against the code/manifest: `packages/herdr/herdr-plugin.toml` and `packages/herdr/README.md` (agent dispatch, downtime worker, hydrator, ship-mode guard, audit/code-freeze orchestration) support the "management and orchestration of teams of agents" framing.
5. The reworded opening uses UK English spelling and stays concise (a short lede, not a new long section).
6. Testing/validation: a reviewer runs a markdown link/reference check over `README.md` (relative links resolve) and confirms by inspection that the issue-tracker-first sentence is gone and the new lede is present; `git diff` shows the change is scoped to the opening (plus any directly related wording).
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Documentation-only change** — no code behaviour changes, no new dependencies.
- **Preserve existing valid content** — the rest of the README (features list, install, quick start, docs index) must not be removed; earlier work (WL-0MM1NDLXT0BP8S83) deliberately slimmed the README, so do not re-expand it into a long architecture page.
- **Accuracy** — do not over-claim orchestration capabilities that the code does not provide; anchor wording to the Herdr plugin manifest and its docs.
- **UK English** spelling throughout (per project conventions).
- Keep the H1 and product naming consistent with the rest of the repo (package name `worklog`, plugin id `worklog-selection-list`); renaming the product is out of scope unless confirmed.

## Existing state

- `README.md` line 1: `# Worklog`; lines 3: "A lightweight, Git-friendly issue tracker designed for AI agents and development teams. Track hierarchical work items with a CLI or REST API -- all backed by SQLite with JSONL-based Git syncing."
- `README.md` `## Features` list currently leads with "CLI + API" and "Git-Friendly Syncing", with agent/orchestration features (Pi agent plugin modules, Heartbeat Skill) lower in the list.
- `README.md` later contains a "Pi agent plugin" section describing the extension and its relationship to the Herdr plugin (`packages/herdr/`).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` documents the Herdr plugin (`worklog-selection-list`) in depth: work-item browse/filter/select, Pi agent pane dispatch, downtime worker (idle local-LLM dispatch), hydrator (self-healing `in_progress` claims), mode-switch worker, ship-mode guard, Code Freeze, agent-status tracking.
- `packages/herdr/herdr-plugin.toml` declares the plugin `id = "worklog-selection-list"` — "Browse, filter, and select Worklog work items from a Herdr pane."
- The repo/remote is `TheWizardsCode/ContextHub` while the npm package is `worklog`; the README title remains `Worklog`. Product naming/rename is not assumed here.

## Desired change

1. Rewrite the opening of `README.md` (the H1 area and the paragraph(s) before `## Features`) so it:
   - leads with the Herdr-extension framing — a tool that assists with the management and orchestration of teams of **agents**;
   - then introduces **Worklog** as the issue tracker **and** the project history that gives each agent the relevant context for the job it is given.
2. Reorder/retune the top of the `## Features` list (if needed) so the agent-orchestration capabilities are surfaced before low-level transport details (CLI/API, Git sync). Keep all existing feature bullets.
3. Keep the rest of the README unchanged; only touch wording that directly conflicts with the new framing (e.g. the Pi agent plugin section wording if it still reads as an add-on rather than the core).
4. Update any cross-references elsewhere that quote the old README description, if any are found.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `README.md` — Primary file: rewrite the opening description and (optionally) reorder the top feature bullets.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Source of truth for Herdr orchestration capability claims; may need a one-line alignment if the framing changes.
- `packages/herdr/herdr-plugin.toml` — Manifest describing the plugin; verify lede accuracy against it.
- `package.json` — `"description": "A simple experimental issue tracker for AI agents"` may also need re-framing (verify whether in scope).
- `AGENTS.md` — Project onboarding text; check the opening description aligns (only edit if it states the same issue-tracker-first framing).

## Related work

- **WL-0MM1NDLXT0BP8S83** — "README Revamp and Content Relocation" (completed): established the slim README structure and documentation index this change builds on; do not undo its slimming.
- **WL-0MUYI3KPB0024U86** — "Docs: interactive item-ID-tab placement": most recent README-touching work; confirms docs for the Herdr plugin live alongside the main README.
- **WL-0MULILQ770097DXF** — "Docs: Update documentation": prior documentation update precedent.
- **`packages/herdr/README.md`** — authoritative description of the Herdr plugin's management/orchestration features referenced by the new lede.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk**: a README framing change can pull in every doc that mentions the project. **Mitigation**: keep the change to the README opening plus directly-conflicting wording; record any further doc re-framing as separate linked work items rather than expanding scope.
- **Accuracy risk**: over-claiming orchestration (e.g. implying autonomy the code lacks). **Mitigation**: anchor every capability claim to `packages/herdr/README.md` / `herdr-plugin.toml`.
- **Assumption**: the product/title remains `Worklog`; only the *description* is re-framed. If a rename to a distinct project name is intended, that is a separate decision recorded as an open question.
- **Assumption**: the "management and orchestration of teams of agents" framing refers to the Herdr plugin's dispatching/hydration/downtime/ship features (not a separate unreleased component).
- **Low regression risk**: docs-only change; the mandated full test suite guards against accidental code impact.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1**: "Should the README lead with the Herdr extension framing and then describe Worklog as issue tracker + project history?" — Answer (user@rgardler): "Yes — lead with the fact that it is an extension for Herdr which assists with the management and orchestration of teams of agents. Then describe the Worklog which is the issue tracker but also provides a project history to ensure agents get the relevant context for the job they are given." Source: interactive seed intent (this request). Priority set to `high` by the operator.
- **Q2**: "Is the product name changing (e.g. to ContextHub), or only the description?" — **OPEN QUESTION** for the producer. The repo/remote is `TheWizardsCode/ContextHub` while the package and README H1 are `Worklog`. **Recommended:** keep the `Worklog` title and re-frame only the description — a rename touches npm, CLI, plugin id and docs and is a much larger change.
- **Q3**: "Should capability claims be sourced strictly from the Herdr plugin docs?" — Answer (agent inference / research): Yes. Research: `packages/herdr/README.md` and `packages/herdr/herdr-plugin.toml` document agent-pane dispatch, downtime worker, hydrator, mode-switch worker, ship-mode guard and Code Freeze; these are the accurate basis for the "management and orchestration of teams of agents" claim.


## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSIXMKOX0052514** – Align wl init with SorraAgents install: delegate agent-guidance/workflow setup instead of duplicating (completed)
- **WL-0MSB3NYMW008APQC** – Tests: pane visibility detection module (visibility.test.ts) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: agent, agents, also, context, currently (+20 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: agent, agents, also, context, ensuring (+18 more)

# Herdr selection list: base the in-progress marker on work-item pane existence

## Problem statement

The "in progress" marker shown in the Herdr selection list is unreliable: it is
derived from the worklog `in-progress` status, which is maintained by the
hydrator — a self-healing loop that decides whether a claimed item is genuinely
being worked on. Every interactive/downtime dispatch now spawns an agent pane
whose **title carries the exact work-item ID** as a preserved trailing suffix
(`pane-title.ts`, `truncatePaneTitlePreservingSuffix`). The hydrator's active
detection must be a single simple rule: if there is a pane in this workspace
with the work item id (as part of) its title the item is being worked on; if
there is no such pane it is not.

> Producer review (2026-10-16): "This isn't reliable at present. review the
> algorith. It should be simple. Look for a pane in this workspace with the work
> item id as the title. If it exists then work item is busy. If it doesn't then
> it is not busy."
>
> An earlier revision matched the exact **label** of a workspace **tab**
> (`herdr tab list`). That proved unreliable: tabs are created by the dispatcher
> *anchor* as a placement side effect, so an item being dispatched can be
> evaluated before its tab exists (a false-demotion race), and tabs can be
> re-parented or renamed. Pane **titles** are set at spawn time, always carry
> the item ID as a preserved suffix, and survive re-parenting — matching them
> is the reliable signal this work item implements.

## Users

- Herdr operator selecting the next work item from the selection list.
- Downtime dispatcher / plugin panes that rely on the hydrator to release stale
  `in-progress` claims so the item re-enters the dispatchable pool.

Example user stories:

- As a Herdr operator, I want the selection list's in-progress marker to reflect
  reality — an item is "being worked on" iff a pane in my workspace has the
  work-item ID in its title — so I can trust the list without opening panes.
- As a dispatched agent, I want my claimed item left `in-progress` for as long
  as my work-item pane is open, so my claim is never released underneath me.
- As an operator, I want a stale claim (no work-item pane) released
  automatically and periodically so abandoned items return to the dispatchable
  pool.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An item is treated as actively worked **iff** a pane in the current
      workspace (`HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, or `herdr pane list --workspace <id>`)
      has a title **containing** the work-item ID (the dispatched pane titles
      always carry the ID as a preserved suffix). A pane title with no work-item
      ID contributes nothing. Verified by unit tests over a pure
      pane-title-matching helper.
- [ ] **Green-circle indicator (producer directive 2026-10-17):** the
      selection list's green circle (the second icon of the row prefix) is
      ALSO pane-title existence — it appears exactly when a pane in the
      current workspace carries the work-item ID in its title and never
      otherwise, independent of the pane's live agent status. The icon is
      stamped/cleared by the same pane-marker pass
      (`markItemsActiveByPane` sets/removes `agentState`), refreshed on the
      initial load, every refresh, the 30 s hydrator cadence, focus-resume,
      and pane lifecycle events (`pane_agent_status_changed` /
      `pane_agent_detected` / `pane_closed` / `pane_exited` → pane-list
      re-check). Verified by `hydrator.test.ts`,
      `worklist-active-pane-marker.test.ts` and the rewritten
      `worklist-agent-state-event.test.ts` (no `herdr agent list` exec in the
      icon path; the old ⛔/⚪ event-driven agent-state flips are retired).
- [ ] The hydrator's active detection is `herdr pane list --workspace <id>` +
      pane-title ID extraction; the pane-matching seam/types (`HydratorPane`,
      `listActivePanes`, `collectPaneWorkItemIds`, `isActivePaneMatch`) are used.
      Verified by code review + updated `hydrator.test.ts` (a `herdr pane list`
      spawn asserted; no `herdr tab list` spawn for active detection).
- [ ] Demotion rules are unchanged: a non-active item at stage `in_review` →
      `completed`/`in_review`; a non-active item with an active outbound blocker
      → `blocked`; otherwise → `open` (stage repaired to a compatible value). An
      item with a matching pane is never demoted. Verified by unit tests.
- [ ] The signal is refreshed periodically from the selection list: the existing
      30 s hydrate task (`HYDRATOR_INTERVAL_MS`) and the hidden→visible
      focus-resume hook both re-evaluate pane existence, so a closed work-item
      pane clears the marker within one cadence and an opened pane keeps it.
      Verified by existing scheduler/visibility tests plus a pane-based
      hydration test.
- [ ] Fail-open preserved: an unavailable/unparseable `herdr pane list` aborts
      the cycle without demoting, and panes outside the current workspace never
      mark an item active. Verified by unit tests.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, README, and any relevant docs site entries (notably the
      hydrator module header and the `pane-title.ts` rationale comment).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Do not change the worklog status/stage vocabulary or the demotion outcome
  rules.
- Keep the bounded/responsive hydrator contract (per-step timeout, per-tick
  cap, stdio isolation, fail-open) unchanged; only the "which items are active"
  lookup changes.
- Reuse the existing pane parsing/seam where possible rather than adding a
  second parser for the same CLI shape.
- Retain exports still used elsewhere: `extractWorkItemIdsFromText`
  (`ship-guard.ts`) and `isActiveBlocker` (`stalled-work.ts`).
- No CLI or socket API change; `herdr pane list` is already used by the plugin.
- Write in UK English; follow the project's test/build conventions.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — fetches `wl list --status in-progress`,
  fetches live panes (`herdr pane list [--workspace <id>]`), collects work-item
  IDs from pane titles (`collectPaneWorkItemIds`), and demotes items with no
  matching pane. Exposes pure helpers (`collectPaneWorkItemIds`,
  `isActivePaneMatch`, `decideDemotion`, `compatibleStage`, `isActiveBlocker`).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — creates the hydrator runner with
  `workspaceId: process.env.HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, runs it every 30 s (`hydrate`
  task) and on hidden→visible focus-resume. The selection list's in-progress
  marker (`statusIcon(item.status)`) and Group N ordering (`status ===
  'in-progress'`) are driven by the worklog status this loop maintains plus the
  pane-based display marker (`applyActivePaneMarkers`).
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-title.ts` — truncation helpers that preserve the
  work-item ID as a trailing suffix so the pane-title match is always reliable.

## Desired change

The hydrator's "is this item active" signal is pane-title existence:

1. A pure helper returns the set of work-item IDs present in the current
   workspace's pane titles (`collectPaneWorkItemIds(tabs)` /
   `isActivePaneMatch(itemId, panes)`).
2. `HydratorDeps.listActivePanes(workspaceId)` is backed by
   `herdr pane list --workspace <id>`.
3. `runHydrationOnce` uses pane membership; `decideDemotion`,
   `compatibleStage`, `isActiveBlocker`, `extractWorkItemIdsFromText` and the
   bounded-run machinery are unchanged.
4. Tests and the module/doc comments describe pane-title detection.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — pane-title matching seam/types/helpers.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — hydrator wiring (workspace id, cadence,
  focus-resume, `active-pane-marker` task).
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts` — pane-title cases; exact, workspace-
  scope and fail-open cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.fixtures.ts` — pane fixtures + `pane list` exec
  router answer.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator-responsiveness.test.ts` — updated to the
  pane-based deps.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-title.ts` — rationale comment for tile-title
  detection.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `applyActivePaneMarkers` production wiring.

## Related work

- WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI — Herdr hydrator: rescue `in_progress` work items with no
  active pane (parent of the hydrator design).
- WL-0MTF5WO2Q008B8US — Hydrator: demote stale `in_progress` items.
- WL-0MUY1CXSV008F8TZ / WL-0MUY1CYCB003DTKO / WL-0MUY1CYV6008BQWX — bounded/
  isolated hydrate steps (contract to preserve).
- WL-0MUKXFWLD006A8XI / WL-0MUYI3JAO002BTNL — item-ID tab anchor and dispatch
  wiring (tab-per-item convention; panes inherit the ID-titled anchor).
- WL-0MUY1CS9E006ZLS0 — re-based Herdr in-progress UI behaviour on `status`.
- WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9 — per-row agent-status icon (separate feature).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (scope):** "the logic for discovering when an item is being
  worked on" is the hydrator's active detection; the selection-list in-progress
  marker follows from the status the hydrator maintains plus the injected
  pane-title display marker.
- **Assumption:** pane titles carry the exact work-item ID as a trailing suffix
  for every dispatch path (manual, shell, downtime builders), so a
  contains-match is correct and robust; no substring false positives because the
  ID token is matched exactly.
- **Assumption:** `herdr pane list --workspace <id>` returns
  `result.panes[].label` (the pane title), as parsed by the shared
  `parseMachinePaneListOutput`; no new herdr capability is required.
- **Risk:** a pane may outlive its agent (kept open after the agent finishes),
  leaving an item `in-progress`. This matches the requested rule (pane = worked
  on); operators close the pane to release the item.
- **Scope-creep risk:** sharing the signal with `AgentTracker` or the
  agent-status icon is a linked follow-up item, not part of this change.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-10 — Created three children (core/verification/docs) and wired
  dependency edges.
- 2026-10-14 — Producer directed tab-label exact matching
  (commit 73463773).
- 2026-10-16 — Producer rejected the tab-label formulation as unreliable and
  directed pane-title matching: "Look for a pane in this workspace with the
  work item id as the title. If it exists then work item is busy." Rework
  updated the hydrator (tab-label → pane-title), the marker, tests, fixtures
  and docs accordingly.

data.description:
## Overview

Switch the Herdr hydrator's "is this item actively worked?" detection from
pane-title ID matching to **exact tab-label** matching, and migrate the existing
unit tests so the package still builds and tests green at the end of this item.

This is the core vertical slice: source + the structural test migration.

## Changes

### Type changes (`packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts`)
- Replace `HydratorPane` with `HydratorTab`: `{ tab_id: string; label: string }`.
- Replace `HydratorDeps.listActivePanes` with `HydratorDeps.listTabs(workspaceId)`:
  `Promise<HydratorTab[] | null>`.
- Replace `isActivePaneMatch` with `hasItemTab(itemId, tabs, workspaceId?): boolean`.

### Pure helper changes
- Replace `collectPaneWorkItemIds(panes, workspaceId?)` with
  `collectTabWorkItemIds(tabs, workspaceId?)`:
  - returns the set of tab labels that are valid work-item IDs (exact labels);
  - tabs outside the current workspace are excluded (same scoping contract);
  - tabs whose label is not a work-item ID (e.g. `Work Items`, `Downtime`) are
    ignored.
- Replace `isActivePaneMatch(itemId, panes, workspaceId?)` with
  `hasItemTab(itemId, tabs, workspaceId?)` using
  `collectTabWorkItemIds(tabs, workspaceId).has(itemId)`.

### Orchestration changes

# Fix test churn analysis status detection and rewrite-ratio denominator

## Defects found in scripts/test_churn_analysis.py (delivered by WL-0MUZRNLFT004H8XJ)

### Defect 1 - File status is hardcoded to M
get_commit_diffs builds every FileChange with status=M and never consults git name-status. Consequences: commits_with_new_tests reported as 0 (actual 340, 20.4%); new_files always 0; analyse_test_first_signal status=A branches never fire, so the 86.0% test-first figure is invalid (it is co-evolution).

### Defect 2 - Rewrite-ratio denominator excludes pure-addition modifications
Correct denominators: deletions/(deletions+additions) over modified test files = 9968/92349 = 10.8%; including new test-file additions (232026) = 3.1%. Reported 21.1% overstates.

### Defect 3 - Temporal rate can exceed 100 percent
feature_commits_with_rewrites counts rewrite events not distinct commits; 2026-05 = 108.6% is not a commit percentage.

### Defect 4 - domain_churn double counts source files
adds len(src files) once per file in commit, inflating counts (section 11 unreliable).

## Acceptance criteria
1. Status detection uses real git name-status (A/M/D/R/T) with a test asserting A vs M.
2. Rewrite ratio computed with documented denominators; report modified-only and including-new-files variants.
3. Temporal rate counts distinct commits with at least one rewrite event.
4. domain_churn counts each file once.
5. Re-run and correct scripts/TEST_CHURN_REPORT.md and scripts/test_churn_data.json.
6. Unit tests cover each fixed function.

## Impact
Corrects AC1/AC2/AC3 evidence on the parent. Qualitative conclusion (tests mostly grow rather than get rewritten) stands; the 21.1% and 86% figures are wrong.

The single largest test file in the repository (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`, 13,103 lines) dominates 10% of the entire test suite with 100 describe blocks, 664 `vi.fn()` calls, and 107 mainline commits. 2. **Shared fixtures/helpers.** A shared fixture module replaces duplicated per-test setup. No test re-implements another group's setup.

3. **Mock budget enforced.** A per-test mock cap is agreed and enforced — either via a lint/CI check (failing tests exceeding N `vi.fn()`/mock declarations) or equivalent mechanism — and the limit is documented. The cap value N is determined from analysis of existing test mock density.

4. **Observable-outcome assertions (DEFERRED — producer decision).** Assertions prefer observable outcomes over `toHaveBeenCalledWith` on internal collaborators, per SorraAgents `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`. 5. **All tests pass, no coverage lost.** All moved tests still pass in the new file locations. Any assertions deliberately dropped are justified and documented on the work item.

6. **Runtime measured.** Suite runtime for this module is measured before and after splitting, and the results are reported as a comment on the work item.

## Constraints

- Do not change production code.
- Do not lose test coverage — every existing test must be preserved unless deliberately dropped (with justification).

- File names should follow existing conventions (e.g. `downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts`).

## Desired change

Split the monolithic file into concern-specific files, introduce a shared fixture module, enforce a mock budget per test, and migrate assertions toward observable outcomes where feasible.

# `wl delete` lost-update: concurrent `wl sync` clobbers in-flight soft delete

Concrete instance of the store-lock lost-update gap tracked by WL-0MUVSQ4EO00092E7.

## Problem

`wl delete <id>...` soft-deletes work items via `db.delete()` (sets `deletedBy` and `deleteReason`), then triggers an auto-sync to push the deletion to remote. The delete loop does **not** hold the store mutation lock. When `wl sync` runs concurrently, its load → merge → write-back can restore a deleted item (the sync's stale snapshot still has the item, and the merge layer prefers the sync's `updatedAt`).

Additionally, `wl delete` triggers an auto-sync after the delete loop — this is a nested sync triggered from inside a mutation. `withFileLock` is reentrant per process, so wrapping the delete in `withStoreMutationLock` must not deadlock the auto-sync.

## Evidence

No production incidents known yet (but `wl delete` is a lifecycle command that may be used during release cleanup, where concurrent `wl sync` is plausible).

## Desired behaviour

1. `wl delete` acquires `withStoreMutationLock` across the entire delete loop.
2. The auto-sync that runs after the delete loop is verified not to deadlock (reentrancy guarantee).
3. A concurrency regression test proves a delete that lands during a concurrent `wl sync` read-modify-write survives.
4. `--no-sync` flag is unaffected.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl delete` acquires the store mutation lock for the duration of the delete loop.
2. A concurrency regression test proves a delete that lands during a concurrent `wl sync` read-modify-write is not lost (item remains deleted).
3. `--no-sync` flag behaviour is unchanged.
4. Existing `wl delete` tests pass.

## Notes

- `src/commands/delete.ts` — wrap the delete loop in `withStoreMutationLock`.
- Auto-sync: `src/commands/delete.ts:206-234` calls `performSync` after the loop. Reentrancy of `withFileLock` must be confirmed.
- Parent: WL-0MUVSQ4EO00092E7.
- Precedent: WL-0MUV2U9QF002S9J1 (wl update, comment add, audit-set).
data.title: wl delete lost-update: concurrent wl sync clobbers in-flight soft delete (item reappears)

# `wl create` lost-update: concurrent `wl sync` clobbers newly created work items

`wl create` creates new work items via `db.createWithNextSortIndex()`, optionally saves an audit result (`db.saveAuditResult()`), and may demote a parent (`db.demoteParentOnChildAdded()`). 1. `wl create` acquires `withStoreMutationLock` across the create + audit + demotion.
2. A concurrency regression test proves a create that lands during a concurrent `wl sync` read-modify-write survives.
3. No behavioural change to create semantics otherwise.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl create` acquires the store mutation lock across the item creation, audit result, and parent demotion.
2. A concurrency regression test proves a create that lands during a concurrent `wl sync` read-modify-write is not lost.
3. Existing `wl create` tests pass.

## Notes

- `src/commands/create.ts` - wrap the action in `withStoreMutationLock`.
- Parent: WL-0MUVSQ4EO00092E7.

## Problem statement

The monolithic `downtime-worker.test.ts` has 664 `vi.fn()` calls spread across 100 describe blocks. After splitting, each test file should have a bounded number of mocks per test to improve test clarity and maintainability.

## Analysis

From analysis of the existing file:
- Total `vi.fn()` calls: ~664 across ~128 describe blocks
- Average: ~5.2 `vi.fn()` per describe block
- The `makeDeps()` fixture creates ~20 default mocks per call (excluded from per-test count — these are shared infrastructure)

1. **Mock cap determined.** Based on the analysis above, agree on a per-test mock cap N. Suggested: **5 `vi.fn()` overrides per test** (excluding the ~20 default mocks from `makeDeps()`). This is a reasonable cap for focused tests.

2. **Enforcement mechanism implemented.** Choose one of:

3. **All split test files comply.** Every new test file respects the mock budget. Tests exceeding the cap are refactored (e.g., by extracting more setup into the fixture module).

# Resume model-exhausted jobs instead of switching to cheap

**Issue type:** feature · **Priority:** medium · **Stage:** intake (draft)

## Problem statement

When the llm-proxy rejects requests with "all providers exhausted",
"all providers unavailable", or "no provider is available during the current
scheduled time window" (HTTP 503), the in-pane recovery loop classifies the
error as a retryable `SERVER_ERROR` and waits out the server-requested
`Retry-After`. While a pane sits in that backoff it holds **no** proxy slot,
so the proxy reports idle and the herdr mode-switch worker flips the shared
proxy to **cheap** on the operator idle window. Cheap mode has *more* slots
than fast (3 vs 1 — `WL-0MUWF763Q003MGUM`), so it adds concurrency, and cheap
windows are observed to correlate with exhaustion bursts. Nothing durably
records that a work item is waiting *because the model was unavailable*, so
neither the cheap-switch decision nor the dispatcher can see the difference
between "quiet" and "blocked on a throttled provider".

## Users

- **Operator/producer** running unattended (downtime) dispatch overnight, who
  wants queued work to resume as soon as a model returns, without piling new
  concurrent requests onto an already-exhausted provider pool.
- **Herdr downtime dispatcher**, which must know when a waiting job is
  eligible to resume and must not spawn more work while the pool is throttled.

Example user stories:

- As an operator, when cloud providers are exhausted, I want the proxy to stay
  in fast mode (or at least not add concurrency) so that my queued jobs do not
  exhaust the pool further.
- As the downtime dispatcher, when a model cooldown elapses, I want to resume
  exactly one waiting pane with a `continue` message rather than opening a
  brand-new pane.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Durable cooldown record.** When a pane's recovery loop
      classifies a model-unavailable error (`SERVER_ERROR` exhaustion
      patterns) and starts a backoff, a durable, machine-readable record is
      written carrying item id, kind, reason, and `cooldownUntil`; it is
      cleared on the next successful provider response. Verified by unit tests
      of the writer/reader and a write→read→clear round-trip test.
- [ ] **AC2 — Cheap-switch gate.** While at least one active model-cooldown
      exists (`cooldownUntil` in the future), the downtime leader's
      `mode-switch-worker.tick()` does **not** POST `cheap`; the hold is
      bounded by `cooldownUntil` (no latch) and the fast-on-command path is
      unaffected. Verified by mode-switch-worker unit tests (cooldown present
      / expired / absent / unreadable).
- [ ] **AC3 — Bounded wake.** At/after `cooldownUntil`, the dispatcher resumes
      **at most one** model-cooldown job via the existing stalled-resume path
      (literal `continue` to a live pane, or relaunch pi `--continue` in an
      exited pane), reusing the attempt-cap and `needsProducerReview`
      exclusions. Verified by dispatcher/stalled-work tests.
- [ ] **AC4 — Cross-root gate.** A cooldown recorded in any worklog root
      suppresses the machine-wide (shared-proxy) cheap switch. Verified by an
      integration test spanning two roots.
- [ ] **AC5 — Fail-closed and bounded default.** An unreadable/absent signal
      never causes a premature cheap switch (existing fail-closed contract
      preserved); an absent/unparseable `Retry-After` yields a **bounded**
      default cooldown rather than an unbounded hold. Verified by tests.
- [ ] **AC6 — Tests.** Unit + integration tests cover detection, gating, wake,
      cross-root, and failure paths; a regression test proves the previous
      client-side drain is **not** reintroduced (no slot-count completion
      gate, no dispatch pause, no unbounded latch).
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect
      the changes, including code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md`,
      `docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md`, and `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.
- [ ] **AC8 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new
      changes.

## Constraints

- **Must not reintroduce the withdrawn client drain** (`WL-0MUWIHUL2000JEFR`):
  no client-side slot-count completion gate, no dispatch pause, no unbounded
  latch. The proxy's own server-side bounded drain is unchanged and stays
  authoritative.
- The cheap-switch gate is **bounded by `cooldownUntil`**; it must never block
  the fast-on-command path (`onOperatorCommand`).
- Live pool sizing is fast = 1 slot, cheap = 3 slots
  (`WL-0MUWF763Q003MGUM`), i.e. cheap *increases* concurrency; the gate's only
  purpose is to avoid adding concurrency during known provider exhaustion.
- The mode-switch worker is leader-only and machine-wide, so the cooldown
  signal must be machine-wide for cross-root correctness.
- First increment must not require a new proxy endpoint; a proxy
  provider-availability endpoint is a **follow-up**, not in scope.
- The recovery loop lives in the TUI extension and the consumer in the herdr
  package, so the on-disk signal format is a cross-package contract and must
  be versioned/tolerant (unknown fields ignored).

## Existing state

- **Detection exists, but is ephemeral.** `error-patterns.ts` classifies the
  exhaustion bodies as `SERVER_ERROR`; `resolveRetryDelay()` /
  `parseRetryAfterHeaders()` (`retry-logic.ts`) extract the server-requested
  delay (ceiling 6 h) and `register-recovery.ts:406` computes it. The result
  lives only in in-memory `RetryState`.
- **No durable model-cooldown state.** The rolling
  `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` (`downtime-log.ts`) has dispatch markers
  and pane-close `reasonCode`s but no cooldown entry; the worklog
  `needsProducerReview` flag is unrelated.
- **Wake machinery already exists.** `classifyStalledPane` /
  `resumeStalledPane` (`stalled-work.ts`) prompt a live pane with the literal
  `continue`, or relaunch pi `--continue` in an exited pane, and the
  dispatcher already prefers resuming a stalled pane over opening a new one
  (`WL-0MUMA5OMH0024PN1`). Its trigger is "not working ≥ threshold", gated by
  the non-terminal cooldown and attempt cap — with **no model-availability
  input**.
- **The cheap path is blind.** `mode-switch-worker.tick()` switches to cheap on
  `operator idle ≥ threshold AND evaluateIdle(proxyStatus)`; a pane in backoff
  holds zero slots, so this looks idle.
- **The proxy cannot report exhaustion today.** `LlamaStatus`
  (`/llama/local/status`) exposes local server/slot/lease state only; there is
  no provider-availability field.

## Desired change

1. **Emit/clear a durable cooldown marker.** On `SERVER_ERROR` exhaustion in
   `register-recovery.ts`, write a record with `cooldownUntil = now + delayMs`
   (item id, kind, reason), machine-wide so any root can read it; clear it when
   `createRetryHintCapturingFetch` observes the next 2xx.
2. **Gate the cheap switch.** Read the marker in the leader's `tick()` (same
   pattern as `readSharedActivity`); while any cooldown is active, hold fast.
3. **Wake one job at expiry.** Feed expired cooldown candidates into the
   existing stalled-resume path so exactly one pane is resumed.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/shared/src/model-cooldown.ts` — the versioned cooldown contract and
  tolerant reader/writer shared by both packages (new).
- `packages/shared/src/model-cooldown.test.ts` — contract tests (new).
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts` — coordination-dir resolver
  (delegates to the shared resolver; single source of truth).
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts` — writes
  the cooldown marker on `SERVER_ERROR`, clears it on the next 2xx.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-logic.ts` — exposes the
  resolved cooldown (`cooldownUntil`).
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-patterns.ts` — bounded
  default cooldown in the recovery configuration.
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts` — reads the cooldown signal and
  gates the cheap switch.
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.test.ts` — gate unit tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/stalled-work.ts` — expired-cooldown candidate source.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — dispatcher branch that resumes one
  cooldown candidate at expiry.
- `docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`,
  `packages/herdr/README.md` — behaviour and contract documentation.

**Corrections from the predicted list (plan time):**
`packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` is **dropped** — the signal is
machine-wide, not the per-root dispatch log (decision Q2 = A). The bounded
default lives in the recovery configuration in the TUI extension (which owns
the cooldown computation), not in `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts`; herdr only
reads the resulting signal.

## Risks and assumptions

- **R: Waking before providers return just re-fails** and burns the per-item
  attempt budget until `needsProducerReview` trips. **Mitigation:** gate the
  wake strictly on `cooldownUntil`; prefer a proxy provider-availability
  signal when one exists (follow-up).
- **R: The premise is unproven.** Cheap mode may help (local-first) or hurt
  (more concurrency) depending on why providers are exhausted.
  **Mitigation:** RESOLVED BY DECISION — the producer accepted the premise
  (interview round 2, Q1 = B): the cooldown machinery is built without a Phase 0
  log-mining gate, so this risk remains open and accepted, not mitigated.
- **R: `Retry-After` may be absent**, making the cooldown best-effort.
  **Mitigation:** bounded default cooldown setting; document best-effort.
- **R: Cross-root staleness** — a crashed pane leaves a stale marker.
  **Mitigation:** `cooldownUntil` TTL + clear-on-success + fail-closed reads.
- **R: Scope creep** into proxy (cross-repo) changes. **Mitigation:** record
  proxy endpoint work as a linked follow-up, not in this item.
- **A1 (VERIFIED at plan time):** the recovery loop can extract the item
  id/kind from `ctx` session entries best-effort. Verified: the TUI extension
  has no herdr import and no pane-label access, so the marker is keyed by
  `paneId`/`sessionId` (plus a best-effort `itemId`) and the dispatcher resolves
  item and kind from the pane label it already reads for the stalled scan. See
  "Plan-time verification".
- **A2 (CONFIRMED by decision Q2 = A):** a machine-wide JSON file in the
  coordination directory (`~/.herdr/downtime/`, alongside `mode-activity.json`)
  is the transport for the first increment, implemented as a versioned shared
  contract (`@worklog/shared/model-cooldown`).

## Decisions (interview round 2 — resolved)

Producer answers recorded 2026-10-12 in the plan session (session id in the
work-item comments):

1. **Build now vs investigate first → BUILD NOW (option B).** The cooldown
   machinery is built without a Phase 0 log-mining gate; the operator accepts
   that "cheap windows worsen exhaustion" is not yet proven. Consequence: no
   investigation gate in the plan; the premise risk stays open and is recorded
   in the appendix. There is therefore **no Phase 0 gate child**.
2. **Cooldown signal source → CLIENT RECOVERY-LOOP MARKER (option A).** The TUI
   recovery loop writes and clears a versioned, machine-wide JSON marker in the
   machine coordination directory (`HERDR_COORDINATION_DIR` or
   `~/.herdr/downtime/`, alongside `mode-activity.json`), best-effort from
   `Retry-After`. A proxy provider-availability endpoint is a separate
   follow-up, not in scope.
3. **Wake trigger → STRICTLY AT/AFTER `cooldownUntil`, ONE JOB PER CYCLE
   (option A).** The wake reuses the existing stalled-resume path and its
   safety gates (attempt cap, `needsProducerReview`); no early wake and no
   batch wake.

**Plan-time verification of assumption A1:** the TUI recovery loop has no
herdr import and no pane-label access, so it cannot derive `itemId`/`kind`
from the pane label. The marker therefore carries `cooldownUntil`, `reason`,
`paneId` (`HERDR_PANE_ID`) and `sessionId`, with `itemId` derived best-effort
from session entries (`ctx.sessionManager.getEntries()`); the herdr dispatcher
resolves `itemId` + `kind` from the pane label it already reads for the stalled
scan (`paneLabelItemId`, `downtime-worker.ts`). The record format is versioned
JSON with unknown fields ignored.


## Plan (features)

Decomposed 2026-10-12 into 7 vertical-slice child items, created test-first
(the contract slice first, then the behaviour slices, then documentation and
verification). No Phase 0 investigation gate (decision Q1 = B).

| 1 | `WL-0MV563825002R9Y1` Cooldown signal contract and tolerant reader | task | — | AC1, AC6 |

| 3 | `WL-0MV5638ZS005I5XQ` Cheap-switch gate honours model cooldowns | feature | 1 | AC2, AC4 |
| 4 | `WL-0MV5639GG00085Q7` Bounded wake of one cooled-down job | feature | 1 | AC3 |
| 5 | `WL-0MV5639X70029BOI` Bounded default cooldown and fail-closed hardening | feature | 2 | AC5 |
| 6 | `WL-0MV563ADO008FT6H` Cooldown behaviour documentation | docs | 2,3,4,5 | AC7 |
| 7 | `WL-0MV563AU2007FM56` Cooldown regression guard and full-suite verification | task | 2,3,4,5 | AC6, AC8 |

Test-first ordering: child 1 (the contract/verification slice) is created first
and blocks every behaviour child; children 2–5 each write their tests before

- 2026-10-12T11:14Z — producer answered B / A / A; questions resolved in the
  appendix above.

  created in test-first order with dependency edges; AC coverage verified at

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Round 2 was asked interactively in the plan session (session id recorded in the

data.description:
Discovered during WL-0MV4V3WJN0013EZZ (discovered-from:WL-0MV4V3WJN0013EZZ).

## Problem

In the implement skill orchestrator, `phase_finish()` handles a non-fast-forward push to dev by attempting a rebase-and-retry, but the retry path references an undefined local `cwd`:

```
ERROR: Unhandled exception: name 'cwd' is not defined
```

File: `implement.py` (phase_finish, `PushNonFastForwardError` handler). The function's working-directory variable is named `worktree_path`/`repo_root`, not `cwd`.

## Impact

When dev advances concurrently (a sibling work item pushes first), `implement.py finish` crashes after commit + worktree removal instead of rebasing and retrying the push. The work item is reset to open and recovery must be done manually.

## Reproduction

1. Start a worktree from dev.
2. Let another commit land on origin/dev.
3. Run `implement.py finish` — the main-checkout fast-forward fails, the direct push is rejected non-fast-forward, and the retry rebase crashes with NameError.

## Expected

The retry path should rebase the feature branch onto origin/dev and retry the push (or report an actionable error), not raise NameError.

## Evidence

Observed 2026-10-12 during WL-0MV4V3WJN0013EZZ; commit c34af4d0 was rebased manually onto a415463d and pushed as 1c34755b.

# Cooldown signal contract and tolerant reader

**Parent:** WL-0MV54ZP3Y00514Y9 (Resume model-exhausted jobs instead of switching to cheap)

## Goal

Lock the cross-package, versioned on-disk contract for the model-cooldown
marker **before** any behaviour slice, so the TUI writer and the herdr reader
cannot drift (parent constraint: the on-disk signal format is a cross-package
contract and must be versioned/tolerant, with unknown fields ignored).

## Target outcome

One shared module (the same pattern as the existing
`@worklog/shared/lease-release`) provides the contract and the tolerant
reader/writer used by both packages:

- `resolveMachineCoordinationDir()` — `HERDR_COORDINATION_DIR` override (with
  `~` expansion) else `~/.herdr/downtime`; `null` when unresolvable.
- `readModelCooldowns(dir, now)` — active entries only (`cooldownUntil` in the
  future); tolerant (unknown fields ignored, malformed entries skipped); `[]`
  for a missing file; fails closed when the file is unreadable/corrupt.
- `writeModelCooldown(dir, entry)` — atomic (temp file + rename) upsert keyed by
  `paneId`/`sessionId`, pruning expired entries.
- `clearModelCooldown(dir, key)` — remove one entry; a missing file is a no-op.

Record shape (versioned; unknown fields ignored by readers):

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "cooldowns": [
    {
      "paneId": "<herdr pane id>",
      "sessionId": "<pi session id>",
      "itemId": "WL-... or null",
      "kind": "plan|intake|implement|audit|risk-effort or null",
      "reason": "all providers exhausted",
      "createdAt": 1700000000000,
      "cooldownUntil": 1700000300000
    }
  ]
}
```

## Minimal implementation

1. Tests first for the five behaviours below (round trip, tolerance, malformed
   entry, expiry prune, missing vs unreadable, dir resolution).
2. The shared module implementing the functions and owning the field semantics
   (its header comment is the contract of record).
3. Export the subpath from the shared package manifest.
4. Make the herdr `getMachineCoordinationDir()` delegate to the shared resolver
   so there is a single source of truth (its existing tests must stay green).
5. No behaviour change in the herdr or TUI packages in this slice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A durable, versioned, machine-readable cooldown contract exists with `schemaVersion` and tolerant readers (unknown fields ignored) in the shared package, importable by both the TUI recovery loop and herdr.
- [ ] A write-read-clear round-trip test proves a record with cooldownUntil and its pane/session key is written, read back and cleared.
- [ ] Tolerant reads: malformed entries are skipped and unknown fields are ignored without throwing, verified by tests.
- [ ] Expiry: entries with cooldownUntil in the past are not active and are pruned on the next write, verified by tests.
- [ ] Fail-closed reads: a missing or corrupt file is distinguished, verified by tests.
- [ ] Memory: the herdr coordination-dir resolver delegates to the shared one and its existing tests pass.

## Verification detail

Elaborates the ACs above (the AC extraction used by planning tooling reads only
the first line of each bullet, so the full wording lives here).

- AC1 elaborates parent AC1 ("Durable cooldown record"): the record is durable
  (on disk, machine-wide) and machine-readable; it carries `paneId`/`sessionId`
  as the key plus `itemId`, `kind`, `reason`, `createdAt`, `cooldownUntil`.
- AC2: writer then reader then clearer, asserting the entry disappears.
- AC3: `{"schemaVersion": 1, "cooldowns": [{"paneId": "p"}]}` (missing fields)
  and `{"cooldowns": "not-an-array"}` must not throw.
- AC4: a past `cooldownUntil` is filtered out of `readModelCooldowns` and
  removed by the next `writeModelCooldown`.
- AC5: `null`/absent dir, a non-JSON file, and an unreadable file each resolve
  deterministically.
- AC6: `HERDR_COORDINATION_DIR`, `~/`-prefixed values, and the `~/.herdr/downtime`
  default are asserted through the shared resolver.

## Deliverables

- The shared cooldown-contract module and its unit tests.
- The subpath export in the shared package manifest.
- The herdr coordination-dir resolver delegating to the shared resolver, with
  its existing tests still green.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/shared/src/model-cooldown.ts`
- `packages/shared/src/model-cooldown.test.ts`
- `packages/shared/package.json`
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.test.ts`

## Dependencies

None. Created first: the contract/verification slice (test-first ordering) and a
prerequisite for every behaviour slice below.

# Recovery loop records durable cooldown

**Parent:** WL-0MV54ZP3Y00514Y9 (Resume model-exhausted jobs instead of switching to cheap)

## Goal

When the in-pane recovery loop classifies a model-unavailable error as
`SERVER_ERROR` (exhaustion patterns: "all providers exhausted", "all providers
unavailable", "no provider is available during the current scheduled time
window") and starts a backoff, write a durable machine-wide cooldown marker;
clear it on the next successful provider response. Today that state lives only
in in-memory `RetryState`.

## Target outcome

- Exhaustion `SERVER_ERROR` → write a marker with
  `cooldownUntil = now + delayMs` via the shared contract from the contract
  slice.
- The next 2xx observed by `createRetryHintCapturingFetch` → clear the marker.
- `itemId`/`kind` derived best-effort from `ctx.sessionManager.getEntries()`
  (first user message carrying a work-item id and a dispatch-kind token); left
  `null` when not derivable — the dispatcher then resolves them from the pane
  label. The marker key is always `paneId` (`HERDR_PANE_ID`) + `sessionId`.
- Best-effort: an unwritable or unreadable marker never throws and never aborts
  the retry loop.

## Minimal implementation

1. Tests first: write on exhaustion `SERVER_ERROR` using the resolved delay; no
   write for a non-exhaustion retryable error; clear on 2xx; id/kind derivation
   present and absent; missing `HERDR_PANE_ID` degrades to a session-only key;
   an unwritable directory does not throw.
2. Expose `cooldownUntil` (`now + delayMs`) from `resolveRetryDelay()` without
   changing the existing `delayMs`/`serverHintMs` results.
3. Call the writer from the `SERVER_ERROR` branch of `register-recovery.ts` and
   the clearer from the existing 2xx path of `installFetchRetryHintCapture()`.
4. Keep the notify/stale-ctx safety contract intact (no new throwing paths).
5. Update the source comments describing the retry loop's side effects.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — Durable cooldown record: when a pane's recovery loop starts a backoff, a durable record with cooldownUntil is written and cleared on success.
- [ ] Detection: an exhaustion SERVER_ERROR writes the marker and a plain retryable 5xx or timeout does not, verified by tests.
- [ ] Item identity: itemId and kind are derived from session entries when present and left null when absent, with the pane/session key always written.
- [ ] Best-effort: an unwritable or unreadable marker never throws and never aborts the retry loop, verified by tests.
- [ ] Constraint: no slot-count completion gate, no dispatch pause and no unbounded latch are introduced.

## Verification detail

Elaborates the ACs above (planning tooling extracts only the first line of each
bullet).

- AC1 (parent AC1 "Durable cooldown record"): the record is written with
  `cooldownUntil = now + delayMs` for the current retry, carrying item id, kind,
  reason and the pane/session key, and is removed when the next provider
  response is 2xx (the same signal that currently clears the retry hint).
- Detection: reuse the existing `ErrorCategory.SERVER_ERROR` classification —
  no new pattern matching; assert the exhaustion bodies listed above and
  assert a plain 500/`TIMEOUT` writes nothing.
- Item identity: session entries are scanned for a work-item id token and a
  dispatch kind; on a miss the key is pane/session only and `itemId`/`kind` are
  null.
- Best-effort: point the writer at an unwritable directory (or a read-only dir)
  and assert the retry loop still resolves.

## Deliverables

- The recovery-loop writer/clearer wiring and its tests.
- `cooldownUntil` exposed from `resolveRetryDelay()` without changing existing
  results.
- Updated source comments describing the new side effects.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts`
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-logic.ts`
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-loop.test.ts`
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-patterns.ts`
- `packages/shared/src/model-cooldown.ts`

## Dependencies

Depends on `Cooldown signal contract and tolerant reader`.

# Cheap-switch gate honours model cooldowns

**Parent:** WL-0MV54ZP3Y00514Y9 (Resume model-exhausted jobs instead of switching to cheap)

## Goal

The herdr mode-switch worker must not switch the machine-wide proxy to `cheap`
while any active model-cooldown exists. A pane sitting in proxy backoff holds no
slot, so the proxy looks idle and the leader currently flips the shared proxy to
cheap — adding concurrency (cheap has more slots than fast) during a known
provider-exhaustion window.

## Target outcome

- `mode-switch-worker.tick()` reads the shared cooldown signal (the same
  pattern as `readSharedActivity`) and holds **fast** while any `cooldownUntil`
  is in the future.
- The hold is bounded by `cooldownUntil`: no latch, no persisted state — the
  first tick after expiry performs the normal idle/cheap decision.
- The fast-on-command path (`onOperatorCommand`) is unaffected.
- Reach is machine-wide: a cooldown written for any worklog root suppresses the
  shared-proxy cheap switch (the coordination dir is machine-wide, not per-root).

## Minimal implementation

1. Tests first in the mode-switch worker test file: cooldown present → no cheap
   POST; expired → cheap POST; absent → cheap POST; unreadable/corrupt →
   fail-closed (no cheap POST); fast path still POSTs `fast` while a cooldown is
   active.
2. Read the cooldown signal in `tick()` before the mode read and return early
   when any entry is active; keep the coordination dir injectable for tests.
3. Cross-root integration test: a marker written for one root suppresses the
   switch when the worker is configured for another root (one machine-wide
   coordination dir, two roots).
4. Update the mode-switch design doc in this slice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC2 — Cheap-switch gate: while at least one active model-cooldown exists, tick does not POST cheap; the hold is bounded by cooldownUntil.
- [ ] AC4 — Cross-root gate: a cooldown recorded in any worklog root suppresses the cheap switch.
- [ ] Fast path: onOperatorCommand still POSTs fast while a cooldown is active, verified by a test.
- [ ] No latch: the first tick at or after cooldownUntil performs the normal cheap decision, verified by a test.
- [ ] Fail-closed: an unreadable or corrupt signal produces no cheap POST, verified by a test.

## Verification detail

Elaborates the ACs above (planning tooling extracts only the first line of each
bullet).

- AC2 (parent AC2 "Cheap-switch gate"): the four-unit-test matrix is cooldown
  present / expired / absent / unreadable, each asserting the cheap POST or its
  absence, plus an assertion that the fast-on-command path is untouched.
- AC4 (parent AC4 "Cross-root gate"): write the marker through the shared store
  for root A, construct the worker for root B, assert no cheap POST; this is the
  integration test spanning two roots.
- No latch: after expiry the tick performs `GET /admin/mode` and the normal
  switch decision exactly as before the change.
- Fail-closed direction: "no cheap switch" is the safe direction (the proxy

# Bounded wake of one cooled-down job

**Parent:** WL-0MV54ZP3Y00514Y9 (Resume model-exhausted jobs instead of switching to cheap)

## Goal

At or after `cooldownUntil`, resume **at most one** model-cooldown job through
the existing stalled-resume path (literal `continue` to a live pane, or a
relaunch of pi `--continue` in an exited pane) rather than waiting for the
generic stall threshold or opening a brand-new pane.

## Target outcome

- The dispatcher consults the shared cooldown signal and, when at least one
  entry has expired, feeds that candidate into the existing stalled-resume
  machinery — at most one resume per cycle.
- The existing safety gates still apply: the non-terminal pane-close cooldown,
  the per-item/per-kind attempt cap, and the `needsProducerReview` exclusion.
- A successful resume consumes/clears the marker so the same pane is not woken
  repeatedly; a failed resume stays bounded by `cooldownUntil` and the attempt
  cap.

## Minimal implementation

1. Tests first in the stalled-work and downtime-worker dispatch test files:
   expired cooldown yields a candidate; unexpired cooldown does not; at most one
   resume per cycle; the attempt cap and `needsProducerReview` still exclude a
   cooldown candidate; a successful resume consumes the marker.
2. Add an expired-cooldown candidate source in `stalled-work.ts` (mapping
   `paneId` to the pane record the scan already reads) or extend
   `classifyStalledPane` with the cooldown input.
3. Wire it into the dispatcher's pre-dispatch stalled scan seam so at most one
   cooldown resume happens per cycle, preferring it over opening a new pane.
4. Ensure the wake uses the unchanged `STALLED_RESUME_PROMPT` and the existing
   attempt accounting.
5. Update the downtime-dispatcher doc in this slice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC3 — Bounded wake: at/after cooldownUntil the dispatcher resumes at most one job via the stalled-resume path.
- [ ] Strictness: an unexpired cooldown never wakes a pane, verified by tests.
- [ ] Safety gates: a cooldown candidate is still excluded by the attempt cap and by the needsProducerReview flag, verified by tests.
- [ ] Bounded concurrency: at most one cooldown resume per dispatcher cycle, verified by tests.
- [ ] Consumption: a successful resume consumes the marker so it is not re-woken on the next cycle; a failed resume remains bounded, verified by tests.

## Verification detail

Elaborates the ACs above (planning tooling extracts only the first line of each
bullet).

- AC3 (parent AC3 "Bounded wake"): reuse `classifyStalledPane` /
  `resumeStalledPane` — the literal `continue` prompt to a live pane and the pi
  `--continue` relaunch for an exited pane both stay the only wake mechanisms;
  the attempt-cap and `needsProducerReview` exclusions are asserted against a
  cooldown-sourced candidate.
- Strictness: `cooldownUntil` in the future must not produce a wake even when
  the generic stall threshold has elapsed.
- Bounded concurrency: the cycle reports `{ ok: true, stalledResume: true }` on
  one resume and must not offer new work in the same cycle.
- Failed resume: a neutral failure reason is not turned into a CLI-error strike,
  a crash or a duplicate resume.
