# Intake Brief — Herdr extension unresponsive on larger worklog databases (WL-0MVJC1EQX001QR9W)

## Problem statement

The Herdr Work Items pane freezes or visibly lags when it refreshes, is slow to
initially appear, and is slow to reflect some changes after agent writes —
problems that scale with the size of the worklog database. On a ~100 MB /
2,600-item worklog the pane's refresh path still spawns slow, memory-hungry
`wl` CLI processes (`wl worklist` ≈ 1 s / 1.2 MB JSON cold; `wl list` subsets
0.5–0.9 s each peaking ~130–145 MB; per-expand `wl dep list` ≈ 0.4 s) and the
auto-sync may spawn a ~36 s `wl sync` every 60 s. Recent fixes (event-driven
refresh, consolidated `wl worklist`, hydrator timeouts) improved the picture but
the extension remains sluggish — "improved but still not good enough".

## Users (example user stories)

- **Agent operators running the Herdr Work Items pane** — the primary user.
  - *As an operator, when the pane auto-refreshes, I want the UI to stay
    responsive (no multi-second freezes, keystrokes accepted promptly) so my
    monitoring flow is uninterrupted.*
  - *As an operator on a large worklog, when an agent writes to a work item, I
    want the pane to reflect the change within a couple of seconds so I can
    trust the list is current.*
  - *As an operator, I want the pane to open promptly and not feel like the
    extension is a drag on my machine even at 100 MB+ worklog scale.*

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Pane stays responsive during refresh:** a default-view refresh does not block the TUI event loop for more than ~200 ms of perceived lag in aggregate (verified with an automated test harness or measured timing on a large fixture DB) — keystrokes/commands process promptly while a refresh is in flight.
- **Single-figure refresh cost on large DBs:** a default-view refresh end-to-end (event → data load → render) is bounded to ≤ ~1.5 s wall-clock p95 on a DB of ~2,600 items / ~100 MB, including per-expand child fetches; the consolidated `wl worklist` single-read path stays the norm — no regression to multi-spawn refreshes.
- **Auto-sync cannot stall the pane:** while a long `wl sync` (measured ~36 s on the 100 MB DB) is in flight in the background, the pane remains responsive — no lock wait, no event-loop stall, at most a brief non-blocking status notice.
- **Change reflection latency:** after a `wl` write, the pane reflects the change within ~2 s p95 via the event-driven watch path at large-DB scale.
- **Reduced memory footprint:** a refresh's spawned `wl` processes peak at no more than a documented per-spawn budget below the ~130–145 MB/spawn observed baseline, OR concurrent spawns are bounded so aggregate RSS for a single pane stays under a documented ceiling (e.g. ≤ ~300 MB).
- **No regressions:** the full Herdr plugin + TUI test suites pass; the zero-spawn-when-idle guarantee and event-driven watch semantics are preserved.
## Constraints

- Must preserve the existing event-driven refresh, in-process SQLite read
  scopes, consolidated `wl worklist` single-read default view, and
  zero-spawn-when-idle guarantees (documented in
  `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` and `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`).
- Must not change the hydrator's core behaviour or the scheduler's sequential
  dispatch model without a separate work item.
- Fixes must target "large worklog" scale (100 MB+/2,600+ items) without
  regressing small worklogs.
- No new heavy dependencies; prefer reuse of the existing in-process SQLite
  read path (`@worklog/shared` `WorklogDatabase`) over new spawns.

## Existing state (measured)

- `.worklog/worklog.db` ≈ 109 MB, ~2,631 items, read cache 81 MB / ~709 entries
  (this repo).
- `wl worklist --json`: ≈ 1.0 s cold, ~1.2 MB payload.
- `wl list` (each of the four subsets): 0.5–0.9 s, peak ~130–145 MB RSS.
- `wl next`: ≈ 0.6 s. `wl dep list`: ≈ 0.4 s per call.
- `wl sync`: ≈ 36 s on this DB; auto-sync spawns fire-and-forget every 60 s
  (single-flight + heartbeat skip across panes).
- Herdr pane refresh: 30 s auto tick + event-driven (≤ ~150 ms debounce),
  single consolidated `wl worklist` read for the default view; in-process
  SQLite reads for actionable counts / child fetches within a refresh scope.
- Previous unresponsiveness work completed: WL-0MMNZWOZ60M8JY6E (TUI
  unresponsive, critical), WL-0MUY0RDBQ001H74P (hydrate timeouts), WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN (snappy event-driven refresh), WL-0MQFRY8TM006DIJ6 (wl next perf), WL-0MQOIBGIR006CWLR (background task runtime), WL-0MSGAEPOJ002824S / WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG (memoization + in-process reads), WL-0MVI0IT4S0070G78 (consolidated worklist read).

## Desired change

Investigate the remaining large-DB cost drivers in the Herdr refresh path and
shave them down to the acceptance criteria above. Known candidates (to confirm
during implementation):

1. **Auto-sync `wl sync` cost (~36 s):** profile why `wl sync` is so slow on a
   100 MB DB (git operations, JSONL export, DB compaction?) and either bound it
   or restructure so the pane never waits on / competes with it.
2. **`wl list`/`wl worklist` RSS (~130–145 MB/spawn):** confirm where the
   memory goes (full JSON materialisation? enrichments?) and consider streaming
   or trimming payloads; cap concurrent spawns.
3. **Per-expand `wl dep list` / `wl list --parent` spawns:** replace with
   in-process SQLite reads (via the existing refresh scope) so expanding nodes
   doesn't spawn more slow processes.
4. **Event-loop blocking:** ensure every remaining spawn is off the TUI event
   loop and each refresh's in-process SQLite work stays within the one-open
   refresh scope (no per-helper DB opens).

- **Risk:** the ~36 s `wl sync` is dominated by git push/network or JSONL

- **Risk:** memory-per-spawn may be inherent to the current `better-sqlite3` +

  needs care to preserve the documented `wl worklist` payload stability.
- **Risk:** in-process SQLite reads on a 100 MB DB can themselves be slow

# F1 — Large-DB refresh budget harness and baseline

## Background

Parent WL-0MVJC1EQX001QR9W needs measurable, repeatable evidence for its ACs
(refresh ≤ ~1.5 s p95, event-loop blocking ≤ ~200 ms, spawn/RSS budgets,
write→reflect ≤ 2 s) at ~2,600-item / ~100 MB scale. Today large-DB numbers are
only reported ad hoc (intake "Existing state"); there is no checked-in harness,
so regressions are not caught and the fix items cannot prove their targets.
This item builds the verification foundation first (test-first), reusing the
ratchet/baseline pattern proven in WL-0MVFRRAXD001E7AN (startup import-budget
harness).

## Target outcome

A checked-in, reproducible large-DB performance harness that records the
pre-change baseline, asserts the parent's AC budgets, and gates the
implementation items (F3–F6).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fixture generator deterministically builds a large worklog DB (~2,600
  items, nested parent/child + dependency edges, ~100 MB on disk) in a temp
  `.worklog` without touching the repo's real worklog; generation is fast
  enough for a default-suite test run (< ~20 s) while a "full-scale" variant
  is runnable on demand via a documented command.
- The harness measures, for a default-view refresh: end-to-end wall time (p95
  over ≥ 5 samples), aggregate TUI event-loop blocking time, spawned `wl`
  process count per refresh, peak RSS per spawn and aggregate for a single
  pane, and write→reflect latency via the event-driven watch path.
- A baseline budget file (e.g. `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-budget.json`)
  records pre-change numbers for each metric, the parent AC targets, and the
  measurement commands so numbers can be re-quoted in work-item comments.
- A fast ratchet/regression test in the default suite fails when a metric
  exceeds its budget plus documented headroom; timing is CPU-time based
  (`process.resourceUsage`) so a loaded shared host does not cause false
  failures (same approach as WL-0MVFRRAXD001E7AN).
- Spawn-count assertions include the zero-spawn-when-idle guarantee and the
  single consolidated `wl worklist` read for the default view — preserving the
  documented no-regression invariants (parent AC 6).
- Documentation: a `docs/dev/` note describes how to run the harness at full
  scale and re-baseline; the reference-host report is quoted in the
  completion comment.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `packages/herdr/test/perf/` with the fixture generator and harness, wired
  to the existing test runner and excluded from editor/agent ignore rules.
- Implement metric collectors (wall/CPU time, spawn accounting via the
  fetcher's injectable exec seam, RSS via `process.resourceUsage` + per-spawn
  `maxBuffer`/`ps` where available).
- Write the budget JSON, ratchet assertion, and docs; run the harness to
  capture the baseline quoted in the completion comment.
- Wire full-scale runs into a documented npm script (`test:perf:large`).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` — fixture generator + metric collectors.
- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-budget.json` — baseline budgets and AC targets.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — reuse the injectable exec seam (`setExecFileAsync`) and refresh-scope helpers for spawn/RSS accounting.
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` — how to run/re-baseline (append).

## Deliverables

- Fixture generator + harness + ratchet test (green at baseline), budget JSON
  with measured pre-change numbers, docs, and a completion comment quoting the
  reference-host baseline.

## Dependencies

- None beyond parent WL-0MVJC1EQX001QR9W.

# F2 — Profile remaining Herdr refresh cost drivers

## Background

The intake brief lists known large-DB cost candidates but none are yet
profiled rigorously: `wl sync` ≈ 36 s (git push/network vs JSONL export vs DB
compaction?), `wl list`/`wl worklist` spawn RSS ~130–145 MB, per-expand
`wl dep list` / single-parent `wl list --parent` spawns, and the in-process
SQLite open cost (~46–70 ms FTS DDL). Parent AC 1–6 need per-driver numbers and
a decision on what is in scope vs. a separate `wl sync` perf item (intake
scope-creep guard: "record a linked child, don't absorb"). Uses the F1 harness.

## Target outcome

A ranked, evidence-backed cost table for one full refresh (event → data load →
render) plus a `wl sync` breakdown, with a decision per driver: in-scope fix
(feeds F3–F6) or separate work item (created with a blocker edge).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A measured cost table (wall time and CPU time, using the F1 harness at full
  scale) attributing refresh cost across: `wl worklist` payload build + JSON
  parse, in-process SQLite open (DDL/FTS) + queries, per-expand child/dep
  reads, hydrator per-item `wl dep list` spawns, and render. Each row states
  measured value, cost driver, and recommended action (fix-in-scope / separate
  item / no-op).
- A `wl sync` profile on a ≥ 100 MB DB breaking the ~36 s into: git fetch/push
  (network), JSONL export, DB compaction/wal checkpoint, and CLI overhead.
  Conclusion explicitly marks whether a `wl sync` perf fix is required and
  whether it is in-scope here or a new work item per the intake guardrail. If a
  separate item is warranted, it is created with a blocking dependency recorded
  on this item — this item itself does NOT absorb a `wl sync` fix.
- Confirmed memory breakdown for a `wl worklist` / `wl list` spawn (~130–145 MB
  peak): full JSON materialisation vs enrichments vs SQLite read cache. States
  whether the payload can be trimmed without changing the documented `wl
  worklist` payload contract (feeding F5's decision).
- The report is recorded as a comment on this item with exact re-runnable
  commands, timestamps, and the reference-host path.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add/reuse the F1 harness for full-scale sampling of each refresh stage
  (probe points via existing spawn accounting and scope helpers).
- Profile `wl sync` with `time -v` / `--loglevel`, git dry-run and
  `git count-objects`/pack inspection, and DB pragma checks (`page_count`,
  `journal_mode`, wal size).
- Triage `wl list`/worklist RSS with `node --cpu-prof`/`--heapsnapshot` or
  `--trace-gc` on the CLI entry; attribute to payload vs enrichment.
- Write the report comment and, if warranted, `wl create` the separate `wl
  sync` perf child with `wl dep add <sync-item> <this-item>`.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` — full-scale sampling driver.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — spawn accounting / probe points.
- `src/commands/sync.ts` and `src/sync.ts` — `wl sync` pipeline to profile.
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — payload build to profile/mem-diagnose.

## Deliverables

- Ranked cost table + sync breakdown comment, decision record, and (if
  required) a separate linked `wl sync` perf work item.

## Dependencies

- F1 (harness and baseline).

# F3 — Auto-sync isolation: pane never stalls on `wl sync`

## Background

Auto-sync spawns `wl sync` (≈ 36 s on a ~100 MB DB) fire-and-forget every 60 s.
Parent AC 3 requires that while a long sync is in flight the pane stays
responsive: no lock wait, no event-loop stall, no "hanging" indication beyond a
brief non-blocking status notice. The current single-flight + heartbeat +
`--if-idle` guards (auto-sync.ts) bound spawns but do not yet guarantee the
pane never competes with or waits on a long-running sync (IO contention with
refresh reads, process-group/PID effects, no UI notice). F2 profiles where the
~36 s goes and whether a `wl sync` fix is a separate item (scope guard).

## Target outcome

A refresh completes within budget while a long `wl sync` is in flight in the
background, with a non-blocking status notice shown; the pane never waits on
the sync lock or its process.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With a simulated/hooked long ~36 s `wl sync` in flight (F1 harness), a
  concurrent default-view refresh completes within the parent AC 2 budget and
  blocks the TUI event loop ≤ 200 ms aggregate (parent AC 1); asserted by an
  automated test in the default suite.
- The auto-sync spawn is verified off the TUI event loop and the pane shows a
  non-blocking status notice ("syncing…") that never blocks input; no "hanging"
  UI state beyond the notice (parent AC 3).
- No lock contention: an in-flight sync does not hold/reset the same SQLite
  handle or filesystem lock the pane's in-process refresh scope uses; a refresh
  never waits for a sync to finish (asserted with in-flight instrumentation:
  e.g. start time monotonic, no wait gap equal to remaining sync time).
- Existing guarantees preserved: single-flight, cross-pane heartbeat skip,
  `--if-idle`, 60 s interval, no concurrent sync spawns (parent AC 6); the F1
  zero-spawn-when-idle assertion still passes.
- If F2 concludes a `wl sync` perf fix is a separate work item, this item stays
  limited to pane-side isolation and references that item — no scope creep.

## Minimal Implementation

- Route auto-sync through the same background-task runtime used elsewhere
  (`packages/herdr/src` background helpers) with explicit event-loop decoupling
  and a tiny status model the pane renders without blocking.
- Add in-flight instrumentation (process start + PID + elapsed) so a refresh
  can verify non-interference; extend F1 harness with a "sync in flight"
  scenario.
- Add the non-blocking status notice and back it with the automated
  responsiveness test above.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — spawn path, single-flight, heartbeat.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — refresh orchestration + status rendering.
- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` — in-flight sync scenario.

## Deliverables

- Off-loop auto-sync with status notice, in-flight instrumentation, an
  automated responsiveness-under-sync test, and updated
  `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` notes.

## Dependencies

- F2 profile results (plus F1 harness).

# F4 — In-process dependency and child reads on expand

## Background

Expanding a node still triggers per-item `wl dep list` (hydrator, ≈ 0.4 s each)
and single-parent `wl list --parent` spawns (`fetchChildrenForItem`); each
spawn costs 0.5–0.9 s and ~130–145 MB RSS. The batching in-process path already
exists for multi-parent fetches (`fetchChildrenForItems` via the refresh
scope) but the single-parent and per-hydrator-item paths still spawn. Parent
AC 2 bounds refresh end-to-end to ≤ ~1.5 s including per-expand child fetches,
and AC 5 bounds aggregate spawn RSS.

## Target outcome

Expanding a node (or hydrating its deps) performs zero `wl` spawns on the
large-DB path: all child/dependency reads are served in-process through the
one refresh-scoped SQLite connection, with the existing fail-open CLI fallback
unchanged for correctness edge cases.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Expanding a parent performs no `wl list --parent` / `wl dep list` spawn (F1
  spawn-count assertion) when the in-process path is available; child and
  dependency rows match the CLI's ordering, fields, depth and enrichment
  semantics on a ~2,600-item fixture.
- Hydrator dependency lookups use the in-process/refresh-scope read (or a
  bounded batched lookup) instead of one `wl dep list` spawn per item; the
  hydrator timeout behaviour from WL-0MUY0RDBQ001H74P is preserved.
- Fail-open preserved: when no worklog dir / SQLite file / `@worklog/shared` is
  available, or a stored audit fingerprint requires CLI enrichment, behaviour
  falls back to spawns exactly as today (existing `fetcher-inprocess` and
  `worklist-expand-refresh` tests still green).
- The one-open-per-refresh scope is kept — no new per-helper DB opens are
  introduced (parent AC constraints).
- Existing Herdr + TUI suites pass with zero-spawn-when-idle preserved (parent
  AC 6).

## Minimal Implementation

- Route `fetchChildrenForItem` through the shared batch/in-process reader when
  a scope is available; keep its signature and fail-open.
- Convert per-item hydrator `wl dep list` calls to a batched in-process dep
  read within the refresh scope (grouping visible items into one pass), with
  fail-open for the fingerprint/enrichment cases.
- Extend F1 harness assertions (expanded-node spawn counts) and the
  `fetchChildrenForItem/ForItems` in-process tests.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — single-parent fetch + batch reader + scope.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — per-item `wl dep list` calls.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — expand orchestration.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-inprocess.test.ts`, `worklist-expand-refresh.test.ts` — extend.

## Deliverables

- Spawn-free expand + hydrator dep reads on the in-process path, updated
  fail-open tests, F1 harness assertions green, and a completion comment with
  large-DB timing/spawn deltas vs baseline.

## Dependencies

- F2 profile results (confirms dep/child reads as a cost driver) and F1
  harness baselines.

# F5 — Bound `wl` spawn memory and concurrency for a single pane

## Background

Each surviving `wl worklist`/`wl list` spawn peaks at ~130–145 MB RSS on a
~100 MB DB (intake measurements). Parent AC 5 is satisfied either by reducing
per-spawn memory below a documented budget or by bounding concurrent spawns so
aggregate RSS for a single pane stays under a documented ceiling (e.g.
≤ ~300 MB). F2 determines where the memory goes and whether the `wl worklist`
payload can be trimmed without breaking its documented contract.

## Target outcome

A documented, enforced per-pane RSS/spawn budget that guarantees parent AC 5
at large-DB scale, without regressing small-DB behaviour or the consolidated
single-read default view.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Per-spawn or aggregate budget confirmed: measured peak aggregate RSS for a
  single pane during a full refresh (F1 harness, full scale) is at or below a
  documented ceiling (target ≤ ~300 MB as in parent AC 5), OR per-spawn peak is
  reduced below the ~130–145 MB observed baseline and the reduced number is
  documented as the new budget.
- Based on F2's evidence, either: (a) a payload trim on `wl worklist` (drop
  unused fields/streaming) with the documented payload contract preserved or
  explicitly revised and tested, or (b) a documented spawn cap (e.g. N
  concurrent `wl` spawns, queueing/deferred reads) whose aggregate RSS is
  asserted by an automated test — without waiting under the event loop.
- The budget and its enforcement are documented in
  `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` (parent AC 5 "documented budget").
- No regression to small worklogs and no change to the consolidated
  single-read default-view norm; zero-spawn-when-idle preserved (parent AC 6).
- All remaining `wl` spawns execute off the TUI event loop, and deferred/
  queued reads never block input: the F1 harness event-loop aggregation stays
  within the parent AC 1 ≤ ~200 ms bound with a spawn-heavy fixture (intake
  candidate 4).
- No new heavy dependencies (parent constraints) — prefer reuse of the
  in-process SQLite read path over new spawns.

## Minimal Implementation

- Apply the F2-validated memory fix (payload trim with contract test, or
  streaming) and/or add a concurrency semaphore around `wl` spawns in the
  fetch path with queued fallback reads.
- Add F1 harness assertions for aggregate RSS, spawn count, and event-loop
  blocking at full scale.
- Ensure every remaining spawn is dispatched off the TUI event loop (existing
  background-task runtime) with a bounded queue; assert no input-lock via the
  harness.
- Update docs; record before/after numbers in the completion comment.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — spawn path, exec seam, spawn cap.
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — payload build (if trim chosen).
- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` — RSS/spawn assertions.
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` — budget documentation.

## Deliverables

- Enforced spawn/RSS budget with automated assertion, validated memory fix
  (trim or cap) per F2 evidence, docs, and measured before/after numbers.

## Dependencies

- F2 (memory breakdown + payload-contract decision), F1 harness.

# F6 — Single, cheap in-process SQLite open per refresh

## Background

In-process SQLite reads on a ~100 MB DB carry a non-trivial open cost (open +
pragmas + FTS DDL ~46–70 ms measured in earlier work; the one-open-per-refresh
scope from WL-0MV6C6SLB005HX7B exists to amortise it). Surviving per-helper
opens, read-only open DDL, and connection reuse across ticks are the remaining
levers. Parent AC 2 (≤ ~1.5 s default-view refresh p95) and AC 1 (no event-loop
stall) constrain this cost; F2 quantifies its share.

## Target outcome

A default-view refresh performs at most one cheap in-process SQLite open
(shared across all refresh helpers, read-only, minimal/no DDL when already
initialised), and the open cost is small enough that it never threatens the
refresh budget.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An automated test (F1 harness, full scale) asserts a default-view refresh
  performs at most one in-process DB open per refresh and that helper reads
  reuse that single connection (no per-helper open).
- The read-only open path is measured and documented: open+pragmas cost is
  recorded after the change (target: eliminate the ~46–70 ms FTS-DDL hit on
  already-initialised stores, e.g. by skipping DDL when schema/version already
  present), with numbers below the refresh budget headroom.
- Open is verified off the TUI event loop / within the existing refresh scope
  (parent AC 1); any background warm-up does not overlap a visible refresh in a
  blocking way.
- Fail-open preserved: a read-only open failure degrades to the existing `wl`
  spawn fallback; no change to the hydrator's core behaviour or scheduler
  (parent constraints).
- Existing Herdr + TUI suites pass; zero-spawn-when-idle preserved (parent
  AC 6).

## Minimal Implementation

- Refactor the refresh-scope open to: one shared connection per refresh across
  all helpers, read-only pragma set, and schema/DDL only when required
  (version check); verify `@worklog/shared` `WorklogDatabase` surface honours
  a read-only/no-DDL mode or the skip is done at the caller.
- Add harness timing for the open step; update docs budgeting the open cost.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — refresh scope + `InProcessRefreshScope` open.
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `WorklogDatabase` open/DDL path.
- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` — open-cost timing.

## Deliverables

- One-cheap-open-per-refresh with automated single-open + timing assertions,
  fail-open tests green, and documented open-cost numbers.

## Dependencies

- F2 (quantifies open cost share), F1 harness.

# F7 — Large-DB responsiveness verification at scale

## Background

The parent's ACs are acceptance criteria for the whole pane behaviour at scale.
F1–F6 each deliver targeted fixes and tests; this item is the end-to-end
verification slice that confirms every parent AC holds together on a
~2,600-item / ~100 MB fixture after all changes, including the AC 4
write→reflect re-verification (extending WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN to large-DB
scale) and AC 6's full-suite no-regression gate.

## Target outcome

One reproducible end-to-end evidence run (documented commands + test suite)
that every parent acceptance criterion 1–6 is met at large-DB scale.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Pane stays responsive during refresh:** a default-view refresh does not block the TUI event loop for more than ~200 ms of perceived lag in aggregate (verified with an automated test harness or measured timing on a large fixture DB) — keystrokes/commands process promptly while a refresh is in flight. (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)
- **Single-figure refresh cost on large DBs:** a default-view refresh end-to-end (event → data load → render) is bounded to ≤ ~1.5 s wall-clock p95 on a DB of ~2,600 items / ~100 MB, including per-expand child fetches; the consolidated `wl worklist` single-read path stays the norm — no regression to multi-spawn refreshes. (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)
- **Auto-sync cannot stall the pane:** while a long `wl sync` (measured ~36 s on the 100 MB DB) is in flight in the background, the pane remains responsive — no lock wait, no event-loop stall, at most a brief non-blocking status notice. (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)
- **Change reflection latency:** after a `wl` write, the pane reflects the change within ~2 s p95 via the event-driven watch path at large-DB scale. (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)
- **Reduced memory footprint:** a refresh's spawned `wl` processes peak at no more than a documented per-spawn budget below the ~130–145 MB/spawn observed baseline, OR concurrent spawns are bounded so aggregate RSS for a single pane stays under a documented ceiling (e.g. ≤ ~300 MB). (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)
- **No regressions:** the full Herdr plugin + TUI test suites pass; the zero-spawn-when-idle guarantee and event-driven watch semantics are preserved. (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)

- All measured numbers are quoted in the completion comment against the F1 baseline; if any criterion is not met, the blocking fix item is referenced with its data rather than accepted silently.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend the F1 harness with an end-to-end "all ACs" report mode aggregating
  every metric into one JSON report plus a human summary.
- Drive the event-driven write→reflect measurement at full scale (reusing the
  watch path from WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN) and assert AC 4 at large-DB scale.
- Run the full suite + full-scale harness, record the report comment, and mark
  this item (and via parent workflow, the parent) ready once green.

# CPU-aware dispatch gate for implement/audit work

**Work item:** WL-0MVK0UO3Q002TXW6 — Only dispatch implement or audit work items if the CPU is below 75%

**Headline:** The downtime dispatcher gains a host-CPU gate: at or above 75% measured CPU utilisation it stops launching new implement/audit panes (and stops waking stalled panes) while intake/plan/risk-effort keep dispatching, reporting a neutral `cpu-saturated` reason.

## Problem statement

Many concurrent implement and audit sessions push the host CPU towards saturation, which slows every agent (including the operator's own session) and lengthens prefill/response latency. The downtime dispatcher currently has no host-CPU signal at all: it gates on local-LLM slot capacity, prefill pacing, code freeze and pane state, so it will happily launch *more* implement/audit panes while the machine is already at or above 75% CPU utilisation.

## Users

- **Operator / producer** — wants the machine to stay responsive; "stop starting new heavy work when the box is loaded, but keep triaging and planning the backlog."
  - As the operator, when CPU is at 80% I want new implement and audit panes to stop being launched, while intake and plan keep flowing.
  - As the operator, I want to see *why* the dispatcher is refusing (measured CPU vs threshold), not a silent NOP.
- **Dispatched agents** — benefit indirectly: less CPU contention for the work already in flight.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Metric.** The dispatcher computes host CPU utilisation as 0–100% from `/proc/stat` `cpu` deltas across the worker's poll interval, normalised across all cores. When `/proc/stat` is missing, unreadable or unparseable, or when the sampling window is too short to be meaningful (< 1 s, e.g. two dispatches in one tick), it falls back to 1-min load average ÷ core count × 100 (capped at 100). When neither signal is available the gate **fails open** (dispatch proceeds unchanged). Unit tests pin the parser, the delta maths, the short-window condition, the fallback and the fail-open paths.
2. **Gate.** When the measured CPU percentage is **greater than or equal to** the configured threshold, new **audit** and **implement** dispatch is refused on every dispatch path — direct Herdr-head dispatch (including the critical-first scan), the coordination leader's offer dispatch, and the own-backlog fallback / audit-batch continuation. **intake**, **plan** and **risk-effort** dispatch continue, and an operator-initiated / manual dispatch is never gated. A reading just below the threshold dispatches normally.
3. **Stalled resume.** While the gate is active, the pre-dispatch stalled-work scan does not resume a stalled pane in place (it would wake an agent and add load). Once CPU falls below the threshold the next idle tick resumes normally, unchanged.
4. **Neutral, non-destructive semantics.** A gated tick is reported with the distinct reason `cpu-saturated` and recorded in the decision log (existing rate limit) with the measured `hostCpuPercent`, its `source` (`proc-stat` / `loadavg`) and the configured threshold. A gated tick is never a CLI-error strike, never enters the `no-candidate` cooldown, never removes a coordination entry, never rolls back or writes a dispatch marker, the coordination offer computation still returns candidates (only its stalled-resume step is skipped), and the reason is **not** counted as a capacity refusal in `CAPACITY_REFUSAL_REASONS` (a CPU-gated night must not be reported as local-model capacity starvation).
5. **Configuration.** New plugin setting `downtimeCpuGatePercent` (default **75**), clamped to **[0, 100]**, where `0` disables the gate. It is re-read live on every dispatch tick (no restart) and wired through the aggregated worker config. `packages/herdr/README.md` and `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` document the gate, the metric, the fallback and the neutral-token semantics.
6. **Testing and validation.** New tests cover: metric parsing/fail-open; gate filter per dispatch kind (audit/implement refused, intake/plan/risk-effort allowed); threshold boundary (`== threshold` blocks, `threshold − ε` allows); `0` disables; critical implement is also gated; stalled resume skipped while gated; all dispatch paths (direct, coordination, own-backlog fallback, batch continuation); coordination entries not evicted; decision-log evidence fields; settings clamp and default; `cpu-saturated` excluded from capacity refusals. Existing downtime-worker suites stay green.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Host-local measurement, no new machine-wide marker.** The downtime leader is the only dispatcher for the host (`~/.herdr/downtime` is machine-wide) and dispatches for every worklog root, so one local reading per tick is authoritative. Do not add a marker file to `~/.herdr/downtime/` and do not add cross-host coordination.
- **Safety class, so criticals are gated too.** Saturation is exactly when starting a new critical implement does harm; the gate is applied like the code-freeze split-by-skill rule, not like the non-safety filters a critical item may bypass.
- **Offers are not gated.** `computeMostImportantItem` ranking stays ungated (only its stalled-resume sub-step is gated) — suppressing offers would strip the leader's candidate list and, when everything is held, drive the 60-minute `no-candidate` cooldown so dispatch would not resume promptly after CPU recovers.
- **No new persistent state.** The `/proc/stat` previous sample lives in memory in the production seam; nothing is written to disk. A worker restart simply re-seeds via the load-average fallback on the first tick.
- **Fail-open in every unwired/partial case.** Unwired `DowntimeWorkerDeps` seam, thrown reader, `NaN`/non-finite values, absent `/proc/stat` → dispatch unchanged; the gate must never crash or block a tick it cannot evaluate.
- **Reason precedence.** If both the code freeze and the CPU gate are active, `code-freeze` keeps precedence (unchanged existing behaviour); `cpu-saturated` is reported when CPU is the reason the remaining candidates were filtered.
- No change to the TUI worklist rendering, selection ranking, or `browseItemCount` windowing.
- No new dependency: `node:fs` + `node:os` only.

## Existing state

- Dispatch gates are **sequential filters over the Herdr list head** (`dispatchDowntimeWork` → `dispatchFromHerdrList`), each with a distinct reason token (see *Ranking contract* in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`).
- `readCodeFreezeStatus` / `frozen` is the direct precedent: it pauses audit/implement while plan/intake/risk-effort continue (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/code-freeze.ts`, WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY).
- Host-wide audit saturation exists (`isHostAuditActive`, reason `audit-host-saturated`), but it only serialises audits via a marker file; it carries no CPU signal.
- Capacity starvation observation (`capacity-starvation.ts`) classifies refusal reasons; a new reason must be classified deliberately.
- No production code reads `/proc/stat`, `/proc/loadavg` or PSI today; only tests (`auto-sync-isolation.test.ts`, perf harness) compute `loadavg / cpus()` as a diagnostic. `machine-hygiene` collects PSI/loadavg but is operator-invoked only and is a Python skill outside the herdr runtime.
- Every neighbouring gate is a live-re-read `downtime*` setting with a `clamp...` helper and a documented default, so the new setting follows an established pattern (`packages/herdr/src/settings.ts`).

## Desired change

1. New module `packages/herdr/src/host-cpu.ts`:
   - `parseProcStatCpu(text)` → `{ busy, total }` (or `null`) from the aggregate `cpu` line;
   - `cpuPercentFromSamples(prev, next)` → percentage (or `null` when the total delta is zero);
   - `loadPerCorePercent(load1, cpuCount)` → fallback percentage;
   - `createHostCpuSampler()` holding the previous `/proc/stat` sample in memory, returning `{ ok: true, percent, source } | { ok: false }` with the < 1 s short-window rule;
   - `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_CPU_GATE_PERCENT = 75`, `clampDowntimeCpuGatePercent(value)` (0–100, invalid → default), and the pure predicate `isCpuGateActive(percent, thresholdPercent)` (`threshold > 0 && percent >= threshold`).
2. `downtime-worker.ts`: add `readHostCpu` to `DowntimeWorkerDeps` (optional, fail-open); thread `cpuSaturated` through `dispatchDowntimeWork`, `dispatchFromHerdrList` (skip `audit`/`implement` in both the critical-first and normal scans) and `dispatchFromCoordination`; skip stalled resume at each resume call site while gated; add `cpu-saturated` to the terminal-reason composition (after `code-freeze`) and the decision-log evidence fields.
3. `index.ts`: implement the seam in `createDowntimeDeps` with a module-level sampler reading `/proc/stat` + `/proc/loadavg` via `node:fs` (whitelisted absolute paths, fail-open), and pass the live `downtimeCpuGatePercent` through `DowntimeWorkerConfig.config()` into the dispatch entry points.
4. `settings.ts`: register the setting, default and clamp.
5. `capacity-starvation.ts`: keep `cpu-saturated` out of `CAPACITY_REFUSAL_REASONS` with an explicit comment and test.
6. Docs: `packages/herdr/README.md` settings list + gate description; `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` new subsection (metric, fallback, gate scope, resume, neutral token, precedence).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/host-cpu.ts` — **new**: `/proc/stat` parser, delta sampler, load-average fallback, threshold default/clamp and the pure gate predicate.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `readHostCpu` dep seam, `cpuSaturated` threading through the tick, Herdr-head scan, critical-first scan, coordination dispatch + own-backlog fallback, stalled-resume call sites, `cpu-saturated` reason and decision-log fields.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — production sampler in `createDowntimeDeps`; live `downtimeCpuGatePercent` wiring into the worker config and coordination check-in.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — `downtimeCpuGatePercent` default, clamping and parse.
- `packages/herdr/src/capacity-starvation.ts` — exclude `cpu-saturated` from capacity refusals.
- `packages/herdr/src/host-cpu.test.ts` — **new**: parser/delta/fallback/clamp/gate-predicate unit tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.cpu-gate.test.ts` — **new**: per-kind gating, boundary, `0` disables, critical, resume skip, all paths, evidence.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.settings.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/capacity-starvation.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — extend for the setting, the refusal classification and the coordination non-eviction.
- `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — operator and deep-dive documentation.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY** — Downtime dispatcher must honour ship-it code freezes — the split-by-skill gate this change mirrors.
- **WL-0MUIVE0YG000UVIA** — host-wide audit-slot saturation marker — adjacent host-pressure control, marker-based and audit-only; this gate is CPU-based and kind-scoped.
- **WL-0MVKNC2N50025HXE** — long-running panes monopolise slots (capacity-starvation observation) — the refusal classifier this change must deliberately exclude from.
- **WL-0MUJLCVRS0093EJJ** — machine-hygiene skill — establishes the host-pressure metric vocabulary (loadavg/PSI) but is operator-invoked only.
- **WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B**, **WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS** — wl process CPU churn and spawn-coalescing — load reduction; complementary, not a substitute.
- **WL-0MVI8YM07002Z9VY** — machine-hygiene threshold miscalibration for multi-agent hosts — may inform future threshold tuning.

**Duplicate-check:** searches for "CPU dispatch gate", "host CPU threshold" and "dispatcher CPU" found no open or completed item that gates dispatch on host CPU; recorded as net-new.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Flapping at the threshold** (assumption): the gate is evaluated once per poll tick (10 s default), so a single threshold is adequate; hysteresis was considered and rejected (second source of truth). Risk: a host oscillating around 75% alternates allow/deny — bounded by the poll cadence and harmless because in-flight work is never interrupted.
- **Metric mismatch** (assumption): `/proc/stat` deltas measure host-wide CPU on Linux. Non-Linux hosts or containers exposing a restricted `/proc` degrade to the load-average fallback or fail open — never a hard block.
- **Load-average fallback is not a percentage** (assumption): load ÷ cores × 100 is treated as an upper-bound proxy and capped at 100; it may be more pessimistic than utilisation when run-queue waiters are high, which is the intended conservative direction for a *dispatch* gate.
- **Short idle windows and audit batching**: audit batching defers the idle reset between sequential audits, so two batches in one idle window could produce a < 1 s sampling window; the short-window rule (fall back to loadavg) prevents a misleading 0% reading from bypassing the gate.
- **Existing load:** the gate cannot reduce CPU already consumed by running panes — it only prevents *new* load. It complements, not replaces, the audit host-saturation marker and the capacity-starvation observation.
- **Scope-creep risk**: related ideas (memory/IO-pressure gates, per-agent CPU budgets, adaptive threshold from machine-hygiene, reaping saturated panes) are explicitly **out of scope** and belong in their own work items; do not fold them into this change.
- **False-negative risk** (assumption): if `/proc/stat` is unreadable the fallback keeps the gate effective; only a fully unavailable host-metrics environment disables it — documented as fail-open by design.
- **No tenant isolation assumption**: the host is treated as a single dispatch domain because the leadership lease is already machine-wide.
- **Critical work can be held** (mitigation required): because the gate is a safety gate, a critical security/release item will not dispatch while the host is saturated. Mitigation: operator-initiated/manual dispatch is never gated, so the producer can always start critical work by hand; the decision-log entry names the measured CPU so the hold is diagnosable.
- **Test determinism**: tests must never read the real `/proc/stat`. The metric module is pure and the `readHostCpu` dep seam is injectable, so tests pin behaviour with fixtures rather than host state.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — What exactly is "CPU ≥ 75%"?** Options: (A) utilisation from `/proc/stat` deltas between poll ticks, normalised 0–100%, with 1-min load-per-core fallback and fail-open; (B) 1-min load average ÷ cores with a 0.75 threshold; (C) PSI `/proc/pressure/cpu` `avg10`.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply): A** — `/proc/stat` delta utilisation, normalised across cores, with the load-average fallback and fail-open. The worker already ticks at 10 s, so the delta costs nothing extra. **Recommended:** A.
- **Q2 — Gate scope?** Options: (A) block new audit/implement only, leave stalled-pane resume ungated; (B) also gate stalled-pane resume while saturated; (C) block audit/implement/risk-effort.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply): B** — audit and implement are refused, intake/plan/risk-effort continue, and in-place stalled-pane resume is also skipped while saturated so a gated tick cannot wake an agent. **Recommended:** A (the literal requirement); producer chose B to keep the saturated host from adding any new agent activity.
- **Q3 — Configuration, hysteresis and observability?** Options: (A) live-re-read `downtimeCpuGatePercent` (default 75, clamp 0–100, `0` disables), single threshold, distinct neutral `cpu-saturated` reason; (B) A plus hysteresis; (C) hard-coded constant with the neutral reason only.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply): A** — setting with default 75 and 0-disable, single threshold (poll cadence is the natural damping), distinct neutral `cpu-saturated` token that is never a strike and never a `no-candidate` cooldown. **Recommended:** A.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MM0WORIS1UCKM55** – Replace sleepSync with Atomics.wait (completed)
- **WL-0MVIPKT8L0070OVC** – machine-hygiene: /proc/pressure (PSI) metrics always report 'unavailable' — parser bug (in-progress)
- **WL-0MVI8YM07002Z9VY** – machine-hygiene: threshold miscalibration for multi-agent hosts (open)

- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0msq0rpqp00636jy, 0mvknc2n50025hxe, absent, acceptance, active (+449 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: 0mvgylu0s004wzus, absent, active, activity, add (+340 more)

# `wl sync` perf — a no-change sync must not re-import and re-index the whole store

## Background

F2 (WL-0MVJV2NNG00771C6) profiled `wl sync` on a 123.7 MB F1 fixture (2,600
items / 26,000 comments / 259 dependency edges, 78.5 MB JSONL) against a local
bare remote with the built (`dist`) CLI. Measured breakdown:

| Phase | Measured |
|---|---|
| CLI start-up (`wl --version`) | 0.23–0.37 s, 59 MB RSS |
| Pull: fetch + `git show` + JSONL parse + merge (`wl sync --dry-run`) | 3.39 s wall, 498 MB peak RSS |
| Persist: `db.import(items + edges + audits)` | **14.0 s** |
| Persist: `db.importComments(26,000)` | **43.5 s** (114.9 s with the host loaded) |
| Export: full JSONL (78.5 MB) | 2.37 s wall, 538 MB peak RSS |
| Git push to a LOCAL bare remote (fetch 0.06 s, `git show` 0.65 s, worktree add 0.90 s, `git add` 0.93 s, worktree remove 0.06 s) | ≈ 3 s |
| Whole `WL_DELTA_EXPORT_DISABLED=1 wl sync` | 91.8 s / 194.4 s wall under host load; 918–920 MB peak RSS |

CPU profiles of the persist phase (`node --cpu-prof`, self time):
`db.import` = 77.9 % `upsertFtsEntry` + 10.3 % `clearWorkItems`;
`db.importComments` = 90.2 % `upsertFtsEntry` (then 2.7 % `saveComment`,
2.6 % `clearComments`).

The sync re-imports every item and every comment and then re-indexes the FTS
row of EVERY item, even when the merge result is unchanged — so a zero-change
sync pays the whole cost. This is the largest measured cost driver in the
worklog tooling, and it is deliberately NOT absorbed by the Herdr epic (intake
scope-creep guard): the Herdr refresh never calls `wl sync` synchronously.

## Target outcome

A `wl sync` whose merge result is unchanged performs no per-record rewrite and
no FTS work, and a changed sync indexes only the changed records — with every
merge/watermark/delta semantic unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Change detection: only records whose merged value differs from the local store are written (`saveWorkItem`/`saveComment`/edges/audits). A no-change sync performs zero writes and zero FTS writes; a CPU profile of the persist phase shows no `upsertFtsEntry` cost for it.
- Persist-phase time on the 123.7 MB F2 fixture drops to ≤ 10 % of the F2 baseline (57.4 s → ≤ 5.7 s in-process `db.import` + `db.importComments`), measured with the documented F2 commands and quoted in the completion comment.
- FTS maintenance is proportional to CHANGED items (per-changed-item `upsertFtsEntry` or one batched/transactional re-index), never a full re-index of all items after a comment merge.
- Records are persisted in one transaction (or batched statements) per record type — no per-row transaction — and the existing sync contracts still hold: delta push/fallback/convergence, watermark advance only after a successful push, divergence → full snapshot, FTS search results. Existing sync and FTS tests stay green.
- Phase timings are observable (log lines and/or `--json` fields for pull, persist-items, persist-comments, export, push) so the F2 stage harness can reproduce a before/after breakdown with the documented commands.
- Docs updated (`DATA_SYNCING.md` and/or a `docs/dev/` note) with the re-runnable measurement commands and the before/after table.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/sync.ts` — `performSync` persist phase (`db.import`, `db.importComments`).
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `import()`, `importComments()`, `upsertComments()`.
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — `upsertFtsEntry`, `clearWorkItems`, `clearComments`, `saveComment`.
- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` — F1 fixture generator and the F2 `runStageProfile` evidence harness.

## Re-runnable evidence (from F2)

```sh
# 1. Generate the full-scale fixture (2,600 items / 26,000 comments / 123.7 MB)
npx tsx packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts --profile full --stages --json

# 2. Time performSync's persist phases on a DISPOSABLE COPY of the store
#    (never mutates the input; prints JSON with --json)
npx tsx packages/herdr/test/perf/wl-sync-phase-probe.ts \
  --worklog-dir <fixture>/.worklog --json
```

Representative measured output on the quietest run (2026-10-22T22:30Z,
host load ~3): `sqlite-open` 9 ms, `read-local` 98 ms, `parse-jsonl` 229 ms,
`merge` 222 ms, **`persist-items` 14.9 s**, **`persist-comments` 68.7 s**,
`export-jsonl` 1.79 s → persist = 97 % of the 85.9 s pipeline. A CPU profile
of the persist calls shows 77.9 % (`db.import`) and 90.2 % (`db.importComments`)
of the CPU in `upsertFtsEntry`. Under shared-host load the same phases ranged
to 43.5 s / 163.2 s, so quote the ratio and the CPU profile shares, not a single
wall number.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by F2 (WL-0MVJV2NNG00771C6): the measured breakdown, host context and
  the decision record live there.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQDR5ICN0098ID6** – Remove unused WorkItem import from index.ts (completed)
- **WL-0MM79H1JR0ZFY0W2** – wl gh import: no progress feedback during comment fetch phase (completed)
- **WL-0MVJV2O7H003HY9N** – F3 — Auto-sync isolation: pane never stalls on `wl sync` (open)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: absorbed, acceptance, add, advance, audits (+157 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: add, audits, background, bare, baseline (+144 more)
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` — matched: 0mvjv2nng00771c6, acceptance, add, baseline, blocked (+141 more)

## Plan

Decomposed into four children, test-first and dependency-ordered:

| # | Child | Delivers | Parent ACs |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Verify: persist write-detection regression tests (WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO) | Default-suite tests pinning zero-write/zero-FTS no-change behaviour and write proportionality | AC1, AC3, AC4 |
| 2 | Impl: change-detection persist in `db.import` / `db.importComments` (WL-0MVK6S9TN00500UL) | Diff-based persist, FTS proportional to changed items, one transaction per record type | AC1, AC3, AC4 |
| 3 | Impl: sync phase-timing observability (WL-0MVK6SD5O001K901) | Per-phase timings for pull, persist-items, persist-comments, export, push | AC5 |
| 4 | Measure and document: persist perf before/after (WL-0MVK6SDU90036BBX) | F2-scale before/after measurement (≤ 10 % target) plus docs | AC2, AC6 |

Dependencies: 1 → 2, 2 → 3, 2 → 4, 3 → 4.

Design decisions recorded for the implementation child:

- `import()` keeps destructive-replace semantics: records absent from the incoming full snapshot are still deleted (with their FTS rows), while records whose merged value is unchanged are not re-saved.
- The later-`activityAt` merge is preserved: an otherwise identical item carrying a later incoming `activityAt` is still persisted, so no comment activity timestamp is lost (this never triggers on a true no-change sync).
- `clearWorkItems()` / `clearComments()` keep their current behaviour for `importData()`, `doctor migrate` and `clear()`; the sync path uses targeted FTS-row deletion instead of a full FTS clear.
- Comment change detection is new (no `hasCommentChanged` exists today): compare the persisted comment identity/content fields.
- The delta path (`upsertItems` / `upsertComments`) is in scope for the "never a full re-index of all items after a comment merge" AC: `upsertComments()` looks up only the affected parent ids instead of scanning every item.
- `docs/DATA_SYNCING.md` does not exist in this repository, so the documentation AC is satisfied by a `docs/dev/` note plus an update to F2's `wl sync` persist section.

Vertical slice check: each child is an end-to-end slice — 1 ships tests plus write instrumentation, 2 ships the rewritten persist path with the suite green, 3 ships instrumentation plus its regression test, 4 ships the measurement and docs. No horizontal-only phases.

Between phases: re-read the next child's description (and any comments on this item) before starting it; the persist diff design in child 2 determines the exact phase boundaries measured in child 4.

Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-23 — plan session decomposed this item into 4 children (WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO, WL-0MVK6S9TN00500UL, WL-0MVK6SD5O001K901, WL-0MVK6SDU90036BBX), wired 4 dependency edges, and reflowed the acceptance-criteria bullets to one line each so machine AC-coverage extraction reads each full criterion.

# Audit fingerprint contract drift: align the TS `computeContentFingerprint` with audit_runner schema 2

## Background

`tests/unit/audit-fingerprint-parity.test.ts` compares the repository's
TypeScript `computeContentFingerprint` (`src/audit-fingerprint.ts`) with the
*installed* audit skill's Python `audit_runner._compute_content_fingerprint`.
The global audit skill is a symlink into `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/audit`,
so its contract can move ahead of this repository between installs.

Two successive drifts were observed while implementing the Herdr large-DB epic
(WL-0MVJC1EQX001QR9W):

1. The installed skill dropped the `comments` keyword argument →
   `TypeError: _compute_content_fingerprint() got an unexpected keyword
   argument 'comments'`.
2. The installed skill (SorraAgents `688d41cb0`,
   `SA-0MVIDI8E00063OOP`) replaced the algorithm with **schema 2**: the digest
   now hashes only the work item's OWN data —
   `{"schema": 2, "title_hash": sha256(title), "description_hash":
   sha256(description)}` serialised with `sort_keys=True` — and performs
   **zero git invocations**. The old scheme hashed
   `path_states`/`description_hash`/`key_files` resolved through `git log`/
   `git rev-parse`.

(A) alone was reported as WL-0MVK5SWZE00254Y7's original scope; (B) makes it a
functional drift, not just a signature skew: the TS `currentFingerprint` that
`wl list`/`wl worklist` emit would never equal the Python-stored
`audit.fingerprint`, so audit freshness would always read as stale — and the
git-based computation is an expensive per-item cost on large worklogs.

At dev HEAD `8ab31397`, `tests/unit` is red (1 failed / 655 passed) with only
this test failing, so the dev-push full-suite gate is blocked for every item.

## Target outcome

One canonical fingerprint contract, implemented identically in Python (audit
skill) and TypeScript (this repo): schema 2, item data only, zero git. The
parity test passes against the installed skill; a *signature* skew (older/newer
helper) is reported as an explicit skip naming the installed signature, while a
genuine digest mismatch still fails.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/audit-fingerprint.ts` `computeContentFingerprint` implements schema 2 exactly: sha256 over the canonical JSON `{"description_hash", "schema": 2, "title_hash"}` (Python `json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True)` separators, UTF-8), taking `{ title, description }`, and performs **no** git invocation.
- The digest is byte-identical to the installed audit skill's `_compute_content_fingerprint` for the same work item; `tests/unit/audit-fingerprint-parity.test.ts` passes against the current global install.
- A parity test where the installed helper's signature cannot accept the repo's call does not fail the suite: it is an explicit, actionable `skip` naming the installed signature/path, while a genuine digest mismatch still fails.
- Callers are updated to the new input (`title` + `description`, no `runGit`) and no longer pay per-item git cost: `src/list-enrichment.ts` (and any other caller) compiles and its tests pass.
- `currentFingerprint` semantics are preserved for consumers: `wl list --json` still emits the field; a changed title/description invalidates freshness, an unrelated commit/comment does not.
- Regression tests cover: schema-2 parity, git-free computation (a throwing `runGit` is never called), title-only change invalidates, description change invalidates, unchanged item stays fresh, and signature-skew skip.
- Documentation (`docs/`) states the schema-2 contract, why git state is excluded, and how to re-run the parity check.

## Key Files

- `src/audit-fingerprint.ts` — TS fingerprint implementation (schema 2, git-free).
- `src/list-enrichment.ts` — the only production caller of `computeContentFingerprint`.
- `tests/unit/audit-fingerprint-parity.test.ts` — Python↔TS parity and skew handling.
- `tests/unit/audit-fingerprint.test.ts` — TS behaviour regression tests.
- `docs/dev/audit-fingerprint.md` — contract documentation (new or appended).

## Dependencies

- Discovered-from: WL-0MVJV2NNG00771C6 (F2 profiling run).
- Blocks: WL-0MVJV2O7H003HY9N (F3) and every other dev push while the full suite is red.

# Verify: persist write-detection regression tests

## Background

Parent item WL-0MVK3WRY9009KV6P requires `wl sync` to stop re-importing and re-indexing the whole store when the merge result is unchanged. Before the implementation item changes `db.import` / `db.importComments`, this item adds the tests that pin the requirement: a no-change import performs zero record writes and zero FTS upserts, and a changed import writes only the differing records.

The default-suite tests must enforce the parent ACs 1, 3 and 4 (change detection, FTS proportionality, sync contract preservation) independently of the perf harness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Instrumented tests (spying on the persistent store's write methods) assert that `db.import()` of an identical full record set performs **zero** `saveWorkItem`, `saveDependencyEdge` and `saveAuditResults` writes and **zero** `upsertFtsEntry` calls; `db.importComments()` of an identical comment set performs **zero** `saveComment` writes and **zero** `upsertFtsEntry` calls.
- Tests assert that a **changed** import writes only the differing records: one changed work item triggers a single `saveWorkItem`; one added/removed comment triggers a single `saveComment` and FTS upkeep only for the affected parent item(s); unchanged sibling records are not rewritten.
- Tests assert records absent from the incoming set are still deleted (work items, comments, dependency edges) and their FTS rows removed — destructive-replace semantics preserved.
- The existing sync contract tests (delta push/fallback/convergence, watermark advance only after a successful push, divergence → full snapshot, FTS search results) stay green in the default suite.
- All new tests run in the default suite (no long/perf-suite gating).

- Change detection: only records whose merged value differs from the local store are written (`saveWorkItem`/`saveComment`/edges/audits); a no-change sync performs zero writes and zero FTS writes — enforced by these regression tests.
- Records are persisted in one transaction (or batched statements) per record type and the existing sync contracts still hold: delta push/fallback/convergence, watermark advance only after a successful push, divergence → full snapshot, FTS search results. Existing sync and FTS tests stay green.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/database.test.ts` — existing `import()`/`importComments()`/`upsertItems()`/`upsertComments()` semantics tests.
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — the write methods (`saveWorkItem`, `saveComment`, `clearWorkItems`, `clearComments`, `upsertFtsEntry`) to instrument.
- `src/commands/sync.ts` — `performSync` persist branch; integration-level assertions may drive a `wl sync` on a copied store.

## Dependencies

- None (prerequisite for the implementation item).

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a store-write spy/agent (wrap `saveWorkItem`, `saveComment`, `saveDependencyEdge`, `saveAuditResults`, `upsertFtsEntry`, `clearWorkItems`, `clearComments`) around a fresh `SqlitePersistentStore`/`WorklogDatabase` in the existing `database.test.ts` describe blocks.
- No-change cases: seed a store, re-`import()` the identical full set and re-`importComments()` the identical comment set, assert all write/`upsertFtsEntry` counters stay at zero.
- Changed cases: mutate one field / add one comment / delete one record, assert only the matching writes and only the affected parents' FTS upserts.
- Keep existing sync/FTS tests untouched; no new perf-suite gating.

## Deliverables

- Default-suite regression tests proving zero-write / zero-FTS behaviour for no-change imports and write-proportionality for changed imports.

# Impl: change-detection persist in db.import / db.importComments

## Background

F2 (WL-0MVJV2NNG00771C6) measured the sync persist phase at 83.6 s of an 85.9 s pipeline on the 123.7 MB fixture, with 78–90 % of the CPU inside `upsertFtsEntry`. `db.import()` clears every work item, re-saves every item and then re-indexes the FTS row of every item; `db.importComments()` clears every comment, re-saves every comment and re-indexes the FTS row of every item. A no-change sync therefore pays the whole cost. This item implements the fix behind parent ACs 1, 3 and 4.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `db.import()` writes only records whose merged value differs from the local store: unchanged work items/edges/audits are not re-saved, while `updatedAt` preservation and the later-`activityAt` merge still hold (an otherwise identical item carrying a later incoming `activityAt` is still persisted so no activity timestamp is lost).
- Records absent from the incoming full snapshot are still deleted (work items, comments, edges) and only those deleted ids have their FTS rows removed — `clearWorkItems()`/`clearComments()` no longer force a full FTS rebuild, with existing callers (`importData()`, `doctor migrate`, `clear()`) keeping their current destructive behaviour.
- `db.importComments()` writes only changed/new comments and performs FTS upkeep only for the affected parent item ids — FTS maintenance is proportional to changed items, never a full re-index of all items after a comment merge (the delta `upsertComments()` path too: look up only the affected ids instead of scanning every item).
- Each record type is persisted inside one transaction (or batched statements): `db.importComments()` gains a transaction wrapping its clear/save/FTS work, no per-row transaction is introduced, and `db.import()`'s existing atomicity is preserved.
- Existing sync contracts still hold — delta push/fallback/convergence, watermark advance only after a successful push, divergence → full snapshot, FTS search results — and the existing sync and FTS tests plus the write-detection tests from the verification item stay green.

- Change detection: only records whose merged value differs from the local store are written (`saveWorkItem`/`saveComment`/edges/audits); a no-change sync performs zero writes and zero FTS writes.
- FTS maintenance is proportional to CHANGED items (per-changed-item `upsertFtsEntry` or one batched/transactional re-index), never a full re-index of all items after a comment merge.
- Records are persisted in one transaction (or batched statements) per record type — no per-row transaction — and the existing sync contracts still hold: delta push/fallback/convergence, watermark advance only after a successful push, divergence → full snapshot, FTS search results. Existing sync and FTS tests stay green.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `import()`, `importComments()`, `upsertItems()`, `upsertComments()`, `hasWorkItemChanged`/`compareTrackedFields`, `mergeAuditsNewestWins`.
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — `upsertFtsEntry`, `clearWorkItems`, `clearComments`, `saveComment`, `saveWorkItem`, `transaction`.
- `src/commands/sync.ts` — `performSync` persist branch (delta via `upsertItems`/`upsertComments`, full snapshot via `import`/`importComments`).

## Dependencies

- Verify item (persist write-detection regression tests) — test-first.

## Minimal Implementation

- In `import()`: compute the diff against the existing snapshot — unchanged records (per `hasWorkItemChanged`) are skipped entirely (no `saveWorkItem`), changed/new records are saved, ids absent from the incoming set are deleted with only their FTS rows removed; keep the transaction and `updatedAt`/`activityAt` semantics.
- In `importComments()`: diff comments by identity fields, skip unchanged saves, delete removed comments, wrap clear/save/FTS in one transaction, and re-index FTS only for the affected parent ids.
- Reduce `upsertComments()` to look up only the affected parent ids (no full table scan) and confirm no full FTS rebuild remains after a comment merge.
- Preserve `clearWorkItems()`/`clearComments()` for their remaining callers; introduce targeted FTS-row deletion for the sync path.

## Deliverables

- Rewritten persist path: writes and FTS work proportional to actually-changed records, transactions per record type, contracts unchanged.

## Problem

The downtime dispatcher's no-dispatch decision log (`<worklog-root>/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log`) is capped at **100 lines** (rolling). On a busy machine that is roughly **one hour** of history, because every tick that is refused for a capacity/prefill reason writes a decision entry.

During the 2026-10-22/23 overnight starvation investigation this meant the whole night could not be reconstructed: the retained window started at `2026-10-23T05:59:58Z` and the decisions for the preceding ~8 hours had already been rotated out. The pre-05:30 reasons had to be *inferred* from pi session activity instead of read from the log.

For contrast, the retained 84-minute window carried 66 no-dispatch decisions — so the cap is genuinely exhausted in about an hour of saturated polling.

## Why it matters

- Capacity-saturation starvation is silent by design (NOP), so the decision log is the **only** forensic evidence that dispatch was attempted and why it was refused.
- Post-mortem of an overnight outage ("why did almost nothing dispatch?") is currently impossible after the fact; the operator has to guess.
- The same problem affects distinguishing `capacity-saturated` / `slots-unavailable` / `prefill-cap` / `idle-age-pending` / `no-candidate` / `review-queue-hold` / `code-freeze` after rotation.

## Goal

As an operator, I want at least a full night (24 h) of downtime dispatch decisions to remain available on a busy machine, so that a post-mortem can report the actual terminal reasons and their counts, with bounded disk use.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — On a machine producing decision entries at the observed rate (≥ 60/hour), at least the **last 24 hours** of `no-dispatch` decisions are readable after the fact (verified by a test that writes > 1,500 entries and asserts the oldest 24 h window is still present).
- [ ] AC2 — Disk growth is bounded: rotation happens on a documented size/time policy (e.g. daily files with a retention window, or size-based rotation with N kept), and the policy is configurable with a documented default.
- [ ] AC3 — An operator-facing, documented way exists to reconstruct a time-range summary (e.g. `wl`/herdr command, or documented `grep`/`jq` recipe over rotated files) that prints a reason tally per hour for a given night.
- [ ] AC4 — Existing readers/parsers of the single `downtime-coordination.log` path are either migrated atomically or continue to read the newest file without change; no dispatch decision is lost across a rotation boundary (test asserted).
- [ ] AC5 — Docs updated: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` log-schema/observability section names the retention policy and the summary recipe.

## Evidence (2026-10-23 investigation)

- `ContextHub/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log`: 100 entries covering `2026-10-23T05:59:58.509Z` → `2026-10-23T07:13:27.061Z`.
- Reason tally in that retained window: `capacity-saturated` 29, `slots-unavailable` 29, `idle-age-pending` 4, `prefill-cap` 2, `idle-age-qualified` 2 (66 no-dispatch decisions).
- Earlier overnight window (roughly `2026-10-22T21:00Z` → `2026-10-23T05:30Z`) had no retained decision records at all.

## Notes

- Related: the starvation investigation item covering long-running panes holding local-LLM capacity.
- No production behaviour change to dispatch decisions is in scope — this is observability only.
data.title: herdr: retain 24h of downtime dispatcher decision history (coordination log rotates in ~1h)

## Problem

On the night of 2026-10-22/23 almost **no work was dispatched** by the downtime dispatcher (one work item + one scheduled prompt in ~9 hours, vs 14–15 ContextHub dispatches per night on Oct 20/21). The local LLM was effectively never idle enough to pass the dispatcher's idle/capacity gate.

The cause: a handful of long-running, **operator/manually-triggered** agent panes held the shared local model continuously, each running **9.5–17.5 hours** and still `agent_status: working` this morning:

| Pane started (local) | Item | Kind | Uptime at inspection |
|---|---|---|---|
| Oct 22 19:27 | WL-0MVJC1EQX001QR9W (Herdr implement, ⚠️) | implement | 13.5 h |
| Oct 22 15:30 | MS-0MUYK064P0032374 (tce-main-street) | implement | 17.5 h |
| Oct 22 15:33 | MS-0MVCRQ475009CDZI (tce-main-street audit, 🚫) | audit | 17.5 h |
| Oct 22 23:32 | SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS (SorraAgents, 🚫) | implement | 9.5 h |

Their pi session logs confirm continuous local `code`/`plan` model usage through the night (the ContextHub one peaking 03:00–05:00Z), while the retained decision log showed 66 capacity refusals in 84 minutes (`capacity-saturated` 29, `slots-unavailable` 29, `prefill-cap` 2, etc.) with both slots in `decode`, `freeSlots: 0` and prefill serialised at `1/1`.

Key config context: `paneCloseEnabled: false` in `worklog-plugin.json`, so nothing reaps these panes; the non-terminal cooldown and stall-resume scan do not apply to panes that stay `working`.

## Why it matters

- A still-`working` pane that never reaches a terminal stage or a blocked/steady state is invisible to every recovery mechanism (stall-resume, non-terminal cooldown, pane reaper), yet it can monopolise **all** local-LLM slots for 12+ hours and starve the whole fleet's downtime dispatch.
- No alert surfaces while this happens — the dispatcher NOPs by design (`capacity-saturated` etc. are non-terminal), and the decision log rotates in ~1 hour.
- Multi-hour single sessions also collide with the serialised prefill gate (`local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1`), turning the scheduler's effective budget to 0 for other work even when one slot is technically idle.

## Goal

As an operator, I want confidence that long-running local-LLM sessions are working productively rather than silently strangling the fleet, and (if they are not) I want them surfaced, recoverable, and — failing that — for the starvation to be visible instead of silent.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — For each of the four panes identified above, a comment records the outcome of triage: was the pane productively working (evidence: stage/claims advanced, commits/tests emitted) or stuck in a loop? Each pane is either cleaned up (closed/reassigned) or explicitly justified.
- [ ] AC2 — The stall/stuck-pane detection (or a new guard) can flag a pane whose item **has not progressed** within a documented window (e.g. no stage/status change, no commit) even when `agent_status` is `working` — without requiring `status = blocked/steady`. Verified by tests.
- [ ] AC3 — When the machine-wide local-LLM capacity is continuously refused for dispatch (e.g. `capacity-saturated`/`slots-unavailable`/`prefill-cap`) for a configurable window (default suggestion: 2–3 h), a visible, documented signal is produced (log marker, coordination entry, work item, or TUI notice) — so a silent NOP night becomes discoverable. Tested.
- [ ] AC4 — Documentation note in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` describing the interaction: serialised prefill (`max_concurrent_prefills: 1`) + multi-slot sessions can hold effective dispatch budget at 0, and what operational levers exist (raise prefill concurrency, close/reap sessions, per-slot lease caps).
- [ ] AC5 — Regression test asserting the dispatcher's reason/token stream remains parseable and that no new terminal reason regresses to a silent NOP.

## Evidence

- Fleet `downtime-dispatches.log` tails (2026-10-22/23): only SA `20:04Z` implement, RISE `20:25Z` plan, WL-0MVK3WRY9009KV6P intake `23:26Z`; scheduled `/skill:refactor` `03:12Z`, `/skill:standup` `06:45Z`.
- `ContextHub/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` retained window: 66 no-dispatch decisions, all capacity/prefill/idle refusals; `freeSlots: 0` in 55/66; every tick `prefillsInFlight: 1, maxConcurrentPrefills: 1`.
- Live proxy at investigation time (07:13Z): both slots `generating (decode)`, 0 free, 2–3 `prefill_gate_waiters`.
- pi session logs (`/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/sessions/...`) for the four panes show model use across the night.
- `model-cooldowns.json`: SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81 plan pane `w45:pK4` cooldown until `2026-10-23T02:23:54Z` reason "provider exhaustion".
data.title: herdr: long-running agent panes monopolise local-LLM slots and starve downtime dispatch overnight (investigate)

# F8 — Bound the pane's cold spawn fan-out inside the ≤300 MB ceiling at full scale

## Background

F5 (`WL-0MVJV2PC2008PY64`) documented a concurrent read-spawn cap of **2** and
claimed the aggregate spawn-RSS bound `cap × per-spawn peak` stays inside the
parent's ≤ ~300 MB per-pane ceiling ("~220–227 MB"). That claim was measured on
the **tsx** (`src`) target with a warm-ish `wl show` burst (~110 MB/spawn).
F7's end-to-end verification run on the **built** CLI (`dist`, the thing
`/usr/local/bin/wl` runs) at the operator's real scale (2,600 items / 123.7 MB)
measured a **cold `wl show` burst peak of 144.6–175.3 MB per spawn**, so
`2 × peak = 289–351 MB` — and the 175 MB case breaches the 300 MB ceiling
(`runSpawnConcurrencyScenario` reports `aggregate spawn-RSS bound 347.8 MB >
300 MB`, `ok: false`). The cold peak varies run-to-run (144.6–175.3 MB), so a
cap of 2 cannot *guarantee* the documented ceiling.

The parent AC 5 permits either a per-spawn budget below the ~130–145 MB
baseline OR bounded concurrency inside the documented ceiling. Route (a) is not
available without a payload/memory redesign; route (b) must hold for the
worst-case spawn the pane can issue, not just the refresh's `wl worklist` read.

## Target outcome

The documented spawn cap guarantees the ≤ ~300 MB aggregate ceiling for the
worst-case cold read on a large DB, with the measured bound recorded and
asserted at full scale on the built CLI.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The documented concurrent read-spawn cap guarantees `cap × worst-case cold
  per-spawn peak ≤ the documented pane ceiling (300 MB)` at full scale on the
  `dist` target, including the cold `wl show` burst scenario (measured, not
  assumed).
- `runSpawnConcurrencyScenario` at full scale on `dist` reports `ok: true`
  (aggregate bound and event-loop blocking inside their documented budgets)
  and the measured numbers are recorded in `large-db-budget.json` /
  `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`.
- The fallback/fan-out latency trade-off is documented (serialised reads cost
  wall time; the consolidated single-read default view and the in-process
  expand/hydrator reads are unaffected).
- No regression: default-suite spawn-cap, large-DB ratchet, refresh-budget and
  expand/hydrator suites stay green; the consolidated one-`wl worklist`-read
  per refresh and zero-spawn-when-idle guarantees are unchanged.

## Minimal Implementation

- Lower `DEFAULT_WL_SPAWN_CAP` from 2 to 1 in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`
  (the FIFO semaphore already supports it) and update its documentation to the
  measured worst-case bound.
- Update `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-budget.json` (`acTargets.wlSpawnCap`)
  and the F5/F7 documentation numbers; keep the cold-burst assertion.
- Adjust the spawn-cap tests' documented constant expectation.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `DEFAULT_WL_SPAWN_CAP`.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-spawn-cap.test.ts` — cap contract.
- `packages/herdr/src/large-db-spawn-cap.test.ts` — measured budget ratchet.
- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-budget.json` — documented cap.
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` — measured bound.

## Deliverables

- Measured, asserted full-scale bound inside the 300 MB ceiling; docs updated;
  default suite green.

## Dependencies

- F5 (`WL-0MVJV2PC2008PY64`) — the cap mechanism this tightens.
- Discovered from F7 (`WL-0MVJV2QHO003K6H3`); blocks F7's AC 5 verdict.
data.title: F8 — Bound the pane's cold spawn fan-out inside the ≤300 MB ceiling at full scale
