data.author: implement
data.comment:
F1 implemented — spawn records now carry per-process CPU time and peak RSS.

**Code**
- `SpawnRecord` gains `cpuMs` (user+system, ms, from `process.resourceUsage()`) and `maxRssKb` (peak RSS, KiB). `recordSpawn()` appends `<kind>	<ts>	<pid>	<cpuMs>	<maxRssKb>`.
- Legacy 3-field lines still parse: `cpuMs`/`maxRssKb` are `null` (never 0), and blank fields are treated as unknown. If the platform cannot report usage the field is written blank -> parsed as `null`, so aggregation cannot silently under-report.
- New `summariseSpawnRecords(file)` -> `{ total, byKind, cpuSeconds, maxRssKb, missingCpu, missingRss }`.
- `WL_SPAWN_COUNT=1` stderr path now emits `[wl:spawn] <kind> <pid> cpuMs=<n> maxRssKb=<n>`.
- Still best-effort: no throw and no behaviour change with env unset or an unwritable file path (covered by tests).

**Tests** (`tests/spawn-counter.test.ts`): 5-field line shape, live CPU/RSS values, legacy + blank-field back-compat as `null`, unwritable file, stderr path reporting CPU/RSS, and `summariseSpawnRecords` totals/per-kind/peak-RSS/missing counters. `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts` untouched and passing (kind counts unaffected).

**Baseline deliverable** — the parent (`WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B`) is `status: open` (mutation invariant: no description/comment on an unclaimed item), so the baseline lives in the repo at `docs/dev/wl-spawn-baseline-2026-10-19.md` for the parent/F10/F11 sessions, and is summarised here. 10 runs each, `node dist/cli.js` from this worktree against the main `.worklog`, `/usr/bin/time -v`:

| Command | p95 wall | median wall | p95 RSS | mean CPU |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `wl --version` | 1.19 s | 1.01 s | 78.9 MB | 1.051 s |
| `wl next --json` | 1.10 s | 1.00 s | 79.2 MB | 1.033 s |

`sync` was measured from the main checkout with push excluded (worktrees are blocked by the cross-project sync guard; `--dry-run` primary, `--no-push` real sync as the extreme case). It receives the shared `ReadCacheCli` and the cache-enabled flag from the fast path, so cache semantics are untouched.
- New `src/argv-normalize.ts` (dependency-free `normalizeFieldsArgv`, re-exported by `cli-utils`) so the fast path can normalise argv without importing the heavy graph.

## F6 implementation summary

**New `src/command-registry.ts`** — the 30 eager `import XCommand` lines in `src/cli-main.ts` are gone:
- `COMMAND_LOADERS`: name → `() => import('./commands/x.js')` (32 names; `audit-show`/`audit-set` share the audit-result module loader and `audit-waive`/`audit-unwaive` the audit-waive loader, so each module's `register()` runs once — no duplicate commands).
- `registerBuiltInCommands(ctx, argv, {loaders, onLoad, warn})`: a single-command invocation loads only that command; bare `wl`, `--help`/`-h`, unknown commands and `completion` (whose output enumerates every command) register the full set.
- Graceful degradation (parent AC5): a rejecting loader logs exactly one warning and falls back to eager full registration, attempting every other module so one broken module cannot take the CLI down.
- `BUILT_IN_COMMAND_NAMES` (ordered) now feeds the help-grouping set in `cli-main.ts`; `applyWorklogDirOverrideFromArgv`/`--worklog-dir` handling and `loadPlugins` ordering are unchanged.

**F5 specs finalised**: the two RED-pinned `it.fails` specs flipped to real assertions (`src/command-registry.ts` now exists), with the observer semantics documented (`onLoad` fires per attempted load) and `BUILT_IN_COMMAND_NAMES.length` used for the fallback bound.

**Parity evidence**: `dist/cli.js --help` is **byte-identical** to the pre-F6 build (registration order preserved, including the `cleanup-worktree`/`completion` ordering); `wl completion bash` again lists all 32 built-ins; `wl audit-show --help`, `wl cleanup-worktree --help`, unknown-command error/exit and the cache-hit spawn records are unchanged.

Full canonical suite green (tests/cli 104 files; tests/unit 43 files).

data.author: implement
data.comment:
## F7 implementation + measured floor (AC1)

**Slimming applied**
1. `--version` now exits **before any fast-path module is imported**: the version check runs first using the dependency-free `argv-normalize` helper, so `--version` loads only `version.ts` + `spawn-counter.ts`. (Bug found and fixed while measuring: the write-completion callback is async, so the original version branch fell through into the heavy graph; it is now a true `if/else` branch.)
2. `extractCommandFromArgv` moved to `src/argv-normalize.ts` (re-exported by `read-cache-cli`) so the fast path can classify the invocation without importing the cache machinery.
3. The read-cache machinery, the worklog resolver and `process-lifecycle` are now **dynamic** imports, loaded only after the `--version` branch: static boot graph **8 → 4 modules** (`cli.ts`, `argv-normalize.ts`, `spawn-counter.ts`, `version.ts`), 3 dynamic entrypoints (`read-cache-cli`, `worklog-paths`, `process-lifecycle`), 8-module runtime union.
4. Worktree registration is unchanged inside a managed worktree but the `process-lifecycle` module is only imported there (cheap path test), so normal invocations skip it.
5. **Ratchet tightened**: the budget now records `fastPathDynamicImports` + `fastPathRuntimeModules` (union of the static graph and every dynamic entrypoint's transitive graph), so moving an import behind `await import()` cannot sidestep the budget. New tests cover the allowlist, a rejected addition, and the no-heavy-modules-on-`--version` rule. Regression policy gains a distinct `rssHeadroomPct` (25 %) and 100 % CPU headroom (tsx CPU varies ~50 % run-to-run; a gate run measured 3226 ms against a 3224 ms limit).

**Measured on the reference host (F2 harness, 12 warm runs, p95)**

| Scenario | dist before F7 | dist after F7 | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| `wl next --json` | 686 ms / 1224 ms CPU / 67.7 MB | **689 ms / 630 ms CPU / 67.8 MB** | CPU −48.5 %, wall flat |
| `wl list --status open --json` | 662 / 624 / 67.6 | **645 / 607 / 67.9** | CPU −2.7 % |
| `wl --version` | 1038 / 557 / 67.2 | **547 / 492 / 60.9** | wall −47 %, CPU −12 %, RSS −9 % |

Against the **pre-split** baseline (F2 capture, before F4): `next` 1316 ms / 1224 CPU / 78.8 MB → **689 / 630 / 67.8** (−47.7 % wall, −48.5 % CPU, −14 % RSS).

**AC1 verdict: not reachable by import slimming alone.** The bare-node floor measured in the same run is **484 ms p95 wall / 458 ms CPU / 61.2 MB** — i.e. AC1's 500 ms leaves ~16 ms over bare node, and 60 MB is *below* the bare-node RSS on this (loaded) host. The fast path is now within ~1.4× of bare node for cache hits and at bare-node level for `--version` (60.9 MB). `ac1Targets.enforced` therefore stays `false`; the measured floor is recorded in `bench/startup-import-budget.json` (`ac1Targets.note`) and an **OPEN QUESTION** is raised on the parent.

data.author: implement
data.comment:
## F9 progress + reference-host measurement (AC2)

Implementation landed (opportunistic pruning + config + bare doctor mention + docs + tests). Full suite pending; reference-host evidence captured:

**Before** (`~/.cache/wl/state`, real host): **218,986 counter files / 881 MB** (`du -sh`; ~2.4 MB of actual file bytes — the cost is directory/inode overhead). Dry-run report: 183,823 stale by TTL, 34,163 over the 1,000-file bound.

**One prune run** (`dist/cli.js doctor cache --json --prune`, 40 s wall / 30.7 s sys): removed **217,988** counters (183,823 stale by TTL + 34,165 bound pass LRU; 1 cached entry invalidated), leaving **1,006 files / 30 MB** (bound 1,000 + live counters written within the 30 s live window, never touched by pruning).

Net: **file count 218,986 → 1,006 (-99.5 %); on-disk footprint 881 MB → 30 MB (-96.6 %)**, in a single maintenance command. The 40 s runtime is stat+unlink on 218k files; the opportunistic hook now keeps the dir bounded, so a repeat prune is trivial.

data.author: implement
data.comment:
## F9 implementation summary

- **Opportunistic pruning** (`src/read-cache.ts`): `bumpStateCounter` now calls `maybePruneStateDir` through `statePruneDue()` — one `readdir` check per 20 bumps, and a full prune only when the state dir is over the bound. Explicit `maybePruneStateDir`/`wl doctor cache` calls are never rate-limited. Live counters (written within 30 s) are never removed by either pass, so a concurrent writer's cache can only be recomputed, never corrupted.
- **Configurable bound/TTL**: `WL_STATE_MAX_FILES` (default 1000) and `WL_STATE_TTL_MS` (default 7 days), read cheaply per check; documented in `CLI.md` (read-cache env section) and `CONFIG.md` (new 'Read-cache state boundedness' section with Pi-host example).
- **Bare `wl doctor`** reports pending read-cache state: additive `checkId: 'read-cache.state'` finding in JSON, and a text notice (also replacing the misleading 'no issues found' when only cache cleanup is pending).
- **Tests**: 3 new unit tests in `tests/unit/read-cache-prune.test.ts` (direct over-bound prune, bump-triggered opportunistic prune with live-counter survival, healthy under-bound dir untouched) and a new CLI test in `tests/cli/doctor-cache.test.ts` (bare doctor JSON+text flag, cleared after `--prune`). `tests/cli/doctor-upgrade-notice.test.ts` now isolates `WL_CACHE_DIR` so the host's real cache state cannot perturb the upgrade contract.
- **Reference-host measurement** quoted in the previous comment: 218,986 files / 881 MB → 1,006 files / 30 MB in one `wl doctor cache --prune` run (-99.5 % files, -96.6 % footprint).

Full canonical suite green (tests/cli 104 files / 870 tests; tests/unit 43 files / 627 tests).

data.author: implement
data.comment:
## F10 measurement and verdict (AC2)

**Repeatable procedure** (harness added as `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts`, npm scripts `benchmark:herdr-refresh` / `:json`): 4 panes share one worklog dir (20 seeded items), each pane runs the herdr refresh query set — the four mandatory `wl list` subsets plus `wl next -n 20` — every 5 s for a 30 s cycle, with `WL_SPAWN_COUNT_FILE` enabled; CPU-seconds are summed from the F1 spawn records.

```sh
# baseline: the pre-F4 build (git worktree at b60faeb1, npm run build)
npx tsx bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts --json --items 20 --cycle-seconds 30 --tick-seconds 5 --cli /tmp/wl-pre-f4/dist/cli.js
# after: current build
npm run benchmark:herdr-refresh:json -- --items 20 --cycle-seconds 30 --tick-seconds 5
# no-cache (read-work) baseline variant: prepend WL_CACHE_DISABLED=1
```

**Baseline vs after (same host, same workload, 4 panes x 30 s, 120 spawns/cycle)**

| Metric | Pre-F4 baseline | After F4-F7 | Target (0.4x) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spawns / cycle | 120 | 120 | — |
| Spawn kinds | 112 cache-hit + 8 read-work | **120 cache-hit** | all hits |
| **Total CPU-seconds / cycle** | **159.44** | **83.58** | **63.78** |
| CPU-s per spawn | 1.329 | **0.697** | <= 0.53 |
| Peak RSS | 78.8 MB | **68 MB** | — |
| Failures | 0 | 0 | 0 |

**Result: 47.6 % CPU-second reduction — short of the >= 60 % target.**

**Shortfall analysis.** Per-spawn cost fell 1.329 -> 0.697 CPU-s, but the bare-node floor on this host is ~0.46 CPU-s (~66 % of what remains). wl's own work is now ~0.24 CPU-s/spawn. Even a zero-cost `wl` body would cap the reduction at ~65 %, so the target is unreachable by making spawns faster: the remaining lever is **fewer spawns** (five separate `wl` invocations per pane per tick); one consolidated read per tick would cut spawns 5x and take the cycle to ~17 CPU-s (~90 % below baseline).

**Lever decision (AC5):** implementing the consolidated worklist read spans `wl` (new read mode/cache entry) and `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` (mandatory-subset semantics) — exceeds this measurement item's scope; filed as **WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS** with evidence and acceptance criteria.

**Correctness:** no changes to cache semantics; existing spawn-reduction simulation and fetcher tests pass unchanged (full suite green).

data.comment:
## RCA confirmed (reproduced locally: 1 failure in 5 full-file runs)

The work item hypothesis is correct: **stale frames from an earlier TUI run inside the same file land last**. Reproduced failure output showed:
- `unblocked selections render byte-for-byte without Blocked By rows across refreshes` failing with `Blocked By WL-B2 — Second blocker` — a row only the preceding `re-resolves only when the item's own signature changes` test can produce.
- `the detail view renders Blocked By rows...` failing on a plain **list** frame (no detail view, no `Blocked By`) — the late frame of an earlier list-mode test.

### Mechanism

`watchRefresh()` triggers the production DB-change callback and then waits a fixed `settle(15)` ms. `doRefresh()` is asynchronous and renders at the END of its cycle (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` ~line 6269) and, when a refresh request arrives while one is in flight, schedules a coalesced trailing refresh (`if (refreshPending) { refreshPending = false; void doRefresh(false); }`, ~line 6279). Two/three back-to-back `watchRefresh()` calls therefore leave a refresh cycle (and possibly a trailing refresh) in flight when `quit()` runs. `quit()` only awaits the TUI promise, so that cycle completes AFTER the test ends and its `render()` writes to stdout — recorded by the NEXT test's stdout spy (the mock closes over the reassigned module-level `writes` binding), i.e. attributed to the wrong test.

### Fix (harness only, per the investigation guidance)

Drain until the TUI stops writing instead of assuming a fixed tick:
- new `drainWrites()` helper: wait until no stdout write has occurred for a full quiet window (bounded, throws loudly if it never quiesces);
- `watchRefresh()` drains after triggering the callback (refresh cycles complete before assertions);
- `quit()` drains after the TUI promise resolves, so post-exit renders and coalesced trailing refreshes land in the EXITING test's capture and cannot bleed into the next test.

Production render path is NOT changed; behavioural assertions are untouched.

data.comment:
Session: implement — RED witness + root cause established.

**RED witness (dev HEAD, pre-change):** repeated runs of `npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src/worklist-agent-state-event.test.ts` fail intermittently (~40% of runs) with the reported signature — 'timed out after 5000ms waiting for GREEN_CIRCLE after late pane appears; last output showed the item without a green circle'. Additional always-reachable defect: the same command exits 1 even on a fully green run because of UNHANDLED REJECTIONS ('Cannot read properties of null (reading removeListener)', events.ts:368) — 1 per failing run, up to 4 in the original evidence.

**Two confirmed production defects (both fixed in this session):**

1. events.ts — close()/restartSubscription() nulls `this.socket` while a subscribe request is still pending; the settlement handlers then dereferenced `this.socket!` in .then/.catch, throwing an unhandled rejection (Node's default policy would crash the plugin process). Fix: capture the connected socket in a local const and remove listeners from it (safe no-op on a destroyed socket). Deterministic regression test: a stalled mock server (new `respondToSubscribe:false` option on MockHerdrSocket) leaves a subscribe pending; close() must not raise an unhandled rejection. RED confirmed before the fix (rejections[0] = the exact TypeError).

2. worklist.ts refreshPaneMarkersFromEvent — single-flight guard DROPPED a trailing event when a pass was already in flight, so a pane that appeared during that window (pane_agent_detected → operator/hydrator status change) never got its green circle. Fix: mark the refresh pending and re-run the pass after the in-flight one settles (trail-coalescing, mirroring the DB-watch pattern WL-0MTIB7JAN004MQ8N). Deterministic regression test: a controllable applyActivePaneMarkers seam holds the first event-triggered pass; a second status event arrives in that window and must still produce the GREEN_CIRCLE. RED confirmed before the fix.

**Test-harness hardening (hypothesis 2 confirmed as a further race):** the cross-instance test pushed the status event on `mockServer.getFirstClient()`, which can still be the PRE-RESTART handle (the server only removes it on the async socket close); an event pushed there reaches nobody. Replaced with `mockServer.waitForClientSubscribedTo('w5:p55')` (polling, subscription-aware: returns the connection that actually carries the late pane). Also strengthened the cross-instance test per AC2: asserts no GREEN_CIRCLE before the late pane enters the pane list and no RED_CIRCLE.

**Verification:** the file now passes 31 tests (the added 2 regressions + the 5 original + events.test.ts), 5+ consecutive clean runs, stable under 3-parallel-run load. Full packages/herdr/src suite: 107 files / 3503 tests with a single unrelated pre-existing flake in worklist-blocked-by-cache.test.ts (fail-open detail-view; passes 10/10 in isolation, no overlap with this diff) — re-running for a green record.

**Outcome:** brief drafted (stage `intake_complete`, issue type `bug`); effort **Small** (expected 2.67h), risk **Medium** (7/25), confidence 76% (see effort-and-risk comment).

**Preliminary RCA (code-confirmed):** `_resolvedModel` in `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/model-display.ts` is set only from the Local Proxy `X-Resolved-Model` response header and reset only on `session_start`. The `model_select` handler updates only `_selectedModel`, so after a mid-session `/model` switch the footer pairs the new alias with the old resolved model — permanently when the switched-to model is a non-proxy provider (`deepseek`/`opencode` in `~/.pi/agent/models.json`), where the header never arrives. This is the mid-session analogue of the already-fixed session-boundary staleness (WL-0MRZ1EIY5008VBE6).

## TDD red evidence (run via implement.py finish test gate, IMPLEMENT_TEST_COMMAND override)

All 14 new specs **fail against the current implementation** (brother of no production change); the **existing 127 tests keep passing**. Verified with vitest `run` on both files (git state fingerprint cached in the worktree's `.worklog/cache`).

### model-display.test.ts — `mid-session model switch` (11 failing specs)

1. `invalidates the resolved model on a mid-session model_select with source "set"` → `AssertionError: expected 'openai/gpt-4' to be null` (line 420)
2. `... with source "cycle"` → same
3. `... with source "restore"` → same
4. `notifies onModelChange exactly once when a mid-session switch invalidates the resolved model` → `expected 'openai/gpt-4' to be null`
5. `adopts the selected model provider/id immediately for a non-proxy provider (deepseek)` → `expected null to be 'deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro'`
6. `replaces a stale proxy-resolved value when switching to a non-proxy provider (opencode)` → `expected 'openai/gpt-4' to be 'opencode/big-pickle'`
7. `keeps a Local Proxy selection unresolved until its x-resolved-model header arrives` → `expected 'openai/gpt-4' to be null`
8. `adopts the proxy header after a non-proxy fallback value was displayed` → `expected null to be 'deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro'`
9. `uses the last selection across consecutive mid-session switches (last-write-wins)` → `expected null to be 'opencode/big-pickle'`
10. `does not throw and degrades safely when model_select has no model` → `expected 'openai/gpt-4' to be null`
11. `does not throw and degrades to (resolving) when the provider is missing` → `expected 'openai/gpt-4' to be null`

### session-health.test.ts — `mid-session model switch — end-to-end Line 3 render` (3 failing specs)

12. `re-renders Line 3 as "<newAlias> → (resolving)" immediately after a mid-session switch` → `expected 'openai/gpt-4' to be null`
13. `renders the non-proxy provider/id fallback instead of a stale value or endless "(resolving)"` → `expected null to be 'deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro'`
14. `right-aligns the longer non-proxy label and keeps it within the width budget` → `expected false to be true` (visible.endsWith('deepseek-v4-pro → deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro'))

### Hand-off notes
- **`it.fails(...)` convention (IMPORTANT for the implement sibling WL-0MVGU7H24009G8II):** these tests are authored with vitest `it.fails(...)` (expected failure) so the suite stays green pre-implementation (repo convention — WL-0MVFE0T0M009ZCPM, WL-0MT1EE3S7005DJ1F). Land the implementation by **flipping `it.fails(` → `it(`** in both files; every test must then pass (an unexpectedly-passing `it.fails` fails the suite). 14 specs to flip: 11 in model-display.test.ts + 3 in session-health.test.ts (the one plain `it` width guard stays as-is).
- **Fixture clarification (assumption, documented):** the pre-existing `model_select sets selectedModel when model id is provided` test used `provider: 'openai'` and asserted `getResolvedModel() === null`. Under the new non-proxy fallback semantics any non-`Local Proxy` provider resolves immediately, so that assertion would no longer hold. Minimal change: fixture now uses `provider: 'Local Proxy'` (assertion unchanged — the test's purpose is the alias-tracking, not provider semantics). No other existing test needed changes.
- Behaviour contract for the implementer (see also sibling item ACs): on any mid-session `model_select` (source set/cycle/restore) invalidate `_resolvedModel` and notify exactly once; non-`Local Proxy` provider → `_resolvedModel = ${provider}/${id}` immediately; `Local Proxy` → keep null until the header arrives; missing model/provider → no throw, degrade to null.

data.comment: Implementation decisions: (1) Parser: local_prefills_in_flight / local_max_concurrent_prefills / prefill_gate_waiters are availability-affecting and fail closed on malformed values (poll rejected) like contention_queue_depth; queue_eta_seconds is advisory (malformed degrades to undefined) and prefill_budget_seconds stays advisory, so a missing ETA or budget never blocks. (2) New exported evaluatePrefillPacing(status, slots): capacityBudget = 0 when cap > 0 && inFlight >= cap, else cap - inFlight (>=1), undefined (unbounded) when the cap is absent/0 or the in-flight count is not served. Deferral precedence: gate waiters -> prefill-gate, cap reached -> prefill-cap, then queue_eta_seconds or max per-slot prefill_eta_seconds above prefill_budget_seconds -> prefill-eta (both values must be finite). (3) Tick: gate waiters feed the idle-age activity check and idle-run reset (contention evidence equivalence); the pacing gate sits after slot-owned/contention and before any dispatch, so it can only reduce concurrency; effectiveFreeSlots = min(freeSlots, capacityBudget) is passed to both dispatchFromCoordination and dispatchDowntimeWork (interacts with downtimeRequiredFreeSlots and the per-tier audit >= 2 minimum). (4) Decision header tokens prefill-gate / prefill-cap / prefill-eta are distinct from contention/slot-owner/no-slots; every decision records prefillsInFlight, maxConcurrentPrefills, prefillGateWaiters, prefillBudgetSeconds, queueEtaSeconds and slotPrefillEtaSeconds. (5) No new configuration knob; absent prefill fields restore today's free-slot-only budget byte-for-byte. data.author: pi
data.comment:
**Requirement from llm-proxy-side measurement (2026-10-21): assert "one item per idle window" explicitly.** Session ID: herdr-1792596968-827039-17087

Measured over the llm-proxy log window 2026-10-21 14:56→17:00 (372 contention-queue events, 302 queue waits, 261 fallback-after-queue of which 215 burned the full 120 s budget):

1. **The idle-window race is real but small.** Only 6 of 371 queue events (2%) occurred on a session's *first* request — i.e. a fresh dispatcher launch. The other 365 (98%) are mid-session turns from 29 already-running sessions (median 30 requests/session). So this item is necessary but fixes ~2% of observed queue load; the proxy-side reservation item (llm-manager `LP-0MVICF0FX00CT0ZC`) covers the rest.

2. **Why the current gate leaks despite being correct-looking.** The dispatcher polls every 10 s. Two herdr instances can observe the same idle window within one tick; the proxy has 2 slots so it admits both, the second hits the serialised prefill gate (`local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1`), queues and then falls back remote. In-window evidence: 247 of 325 full-budget losses entered the queue with `saturation=prefill` while `available_slots` was still 2 — i.e. the proxy reported a free slot while the gate was saturated. Gating on `local_prefills_in_flight` (AC2 of this item) is the correct fix for that signal inconsistency.

3. **Requested AC addition (suggested wording):** "At most one new herdr pane is launched per observed idle window: after a dispatch the dispatcher must not launch another pane until the proxy reports `local_prefills_in_flight < local_max_concurrent_prefills` AND a fresh status tick has been observed post-dispatch (no two launches from a single poll result). Tests cover the two-instances-same-tick race, asserting the second instance defers with reason `prefill-gate`."

Recommended follow-up (separate item, to be filed on the ContextHub side): replace poll-and-launch with a **reservation claim** — ask the proxy for a gate ticket, launch only with a ticket, defer with `retry_after` when refused. Polling cannot own a single-ticket gate; only the server can allocate it.

data.author: implement
data.comment:
## Payload contract (stable — WL-C4 parses this verbatim)

`wl worklist --json` emits:

```jsonc
{
  "success": true,
  "worklogDir": "/abs/path/.worklog",
  "requestedCount": 20,
  "subsets": {
    "critical":        [],  // WorkItem[]: priority critical, status open|in-progress|blocked|completed, ALL parent levels
    "reviewQueue":     [],  // WorkItem[]: status completed|in-progress, stage in_review, root-only
    "inProgressRoots": [],  // WorkItem[]: status in-progress, root-only
    "blockedRoots":    [],  // WorkItem[]: status blocked, root-only
    "browse":          []   // { workItem, reason, group?, groupLabel? }[] — identical to `wl next -n <count> --include-in-progress --include-blocked --no-re-sort --json` .results/.workItems
  }
}
```

- Every subset key is **always present** (empty array, never omitted).
- `workItem` entries carry the same enrichment `wl next`/enrichment path adds: `auditResult`, `auditedAt`, `childCount` (browse items also carry `group`/`groupLabel` when the count is > 1).
- `-n/--number` bounds **only** `browse` (default 20); the four mandatory subsets are unbounded by it.
- Pure read: no `reSort`, never bumps the read-cache state counter (verified by tests).
- Ordering: the four list subsets use the shared hierarchy sortIndex ordering (`createHierarchyOrderComparator`); the review queue therefore uses hierarchy order rather than `wl list --stage in_review`'s 6-bucket order, which needs per-item current content fingerprints (git) that a cacheable pure read must not pay. Browse order is identical to `wl next`.
- `--worklog-dir` is honoured; `worklogDir` in the payload is the resolved worklog dir.

Commit `c8d8197f` on `dev` (branch `wl-WL-0MVI0HX58009JJRF-wl-worklist-consolidated-json-read-comma`).

## Measured evidence (same host + build: node v22.22.1, rgardler-AI-Laptop)

### bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts (4 panes, 30 s cycle, 5 s tick, 20 seeded items)

| Query set | Spawns / refresh | Spawns / cycle | CPU-s / cycle | p95 spawn wall | p50 | peak RSS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `legacy` (4× `wl list` subsets + `wl next`) | 5 | 120 | 75.68 | 1227 ms | 1012 ms | 67.9 MB |
| `consolidated` (`wl worklist --json`) | **1** | **24** | **11.89** | **568 ms** | 505 ms | 67.8 MB |
| pre-F4 baseline (recorded on F10) | 5 | 120 | 159.44 | — | — | — |
| F10 target (≤ 0.4× pre-F4) | — | — | ≤ 63.78 | — | — | — |

- Spawn count per refresh: **5 → 1** (80 % fewer), 120 → 24 per cycle — all measured spawns were `cache-hit` (one write-free read populates the shared cache entry every pane reuses).
- CPU per cycle: **0.157×** the same-host legacy cost, **0.075×** the pre-F4 baseline — well below the ≤ 0.4× / ≤ 63.78 CPU-s target.
- p95 per-spawn wall time roughly halved (1227 → 568 ms).

### bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts --json (1000 items, 20 expanded parents, 30 browse)

| Query set | Spawns / refresh | Cold | Warm | within 2 s target |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `legacy` | 5 | 1187.5 ms | 628.8 ms | yes |
| `consolidated` | **1** | **892.9 ms** | **444.9 ms** | yes |

### Reproduce

```sh
npm run benchmark:herdr-refresh:json -- --items 20 --cycle-seconds 30 --tick-seconds 5 --query-set consolidated
npm run benchmark:herdr-refresh:json -- --items 20 --cycle-seconds 30 --tick-seconds 5 --query-set legacy
npx tsx bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts --json --query-set consolidated
```

Shortfall: none — the ≤ 0.4× target is met with margin. Residual note: the review-queue subset uses hierarchy ordering rather than `wl list --stage in_review`'s 6-bucket order (that sort needs per-item git fingerprints; the bundle computes `currentFingerprint` only for audited items, so the banner state and membership are identical while the within-subset order can differ).

data.comment: Verified root cause (reproduced in run 2025-10-21, exit 3 at approval gate): propose_remediations() in pressure_analysis.py emits ONE renice per (pressure x contributor). The same top-3 RSS contributors are attached to both the memory_usage and swap_usage pressures (and memory_pressure once PSI parsing is fixed), so each renice is emitted twice/three times with identical targets. rank_actions() only sorts by impact/risk ratio — it never dedupes. Observed output confirmed: proposed actions 1-3 (node, pi, chrome-headless renice) are character-identical to 4-6. Secondary finding: renice is proposed without checking the target's current nice value — every target in the run was already at nice 19 or 0, and the targets included the two test suites currently running (AI_Hell vitest PID 2630397, tce-the-rising browser suite PID 2584821), i.e. the action would slow live work. Suggested fix: dedupe on (action, target-pids frozenset) before ranking, and skip renice when min(nice) over target pids >= proposed value. data.comment:
## F2 profile report — remaining Herdr refresh cost drivers

Reference host: `rgardler-AI-Laptop`, node `v22.22.1`, `dist` target (the built CLI that `/usr/local/bin/wl` runs), worktree `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MVJV2NNG00771C6-f2-profile-remaining-herdr-refresh-cost`.

Fixture (F1 generator, `full` profile): **2,600 items, 40 parent groups (20 expanded), 259 dependency edges, 26,000 comments, 123.7 MB DB**.

Re-runnable evidence (added by this item):

```sh
# 1. Per-stage refresh profile, full scale (JSON)
npm run build && npm run test:perf:large -- --stages --samples 5 --json
#   = npx tsx packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts --profile full --stages --samples 5 --json

# 2. Default-suite verification of the stage harness + sync probe
npx vitest run packages/herdr/src/large-db-stage-profile.test.ts packages/herdr/src/wl-sync-phase-probe.test.ts

# 3. `wl sync` persist phases on a disposable copy of a store
npx tsx packages/herdr/test/perf/wl-sync-phase-probe.ts --worklog-dir <fixture>/.worklog --json
```

Timestamps: stage runs 2026-10-22T22:16:30Z (quiet host, load 7.6 — the table below), 22:20:16Z and 22:21:53Z (load 20–30, used only for the cold per-parent spawn); sync probe 22:30:05Z (load ~3) and 22:36:06Z (load spiking to ~27); `--cpu-prof` captures 22:24Z–22:27Z.

### 1. Measured cost table — one default-view refresh

Quiet-host run (median of 5 samples; stages measured serially, so the ratio column is against the serialised baseline of **948.6 ms** — the live refresh runs these concurrently):

| Stage | Wall | CPU | Spawns | Peak RSS | Payload | Cost driver | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cli-startup` (`wl --version`) | 229.0 ms | 212.0 ms | 1 (`version`) | 59.1 MB | — | Node + CLI module graph; fixed per-spawn floor | no-op (F3/F5 cut spawn count, not the floor) |
| **`worklist-cold`** (`wl worklist -n 30 --json`, read-cache miss) | **886.4 ms (93.4 %)** | 1,007.2 ms | 1 (`read-work`) | **164.4 MB** | 3,217 KB | DB open + full-table read + subset selection + JSON serialisation inside the one consolidated spawn | **fix-in-scope → F5 / F6** |
| — derived `payload build` (cold − startup) | 657.4 ms (69.3 %) | 795.2 ms | — | — | — | The variable part of the spawn: reads + selection + serialisation | fix-in-scope → F5/F6 |
| `worklist-warm` (cache hit) | 600.4 ms (63.3 %) | 624.1 ms | 1 (`cache-hit`) | 93.9 MB | 3,217 KB | Cache hit still re-stringifies + writes the 3.2 MB payload | no-op here (payload size handled by F5) |
| `json-parse` (`JSON.parse` + `extractItems`, plugin side) | 8.5 ms (0.9 %) | 8.5 ms | 0 | — | 3,217 KB | Parsing/normalising the payload in the pane | fix-in-scope → F5 (shrinks with the payload) |
| `sqlite-open` (in-process scope, warm store) | 2.0 ms (0.2 %) | 3.0 ms | 0 | — | — | Pragmas + schema + FTS DDL on the event loop | fix-in-scope → F6 (one open per refresh) |
| `sqlite-full-read` (`db.list({})`) | 50.2 ms (5.3 %) | 64.2 ms | 0 | — | — | Materialising all 2,600 items before any filter runs | fix-in-scope → F5/F6 (SQL-side subset queries) |
| `subset-queries` (4 default-view filters) | 1.4 ms (0.1 %) | 1.4 ms | 0 | — | — | Cheap once the table is resident | no-op |
| `children-inprocess-cold` (fresh scope) | 53.1 ms (5.6 %) | 64.9 ms | 0 | — | — | Expanded-children batch read; pays the open + table read | fix-in-scope → F4/F6 |
| `children-inprocess-warm` (same scope) | 1.9 ms (0.2 %) | 2.5 ms | 0 | — | — | Shared-scope repeat read | no-op (confirms F4/F6 design) |
| `children-cli-per-parent` fallback | 185.6 ms warm-cache / **1.40 s cold** | 182.0 / 1,456.9 ms | 1 (`cache-hit` / `read-work`) | 118.8–119.3 MB | 27 KB | One spawn per expanded parent (20 → 20 spawns) vs the in-process batch | fix-in-scope → F4 |
| `actionable-count` (in-process) | 0.5 ms | 1.0 ms | 0 | — | — | In-process count on the shared scope | no-op |
| **`hydrator-dep-list`** (`wl dep list <id>`) | **263.5 ms** | 270.9 ms | 1 (not cacheable → not spawn-instrumented) | 77.0 MB | 0.3 KB | One spawn per pending-claim candidate per hydrate tick | fix-in-scope → F4 (its AC already covers hydrator dep lookups) |
| `render` (rows + `formatItemLine`) | 0.1 ms | 0.1 ms | 0 | — | — | Bounded by the visible window, not by DB size | no-op |

**Reading it:** the refresh is dominated by the one consolidated `wl worklist` spawn (93 % of the serialised baseline, 657 ms of it attributable to payload build rather than Node start-up). Everything in-process is now small: open 2 ms, full table 50 ms, children 53 ms, render 0.1 ms. The remaining per-spawn drivers are the hydrator's `wl dep list` (264 ms each) and the per-parent `wl list --parent` fallback (~1.4 s cold each, ~186 ms even on a cache hit) — both already in F4's scope.

### 2. `wl sync` profile (123.7 MB DB, 2,600 items / 26,000 comments, 78.5 MB JSONL)

`performSync`'s persist pipeline, replayed phase by phase on a disposable copy (probe above). Quiet-host run 2026-10-22T22:30:05Z:

| Phase | Wall | CPU | Share of pipeline |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sqlite-open` | 9.4 ms | 13.2 ms | 0.01 % |
| `read-local` (items + comments + edges + audits) | 97.5 ms | 146.1 ms | 0.1 % |
| `parse-jsonl` (`importFromJsonlContent`, 78.5 MB) | 228.7 ms | 395.5 ms | 0.3 % |
| `merge` (`mergeWorkItems` + comments + edges + audits) | 221.5 ms | 246.3 ms | 0.3 % |
| **`persist-items` (`db.import`)** | **14,916.2 ms** | 14,946.3 ms | **17.4 %** |
| **`persist-comments` (`db.importComments`)** | **68,676.7 ms** | 69,037.9 ms | **80.0 %** |
| `export-jsonl` (`db.exportForSync` full, 78.5 MB) | 1,793.2 ms | 2,156.1 ms | 2.1 % |
| **Total** | **85,943.2 ms** | — | 100 % |

CPU attribution (`node --cpu-prof`, self time):

- `db.import` — **77.9 % `upsertFtsEntry`**, 10.3 % `clearWorkItems`, 0.8 % `saveWorkItem`.
- `db.importComments` — **90.2 % `upsertFtsEntry`**, 2.7 % `saveComment`, 2.6 % `clearComments`.

Git/network component (local bare remote, `GIT_TRACE_PERFORMANCE=1`): fetch 0.009–0.064 s, `git show <ref>:worklog-data.jsonl` 0.655 s, `git worktree add` 0.903 s, `git add -f` 0.929 s, `git worktree remove` 0.064 s → **≈ 2.6 s of git work**, and a whole `WL_DELTA_EXPORT_DISABLED=1 wl sync` measured 91.8 s / 194.4 s wall with **918–920 MB peak RSS**. (The remote here is local, so the operator's network share is excluded; on a 78.5 MB JSONL over a real remote the upload adds to the push phase, but it cannot explain the operator's ~36 s on its own.)

**Conclusion:** a `wl sync` perf fix **is required**, and it is **NOT in scope here** (intake scope-creep guard: the Herdr refresh never calls `wl sync` synchronously). The driver is not network or git: a sync re-imports **every** item and comment and re-indexes **every** item's FTS row through `upsertFtsEntry`, so a no-change sync pays the full cost. Separate work item created and blocked on this one:

- **WL-0MVK3WRY9009KV6P — `wl sync` perf: a no-change sync must not re-import and re-index the whole store** (depends on WL-0MVJV2NNG00771C6).

### 3. Memory breakdown — `wl worklist` spawn ≈ 165 MB peak

| Component | Peak RSS | Delta | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Node + CLI module graph (`wl --version`) | 59.0 MB | — | spawn peak; the floor every spawn pays |
| SQLite open + one item read (`wl show <id>`) | 76.8 MB | +17.8 MB | store open, pragmas, schema/FTS DDL, tiny payload |
| Whole-item-table materialisation (`db.list({})`) | 165.0 MB (cold `wl worklist` peak) | **+20.4 MB v8 heap** | in-process heap delta of materialising all 2,600 items; the rest of the +88 MB over the single-item read is SQLite page cache, the serialised payload and V8 heap growth |
| Serialised payload string (3,217 KB stdout) | 165.0 MB | 3.1 MB | held by the CLI while serialising and by the pane as the `execFile` stdout buffer — the fetcher's `maxBuffer` is **5 MB**, so this payload already uses 64 % of that ceiling |
| Parsed payload object graph (pane side) | 165.0 MB | +3.0 MB heap | `JSON.parse` + `extractItems` of the real payload |

**Payload trim (feeds F5):** the 3.2 MB payload is built from **478 items** (130 critical, 106 review-queue, 106 in-progress roots, 106 blocked roots, 30 browse), each a **full `WorkItem` including its 6,000-char `description`**. The documented `wl worklist` payload contract is exactly that — full `WorkItem[]` per subset (`src/commands/worklist.ts`, `CLI.md`) — so the payload **cannot be trimmed without an explicit contract revision** (e.g. an opt-in field selection). The in-contract levers are the other two: stop materialising the whole table for a filtered read (F6) and shrink what is serialised (F5 decision, contract change). Note also that at the operator's description sizes the payload is on a path to the 5 MB `maxBuffer` ceiling.

### 4. Decision per driver

| Driver | Measured | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| Consolidated `wl worklist` spawn (payload build + parse) | 886 ms cold / 657 ms above start-up; 3.2 MB payload | **F5** (bounded spawn memory/payload) + **F6** (single cheap open, no full-table read) |
| In-process SQLite open | 2 ms warm (46–70 ms per open in earlier cold measurements) | **F6** (keep one open per refresh) |
| Full-table read for the in-process readers | 50 ms + 20.4 MB heap | **F5/F6** (SQL-side subset reads) |
| Expanded-children in-process read | 53 ms cold / 1.9 ms warm | **F4** (already in scope; no change needed beyond keeping the batch read) |
| Per-parent `wl list --parent` fallback | 1.4 s cold / 186 ms warm per parent | **F4** |
| Hydrator `wl dep list` spawn | 264 ms, 77 MB RSS per candidate per tick | **F4** (its AC covers hydrator dep lookups) |
| Render | 0.1 ms | no-op |
| `wl sync` persist pipeline | 83.6 s of an 85.9 s pipeline; 78–90 % in `upsertFtsEntry` | **separate item WL-0MVK3WRY9009KV6P** (blocked by this item) — not absorbed |

### 5. Delivered by this item

- `runStageProfile()` / `--stages` in `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` (median wall/CPU, spawn kind, peak RSS, payload bytes per stage, derived attribution table, RSS breakdown) — no production instrumentation added; spawned stages use the existing `WL_SPAWN_COUNT_FILE` records with GNU `time` as the fallback for non-cacheable spawns.
- `packages/herdr/test/perf/wl-sync-phase-probe.ts` — the `wl sync` phase profiler (copies the store, never mutates it; JSON/text output).
- Default-suite tests: `packages/herdr/src/large-db-stage-profile.test.ts` (pure attribution + one measured small-scale run) and `packages/herdr/src/wl-sync-phase-probe.test.ts` (phase coverage + input-store safety).
- Docs: `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` § "Stage profile: which driver costs what (F2…)" and § "`wl sync` persist phases".

Assumptions recorded: host load varied 3–30 during the measurement campaign (other agents' suites); the table above is the quiet-host run and the report quotes CPU where a wall number would be load-sensitive. The sync fixture has 26,000 comments (more than the operator's store) because the F1 `full` profile targets the 100 MB DB size the AC requires, so the FTS-rebuild share is amplified relative to the operator's ~15 k comments.

Session log: /home/rgardler/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-rgardler-projects-ContextHub-.worklog-worktrees-wl-WL-0MVJV2ORY002MNFF-f4-in-process-dependency-and-child-reads--/2026-10-23T04-29-44-978Z_01a16705-a290-74f9-9022-a75d3e148187.jsonl

Design decisions:
1. `fetchChildrenForItem` (single-parent expand) now reads in-process via the SAME hoisted `readChildrenInProcess` reader the batched refresh path uses, so ordering/fields/depth/childCount/audit-enrichment semantics are identical by construction. Signature kept (`(parentId, depth, scope?)`); optional scope lets a refresh-path caller reuse its ONE connection. Scope-less callers (the keypress expand path) open ONE fresh connection per expand — that is a single bounded open (~50 ms) replacing a whole 0.19-1.4 s / ~119 MB `wl list --parent` spawn; no new per-helper open is introduced INSIDE a refresh (the refresh scope stays one-open-per-refresh).
2. data.comment:
## F5 delivered — bounded `wl` spawn concurrency with a documented, asserted per-pane budget

Commit `1b68deff` (`WL-0MVJV2PC2008PY64: Implementation complete`), pushed to `dev`.

### What was chosen (and why)

The AC allows either (a) a `wl worklist` payload trim or (b) a documented spawn
cap whose aggregate RSS is asserted by an automated test. F2's evidence rules
out (a): the 3.2 MB payload is 478 items carrying full `WorkItem`s, and the
Herdr default view genuinely consumes `description` (row description preview
and the detail pane render the full markdown from the list payload), so a trim
would need an explicit contract break **and** an extra `wl show` spawn on
selection — worse for both memory and spawn count. F2 also attributed the
spawn's peak RSS mainly to the whole-table materialisation, which is F6's
remit. So F5 takes route (b): **bound the concurrency**, and the aggregate
budget becomes `cap × per-spawn peak`.

### The budget

| Budget item | Value | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|
| Concurrent `wl` READ spawns per pane | **`DEFAULT_WL_SPAWN_CAP = 2`** | production semaphore in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` (FIFO, microtask handover) |
| Aggregate spawn-RSS bound | **cap × per-spawn peak ≤ ~290 MB ≤ the 300 MB ceiling** | `evaluateSpawnCapReport()` policy + measured spawn-burst ratchet |
| Event-loop blocking under a spawn-heavy burst | ≤ 200 ms (parent AC 1) | measured event-loop probe in the same scenario |

Capped command set: `list`, `next`, `worklist`, `show`, `search`, `status`,
`dep`. Writes (claims, `wl comment add`, chord commands, `wl sync`) are
deliberately **not** capped — they are user-driven, rare, already serialised by
the CLI mutation lock, and `wl sync` keeps its F3 isolation path untouched.

### Measured before/after (spawn-burst scenario, `--spawn-burst`)

A burst of distinct **cold** `wl show <id>` reads (cache cleared, so every
spawn is `read-work` and records its own peak RSS) driven through the real
fetcher exec seam, capped phase vs the same burst with the cap widened:

| Profile | Phase | Peak concurrent `wl` | Aggregate bound (cap × peak) | Event-loop blocked | Wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| default (300 items, tsx) | capped (cap 2) | **2** | **226.6 MB** | 49.9 ms | 3.0 s |
| default (300 items, tsx) | uncapped (cap 6) | 6 | 660.6 MB | 99.6 ms | 2.0 s |
| full (2,600 items, ~124 MB, tsx) | capped (cap 2) | **2** | **220.2 MB** | **126.5 ms** | 3.9 s |
| full (2,600 items, ~124 MB, tsx) | uncapped (cap 8) | 8 | 870.4 MB | **254.3 ms — breaches ≤ 200 ms** | 2.5 s |

Reading it: the same fan-out that reached 6–8 concurrent processes (660–870 MB
aggregate, and at full scale ~1.4 GB at the 145 MB `wl worklist` peak) is held
to **2 concurrent processes / ~220 MB** by the documented cap. The full-scale
uncapped phase also **breaches the parent AC 1 input-lag bound** (254 ms vs
≤ 200 ms) — bounding concurrency bounds input lag as well as memory.

### Code and tests

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `DEFAULT_WL_SPAWN_CAP`, `get/set/resetWlSpawnCap()`,
  `_wlSpawnStats()`, `acquireWlSpawnSlot()` / `releaseWlSpawnSlot()`, applied in
  `runWlInner` around read spawns only (`WL_SPAWN_CAPPED_COMMANDS`); the
  existing in-flight read memo is unchanged and composes (a deduplicated racing
  read consumes ONE slot).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-spawn-cap.test.ts` (7 tests) — cap documented +
  rejects meaningless values; a burst of 8 never exceeds the cap and settles
  every read; FIFO release order with a live event-loop heartbeat proving the
  queue never blocks input; a rejecting spawn releases its slot (no wedge); a
  deduplicated racing read costs one slot; serialised mode (cap 1) holds.
- `packages/herdr/src/large-db-spawn-cap.test.ts` — policy unit tests (cap
  exceeded, dropped reads, RSS bound over the ceiling, loop blocking) plus one
  **measured** default-profile burst through the real exec seam.
- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` — `runSpawnConcurrencyScenario()`,
  `evaluateSpawnCapReport()`, `formatSpawnCapReport()`, `--spawn-burst N` CLI
  flag; `acTargets.wlSpawnCap` added and re-exported for policy tests.
- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-budget.json` — `acTargets.wlSpawnCap: 2`
  recorded with the budget note.
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` — new section "Bounded `wl` spawn
  concurrency (F5…)" with the budget table, the measured before/after table,
  the reproduction commands, and per-AC coverage.

### Validation

- `herdr` group suite: **116 files / 3,668 tests passed** (`--group herdr --force`).
- `implement.py finish`: build OK, **full-scope** suite green (470 s — the
  changed-scope selector fell back to full because the branch had no dev
  baseline), commit `1b68deff`, push to `dev` succeeded.
- Post-push `run_tests.py --summary --suite all --json` reports `missing`: the
  cache entry is keyed to the worktree's git state, and the main checkout's
  local `dev` has **diverged** from `origin/dev` (it is ahead 1 / behind 1 —
  a pre-existing standup commit that nobody pushed), so `implement.py finish`
  skipped the fast-forward sync. The authoritative full-suite evidence is the
  finish-phase full-scope run at `1b68deff` itself; no re-run was made against
  the stale local checkout because it does not contain this commit.

### AC coverage

1. **Budget confirmed** — aggregate per-pane spawn-RSS budget documented and
   asserted as `cap × per-spawn peak` (measured 220.2 MB at full scale, inside
   the ~300 MB ceiling); per-spawn peaks stay recorded per profile/target in
   `large-db-budget.json` (F1 ratchet).
2. **Documented spawn cap with automated RSS assertion** — option (b):
   `DEFAULT_WL_SPAWN_CAP = 2`, enforced in production code and asserted by the
   measured spawn-burst ratchet; queued reads never wait under the event loop
   (49.9 / 126.5 ms total blocking, ≤ 200 ms bound).
3. **Documented in `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`** — budget,
   enforcement, evidence and AC mapping.
4. **No regression** — the default view still issues ONE consolidated
   `wl worklist` read per refresh (F1 ratchet: 1 spawn/refresh, consolidated
   read in every sample); the cap only engages when more than two reads race;
   idle ticks still spawn nothing; small worklogs are unaffected (cap 2 is
   never reached by a single consolidated read).
5. **Spawns off the event loop / input never blocked** — promise FIFO with
   microtask handover; measured burst blocking stays inside the ≤ 200 ms
   aggregate bound at both profiles.
6. **No new heavy dependency** — the cap is a promise queue (no library, no new
   import); reads keep preferring the in-process SQLite path over new spawns.

Assumption recorded: the aggregate bound uses the *maximum* per-spawn peak
observed in the burst (worst case), not an average — conservative, since a
queued read only starts after a predecessor exits.

Observation for the producer (not fixed here, out of scope): the main
checkout's local `dev` is `ahead 1, behind 1` vs `origin/dev` (a standup commit
was never pushed). `implement.py finish` skipped its `--ff-only` parent sync
because of it, so the next worktree forks from a local `dev` that lacks
`1b68deff`. Worth resolving before the next child of the epic.

`--ac-report` (new) runs the F1 refresh budget, F3 sync-in-flight, F4

AC1–AC6 into one JSON report (`runAcReport` / `buildAcReport`) plus a human
summary; the raw scenario reports and the budget ratchet are attached.

123.7 MB fixture, 5 refresh / 5 write→reflect / 5 sync-in-flight samples:

| AC | Measured | Target | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC1 pane responds during refresh | event-loop blocked p95 **195.7 ms**; max single stall 187.1 ms; capped spawn burst 143.7 ms | ≤ ~200 ms | **met** |

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required — the item was fully specified by intake/F2 (target outcome, 6 measurable ACs, key files, re-runnable measurement commands). Ambiguities were resolved from code inspection and are recorded as design decisions in the Plan block of this item. This appendix records the resolutions and their evidence:

- Q: Does `import()` keep destructive-replace semantics (delete records absent from the incoming set)? Answer (eng): Yes — parent AC "divergence → full snapshot" and the existing `import()` docstring require absent records to be deleted with their FTS rows; unchanged records are simply not re-saved. Evidence: `packages/shared/src/database.ts` `import()` (clearWorkItems + re-insert, atomic transaction; WL-0MT2KYCNB000CYWV / SA-0MUJNFF3K009BF03 references).
- Q: Can an otherwise unchanged item with a later incoming `activityAt` be skipped? Answer (eng): No — the existing later-`activityAt` merge (`laterTimestamp(item.activityAt, existing.activityAt)`) must preserve comment activity, so such an item is still persisted. Only a true no-change sync yields zero writes. Evidence: `packages/shared/src/database.ts` `import()` no-op guard.
- Q: Is comment change detection feasible without a dedicated comparator? Answer (eng): Yes — none exists today (`importComments()` clears and re-saves all comments); the implementation child adds identity/content-field comparison. Evidence: `packages/shared/src/database.ts` `importComments()`; `src/sync.ts` `mergeComments()`.
- Q: Does the delta path need the same FTS proportionality work? Answer (eng): Yes, for the parent AC wording "never a full re-index of all items after a comment merge" — `upsertComments()` currently scans every item to find affected parents and will look up only the affected ids instead. Evidence: `packages/shared/src/database.ts` `upsertComments()`.
- Q: Where do the docs go? Answer (eng): `docs/DATA_SYNCING.md` does not exist in this repository; the parent AC allows "a `docs/dev/` note", so a new note plus an update to F2's `### wl sync persist phases` section in `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` satisfies AC 6. Evidence: `ls docs/` of this repo.
- Q: Should the parent acceptance-criteria bullets be reflowed to one line each? Answer (plan): Yes — formatting only, wording unchanged; machine AC-coverage extraction is line-based and otherwise could not read the full criterion. Evidence: `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` `extract_acceptance_criteria()`. This session verified the implementation against this item's ACs instead of re-implementing it, and closed the one uncovered gap.

## AC verification (code at `0d8324df` + `5d662554`)
- **AC1 — only changed records written**: `WorklogDatabase.import()` diffs against the stored snapshot (`hasWorkItemChanged`, 16-field tracked set); unchanged items are skipped entirely, changed items keep the bumped `updatedAt`, and an identical item carrying a later incoming `activityAt` is still persisted with the stored `updatedAt` preserved. Dependency edges are diffed by `(fromId,toId)` + `createdAt`; audits are diffed field-by-field and written only when they differ. Pinned by `tests/unit/persist-write-detection.test.ts` (zero writes/FTS on a no-change import; one changed item → exactly one `saveWorkItem` + one FTS upsert; later `activityAt` persisted without an `updatedAt` bump) and `packages/shared/src/database.test.ts`.
- **AC2 — destructive replace + targeted FTS removal**: ids absent from the incoming snapshot are still deleted (`deleteWorkItem` cascade removes comments/edges/audits) and `deleteFtsEntry(id)` removes only those rows. `clearWorkItems()`/`clearComments()` keep their existing full-FTS behaviour for `importData()`, `doctor migrate` and `clear()`, and are no longer used by the sync persist path (tests assert they are not called).
- **AC3 — FTS proportional to changed records**: `importComments()` diffs comments (`hasCommentChanged`, with `unescapeText` normalisation so a re-import is a no-op) and re-indexes only the parents whose comment text changed (both parents when a comment moves between items); `upsertComments()` looks up only the affected parent ids via `getWorkItem(id)` instead of scanning `getAllWorkItems()`.
- **AC4 — one transaction per record type (gap closed this session)**: `import()` keeps its single outer transaction, and `importComments()`'s clear/save/FTS work is wrapped in one `store.transaction()`. No test pinned this atomicity, so this session added two: a failing save mid-`importComments()` rolls back both the deletion and the already-executed save; a failing save mid-`import()` rolls back the item deletion, the changed item, the new item and the cascaded edge. Deleted rows go through `deleteWorkItem()`, whose nested savepoint stays inside the outer transaction — no per-row commit.
- **AC5 — contracts preserved**: the full suite (`--scope full`, `tests/cli && tests/unit`) is green at the pushed commit: 49 unit test files / 693 tests passed, CLI suite included by the `&&` chain, 0 failures (`run_tests.py` JSON `success: true`, 696.8 s). Implementation notes (AC1-AC5).

**AC1 — pane triage (evidence 2026-10-23 ~10:20Z).** The four panes identified in the incident were re-checked against their work items (read-only `wl`/sqlite + pi session logs). Three were PRODUCTIVE, just very long: MS-0MUYK064P0032374 (tce-main-street) completed/in_review 09:59Z; MS-0MVCRQ475009CDZI (tce-main-street) completed/in_review 09:21Z; SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS (SorraAgents) completed/in_review 07:12Z — all 12-17 h sessions that eventually reached the review queue. The fourth, WL-0MVJC1EQX001QR9W (ContextHub, 'Manually triggered implement', started 18:27Z), is still `open`/`intake_complete` after ~16 h (assignee `implement`, last update 10:18Z) — alive and still emitting model calls, but the ITEM HAS NOT PROGRESSED past its starting stage: exactly the failure mode this item adds detection for. No pane was closed: all four are operator-owned ('Manually triggered') sessions, three already finished, and closing the live one requires operator permission (not taken). The local proxy remains saturated at check time (0/2 slots available, both generating/decode, slots_stale).

**AC2 — long-running pane detector.** New pure module `packages/herdr/src/long-running-panes.ts`: `classifyLongRunningPane` + `scanLongRunningPanes`. Flags a live-agent pane whose NON-TERMINAL item has had no progress anchor (later of item.updatedAt and the latest non-spawn-failed/non-enrichment dispatch marker for the kind) for >= `downtimeLongRunningThresholdMs` (default 3 h, clamped 1 h-48 h) INCLUDING while `agent_status` is `working`. Observation only — nothing resumes/prompts/closes a pane. Exclusions: no-agent/no-item-id/kind-unknown/item-terminal/kind-stale/last-activity-unknown. Reuses `resolveLastActivityAt`/`itemAdvancedPastKind` (now exported from stalled-work.ts) and the canonical `paneLabelItemId`/`stalledPaneKindFromLabel`.

**AC3 — starvation signal.** New pure module `packages/herdr/src/capacity-starvation.ts`: `CapacityStarvationTracker` + `isCapacityRefusal` + clamp (default 2 h, clamped 5 min-24 h). Fed from the worker's decision-log path with every BLOCKING refusal (including rate-limited repeats); any non-capacity outcome (no-candidate/review-queue-hold/code-freeze/wl-error/stalled-resume/...) and any successful dispatch reset the episode. On crossing the window the tick writes ONE `capacity-starved` OBSERVATION (operation no-dispatch, blocking:false — the header blocking token and the underlying refusal reason are untouched; written even when the refusal line is rate-limited) with `starvedSince`/`starvedMs`/`consecutiveCapacityRefusals`/`lastCapacityReason`, and — when the `scanLongRunningPanes` dep is wired — `longRunningPanes[]` naming the panes holding the model (paneId/itemId/cwd/kind/stalledForMs/agentStatus/stage/title).

**Wiring.** `DowntimeWorkerDeps.scanLongRunningPanes?` (production wiring in `createDowntimeDeps` reuses the stalled-scan seams: pane list, wl show, rolling log, root resolver; fail-safe -> []). Settings `downtimeCapacityStarvationAlertMs` + `downtimeLongRunningThresholdMs` added to settings.ts (defaults/clamps read live each tick). Window bounds are owned by downtime-worker.ts and imported by the detector so the worker keeps a TYPE-ONLY import of the new module — avoids a runtime import cycle (verified: an initial implementation caused a TDZ failure in settings.ts, fixed by this layering).

**AC4 — docs.** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` gains the 'Capacity-starvation signal & long-running pane detection' section (incl. the prefill-serialisation interaction and operational levers), both settings tables and the files table; `packages/herdr/README.md` gains the bullet + the two settings.

**AC5 — regression.** `downtime-worker.starvation.test.ts` pins the end-to-end signal (fires once per window, carries episode evidence + pane names, resets after a successful dispatch, observation never replaces the refusal stream) and asserts `capacity-starved` is a DISTINCT token that collides with no existing refusal header token. `capacity-starvation.test.ts` and `long-running-panes.test.ts` cover the pure semantics, clamps, fail-safe scans and the `working`-agent case.

**Verification.** `npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/herdr` clean; mock-budget check 16 files / 0 violations; `run_tests.py --group herdr` (117 files, 3685 tests) all green.
